Lions Insider Answers 5 Biggest Questions Ahead of Cardinals Week 5 Clash
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Detroit Lions are set to meet at State Farm Stadium for a Week 5 clash that could sway either team's season.
Both teams have strong offenses that are countered with dissapointing defensive outings, and a loss could place either defensive play-caller on the hot seat after just five weeks of play.
We're expecting a shootout in the desert, and to gain a better idea of what will transpire today, we spoke with Detroit Lions On SI's John Maakaron.
The five biggest questions we had, and his answers:
JM: The Lions offense has been challenged already by Dan Campbell to score more points. It is not that the offense is not playing well, but they are leaving a lot of points on the table. Early in the season, Detroit has not had the most explosive offense, but Petzing has found a way to utilize Jahmyr Gibbs correctly.
In the second quarter of the season, I would expect Petzing to get more of the weapons involved, especially Jameson Williams, who has had a slow start to the 2026 season.
JM: It is a combination of everything. General manager Brad Holmes failed to properly address the secondary after first-round pick Terrion Arnold ran into legal troubles. The secondary is below average and Detroit is realizing having a cornerback room full of undersized cornerbacks might not be the best plan.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard is just in way over his head. Supporters want him dismissed, as the defense is ranked last in several statistical categories to start the season. As good as the Lions' offense is, the defense is un utter disarray.
JM: Wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa is a young wide receiver with high upside. Jameson Williams has had issues with drops to start the season. TeSlaa is know for his ability to make contested grabs. He is not the quickest off the line of scrimmage, but his big frame allows him to be in position to make big grabs.
Being that the Cardinals pass defense has struggled, TeSlaa could find some additional targets this week. Detroit's front office and coaching staff are high on him.
JM: If Campbell wants the Lions to score 35 points every week, I think this is the week to unlock the passing attacks. The Cardinals passing defense is not that prolific, so I would expect Jared Goff to test the secondary early and often. Gibbs will get his fair share of touches, but I expect Williams, TesLaa, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Sam LaPorta to put up some relevant statistical numbers.
JM: I am hoping for a shootout. Both teams seem to struggle defensively, so there may not be much defense being played in this Week 5 contest.
Detroit is desperate to enter the bye week with a 3-2 record. The defense has been besieged with scrutiny. Even if the Cardinals fall behind early, they should be in the game, as Sheppard's defense has not been good at keeping opponents out of the end zone.
In the end, Goff is better than Jacoby Brissett, so I got the Lions winning 35-31.

title: Cardinals Get Huge Walter Nolen Injury Break Before Lions Showdown
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals initially listed defensive lineman Walter Nolen III as questionable entering Week 5's matchup against the Detroit Lions due to a calf injury.
Nolen, limited in Thursday and Friday practices, is set to play barring any setbacks according to Arizona Sports' John Gambadoro.
"Looks like Cardinals DT Walter Nolen, who is listed as questionable with a calf injury, will be a go for tomorrow vs Detroit at State Farm Stadium. This is of course barring any late-minute setback," he wrote on X.
Looks like Cardinals DT Walter Nolen, who is listed as questionable with a calf injury, will be a go for tomorrow vs Detroit at State Farm Stadium. This is of course barring any late-minute setback.
The Cardinals didn't elevate a defensive lineman from their practice squad for Sunday, which gave confidence that Nolen would play in Week 5.
Official inactives are due at 11:55 AM, so we'll know then if Nolen is actually good to go — though by all accounts he's set to have the green light.
Entering 2026, Nolen was fresh off a pair of injuries that limited the former first-round pick to just six games in his rookie season.
However, Nolen showed just how dominant he could be in such a small sample size in 2025, which opened the door for fairly large hopes entering this season.
"I feel like it starts with us (along the interior), especially talking about my position. I feel like I’m the heartbeat of the defense a lot of times," Nolen said before the season began, showing an understanding of just how impactful he could be.
“When I’m on the field, things move a little bit differently. So as long as I’m out there, I feel like we’re going to kick ass.”
However, Nolen's start to his sophomore campaign hasn't exactly gone as planned. He's tallied just eight tackles and one sack through four games.
The Cardinals' pass rush again has been underwhelming, and despite offseason additions such as Roy Lopez added to the front seven, the onus is again on figures such as Nolen and Josh Sweat to step up and produce to high levels.
Unfortunately for Arizona, both Sweat and Nolen haven't exactly shot out of a cannon in the first four weeks of the season.
For what it's worth, Nolen's 19% ESPN win rate on pass rushes is on par or higher than Leonard Williams, Daron Payne and Dexter Lawrence thus far.
Will that come against the Lions? Detroit is middle of the pack when it comes to team sacks allowed (8). In a game that is positioned to be a shootout, the Cardinals will need every ounce of help possible.
Nolen's presence is massive.

title: Cardinals Mailbag: When Will Arizona Finally Start Carson Beck?
full_text:
It's gameday, Arizona Cardinals fans.
The Cardinals play host to the Detroit Lions in Week 5 with a 1:25 PM kickoff at State Farm Stadium. Arizona, sitting at 1-3, has to find the win column before their season threatens to spiral.
Thanks to everybody for your mailbag questions ! For those curious, I did ask this before Marvin Harrison Jr. was reportedly pushed out the door for a trade.
That's a great question, Evan. It's entirely team-dependent.
In most cases, the general manager assembles the roster through acquisitions/offseason and will trust the coach to make the correct lineup decisions throughout the season. Much like Mike LaFleur will have his opinion on moves made through the offseason, Ossenfort will be able to throw his two cents in when it comes to decisions.
If we're trying to identify if Ossenfort has major influence on personnel decisions, that's pretty unknown to the public. Using my best educated guess, I'd say LaFleur has open conversations with Ossenfort about various decisions throughout the week while major moves (such as benching your quarterback) are a bit more collective.
Mike LaFleur was asked earlier in the season about both players but didn't want to divulge much information on either player. He said both were progressing but didn't mention anything about their practice windows potentially opening up.
Conner and Reiman were eligible to return after Week 4, though unless LaFleur's simply hiding their close return up his sleeve (which may be possible), I wouldn't believe Reiman or Conner are on the immediate doorstep of returning.
Assuming this is in the offseason, that's pretty plausible. Rallis' contract is reportedly up after this season and I'm not quite sure he makes it through the regular season as Arizona's defensive coordinator.
If the year goes as expected , the Cardinals will eventually promote Teryl Austin to their defensive play-caller in hopes of getting something different out of this defense. From there, it all depends on how Austin does the rest of the way.
For what it's worth, I do think the Cardinals would target a seasoned defensive coordinator. Bowles' resume as a DC is strong and at least in the moment would be an upgrade over Rallis, though Rallis' future departure and Bowles' arrival aren't tied together.
I think every fan is entitled to their opinion and their expectations, but personally I was never going to count wins and losses as a major measuring stick in LaFleur's first season.
I simply wanted to see building blocks established in 2026, which won't be really seen until we're closer to the end of the season.
Look, I tend to lean more towards the optimistic/patient side of things. That's not always for the best. However, the Cardinals are just a few plays away from being a 3-1 team. The moral scoreboard isn't real, though Arizona looks much better than initially anticipated.
There's still so much of the season left. I'm intrigued to see how things unfold.
At least for now, trust the process.
Sam, we're not sure what Michael Bidwill thinks because we don't talk to him. The only opportunities we have to speak with Bidwill are when a major firing/hiring happens — and then the facility groundbreaking event you're referring to with the team president label.
I'd probably assume he's not a fan of what's happening but wants to be patient with a first-year coach. With that said, I would tend to believe general manager Monti Ossenfort's seat is only getting warmer with each loss.
Heavy, you asked a ton of questions and I appreciate you for them — but I wanted to touch on this since it's such a hot topic.
At some point we're bound to see Beck. Unless Brissett and/or Gardner Minshew can really turn things around, it's when — not if — Beck comes into the lineup.
Exactly when remains to be seen. My educated guess is Week 12 at the latest, which would give Beck two games before a quick bye week and three more games to finish out the regular season.
Would more time be beneficial for Beck? Absolutely, though the Cardinals are locked into a "try to win now" mode and they're not thinking about the future.
As for who makes the call, I'd imagine Ossenfort and LaFleur have their respective opinions. If the Cardinals didn't need to evaluate Beck for the future I'd imagine it would be mostly LaFleur's call, though circumstances probably dictate Ossenfort (or perhaps even Bidwill) has pull there.

title: Cardinals' Trade Partner for Marvin Harrison Jr. Finally Becoming Clear
full_text:
ARIZONA — Arizona Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison Jr. made waves through the NFL world early Saturday morning when it was revealed the organization was trading the former No. 4 overall pick.
Yet in an odd turn of events, nobody was able to pinpoint where Harrison was being traded to — or for what compensation — ahead of Week 5. Harrison's expected to be inactive for the Cardinals' home game on Sunday against the Detroit Lions with a deal expected to be completed early next week.
We've gone the entire day with no clear picture of where Harrison will ultimately land, though ESPN's Jeremy Fowler says the Houston Texans are the expected team across the league:
"As of Saturday night, multiple execs gauging the overall trade market as well as an Arizona player source believe Harrison Jr. will be a Houston Texan," he put on X.
As of Saturday night, multiple execs gauging the overall trade market as well as an Arizona player source believe Harrison Jr. will be a Houston Texan https://t.co/cfmKj5FPNH
Harrison's had a slow start to his third NFL season, catching just five passes for 85 yards and a touchdown in four weeks. Harrison's by far been a massive secondary option to top Cardinals weapons in Trey McBride and Michael Wilson.
All offseason, expectations around the desert were high for new head coach Mike LaFleur in terms of getting the Ohio State product going on the field. Despite flashes through his first two seasons, Harrison's been a forgotten commodity in Arizona's new offense.
Harrison projects to land with the Texans, who are 0-4 entering Sunday and are looking for a massive change of pace on the offensive side of the ball.
In terms of compensation, the Cardinals are reportedly eying a second-round pick on top of extra capital to move off Harrison, who will have his fifth-year option due in the 2027 offseason, which was a major point for the urgency from other teams to potentiall get a deal done.
"Harrison is due $4 million this year and $5.62 million next year. He also has a fifth-year option decision coming up this offseason. His $22.5 million signing bonus was already paid by the Cardinals," wrote ESPN's Josh Weinfuss.
"Some of the urgency for a trade can be explained in that acquiring teams want to have him for as many games as possible, not only to play him but also to get information for the looming fifth-year option decision."
Eyes in Arizona were raised earlier this week when it was revealed Harrison hired two NFL agents — spring-boarding trade speculation that consistently grew as the early stages of the regular season unraveled.
The NFL's trade deadline is Nov. 10, though Harrison is expected to be moved much sooner as opposed to later.

title: 2027 NFL Mock Draft: Cardinals Land Future QB, Offense Dominates Top 10
full_text:
We're somehow already a quarter of the way through the 2026 season, and it hasn't been without its fair share of surprises.
Multiple championship-contending teams are winless, while last year's bottom-dwellers are making waves as playoff hopefuls. Unfortunately, the Arizona Cardinals find themselves about where they were expected to be: a bad team looking ahead to the 2027 NFL Draft.
That leads us to our newest 2027 NFL Mock Draft at the quarter mark of the year. The Cardinals are in the running for the top overall pick, with their Super Bowl odds near the bottom of FanDuel's book. We will be sticking with FanDuel's Super Bowl odds inverted for this mock draft, as I am not ready to count on teams like the Houston Texans, based on their current records, to stink it up for an entire year and pick first overall.
We will move on from inverted odds for our mock marking the halfway point of the season.
Until then, we will dive into this new mock draft, this time with a different team drafting first overall and the Cardinals waiting a couple of picks before making their move.
The Miami Dolphins are on the clock...
Sorry to anyone who thinks Jeremiah Smith should go 1.01 to the Dolphins in any scenario; Malik Willis is not remotely good enough to win games no matter what he has around him. Willis is fine and a really good backup option. Miami needs a much better quarterback to compete.
Darian Mensah is now my QB1 until further notice. Mensah has diced up everyone he’s faced this season and has proven success at two other programs to make me confident that his progression is legitimate. It will be telling to see how he performs as the competition gets better, but I’m all-in on Mensah right now.
The pick: Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State
It’s only year two, and I usually believe that rookie quarterbacks need/deserve three seasons before moving on. Cam Ward has given me serious pause about his ability to be a franchise quarterback, but he and the franchise are staring at the ultimate player to see if he can turn it around.
Jeremiah Smith is undeniably the best prospect in the entire 2027 draft class and would’ve been just as coveted in the past two classes as well. Smith has put together perhaps the greatest college career a wide receiver has ever had, and the only thing currently missing from his mantle, a Heisman Trophy, could be his this year. Adding Smith gives this offense less than zero excuses to become potent with the talent and upside that Ward has.
The pick: Dante Moore, QB, Oregon
Jacoby Brissett has been predictably terrible and the hope is that the Cardinals will give Carson Beck a chance to advertise himself as the quarterback of the future sooner rather than later. The offense hasn’t been as great as fans hoped outside of Trey McBride and, unfortunately, Marvin Harrison Jr., who may be traded at this point. Still, the offense won’t succeed with whomever they put out there until they finally get their quarterback under center.
The rumor was that the Arizona Cardinals did a lot of homework on Dante Moore last year before he chose to return to Oregon for another season. The same front office is (currently) intact, and offensive-minded head coach Mike LaFleur could lead to Moore being their guy over others if they’re in range of a quarterback. Moore has still looked great despite Oregon’s struggles and feels like a surefire top-five pick if/when he declares.
The pick: Arch Manning, QB, Texas
Geno Smith has been a pleasant surprise over the first month of the season for the Jets. Sure, the Jets are just 1-3, but they’ve been competitive while Smith plays efficient and turnover-free football. Still, the soon-to-be 36-year-old shouldn’t be viewed as the long-term quarterback for a Jets team that appears to be making all the right moves for the first time in a while.
Arch Manning’s “fall” from the top pick doesn’t mean he’s been bad, but he is showing the same growing pains as he did a year ago. Still, the box score is far less flattering to Manning’s 2026 campaign than it’s actually been, and I’m still in on the legacy quarterback. With the weapons that the Jets have managed to put around their offense, Manning should have no trouble making friends and creating big plays out of the gate.
The pick: Colin Simmons, EDGE, Texas
Speaking of surprising quarterbacks, Deshaun Watson has been terrific. That said, Watson is a free agent following the season, and the Browns may want a fresh start regardless of how he plays this year considering the previous four seasons. But let’s pretend for a moment that Cleveland decides to hitch its wagon for even just another season and grabs the best player on the board rather than taking the fourth quarterback in the top-five picks.
Insert Colin Simmons, college football’s best defensive player in the nation. Simmons wrecked a good Tennessee offensive line (the offensive tackles specifically) and has been highly productive since his freshman season. To this point, even Simmons’ somewhat “less-than-ideal” measurements feel like nitpicking, and teams should be focused on what's in front of them: a great player.
The pick: Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame
Although the Giants have found ways to be competitive this year, they’ve shown flaws that keep them from being contenders even under the great John Harbaugh. Injuries haven’t helped any, but the obvious holes this team faced going into the season have proven to be the team’s biggest weaknesses; cornerback has been as concerning as we feared, but an elite solution is available.
Pound for pound, Leonard Moore is as elite a defender as Colin Simmons is, just at a different position. Like Simmons, Moore has been a gamer since his freshman season and has only gotten better and better with each game he plays. Moore is a no-brainer pick for any team, and the Giants should be thrilled to add him to a shaky secondary.
The pick: CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame
Father Time has finally caught up to Aaron Rodgers, who looks like one of the worst quarterbacks in the NFL. The offense has been pitiful as a whole and cannot complement a defense that is still winning games for the Steelers for yet another season. Pittsburgh must secure its quarterback of the future in 2027, or its luck of staying above .500 will face doubts beyond this season.
I entered the year a big fan of CJ Carr and he hasn’t done anything to make me regret that belief. Notre Dame is among the best teams in all of college football this season and Carr has been at the forefront of that success. There’s still a chance Carr will be taken even earlier than pick number seven, making him an elite option for the Steelers to fancy and become their franchise signal caller.
The pick: Ellis Robinson IV, CB, Georgia
The Buccaneers have been one of the biggest surprises of the season through the first month of 2026. Baker Mayfield has been nothing short of miserable at quarterback, but the team appears to have hit its wall after years of overachieving and benefiting from a weak conference. Given Mayfield’s contract extension before the season, it would be very inappropriate and bad team-building to draft someone in the first round, let alone the fifth quarterback with a top-eight pick.
Instead, I have Tampa Bay adding a freaky athlete and an elite option to shore up a rebuilding cornerback room. Ellis Robinson IV developed nicely the last two years after sitting and learning as a freshman. Considering his current trajectory, Robinson could be one of 2027’s best prospects overall and not just for the cornerback position.
The pick: Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana
Where do we even start with the Chargers? The entire team top to bottom has been atrocious, including the coaching staff, but how much is replaceable? It's unlikely the team moves on from Jim Harbaugh, and even less likely that it moves on from Justin Herbert despite their struggles being arguably the biggest weights to their sinking season. The best thing the Chargers can do is add some…

title: Cardinals Roster Moves Send Clear Message on Walter Nolen’s Injury
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals made two roster moves on Saturday ahead of their Week 5 matchup against the Detroit Lions.
The Cardinals elevated cornerback Art Green to the active roster from the practice squad as a standard elevation while also placing offensive lineman Isaiah Adams on injured reserve.
With Walter Nolen III questionable due to a calf injury, this is a fairly good sign for his expected availability ahead of Sunday. This also spells good news for linebacker Karson Sharar, who is questionable with a hamstring injury.
Final actives are due at 11:55 AM on Sunday. Kickoff is at 1:25 PM at State Farm Stadium.
Nolen was limited in practice on Thursday and Friday leading into the weekend after practicing fully on Wednesday.
"He's trending good," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of Nolen.
Nolen suffered a calf injury ahead of his rookie season which saw him miss the first half of 2025. He returned and displayed every bit of potential that made him a potential game-wrecker before suffering a meniscus injury that landed him on injured reserve.
Nolen was cleared for training camp, avoiding the PUP list and survived a knee injury in training camp.
Thus far, the former first-round pick's gotten off to a slower-than-expected start, though the Cardinals didn't seem concerned .
“Yes, he just needs to keep going at it. I love Walt and he wants it really, really, really bad. And that's what I respect," LaFleur said on Nolen.
"I look at people's intentions, and I know his intentions are that he wants to help this team and he wants to be productive. He just needs to keep going."
Thus far, Nolen has eight tackles, three quarterback hits and one sack on the season.

title: Cardinals Slammed by Franchise Legends, Fans Amid Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade Chaos
full_text:
ARIZONA  — No official deal is in place, nor is the other team known, though word is out on the Arizona Cardinals trading Marvin Harrison Jr. this weekend.
In perhaps the most bizarre reporting ever around a deal, numerous NFL insiders first reported the Cardinals were trading Harrison early this morning. However, seemingly nobody is able to precisely pinpoint where he's going, what Arizona's getting back in return for Harrison and when the deal is expected to be processed.
It's a massive move that has found the Cardinals again in the spotlight for all the wrong reasons, and everybody from franchise legends to fans in Arizona are sounding off on social media:
Ring of Honor member Adrian Wilson kicks off festivities with a string of laughing emojis posted on X with this message as followed:
"I got so much to say but I certainly don’t want to hurt anyone’s feelings or burn any bridges with anyone. I don’t work for the team or NFL any longer and I hate what’s happening to the @AZCardinals right now," he said .
Many fans are completely done with the Cardinals after the move.
No longer a fan of this disastrous organization

title: 5 Instant Reactions to Cardinals Reportedly Trading Marvin Harrison Jr.
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are trading Marvin Harrison Jr., per several reports.
Where exactly and for what compensation remains apparently a mystery so massive the NFL's top insiders can't figure out.
Breaking: the Arizona Cardinals are finalizing a deal to trade WR Marvin Harrison, sources tell me and @RapSheet . The team informed Harrison this morning that he will be inactive for Sunday’s game vs Detroit as details of the trade are finalized. pic.twitter.com/x6n0Hsfzzj
While we still wait for details to trickle in, here's five honest (and immediate) takeaways:
The Cardinals tried their very best to throw people off their scent when it came to discussing trades involving Harrison. Just yesterday, Arizona general manager Monti Ossenfort appeared on Arizona Sports' 98.7 FM and downplayed any rumors.
“I think this time of year, and really all throughout the year, there’s a lot of talk. There’s a lot of stuff that’s written out there. I think really in the end, like, Marv is a big part of what we’re doing,” he said.
Harrison also reportedly hired an agent to help speedrun trade talks, and the writing appeared to be on the wall after.
Even the player himself addressed the trade rumors at his locker days ago:
"I'm only focused on Detroit, helping the Cardinals win football games at the moment. So whatever rumors you're talking about, I don't pay it no mind."
This has to be one of the weirdest trade reports of our time, as news leaked the day before a game... with no team immediately on the receiving end. Still, an hour after the news first dropped, we're not sure of who Harrison will be playing for this season or what the trade compensation is.
Sources within teams typically have details ironed out or at least an initial destination in mind. The league's top insiders in Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport couldn't crack who the other team is, with the Cardinals apparently wanting to wait until after the weekend to make the deal final.
That's a strong sign the news leaked from Harrison's own camp, especially with Harrison being (reportedly) inactive this weekend to preserve his health and facilitate a trade. It's unlikely Arizona would float a deal has been done with the possibility of losing leverage still very much in play.
The Cardinals had a massive fifth-year option coming on Harrison next offseason, one that was projected around $20 million (fully guaranteed). Michael Wilson was just paid handsomely this offseason, and not even Mike LaFleur could maximize Harrison or even get the wideout to be close to impactful.
The writing was on the wall for Harrison to depart before the Cardinals activated that fifth-year option. Harrison unfortunately was only impactful on sporadic occasions, and unless the wideout was wanting to return to the Cardinals for an ultra-cheap contract, his exit was simply accelerated.
Harrison needed to make a noticeable third-year jump to justify his long-term presence. That didn't happen.
Harrison being traded isn't surprising. What is a bit shocking is the Cardinals doing this now, in the middle of the season.
The one facet potentially keeping Arizona from orchestrating a deal in-season was their lack of top-level weapons on offense, at least in terms of the passing game.
Downgrading from Harrison to Jalen Brooks, Reggie Virgil or Simi Fehoko isn't exactly preferred, and more than anything Harrison's presence on the field as a potential threat could have kept defenses more honest.
For a general manager like Ossenfort — who very well might not be in his seat next season — moving off one of your biggest assets before the fifth game of the season is just a tad surprising in terms of having as many weapons for your offense as possible.
The optics here reflect poorly on the Cardinals, undoubtedly.
Regardless of how you slice it, Harrison has been underwhelming during his tenure in Arizona. He clearly isn't the player many had hoped and he thought he would be.
And for as much flack as the Cardinals are getting for not maximizing his talent/potential, the player also carries responsibility in growth not happening. At least in the desert, Harrison's issues with drops/concentration lapses were a massive theme of his early stint.
While a fresh start should do Harrison well, he's also partly responsible for things not working out — even if it's just a fraction compared to the organization.

title: Cardinals Trade Marvin Harrison Jr. to Mystery Team
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals surprisingly made good on trade rumors Saturday morning in the most unexpected way.
The Cardinals are trading Marvin Harrison Jr., according to several reports. In one of the oddest developments in quite some time, no team has been reported initially on the receiving end of Arizona's former first-round pick.
Okay here’s the deal: Marvin Harrison Jr. is expected to be traded. You know that by now. He’s inactive for Sunday’s game and the teams involved would “prefer the trade destination is NOT announced” until both team’s play this weekend, according to multiple sources. https://t.co/kNbVGVdHMM pic.twitter.com/E28AHpeDrz
Colts insider Mike Chappell says it's not the Indianapolis Colts. Adam Schefter says the Houston Texans have potentially been in the mix. Mike Florio is reporting the Texans have engaged and are the "likely" team to land Harrison.
Trade rumors have run rampant over Harrison after a sluggish start to 2026. In his third NFL season, Harrison's been an eye-opening bystander in Arizona's offense under first-year head coach Mike LaFleur.
"Truthfully, I pay it no mind," Harrison told reporters on trade rumors this very week. "I'm only focused on Detroit, helping the Cardinals win football games at the moment. So whatever rumors you're talking about, I don't pay it no mind."
Just this week, Harrison reportedly hired an agent after spending his first two years without representation — signaling to some that a deal may be in the works ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
Harrison, the former No. 4 overall pick, had a roller coaster start to his NFL career. Production never matched expectations after dominating at Ohio State and hailing from a father who is in the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
Through four weeks, Harrison has just five receptions for 85 yards and one touchdown.
“I think this time of year, and really all throughout the year, there’s a lot of talk. There’s a lot of stuff that’s written out there. I think really in the end, like, Marv is a big part of what we’re doing,” Cardinals GM Monti Ossenfort just told Arizona Sports’ Wolf & Luke on Friday (h/t Tyler Drake).
“He’s focused 100% on trying to get better, helping our team creating explosive plays, putting points on the board. And so, with respect to all the stuff that’s written out there, we’re excited to move forward and really not pay any credence to any of that.”
Harrison's lack of involvement in the Cardinals' offense was surprising given his stature and generational tag emerging out of the draft. However, Arizona touts star tight end Trey McBride with the recently paid Michael Wilson as their clear top two receiving weapons.
The Cardinals also had Harrison's fifth-year option on their 2027 offseason slate.
LaFleur, asked many times about Harrison's role, downplayed any credence to a potential move.
"Marv seems like Marv to me. I'm not going to sit here and act like I don't know the narrative going on. I mean, this is the league, and naturally stuff gets across my desk," said LaFleur earlier in the year.
"But in between those walls, Marv is Marv. He's attacking it every single day like he always does, just like his teammates do. I appreciate the way he goes about his business."
What an odd end to Harrison's time.

title: Walter Nolen Headlines Final Cardinals-Lions Week 5 Injury Report
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Detroit Lions have unveiled their final practice reports for Week 5's bout at State Farm Stadium.
For the Cardinals, Walter Nolen and Karson Sharar are both questionable while Jeremiyah Love is good to go.
As for the Lions, four players including Brian Branch have been ruled out.
Full lists for both sides:
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur says nothing really changes in terms of preparation despite a familiar face in former Arizona offensive coordinator Drew Petzing returning to the desert.
“Yes, it’s a good question. People are going to have their narratives probably about it, including us. Drew definitely has his spin on that offense, but it’s the Detroit Lions offense. They’re doing a lot of the stuff that they’ve done in the run game," he said.
"They’re doing a lot of stuff that (Lions QB) Jared’s (Goff) has been really, really successful at — almost at MVP caliber levels and stuff. With all the same basically skill that they’ve had there for four years now or so. Then the bookend tackle and all those kinds of things. A lot of the same, but he’s definitely put his little flavor on it for sure.”
Lions head coach Dan Campbell gave some glowing reviews for the Cardinals ahead of Week 5:
"New week, new opponent, Arizona. These guys are playing hard. (Cardinals Head) Coach (Mike) LaFleur's doing a really good job with them, man. They've been in all these games. I know the Seattle game got a little bit out of whack there, but these guys play hard. And they're in all these games, man. They can score points on offense. They have got weapons," he said Wednesday.
"In this defense, man, it gives you different looks. They have got length. (Cardinals S) Budda Baker is problematic. (Cardinals WR Michael) Wilson, man, he kind of runs the show over there. And we know (Cardinals DL) Roy Lopez, man. He's a lunch pail guy, going to give it everything you got and make you earn it, among others over there. So, pretty good special teams group. So look, we're going to get this team's best. They're going to be ready to go. They're looking for a win and so are we.”

title: 5 Bold Predictions for Atlanta Falcons vs. Baltimore Ravens
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are the consensus pick against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday Night Football. Even with a healthy Lamar Jackson, who is out for the game , the Falcons still might have been the popular pick as one of the most dominant teams over the last two weeks.
The Falcons find themselves in unfamiliar territory as frontrunners, as the love poured in from national media after back-to-back prime-time blowouts. We'll find out if the Falcons can handle the prosperity on NBC at 8:20 on Sunday, but until then, here are five bold predictions for the Falcons against the Ravens.
OK, so this doesn't feel like that bold a prediction, but much has been said about the lack of atmosphere at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. That's a combination of less-than-mediocre play over the last decade and a pricing structure that put lower-bowl seating into the hands of non-Falcons fans.
Atlanta is a transient city, full of transplants who have gravitated south through the years and brought their loyalty with them, but the Baltimore Ravens do not have a huge presence in the city like, say, the Pittsburgh Steelers, Chicago Bears, Philadelphia Eagles, or any team from New York.
Neutral fans tuning into the game tonight are going to see as loud a Falcons crowd as they've seen in a long, long time.
The Falcons are fifth in the NFL in quarterback pressures , but they're only 22nd with seven sacks. The Ravens have only given up seven sacks this season, tied for ninth-best in the NFL.
But most of those numbers have been accomplished with Lamar Jackson at quarterback. He's out, and it's time for the good pressure to pay off on Sunday. Atlanta has been playing with leads the last two weeks, setting up more pass-rush opportunities. That happens again on Sunday night.
The Falcons get at least three sacks of Tyler Huntley.
As the national media has been gushing about Bijan Robinson (rightfully so), everyone has taken notice, including the Baltimore Ravens. Drake London has 290 receiving yards in his two games with Michael Penix Jr. at quarterback.
The Ravens will crowd the line to try to stop Robinson. All-World safety Kyle Hamilton will keep a close eye on London. That's going to leave Kyle Pitts Sr. plenty of room to operate. Juwan Johnson of the Saints went for 4 catches and 66 yards against the Ravens in Week 2, and the Cowboys' Jake Ferguson had three catches for 24 yards and a touchdown in Week 3.
Pitts goes for 100+ yards and a touchdown.
Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry finished last season with four straight 100-yard games. He began this season with 144 yards against the Colts. He hasn't broken 100 yards since. He rushed for 73 yards last week in a win over the Titans, and his season low is 68 against the Saints in Week 2.
The Falcons have the No. 1 rushing defense in the NFL by some distance. They'll be looking to hold Henry to a season low, but why not dream a little bigger?
The last time Henry was held under 50 yards was in a 44-10 loss to the Texans in Week 5 last year. Week 5 last year, Week 5 this year?
Henry breaks 50 yards, but is kept under 75.
The Falcons are a near-unanimous pick from the national media and FalconsSI staff alike . This is a team unaccustomed to the spotlight, but they are built to avoid the massive highs and lows they've experienced over the last three seasons.
They're better in the trenches. They're better at quarterback. Dare we say they're better at running back?

title: FalconsSI Staff Unanimous in Falcons vs. Ravens Predictions
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons enter their Week 5 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens, looking to continue their recent momentum and secure another important victory under the Sunday night lights. With Lamar Jackson ruled out and Tyler Huntley expected to start at quarterback for Baltimore, the Falcons have an opportunity to take advantage of a banged-up Ravens team. However, Atlanta cannot afford to overlook an opponent that still features Derrick Henry and plenty of talent on both sides of the ball.
The Atlanta Falcons On SI staff enter the matchup each 3-1 with a collective 15-5 record in weekly predictions, and the group is expecting Atlanta to come away with a victory in Week 5.
The Falcons find themselves as the new big thing in the NFC after blasting the Saints and the Packers. This time, though, they’re expected to handle the Ravens in their third straight prime-time game.
Can they handle being frontrunners?
Yes. Yes, they can. They’re good in the trenches. Their special teams are improved. They have an experienced coach, an offensive coordinator on a heater, and Bijan Robinson.
The Ravens are banged up. While a wounded animal is still dangerous, the Falcons should win this one.
Prediction: Falcons 27, Ravens 19
This game was going to be a true test for Atlanta against one of the NFL’s premier players, Lamar Jackson. Without him, the game lacks a little bit of luster. But the Falcons are notorious for losing games they’re supposed to win. Tonight can help reverse that narrative. Plus, it’s Sunday Night Football — primetime. Atlanta shows up. Chalk it up as another win for Atlanta to remain undefeated with Michael Penix Jr. at quarterback.
Prediction: Falcons 28, Ravens 9
The Falcons come into this game vs. a team that is very dangerous when Lamar Jackson is at the helm, along with the combination of Derrick Henry. However, without Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley still makes them very formidable but less dangerous.
I expect the Falcons' defense to hone in on Henry as the #1 run defense in the league. Also, as it is National Running Backs Day for SNF, I expect Bijan Robinson to continue his primetime run with the help of his running mate Brian Robinson to help keep this offense rolling. Tough atmosphere for the Ravens coming in here during the Red Out game, a lot of energy, but I expect the Falcons to take care of business and move to 3-2.
Prediction: Falcons 28, Ravens 17
No NFL team is hotter than the Atlanta Falcons, and they'll be coming home for the first time since Michael Penix Jr. returned to the starting lineup. This team is humming, outscoring the Packers and Saints by 42 points combined.
Their rushing attack/defense have been particularly impressive. They have totaled 447 yards while allowing just 67 (a +380 rushing differential). Penix, meanwhile, has a 73.3% completion percentage and is keeping this offense moving.
It's been a lot of good for the Falcons, and now they'll welcome a team without its MVP quarterback. Derrick Henry will still be a tough test, but the Falcons will keep rolling. Prediction: Falcons 24, Ravens16
Who would have thought the Falcons would be going into a game against the Ravens as the favorites?
The injuries to Lamar Jackson and Trey Hendrickson will grab the headlines, but I think their injuries at o-line will be even more crippling. Every center on their roster is hurt, their rookie right guard will be playing out of position, and their backup right guard is questionable. I don’t see the Ravens creating lanes for Derrick Henry or giving Tyler Huntley time to throw against a d-line that is playing excellently.
The story on the other side of the ball is that the Falcons have been the league’s best rushing team the last 2 weeks against a defense that struggles to stop the run. As long as Penix and the offense can limit mistakes, the Falcons should run away with this one.
Prediction: Falcons 31, Ravens 13

title: Falcons Make Roster Moves Ahead of Ravens SNF Showdown
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have announced several roster moves ahead of their Sunday Night Football matchup against the Baltimore Ravens at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
Linebacker Yasir Abdullah has been placed on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury, while defensive end Za’Darius Smith has been downgraded to out for Sunday’s game with a concussion/neck injury. Atlanta has also signed safety Jammie Robinson to the 53-man roster and elevated defensive ends Bralen Trice (his third and final elevation before needing to be signed to the active roster) and Drake Jackson from the practice squad.
Abdullah was ruled out for Sunday’s matchup with a hamstring injury before being placed on injured reserve. The linebacker appeared in all four of Atlanta’s games this season, recording two tackles and one pass defended. His absence leaves the Falcons with one less defensive option as they prepare for a physical matchup against Baltimore.
Robinson’s promotion adds depth in the secondary and on special teams. Atlanta previously elevated him from the practice squad for Week 4's Monday night matchup against the New Orleans Saints, before signing him to the active roster ahead of Sunday night’s contest.
The safety appeared in six games for Atlanta last season after joining the practice squad in November. Before arriving in Atlanta, Robinson spent two seasons with the Carolina Panthers. He was a fifth-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft and has appeared in 27 career games. Robinson also made an impact on special teams last season, blocking a punt against New Orleans in Week 18.
The Falcons also elevated Trice and Jackson to bolster their defensive front. Trice has appeared in two games this season, recording one tackle and one pass defended. Sunday will mark his third and final standard practice squad elevation of the season, meaning Atlanta would need to sign him to its 53-man roster to make him eligible for additional game appearances through future elevations.
Jackson joins the game-day roster as another option along the defensive line. He appeared in two preseason games for Atlanta this year, recording one assisted tackle, but has yet to record a regular-season defensive statistic for the Falcons.
These moves follow Atlanta’s Week 4 win over New Orleans. The Falcons will look to carry that momentum into Sunday night’s primetime matchup while managing injuries and maintaining defensive depth.
With Abdullah sidelined, Robinson joining the active roster, and two additional defensive ends available, Atlanta will need contributions across its defense and special teams as it prepares to face Baltimore on Sunday Night Football.

title: 3 Keys to Victory for Atlanta Falcons against Baltimore Ravens
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have an opportunity to extend their winning streak when they host the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday night. With Lamar Jackson ruled out because of an ankle injury, Atlanta will face Tyler Huntley at quarterback and look to capitalize on Baltimore’s change under center.
The Falcons have several advantages entering the matchup, including a dominant run defense, a productive backfield tandem, and a pass rush capable of disrupting opposing quarterbacks. Here are three keys to victory for Atlanta.
Stopping Derrick Henry will be one of Atlanta’s biggest priorities. The Baltimore running back has rushed for 374 yards and seven touchdowns on 89 carries through four games, averaging 4.2 yards per attempt. His combination of power, speed and ability to break tackles makes him a threat to change the game with every carry.
Fortunately for Atlanta, its run defense has been outstanding. The Falcons rank first in the NFL in rushing defense efficiency, allowing just 2.7 yards per carry through four weeks. They will need that physicality against Henry, who can wear down defenders and create additional yards after contact.
Atlanta must approach Henry as a collective effort. The first defender needs to slow his momentum, while teammates rally to finish the tackle. Maintaining gap discipline, taking proper angles and limiting missed tackles will be essential.
The Falcons also need to prevent Henry from establishing himself early. Forcing Baltimore into third-and-long would allow Atlanta to focus more attention on Huntley and give its pass rush additional opportunities. If the NFL’s top run defense can limit Henry, it will significantly improve Atlanta’s chances of controlling the game.
Atlanta’s backfield has been one of its biggest offensive strengths this season. Bijan Robinson has recorded 494 rushing yards and four touchdowns, while Brian Robinson Jr. has contributed 194 yards and four touchdowns through four games.
Bijan has been especially impressive in primetime. He rushed for 194 yards and two touchdowns against Green Bay before following that performance with 145 yards and two touchdowns against New Orleans. His ability to produce explosive runs and consistently gain yards has helped Atlanta establish its offensive identity.
Brian has complemented that production with a physical running style, including three rushing touchdowns against New Orleans. Having both backs involved makes Atlanta more difficult to defend and prevents opposing defenses from concentrating exclusively on Bijan.
The Falcons must continue establishing the run early against Baltimore. Consistent production on first and second down will create manageable passing situations for Michael Penix Jr. while helping Atlanta control the clock.
If both Robinsons continue producing, Atlanta can keep Baltimore’s defense on the field and limit the opportunities available to Henry and the Ravens’ offense.
Atlanta must take advantage of Huntley’s opportunity as Baltimore’s starting quarterback. Although Huntley has experience in the Ravens’ offense, consistent pressure could force hurried decisions and disrupt the timing of Baltimore’s passing game.
Cameron Thomas has been an important contributor to Atlanta’s pass rush, recording 19 pressures through the first four games. Maason Smith has also provided an interior presence, generating seven pressures and helping collapse the pocket.
Za’Darius Smith, Samson Ebukam and the rest of Atlanta’s defensive front will be equally important. The Falcons need contributions from multiple rushers rather than relying on one player to consistently win individual matchups.
The defensive line must also remain disciplined. Huntley can escape pressure with his mobility, so Atlanta’s defenders need to maintain their rush lanes and prevent him from extending plays.
If the Falcons stop Henry on early downs, they can force Baltimore into predictable passing situations and unleash their pass rush. Turning pressure into sacks, hurried throws, and turnovers could give Atlanta’s offense valuable opportunities.
Ultimately, Atlanta’s path to victory starts with controlling the line of scrimmage. If the Falcons contain Henry, continue their productive rushing attack, and pressure Huntley with a collective defensive effort, they will put themselves in a strong position to secure another victory.

title: Falcons vs. Ravens Predictions Find Atlanta in Unfamiliar Territory
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons fans might be rubbing their necks after suffering whiplash from the sudden turnaround. Left for dead after an 0-2 start with journeyman quarterback Cooper Rush at the helm, the Falcons are now the talk of the town after bullying the Green Bay Packers and New Orleans Saints in consecutive weeks on national television.
They'll get a third straight week in front of a big audience when they take on the Baltimore Ravens on NBC's Sunday Night Football at 8:20 p.m. EST.
The Ravens are missing several key players, including quarterback Lamar Jackson , edge rusher Trey Hendrickson, and newly acquired Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens. The Falcons find themselves in unfamiliar territory: heavy favorites.
While Jackson has been doubtful most of the week, it should be noted that all of these predictions were made before he was officially ruled out on Friday afternoon by the Ravens.
NFL Network has all five of its analysts picking the Falcons , with Brooke Cersosimo saying this about Atlanta: "Is anyone better in prime time than Bijan Robinson? Not in my book, though Derrick Henry might have something to say about that. But God bless the schedule-makers for giving us Bijan thrice in night games over the first five weeks."
ESPN analytics writer Seth Walder is a long-time Falcons detractor, and he's not ready to get on the bandwagon, but he's the lone holdout of his co-workers. Pamela Maldonado and Eric Moody both pick Atlanta .
With Jackson out and Tyler Huntley under center, the Ravens will lean heavily on running back Derrick Henry. Earlier this week, Henry said Bijan Robinson was the best in the game right now, but defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich knows Henry can carry a team.
UUlbrich's unit is No. 1 in the NFL against the run after the season's first month.
"This is a great challenge," Ulbrich said this week. "We've had some success. Not saying it's been perfect by any means, but we've had some success versus the run so far this season. You want to be the best. You want to play the best.  Derrick Henry is one of the best maybe ever in that way. Just the physicality, the toughness, and then the speed that you're not ready for as he runs by you and the stiff arm, etcetera.
"But like the commitment by the offense, the organization, the offensive line to run the ball and play that that style of football. I'm excited about that.”
Falcons fans have been burned more than once when the spotlight is on their team, but they're flying high right now on both sides of the ball. They're coming home to Mercedes-Benz Stadium, and they're eager to prove in front of a national audience that this team has turned a corner and can thrive as frontrunners.

title: Falcons Get Final Word on Baltimore Ravens QB Lamar Jackson
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons will face the Baltimore Ravens without one of the NFL's biggest stars on Sunday night, as quarterback Lamar Jackson has officially been ruled out with an ankle injury. Tyler Huntley will get the start for Baltimore when the two teams meet in Week 6.
Jackson has not practiced this week after suffering the injury during the Ravens' Week 5 victory over the Tennessee Titans. His absence is a significant development for Baltimore, which will have to adjust its offensive approach without its two-time MVP quarterback.
Jackson's ability to create explosive plays as both a passer and runner has been central to Baltimore's offensive identity. Without him, the Ravens will turn to Huntley, who has experience starting games and familiarity with the team's offensive system.
Huntley has a career record of 7-9 as a starter, including a 5-6 record with Baltimore and 2-3 record with the Miami Dolphins. He will make his 12th career start for the Ravens, giving the team an experienced option despite the challenge of replacing Jackson.
Huntley also saw action against Tennessee after Jackson exited with the injury. He completed eight of nine passes for 63 yards without a touchdown or interception, helping Baltimore secure the victory.
The backup quarterback's mobility gives the Ravens another option to execute designed runs and extend plays outside the pocket. Baltimore could lean more heavily on its rushing attack, particularly with Derrick Henry serving as a key component of the offense. Huntley will need to protect the football, make quick decisions, and take advantage of opportunities in the passing game.
For Atlanta, Jackson's absence presents an opportunity to build on its recent success. The Falcons are coming off a convincing 45 -24 victory over the New Orleans Saints and will look to carry that momentum into Sunday night's contest.
Atlanta has historically struggled against Baltimore, holding a 2-5 all time record against the Ravens. Baltimore won the last two meetings, defeating the Falcons 26-16 in December 2018 and earning a 17-9 victory in December 2022.
The Falcons will look to reverse that trend while taking advantage of Baltimore's quarterback situation. Atlanta's defense must remain disciplined against Henry and prevent Huntley from finding a rhythm, particularly if the Ravens attempt to control the game with their running attack.
Jackson's absence changes the complexion of Sunday's matchup, but Baltimore still has playmakers capable of creating problems. The Falcons will need to control the line of scrimmage, limit explosive plays and capitalize on the opportunity to secure another important victory.
The Ravens and Falcons are scheduled to kick off Sunday, October 11, at 8:20 p.m. ET in Atlanta.

title: Falcons Injury Updates ahead of Ravens Clash, Including OL Jake Matthews
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons received encouraging news on the injury front Friday as they completed their final practice before Sunday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. Left tackle Jake Matthews returned to full participation, while several defensive contributors remain questionable for the upcoming contest.
With the Falcons looking to build on their victory over the New Orleans Saints, the availability of several key players could prove important against Baltimore.
Matthews provided the biggest positive development of the day. The veteran offensive tackle suffered a groin injury during Monday night's win over New Orleans , forcing him to leave the game without returning. His availability for Sunday's matchup was initially uncertain after he was listed as a nonparticipant on Wednesday's estimated injury report.
However, Matthews made progress throughout the week, participating on a limited basis Thursday before practicing fully on Friday. The improvement puts him in a better position to potentially extend his streak of consecutive NFL starts to 201 games.
Having Matthews available would be a significant boost for Atlanta's offensive line as it prepares to face Baltimore's defense. His experience and consistency at left tackle are valuable assets, particularly when protecting quarterback Michael Penix Jr.
The Falcons also received positive news regarding defensive end Cam Thomas and offensive tackle Michael Jerrell, who were full participants Friday. However, Atlanta still has several defensive injury concerns heading into the weekend.
Defensive end Za'Darius Smith practiced fully despite dealing with a concussion and neck injury. He remains questionable for Sunday night's game, leaving uncertainty surrounding his availability. Smith's potential absence would be notable for a Falcons defensive front that has performed well to begin the season.
Linebacker Divine Deablo and defensive end Samson Ebukam were both limited participants Friday because of hamstring injuries. Both players are listed as questionable against Baltimore.
There is reason for optimism regarding their availability. Deablo and Ebukam also carried questionable designations before Monday night's game against the Saints, but both ultimately played and made contributions in Atlanta's victory.
Meanwhile, linebacker Yasir Abdullah did not participate Friday and is listed as out for Sunday's game because of a hamstring injury. His status presents another concern for Atlanta's defensive depth heading into the matchup.
With the final practice complete, the Falcons will have to monitor their remaining injury situations before Sunday's kickoff. Matthews' progress is an encouraging sign, but the availability of Smith, Deablo, and Ebukam could be equally important as Atlanta prepares for a challenging test against Baltimore.

title: Falcons No. 1 Rush Defense to Face Biggest Test to Date in Ravens
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are preparing for one of their biggest defensive challenges of the season when Derrick Henry and the Baltimore Ravens arrive in Atlanta.
Henry has been productive through the first four games of the season, rushing for 374 yards and seven touchdowns on 89 carries. He is averaging 4.2 yards per carry and has added 44 receiving yards on seven catches. Henry is coming off a 73-yard performance against the Tennessee Titans in which he scored a touchdown.
Henry also has a history of success against the Falcons, rushing for 201 yards on 49 carries in two career regular season games against Atlanta. He has yet to score a touchdown in those matchups.
Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich knows the defense will need to be at its best.
“This is a great challenge,” Ulbrich said. “We’ve had some success, not saying it’s been perfect by any means, but we’ve had some success versus the run so far this season.”
The Falcons have the NFL's No. 1 rushing defense by some margin at 48.3 yards per game. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers check in at No. 2 with 72.8 yards per game. They're closer to the No. 7 Cincinnati Bengals than they are the Falcons.
“You want to be the best, you want to play the best,” Ulbrich said. “From that perspective, it’s going to be an amazing challenge.”
Henry's physical style makes him difficult to bring down, but Ulbrich also emphasized the running back's speed.
“Derrick Henry is one of the best, maybe ever, in that way,” Ulbrich said. “Just the physicality, the toughness, and then the speed that you’re not ready for as he runs by you.”
Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels will have a role in trying to slow Henry down, but he knows the defensive line can make the job easier.
“Our D line gets after it, and you never want to slow your defensive line down,” Daniels said. “So that really helps us be able to play off them and just let them go make plays, and we play off of them.”
Ulbrich stressed the importance of Atlanta's tackling fundamentals.
“Population of ball is critical. Stiff-arm defense is critical. A really defined tackling plan is critical,” Ulbrich said.  "Getting to the thigh boards, wrapping, rolling, taking the extra step, putting my body on, and not leaving my feet.”
There aren't many players like Henry who have ever played in the NFL with his combination of size and speed, so it's no surprise this will be a unique challenge for the rookie Daniels.
“I went to school with Ollie Gordon. So that’s the closest I’ve got to Derrick Henry,” Daniels said. “I feel like we’ve gotten closer. I feel like when I first got here, it was kind of everybody figuring out their role, and then I feel like everybody’s figuring out their role. Everybody’s excited for each other.”
The only returning starters on the Falcons' front seven are Brandon Dorlus and Divine Deablo. So it's taken some time to find chemistry. That chemistry could be critical against Baltimore.
For Atlanta, the goal will be to prevent Henry from getting into a rhythm. The Falcons will need disciplined run fits, strong play at the line of scrimmage, and multiple defenders arriving at the football.
If they can limit Henry early and prevent Baltimore from establishing its physical identity, Atlanta will have a much better chance of controlling the game and continuing its defensive progress.

title: Is King Henry Ready to Pass the Crown to Bijan Robinson?
full_text:
It’s starting to seem like a daily occurrence that Bijan Robinson is garnering praise across the NFL.
As the Atlanta Falcons fourth-year running back sits at No. 2 in rushing and scrimmage yards, he’s gotten another bold admission.
This time, from a multi-time rushing leader and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year, “King” Derrick Henry.
“He’s the best in the game right now, he’s doing it all,” Henry discussed Robinson to reporters on Thursday. “I ain’t going to shy away from it. He’s doing a great job, hell of a back.”
Robinson and Henry will be in a running back battle when the Falcons host the Baltimore Ravens at Mercedes-Benz Stadium for Sunday Night Football. Henry may see an increase in touches for Baltimore, which may be without its starting quarterback, Lamar Jackson, due to an ankle injury .
Through four games, Robinson has accrued 614 scrimmage yards: 494 rushing, 120 receiving. He’s added five total touchdowns, with one coming on a pass. According to Pro Football Focus, Robinson has broken 17 tackles through four games.
He’s a star in Atlanta’s reinvented attack under new offensive coordinator Tommy Rees .
“Does a great job in the system, then does a great job when the play is not exactly how they want it,” Henry said. “Know how to make guys miss, get vertical – get the most out of the play for sure.”
Henry added that he and Robinson speak on Instagram “here and there.”
Robinson looks to build on a 145-yard rushing and two-touchdown performance in a 45-24 beatdown on NFC South rival New Orleans Saints . Per NFL Next Gen stats, Robinson hit a top speed of 21.78 mph as he sprinted past the New Orleans defense untouched for a 59-yard rushing touchdown on the game’s third play from scrimmage.
Last week, Robinson was also named the NFC Offensive Player of the Week for his role in the Falcons’ dominating the Green Bay Packers 35-14 on Lambeau Field during Sept. 24’s Thursday Night Football on Sept. 24.
The NFL Top 100 member, ranked third , is on the early NFL MVP watchlist.
Falcons (2-2) versus Ravens (3-1) kicks off at 8:20 p.m. in Atlanta. CBS will stream the game as the Falcons search for their third consecutive win.
Primetime games are Robinson’s forte.
He leads the NFL all-time scrimmage yards average in primetime games , with 145.5, since the 1970 NFL-AFL merger. He’s over the likes of Barry Sanders, OJ Simpson, and current Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.

title: How Can Ravens Stop Bijan Robinson? Film Analyst Greg Cosell Suggests A Radical Change
full_text:
The goal of Ravens head coach Jesse Minter most weeks is to defend the run with as little manpower as possible.
That needs to change in a very fundamental manner tonight in Atlanta. And after watching every snap the Ravens and Falcons have played this season, longtime NFL analyst Greg Cosell from ESPN/NFL Films who studies every matchup, agrees with me that Minter will have to delve into some looks we have not seen all season in an attempt to mitigate the Falcons dynamic run game, specifically Bijan Robinson, the best back in the NFL, running outside zone stretch plays (7.4 yards/carry).
Minter enters Week 5 having used a four-man front just five times all season and being in nickel or dime (five or more defensive backs) over 90% of the time. That won’t work against this Atlanta scheme and offensive line and a pair of running backs (Brian Robinson also) and requires a total rethink of how they plan to operate up front, especially knowing the offense is limited with Snoop Huntley at quarterback and not Lamar Jackson and with new center Cam Jurgens on the concussion list and carrying serious injury red flags.
In fact, Cosell believes that with top pass rusher Trey Hendrickson out (he is not good against the run, anyway) that Minter could look into using anchors Tavious Robinson and Zion Young on the edge in base looks and lean into perhaps three defensive tackles at times. Minter also has flexibility to deploy hybrid defensive back/linebacker Kyle Hamilton in a multitude of ways at the line of scrimmage.
“They could play a 5-2 front, too, you know, and get the wider defender for the outside zone run game,” Cosell explained in detail on “The Daily Flock Show” this week. “Because that's where it starts with the Falcons with Bojan Robinson and outside zone. I think Bijan Robinson is the best back in the league. So you've got to be able to stop outside zone.”
Minter wants to flood the field with defensive backs of all shapes and sizes and responsibilities but that’s not going to play here. Tight end Kyle Pitts is a glorified outside receiver and he still doesn’t look fully vested in Atlanta’s pass game, Drake London is a bigtime receiver but young quarterback Michael Penix Jr is still feeling his way back from his third ACL surgery and it’s doubtful coach Kevin Stefanski wants him dropping back a ton if he doesn’t have to.
Cosell believes that Minter will devise a plan to get both linebackers Teddye Buchanan and Trenton Simpson on the field at the same time on some early-down looks; Simpson replaced Buchanan as a starter after Buchanan suffered an ACL tear late last season, and is playing the best football of his career by far, with him popping off the film for Cosell, along with Robinson in the front defensive front.
Here’s how some of the new base looks might shape out in a 5-2 framework:
“Hamilton would then be a (box) safety with (free safety Malaki) Starks as opposed to the big nickel where (Jaylinn) Hawkins is the third safety,” Cosell suggested. “So I think you're going to see more of that. But again, it also depends on the personnel. the Falcons put out there.
“You know, if they run out of base personnel (one back and two tight ends), you'll see that. If they run out of 11 personnel, then Jesse Minter has to decide how he wants to play that. Now, they don't have a big-time receiving core. So, you might feel that you can still play in your base even if they put 11 out there depending on distance and field location.
“Nothing, as you know, is 100% in an NFL game. So, other than Drake London, you're probably not necessarily believing that there's someone like, ‘Oh, we better stop that guy or else.’ So we'll see. But if you can widen your front, you have a better chance of setting the edge and dealing with that outside zone run game.”

title: Ravens Must Try These 3 Things To Unlock Zay Flowers With A Back-Up QB Sunday Night
full_text:
Few wide receivers have carried a heavier load in the first month of the NFL season than Ravens’s sparkplug Zay Flowers.
He has been something of a one-man army once again in their downfield passing game , he is as connected with two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson as anyone has ever been and the “Zay And Pray” passing game is alive and well. But it’s time for a calibration. It’s time for a rethink. At least for a few weeks, as Jackson is out this week and he could very well be out next week too, and Snoop Huntley, when it comes to pushing the ball downfield, has almost nothing in common with Jackson’s intent and acumen .
Rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is going to have to experiment even more to get Flowers unlocked on Sunday night against a Falcons defense that is stuffing the run without devoting extra man power to doing it, at the same time generating the NFL’s highest pressure rate (and, you guessed it, without blitzing to devote extra manpower to that endeavor, either).
Here is what Doyle is up against, whether he wants to admit it or not . He can try to amp Huntley up by opining about, “I do not think the mentality of how you want to run the offense changes at all,” but that’s baloney. We have an established body of work with Flowers and these two quarterbacks and the differences are stark:
Zay with Lamar : 14.4 yds/reception               7.5 YAC/rec                 10.12 air yds/target
Zay with Snoop : 6.5 yds/reception                 2.4 YAC/rec                 6.39 air yds/target
Here’s a snippet of what needs to happen to try to keep Flowers vested in the game plan and an elite weapon:
Flowers has been in motion 27% of the time this season. It was around 24% last season with Todd Monken. Even with some serious OL issues ( prompting a fairly desperate trade ) and the need to avoid pre-snap penalties, some simple motions for Flowers make all the sense in the world.
He won’t be latching on to deep balls. Putting him in motion before he catches a bubble screen seems to be something they should lean into. Making the defense at least wonder about a jet sweep or end around can’t hurt. At some point the Ravens are going to need a complimentary winner downfield - seems unlikely that will be Marvin Harrison Jr . though they have at least checked in on that situation - and maybe it's rookie Ja'Kobi Lane at some point when he is healthy, but they need to keep scheming it up in the interim .
I fully understand that Huntley is better off delivering the ball on a shorter distance and that his throws to the far reaches on the boundary tend to be a little late and turnover-worthy. And I know Flowers has been particularly devastating in the slot this season, where he’s been for 60% of his reps, nearly doubling his career average. But, well, Atlanta is without its best cover corner in AJ Terrell (on IR) and teams have thrown on in them in the slot 46 times (second-most in the NFL) and those targets are going nowhere, while outside throws are eating them up.
We still need Flowers on a fair share of crossers, but Doyle should be cognizant of these splits with his best receiver.
Opposing QBs throwing to slot vs AT L: 72.9 rating, 52% completions
Opposing QBs throwing to outside vs ATL: 114.7 rating, 70% completions
Flowers has been lined up in the backfield four times this season. That’s already twice as much as all of last season. Might need four times Sunday night alone.
We don’t want him doing anything running inside, but designed sprints behind the tackles and running wheel routes out of a pony package in a gun look with either Derrick Henry or Justice Hill on the field and maybe, maybe a Wild Cat look or two might be in order.
The Falcons’ run defense is ridiculous thus far, allowing just 2.7 yards/carry and this is another game where Henry might be running into a wall 25 times , bleeding clock and keeping things close but not generating much explosion. They need creativity and multiplicity in the run game more than ever with Huntley taking over at a time the run game is in a deep funk and the offensive line has major issues.

title: Ravens Are Aware Of Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade Market, NFL GMs Say
full_text:
The Ravens are at least monitoring the trade market for former first-round pick Marvin Harrison Jr., according to multiple NFL general managers who are aware of the process, though many around the league believe the youngster will end up with Houston or Kansas City.
The Ravens made a bold move already this week, trading a fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to the Eagles for center Cam Jurgens, a player with a deep injury history; many NFL execs believe the Ravens paid too steep a price due his performance since back surgery , while longtime Eagles team president told us he heard from sources in the Eagles headquarters that Jurgens was getting benched.
Baltimore is giving off a strong signal that it is fairly desperate to win right now with two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson in the last guaranteed year of his deal and holding extreme leverage over the franchise in 2027, while a nucleus of older/injury prone players are likely in their final year with the team. The Ravens are aware that outside of Zay Flowers no one has delivered with even a modicum of consistency in their downfield passing game for two seasons and multiple GMs passed along their informed belief that the Ravens were involved in Harrison’s market at least to some degree.
“We hear they explored it,” said one GM who is also interested in a potential Harrison trade. “He’s probably going to Houston. Maybe it’s just a rumor but that’s what we hear.”
Another GM expressed a similar sentiment. The Cardinals informed Harrison, selected fourth overall in 2024, that they will trade him after Week 5 games are completed according to reports, though no agreement is formalized Arizona could find an offer from another team that exceeds what the team essentially has in its back pocket. And an injury to a superstar receiver for a contending team could reshape the market as well.
The Ravens are in a cap crunch after the Jurgens deal though a few simple restructures would amend that, and Harrison has a base salary of just $1.075M on his rookie deal, and is signed for next season with a fifth-year option for 2028. He had nearly 900 yards and eight touchdowns in his rookie season but has struggled to fit into the offense since and his play has slipped and there are also serious concerns about his overall mentality in the scouting community.
Because of all of that, the Cardinals are not expected to yield close to what they have already invested in the 24-year-old thus far in trade compensation.
Despite years of pronouncements about Rashod Bateman being a quality NFL receiver, he has been ineffective most of his career outside of 2024 and offers more as a blocker and decoy than anything else. He has never clicked with Lamar Jackson for any period of time, Devontez Walker has yet to show he can stay healthy enough and consistent enough to make a dent downfield and rookie third-round pick Ja’Kobi Lane already broke his wrist and likely faces a tough adjustment to the NFL game.
Flowers has twice as many receiving yards as anyone on the team despite running just 56 routes this season and is the only receiver on the team generating any yards after the catch. Baltimore is playing with back-up quarterback Snoop Huntley Sunday and perhaps for another week and needs to find ways to generate explosion in other ways with him, because he does not push the ball downfield .
Harrison was a highly-explosive receiver at Ohio State, his father is a Hall of Fame receiver and he has elite athletic traits. He played in college with Texans quarterback CJ Stroud for two seasons, the Texans are more desperate than most teams at 0-4, and they have dealt with significant injuries to their receivers.

title: Ravens Were Fleeced In Cam Jurgens Trade, Longtime Eagles President Contends
full_text:
The Ravens made a significant leap and paid a steep price trading for Philadelphia center Cam Jurgens this week, with longtime Eagles team president Joe Banner speaking for many working for teams around the league in saying Baltimore general manager Eric DeCosta overpaid for the player.
The Ravens were in a pretty dire situation at center, in part due to injuries to fringe players and in part due to their own mismanagement of the position , and it began with not getting an extension done with star center Tyler Linderbaum  well before he became a free agent and ignoring the position despite having  picks in the draft. Jurgens, 27, underwent back/nerve surgery in February 2025, has not been the same player since and Banner, who watched his film closely and was integral in the rise of that franchise along with current Eagles GM Howie Roseman, a former Banner protegee  and former coach Andy Reid, believes Jurgens was losing his grip on a starting guard job with the Eagles.
Therefore, giving up a second-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027 seems quite desperate.
The fact that Jurgens cannot even play this week as he is still in the concussion protocol following a loss to the Rams Sunday, even further speaks to the quirky timing, with Roseman moving on from one of his highest-paid lineman at a time he is already down All-Pro guard Landon Dickerson and with superstar tackle Lane Johnson just retiring. Hence why DeCosta is drawing criticism around the league for this move.
“I think it's hard to disagree with that word,” Banner explained of that "desperation" on “The Daily Flock Show” this week. “It's obviously a very strong word, but I don't think it's an exaggeration or more provocative than it intends to be. That's at least my opinion. I mean, I obviously follow the Eagles as closely as any team in the league. So, at least I have a strong, informed opinion on what they do and who the player is.”
As to who that player is, since the nerve problems created pain up and down his legs that marred his 2025 campaign, there are real questions being asked around the NFL about how he will hold up. The Eagles clearly did not want him snapping the ball regularly despite being a former Pro Bowl center; he was struggling mightily at guard, and, making $16.5M this season with essentially $17.5m guaranteed for next season, Banner believes Roseman was eager to shed this salary despite his line woes.
“The Eagles were really highly motivated to make a trade,” Banner said. “Even with all their problems at the moment (on the line), I mean, I guess I can't prove this, but from talking to people in the building, my impression is that he's about to be benched. You know, he comes in Monday, all of a sudden he's got a concussion. I think they were actually benching him.”
Banner was the president of the Eagles from 2001-2012 and then ran the Browns for two years. He is still very plugged in around the NFL and has always had a strong pulse on the Eagles and has known their owner for quite a long time. He is not one to come off half-cocked and he went back and watched all of Jurgens’s snaps this season again before we chatted.
He knows and understands how Roseman operates as well as anyone and was adamant the Eagles are not waving the white flag on trying to win this season and simply start cashing in good players for draft picks. Banner just thinks it was over-the-top offer they couldn't refuse for a player they saw as steadily on the decline.
“The Eagles are in a real cap problem,” Banner explained. “So getting out of cap is a huge benefit to them. Cap number this year isn't very big but starting next year where it's guaranteed the cap number is very high. You know some people say, ‘Oh it's a great value.’ He's the fourth-highest paid center going forward from today in football. I mean he's not even close at this point in his career to the fourth-best center the league.”
The Ravens are now able to move rookie Vega Ioane back to guard and Jurgens brings leadership, a warrior-mentality and excellent communication skills to a position that was sorely lacking in it in Baltimore and should be a decent upgrade over the likes of Jovaughn Gwyn. That’s if he can return to form at center and stay healthy for a considerable period of time. So, yeah, people around the league are a little baffled.
“You got to the point where you're offering a two for a center who's, you know, really struggled recently and they somehow convince you that's not enough,” Banner exclaimed, “that you need you need to throw more into the pot.”
