title: Four Storylines For Ravens' Primetime Matchup vs. Falcons
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will be back on the road in Week 5 under a national spotlight for the first time this season when they take on the red-hot Atlanta Falcons on Sunday Night Football.
Coming off an injury-riddled victory over the Tennessee Titans in Week 4 at home, in which they held on to establish their first winning streak, the Ravens are currently tied for the best record in the AFC North division, right next to the competitive 3-1 Cleveland Browns.
There are several intriguing storylines surrounding this interconference matchup between these two teams. Here are the top four.
Absent from all three days of practice this week as they prepare for this matchup have been two players who rank among their highest cap hits for the 2026 season. Franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson is dealing with an ankle sprain, and prized offseason addition and star pass rusher Trey Hendrickson is still recovering from finger surgery.
Earlier in the week, head coach Jesse Minter expressed that players of Jackson status and experience could play in a game despite not having practiced all week. As a four-time Pro Bowler and former First Team All Pro, Hendrickson likely falls into that category as well, but following Friday's practice, Minter ruled out both of them .
With the Ravens' first AFC North matchup coming up next week against the Browns, with whom they're currently tied atop the division, risking the long-term health of two of their most pivotal players on the team for a nonconference primetime game doesn't make much sense.
Cornerback Marlon Humphrey, the longest-tenured defensive player, is suffering from both hamstring and calf soft tissue issues, but he was on the practice field on Friday, and Minter expects him to be available.
A week of rest for each would increase the likelihood that they'd be closer to full strength for a game with major implications. Even if the Ravens fall to the Falcons on Sunday and the Browns prevail over the New York Jets, a win in Cleveland in Week 6 would still put them back atop the division standings.
The Ravens are fortunate to not only have one of the best backup quarterbacks in the league in Tyler 'Snoop' Huntley, but he possesses a skill set that is very similar to their starter's, which means the playbook won't be limited. With a full week of reps instead of just being thrust into the starting lineup at halftime like he was last week against the Titans , the former Pro Bowler will be much sharper in the passing game because he'll have had the necessary time on task to get more in tune with top pass catchers, especially two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers, who has been off to a torrid start to the season.
This will mark Huntley's 17th career regular-season start, but it wouldn't be the first time ever, or even in the last year, that he's been asked to help lead the team to victory against long odds. The former undrafted gem was under center for two of the Ravens' most impressive wins of the 2025 season, both of which came at junctures when they desperately needed to come out on top to keep their playoff hopes alive. Huntley led them to a 30-16 home win over the Chicago Bears in Week 8 to avoid falling to 2-6, and he stepped up again in Week 17 in a 41-24 road win over the Green Bay Packers.
Back in Week 16 of the 2022 season, Huntley picked up his third career win as a starter against the Falcons. That was two offensive coordinators ago, and count first-year play-caller Declan Doyle among the coaches and teammates who have unwavering belief in the seventh-year veteran's ability to answer the call once again and perform at a high level.
"I have a lot of confidence in him to be able to operate the system," Doyle said. "I don't think the mentality of how you want to run the offense changes at all. You're trying to hunt explosives. The standard is still the standard regardless of who's in there and that can't change."
As tough as a blow as not having a two-time league MVP at the helm will be for the Ravens' offense, the side of the ball facing the toughest task in this matchup is their defense. After being the most inept offensive unit in the league with former Ravens backup Cooper Rush under center, the Falcons have fielded the most productive and well-balanced offenses in the league over the past two weeks since 2024 first-rounder Michael Penix Jr. was inserted as the team's starting quarterback.
The third-year signal caller has helped their play-action passing game take flight. Still, their offense begins, ends and is predominantly predicated upon their dominant rushing attack, spearheaded by star running back Bijan Robinson . The two-time Pro Bowler and frontrunner for Offensive Player of the Year is second in the league in rushing yards and yards from scrimmage and is a house-call waiting to happen anytime he touches the ball.
Slowing down Robinson on the ground will be an all-hands-on-deck situation for the Ravens in this game, as tackling in space and maintaining gap integrity will be paramount. Failing to execute either would almost certainly result in a long night for them, and they'd be the third straight team to get embarrassed by the "Dirty Birds" in primetime.
"It is a necessity against guys like Bijan, 11 is needed because he can make 10 miss," safety Kyle Hamilton said. "That 11th guy might be the touchdown-saving tackle, game-saving tackle — whatever it may be — but you have to go in there confident. I think if we run and hit well, we will do what we need to do. And at the end of the day, that is what this game comes down to — a very fundamental approach to this game."
No matter who's been under center for the Ravens through their first four games, the only obstacle, aside from injuries, that has kept them from taking full control, putting opponents away sooner and avoiding late-game theatrics has been themselves. According to NFLpenalties.com, they've been flagged the fourth-most times (39) and have accumulated the fifth-most penalty yardage (329), narrowly behind the Green Bay Packers (344). In Week 4 alone against the Titans , they were flagged a season-high 13 times for a season-high 131 penalty yards.
The bulk of their infractions have been committed by their offense as far too many times; they're having chunk plays and key first-down conversions negated and promising drives are stalled out because of a false start, illegal shift, ineligible man downfield or an unnecessary hold downfield away from the ball carrier. While some growing pains were expected, as the Ravens are in their first year of a new offense under Doyle. His scheme uses a lot of pre-snap motion, heavily utilizes screens and requires skill players to block downfield to turn chunk plays into explosive plays of 20-plus yards.
"You do want to use motions and shifts and cadences as a weapon, and I think when we see our offense really operate, it creates problems," Miner said. "It creates explosives. It creates running lanes [and] it creates angles blocking.
"We need to make sure that we are doing the things with the guys that they are capable of doing, that we are not trying to do too much, that it might not be something that is a one- or two-time thing [and] that it is things that we are working on a lot. Again, I challenge the coaches and myself more than anybody for us to get that right, and we will continue to strive for that."
Defensively, they've been penalized at the most inopportune times and for chunks of yardage and key drive-extending conversions for the opponents, which has prevented them from getting off the field consistently and when it's mattered most, late in games. They needed to keep their composure in coverage, especially on third downs where they're ranked in the middle of the pack in terms of conversion rate (37.5%).

title: Ravens Coach Jesse Minter Provides Troubling Injury Updates Ahead Of Sunday's Game
full_text:
Ravens head coach Jesse Minter ruled out quarterback Lamar Jackson and top edge rusher Trey Hendrickson ahead of Sunday night’s game in Atlanta, confirmed what we had been explaining with virtually certain to be the case all week.
Baltimore is without its highest paid players on both side of the ball to face the Falcons who have boasted one of the best offenses and defenses in the NFL the last two weeks since starting quarterback Michael Penix Jr. returned from his third ACL surgery. However, $19M corner Marlon Humphrey, having another rough season so far, did return to practice after treatment for a calf strain and Minter said Humphrey is expected to face the Falcons.
The Ravens resigned longtime back Snoop Huntley this offseason, even while installing a new and unfamiliar offense with a new coaching staff, and he faces a tall task Sunday behind an offensive line that has a number of issues protecting and run blocking. It will require a comprehensive rethinking of the offensive approach Sunday without Jackson.
Minter praised all the work Jackson is doing behind the scenes to come back from the ankle injury he suffered last weekend as quickly as possible, but this week was always a stretch . Minter said Jackson, a two-time MVP, is “working his tail off” to get back but was noncommittal about what is in store for Week 6 when the Ravens travel to Cleveland.
“I don’t know the specifics of next week,” Minter said.
The Ravens paid a steep price to trade for Eagles center Cam Jurgens this week while he was still in the concussion protocol. He was never really in the mix for Week 5 and was ruled out but Minter said “our hope and expectation is that he’s ready to rock,” in Cleveland.
The Ravens are likely to lean heavily into big defensive fronts to try to mitigate Atlanta’s dominant rushing attack, and Hendrickson is not stout against the run and is being paid top dollar to get to the quarterback. He dealt with a finger issue for a few weeks before the decision was made for a surgical procedure last week, which Minter said would not keep Hendrickson out long. Minter hinted that could come next week.
Humphrey is in the final year of his deal and has battled injuries the last few years. He left Sunday’s game with a calf injury and did not return. He has the highest cap hit in the NFL among all corners and is a favorite of general manager Eric DeCosta, but could be in his final season in Baltimore. With Minter's updates, the specifics of the Ravens' injury report, to be released later Friday, carries little mystery with the rest of the team's starters in line to play.

title: These 4 Individuals Must Step Up Big For Ravens To Upset Falcons Sunday
full_text:
It’s not just who you play, it’s when you play them.
The Ravens may be catching the Falcons at the wrong time, and the Falcons might be catching the Ravens at the right time from a health and personnel and match-up standpoint. That’s how it goes sometimes. Playing any game without Lamar Jackson – as people around the NFL anticipate the Ravens will be – is difficult enough and doing it with another cobbled-together offensive line dealing with injuries only compounds it.
Yes, the Ravens want you to believe that back-up Snoop Huntley has the goods … but this is the same guy they had seen enough of after the 2024 season and moved on from and who had no real market outside of Baltimore save for a few brief-and-cheap dalliances with the Browns and he couldn’t stick in Cleveland. Let’s be real about this situation.
This Sunday night game is going to require some individuals truly standing out, and making an indelible mark on the outcome, or the Ravens will be 3-2 going into Cleveland in Week 6 (which is perfectly fine). The more I study the Falcons and Ravens the more I believe these individuals will have to be truly special Sunday night, and, no, I’m not including the back-up QB in this list because if he tries to be special, and they concoct a game plan for him to attempt to be special it will reflect poorly on all of them.
Here are the four individuals who need to step up:
He’s had a very nice start to the season, but he hasn’t been taking games over and he hasn’t been as disruptive as, say, hybrid defensive back Derwin James at his peak in this system for the Chargers under Jesse Minter. You get the sense Minter has been holding back some with how creative he gets with this unicorn, and that his homecoming in Atlanta might be just the time to create a Hamilton-centric plan.
They need him to be a playmaker in run support with tackling but also maybe trying to punch another ball loose on a jump cut, with Falcons backs Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson dominating the last two weeks. This is a game where he should be all over the line of scrimmage and I also wonder if, with Atlanta young QB Michael Penix still a little skittish coming back from a third ACL surgery, and with top pass rusher Trey Hendrickson not expected to play, if we see intense blitzing – run blitzing and on passing downs – from Hamilton.
“I think if we run and hit well, we will do what we need to do,” Hamilton said Wednesday. “And at the end of the day, that is what this game comes down to — a very fundamental approach to this game. I am excited to see what we do."
Hamilton is blitzing more this season (17% of opposing dropbacks as opposed to 10% last year), but has three pressures on 25 rushes, a 12% rate that is half his career total.
Another Ravens player who is returning to Georgia – Smith played high school ball a few hours from Atlanta and went to UGA – who will want to show out. If Minter does what we expect here and leans into heavy fronts, Smith should be freed to run around and make plays. Dare I say it, I expect to see some 8-man boxes on Sunday night; the Ravens have only played about 5 snaps of 4-3 looks all season.
Atlanta will run the outside zone all night long until or unless it’s stopped ( Bijan averages 7.4/carry in the stretch play ) and the linebackers will have a lot to say about it and this one carries the biggest cap hit of any inside linebacker in the NFL ($33M) and the second-highest salary among all veteran inside backers – and we all know that’s not to make plays on the ball in flight. He’s not getting sacks and passes defensed. He’s here to organize and set a tone and be connective tissue between all three levels of the defense and be a tackling machine.
“Lot of respect for (Bijan Robinson) as a runner, their offensive line, their receivers, with their willingness to block,” Smith said. “I think it is a great challenge for us. I look at this as a front-seven game.”
Some looks with four linemen and four linebackers – with Hamilton essentially serving as one – make a lot of sense to me.
We are hesitant to include a rookie on this list but the personnel on the offense is what it is right now. Snoop hooking up with Zay Flowers deep is a silly ask and he has nine completions over 20 yards in his career . The receivers will be doing a lot of blocking, but the back-up QB did connect with the young tight end on some under-center, bootleg plays in the preseason and some quick catch-and-run plays for Hibner in the slot make a lot of sense.
He is a better athlete than highly-paid vet Mark Andrews, and with Durham Smythe now out for the season, and Nick Vannett not as well-rounded as Smythe, there is a runway for Hibner. No Ja’Kobi Lane – another big body who was doing slot work before his injury Week 1 - and a QB who is not going to be pushing it deep. Could see a lot of action underneath and the Ravens badly need YAC; Andrews ain’t that guy and Derrick Henry is somehow second to Flowers on the team in that key metric.
“(Smythe) is such an incredible player, an incredible person and teammate, and he's going to be sorely missed,” Andrews said. “But, we are going to do the best that we can in the tight end room to be ready. [Hibner and rookie Josh Cuevas] have been playing outstanding, just growing each and every game. So we have a lot of trust in them, and it's just going to be all hands-on-deck from us."
I really hope he is playing word games with the Falcons and trying to sell them on a mode of operation that he wouldn’t exactly espouse. Hopefully, he is just gassing up Snoop and trying to send messages to the locker room.
Because if he actually calls this game like he would for Lamar, it will be over at halftime. He needs to lean heavily on run-game coordinator Dwayne Ledford, who coached Atlanta’s offensive line before coming over here, and get creative with perimeter runs and attacking the boundary with speed. Doyle has a minute body of work and is trying to fool the Falcons, surely, when he says the stuff he’s said this week. But just in case, he’s on notice.
He needs to be smart and calculated and conservative with his approach Sunday night.
“I do not think the mentality of how you want to run the offense changes at all,” Doyle said Thursday. “I think regardless of who is in there, you are trying to hunt explosives. I want us to be physical outside, whether that is our first receiver or our seventh receiver that came up from the practice squad. I think that the standard is still the standard regardless of who is in there, and that cannot change.”

title: Ravens Say They Won't Scale Back Offense For Their Back-up QB. They Better Be Bluffing
full_text:
There is some serious mythologizing of Snoop Huntley going on in Owings Mills these days.
The Ravens back-up quarterback, to hear people in The Castle talk about, is one of the premier No. 2 QBs in the NFL, and a trusted piece and an excellent alternative to Lamar Jackson. Rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is so head-over-heels about the potential to win a game as a young play caller with a No. 2 QB that he’s threatening to bring a Lamar Jackson game plan into a very difficult game Sunday night in Atlanta .
Good grief. Give me a break.
A year ago these are the same executives who wanted nothing to do with Huntley anymore and believed that thoroughly washed Cooper Rush was an upgrade (Rush is now in Atlanta and “played” two games for the Falcons picking up as the complete mess he was in Baltimore). So spare me the hyperbole and over-the-top compliments. Jackson is almost certain not to play this week and maybe not next week, either , and things are going to be tough for this offense and Doyle better figure that out quickly and make major adjustments.
The combination of Huntley with a makeshift offensive line and one that can’t even really run block for Derrick Henry , is potentially perilous and thinking you can air it out like Jackson was – 10.1 yards/attempt, highest in the NFL – with Huntley (5.9/attempt and very limited as a downfield passer ), is taking people for fools.
“I do not think the mentality of how you want to run the offense changes at all,” Doyle said with a straight face on Thursday. “I think regardless of who is in there, you are trying to hunt explosives.”
The Falcons are getting pressure as readily as any team in the NFL right now, they are doing it without blitzing, and they are facing an incredibly suspect offensive line that is so bad the GM, who created the mess starting with letting elite center Tyler Linderbaum walk as a free agent, just traded a second-round pick for a veteran who hasn’t been the same since back surgery and who the Eagles didn’t even really think was a center anymore .  And Huntley, for all his limitations, is a an acute problem when he is put under any sort of pressure.
Huntley is 7-9 in his career (Jackson covers up a ridiculous amount of roster warts for one of the most overrated GMs in the NFL). Huntley is pretty pedestrian when not pressured _ again this franchise was done with him and so was the rest of the league before Rush crashed out – with a rating of 89.8. One thing Huntley can do when not under duress is complete the lay ups (73% completion percentage).
Everything falls apart when he gets some heat, especially if you can generate that rush without bringing five defenders – which the Falcons do as well as anyone in the NFL.
Huntley has a career rating of 62.0 under pressure, completing just 46.8% of his passes with four TDs and three picks and averaging a scant 4.9 yards per attempt. Yikes. He has a career 84.8 rating against the blitz, so, again, the big problems occur when you get him rattled with four up front. Against this OL, that’s well within reason.
And the idea he is going to attack downfield is taking people for fools. Huntley is 9-for-47 in his career on passes that travel over 20 yards in the air, with four picks and no TDs and a 20-something rating. Going there in a dome with this group around him would be courting disaster. Go for it rook, sitting up there in the press box with your long script of plays. I dare you.
The Falcons will destroy those seven-step drops.
Atlanta leads the NFL generating a 47.3% pressure rate. They have nine more pressures than any team in the league and they are second with 32 QB hits and they are doing all this despite being 29th in blitz rate (around 20%). If Huntley isn't leaning into checkdowns and the ball isn’t coming out very fast and not going not very far, big problems will arise.

title: The Ravens Must Emphasize These 3 Things To Upset The Falcons
full_text:
The Ravens are underdogs for the first time under rookie head coach Jesse Minter, and rightfully so.
The Falcons board the second-best run game in the NFL – and at 477 yards the last two weeks since Michael Penix Jr. took over at quarterback, it’s really the best (Bijan Robinson is averaging a cool 7.4/carry running outside zone). They are allowing an NFL-best 2.7 yards per carry – a half yard better than the rest of the NFL – and also have the number one pass rush in the league. And they are at home on a Sunday night.
The Ravens’ injury report continues to look quite imposing, from quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) not practicing all week, on down ( there are going to be quite a few absences ) and rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle must also navigate a makeshift offensive line for at least another week until new trade acquisition Cam Jurgens is out of the concussion protocol ( a lot about that risky trade is odd ).
It’s a lot to digest and the team is also in its second week back from traveling to another continent to play a football game in Brazil and some around the game believe the impact of that can take hold more acutely in the second week back. Baltimore’s run game is going nowhere with this offensive line right now no matter what Derrick Henry tries, which could spell big problems with backup QB Snoop Huntley not nearly as adept pushing the ball downfield as Jackson is (Lamar is leading the NFL at 10.1 yards/attempt and Huntley is at 5.9/attempt in his career.
Still, the Falcons have not yet proven to be a juggernaut under new coach Kevin Stefanski, the Ravens have a strong understanding of how he likes to operating facing him for years in Cleveland and Ravens offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford came over from Atlanta so he should have as good a read on Bijan Robinson as anyone, not that it will matter.
There is a path to win, and it will take the Ravens adhering to these principles:
The Ravens have played just five snaps in a 4-3 look all season. They should double that in the first half Sunday night. They’ve played just 24 snaps in a 3-4. Being in nickel or dime 90% of the time won’t fly against these Dirty Birds, and Minter has to know that .
“I think it is an exciting challenge for us, when you pride yourself on stopping the run,” middle linebacker Roquan Smith said. “Lot of respect for [Bijan Robinson] as a runner, their offensive line, their receivers, with their willingness to block. I think it is a great challenge for us. I look at this as a front-seven game. It is about showing up, and obviously the whole world's watching, so showing up and showing out."
Um, maybe a front-eight game. Could line up with Zion Young and Tavius Robinson on the edge, Calais Campbell (a former Falcon) and Nnamdi Madubuike inside (or even a Broderick Washington type), with hybrid defensive back Kyle Hamilton mugging the line of scrimmage as a de-facto LB, along with linebackers Smith, Trenton Simpson and Teddye Buchanan on the field.
We should see some personnel deployments Sunday that we have not seen prior. This difficult of this assignment dictates it.
So the line is still shaky and do-it-all-blocking tight end Durham Smythe was lost for the season, and we are asking more of a rookie tight ends that was expected. But, it appears both starting tackles – Ronnie Stanley and Roger Rosengarten are good to go. Running behind them has been one of the few things to work for the Ravens lately on the ground, and the perimeter attack will be huge all around Sunday , and extra tackle Carson Vinson should see plenty of the field.
The Falcons are mauling people at the line of scrimmage (72% success rate against the run is nuts) and not devoted a ton of manpower to do so. Ravens have to find a way to swing the math at least a little more in their favor and unbalanced lines and tackle-eligible plays can make that happen.
“For you to be No. 1 in the run game,” Henry explained of the Falcons, “you have to have guys that are willing to go tackle by any means. And it means something to them, from what we see on tape."
Doyle kept going on and on Thursday morning about nothing changing in terms of his overarching offensive goals if he has to play Huntley (he will). Um, that best just be lip service.
“Absolutely, when we put the game plan together, the mindset is still the same,” Doyle opined on Thursday. "We are still trying to stress and attack rules. We are still trying to go after a defense and see if we can pry out bigger plays and be able to move the ball down the field."
This needs to be a scaled -down approach loaded with high-percentage routes and checkdowns everywhere against a team getting a 47% pressure rate without having to blitz (20%, 29th in NFL). Short routes to the outside and trying to crate situations for big YAC is what is required here. Huntley is erratic throwing downfield and doesn't have Jackson's arm; the approach must reflect that.
Henry is already on pace to shatter his 15 receptions last season (seven through four games) and he should get fed some in the air by design – again, to the outside. More bubble screens and passes behind the line of scrimmage might be in order.

title: What The Ravens Thursday Injury Report Reveals About Sunday's Game
full_text:
Ravens coaches continue to claim two-time MVP Lamar Jackson could face the Falcons Sunday, while execs around the NFL wonder if he will even face the Browns in Week 6.
The superstar quarterback did not practice again Thursday with an ankle injury that kept him out of the second-half last week, had him in a walking boot and required an MRI test. Head coach Jesse Minter and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle certainly want Atlanta to wonder who will be at quarterback Sunday night, but trust me, the Falcons are expecting back-up Snoop Huntley for myriad and obvious reasons.
Minter claims the Ravens could take it right up until game time, but having Jackson play this early in the season on an injury like this would run counter to how they have already handled similar situations with star receiver Zay Flowers and left tackle Ronnie Stanley and $30M pass rusher Trey Hendrickson. Jackson, who is essentially in a walk year with no guarantees beyond this season , has traditionally required a week or two to be able to trust his body fully enough to play with lower-grade injuries in the past, and the Ravens offensive line remains under duress (we’ll see if just-acquired center Cam Jurgens can return from a concussion in Week 6 ) and the Falcons have the NFL’s premier pass rush right now.
So, yeah, it will be Huntley at QB, and the Ravens will also almost certainly be without Humphrey (calf) – in a career tailspin for years and injury-prone but carrying the top cap hit of any corner in the NFL and making $19.3M – as well. Hendrickson, also with a significant injury history, has yet to practice since getting a procedure on his finger last week that Minter said would get him back on the field quickly.  Hendrickson was signed to a $30M/year deal after Ravens general manager hid behind Maxx Crosby’s alleged medical issues ( he’s only playing about 95% of the reps for the Raiders ) to bail out of that trade.
Thursday is the last heavy practice day of the week and the participation generally is a strong indicator about Sunday.
Flowers has been limited with an ongoing hamstring injury but he is playing barring some unforeseen setback. The Ravens are trying to navigate left tackle Ronnie Stanley through a painful toe injury and limiting his practice reps but he practiced in full Thursday. Hybrid defensive back Kyle Hamilton has been nursing a groin injury and was limited Wednesday but practiced full on Thursday and also is in line to play.
Guards John Simpson (groin) and Andrew Vorhees (foot) did not practice Wednesday but returned in a limited capacity on Thursday. Simpson has been playing through this situation all season and started every game. The Ravens would be foolish to move rookie guard Vega Ioane from center . He should remain deployed between those two (on youngster Emery Jones Jr. if he has to fill in) for one more week until Jurgens can likely return.

title: Bills' Final Week 5 Injury Report: DJ Moore Practices Saturday, Two Ruled Out for MNF
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills won't have wide receiver Josh Palmer available when they visit the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football, and wide receiver DJ Moore is officially questionable to play.
Buffalo was forced to add Palmer to the injury report on Friday after he banged up his shoulder during practice.
"He got kind of twisted up yesterday in practice. We're still kinda going through some of the testing and whatnot," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady.
Palmer and Moore are two of 15 players listed on the Bills' final Week 5 injury report. Ten of those 15 have been cleared for the October 12 road game.
Palmer and starting defensive lineman Ed Oliver have been ruled out. With Palmer unavailable, Buffalo will activate fourth-round rookie wide receiver Skyler Bell for the first time.
Meanwhile, Moore, slot cornerback Dee Alford and rotational defensive lineman Landon Jackson all carry questionable tags as the Bills head west.
"We got 48 hours to kind of keep working through with these guys," said Brady following Saturday's practice in Orchard Park.
Brady claimed he's comfortable with taking it up to kickoff with the three questionable players, and he dismissed the idea that their lack of practice makes them less prepared for the game.
"We're at the point, these guys are vets that have practiced and have taken a lot of reps with us. It's not like these guys were out for an extended period of time and they haven't gotten a lot of time on task with the defense or the offense."
Despite leaving two games early because of his AC joint sprain, Moore has been available for the Bills all four games thus far.
As a result, the veteran wide receiver has appeared in 91 consecutive regular season games dating back to December 2020. He has 12 receptions for 178 yards and one touchdown thus far in his first season with the Bills.
"DJ has already shown that he can go out there and go play in a game and have success without the [practice] reps," said Brady, who was Moore's offensive coordinator with the Carolina Panthers in 2020 and 2021.
It seems to be a pain tolerance issue for Moore, who reaggravated the injury during the Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
"Nothing different. It's just the same thing kinda going on," said Brady.
Our guess is that Moore takes an injection to manage the pain and suits up for Buffalo on Monday night.
While Alford may not be available after tweaking his ankle during the October 4 loss, the Bills' ailing secondary will welcome back starting cornerback Christian Benford after a one-game absence.
"Christian's good to go," said Brady.
Benford, who suffered a non-contact toe injury in the Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers, returned to practice in a limited capacity on Thursday and Friday. He was upgraded to a full participant on Saturday.

title: Two Lineup Changes Jim Leonhard Must Make to Improve Bills' Struggling Defense
full_text:
It's been a mixed bag of results thus far for the Buffalo Bills ' new-look defense.
While the pass rush and run defense have been solid, opposing passers have beaten Buffalo through the air on too many occasions.
In the Week 4 home loss to the struggling New England Patriots , the Bills allowed Drake Maye to pass for 269 yards and three touchdowns with a motley crew of wide receivers.
Although it's unreasonable to pin the defensive failures strictly on two players, the Bills simply need more production from the cornerback and linebacker positions.
The solution is not as simple as changing out two starters, but it's a good way for defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard to begin addressing the problem.
There's no sugarcoating it. Cornerback Maxwell Hairston has been overmatched as a starter thus far.
His struggles were highly visible in the Week 4 loss to New England. Hairston, a 2025 first-round draft pick, allowed two touchdown receptions in one-on-one coverage. He also permitted a drive-extending fourth-down catch on the possession that ended with the second TD reception allowed.
Capping off a disappointing performance, Hairston failed to close on Patriots' tight end Hunter Henry as he ran past the first-down marker to convert a 3rd-and-10 that sealed the win.
“I think he's an emotional player that the emotions are getting the best of him right now. And it's our job to help settle that down. He's got a ton of pride," said Leonhard.
It's time to settle Hairston down by sitting him down in favor of second-round rookie Davison Igbinosun , who has been solid while seeing rotational snaps. He has 18 tackles and three pass break-ups over 133 reps. The Ohio State product has an aggressive play style that brings energy to the defense.
While head coach Joe Brady confirmed that Hairston remains the starter, it wouldn't be surprising to see Igbinosun's snap share to increase.
Williams, a 2023 third-round pick, has possesses good athleticism, but his instincts have been questionable. He especially seems to struggle in pass coverage.
Opposing passers have completed 81 percent of attempts when targeting Williams, who has permitted two touchdown passes over the first four games. He also has three missed tackles on the year.
While Williams has shown to be a serviceable injury replacement over his first three-plus seasons, he has yet to prove worthy of a full-time starting job . He likely won the role by default with his lone competition being green fourth-round rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr.
With veteran Shaq Thompson in the building and ramping up over the last five weeks, it seems like it's a good time to move him off the practice squad and into Williams's starting spot.
Thompson, a 2015 first-round pick, was Buffalo's best defensive player at times last season. Over two playoff games, he totaled 13 tackles, 2.0 TFL and one interception. Provided he's in playing shape, the grizzled veteran is an instant upgrade over Williams.

title: Bills Linked to Intriguing Buccaneers' CB Amid Secondary Concerns
full_text:
Through four games, the Buffalo Bills have struggled in pass coverage , surrendering 1,025 yards and 10 touchdown passes. They're currently ranked 27th in the NFL in defensive passing yards and 29th in defensive passing touchdowns.
Making matters worse is the lack of turnovers being created by the secondary. Entering Week 5, the Bills have just two interceptions. One from C.J. Gardner-Johnson and another from Dee Alford. The concerns with their passing defense have been well documented and that's why PFF's Bradley Locker says the Bills would be a logical landing spot for Tampa Bay Buccaneers cornerback Zyon McCollum .
The Bucs recently won their first game of the season, taking out the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football, but they're still just 1-4 on the year. Chances are high that they could look to stockpile draft picks to reload their roster. If so, McCollum would be an intriguing name, even though he didn't shine during the first four games of the season.
"McCollum enjoyed a tremendous start to the 2024 season, but since then, his production has certainly waned. Over the first four games of 2026, McCollum sports just a 58.3 PFF coverage grade, although his passer rating against (80.4) and forced incompletion rate (13.3%) are both in at least the 60th percentile," Locker wrote. "In the first year of a three-year, $48 million extension, McCollum is another defender the Buccaneers could look to shed."
In Week 5, McCollum reminded everyone why he was given that contract to begin with. The fifth-round pick out of Sam Houston State was excellent in coverage during their win over Dallas. He stuck with CeeDee Lamb and surrendered no receptions while being targeted just twice .
At 6-foot-2 and 199 pounds, McCollum offers excellent size and uses his long arms to disrupt the opposing receiver. He did that throughout the night against Lamb and would bring some instant credibility to a Buffalo secondary that has been suspect.
General manager Brandon Beane might be hesitant to make a move after using a first-round pick on Maxwell Hairston in 2025 and a second-round selection on Davison Igbinosun in 2026. He also recently signed Christian Benford to a lucrative extension.
That said, they fired Sean McDermott because he didn't get to the Super Bowl, meaning they were selling their fan base on urgency. Sitting back and doing nothing to fix the secondary would run counter to that urgency.

title: New Bills' 2027 NFL Mock Draft Lands Intriguing High-Upside CB
full_text:
Cornerback has been a sore spot for the Buffalo Bills this season. Not only has Maxwell Hairston struggled to hold his own as a full-time starter , but veteran Christian Benford is off to a rough start as well.
Injuries have made things worse, with Benford missing their Week 4 loss to the New England Patriots. He should be back against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5, but it's clear the Bills need more depth. That's discouraging since they used a first-round pick on Hairston in 2025 and a second-rounder in 2026 on Davison Igbinosun.
That said, the continued need is too great to ignore, which is why The Athletic's Nick Baumgardner has Buffalo using its top pick in his most recent 2027 NFL mock draft on Mississippi State cornerback Kelley Jones.
The first thing that stands out with Jones is his size. The 6-foot-4, 195-pound cornerback has more than enough length to match up with any wide receiver in the league. Speed is often an issue when it comes to tall corners, but as Baumgardner says, Jones has plenty of speed and possesses a strong burst which helps him make up ground in a hurry.
"A former high school quarterback, Jones (6-4, 195) is a very active outside corner with good speed and burst at his size. He still has some raw spots in his game, but the athletic potential is crazy. There are some Tariq Woolen flashes in here," Baumgardner wrote.
Being a former quarterback is also a plus for Jones, since it means he's familiar with how offenses want to attack the defense.
During his redshirt sophomore season in 2025, Jones became a breakout star. He recorded 34 tackles, but it was his ability to get his hands on the ball that stood out.
Jones had just one pass breakup in his career entering the year, and ended up with 11 . He also had his first two career interceptions, putting him in the discussion to be a first-round pick once he declared for the draft.
In Buffalo, he could serve as a CB2 opposite Benford while allowing Hairston and Igbinosun to fight for the third spot. It might not seem ideal to have two premium picks fighting for a reserve spot, but the Bills have to do something to fix the secondary, and adding as much talent as possible is a smart first step.

title: Josh Palmer Added to Bills' Week 5 Injury Report Joining WRs DJ Moore, Keon Coleman
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills increased the number to 15 players on their Week 5 injury report with another wide receiver joining the group on Friday.
With the Bills preparing for an October 12 primetime road test against the Los Angeles Rams, wide receiver Josh Palmer popped up on Friday's post-practice report. Buffalo listed Palmer as a limited participant with a shoulder issue, suggesting that he could have suffered an injury mid-practice.
Although the extent of Palmer's shoulder problem is unknown, it's never usually a good sign when a player is added to the injury report this late in the week. The Bills will hold one more official practice on Saturday before traveling west.
Palmer is one of three Bills' wide receivers currently fighting through injury . DJ Moore, who sprained his AC joint in Week 2, missed his second straight practice on Friday. Continuing to play through a nagging ankle issue, Keon Coleman was a full participant for the second day in a row.
Palmer had been healthy through the first four weeks after playing through an ankle/knee injury for much of a disappointing 2025 season.
With the uncertainty at the WR position, it seems as if fourth-round rookie Skyler Bell could potentially make his debut on Monday Night Football.
"I hope to have everybody. We're gonna prepare. If there's guys that aren't playing in this game, I'm going to have the full confidence [in those who are playing]," said Bills' rookie head coach Joe Brady.
Of the 15 injured players, 10 were full participants on Friday. Defensive lineman Landon Jackson, who banged up his knee last time out, improved from limited to full participation.
In  addition to Moore, defensive lineman Ed Oliver and slot cornerback Dee Alford did not practice . All three players left the October 4 game due to injury.
Moore reaggravated his shoulder injury during the Week 4 loss, and giving him multiple days off for rest and recovery is likely part of the plan to maximize his chance on playing on Monday night. Moore has a 91-game availability streak that dates back to December 2020.
"DJ's a competitor," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady. "You see the difference with us with DJ out on the football field. I think that that's natural and that's real. He is always going to do, literally, everything he can to be out there, not just for himself, but for his teammates."
Oliver left last Sunday's game after taking a hit to the knee area. While the game nauru is said to not be severe, it's trending in the direction of missing this week's game.
Meanwhile, Alford was forced out by what appeared to be a mild ankle sprain against the Patriots. Although he didn't return to the game, he addressed reporters in the locker room afterwards.
"I'm feeling pretty good. Gotta get an MRI, see how things go. I don't really know too much right now, but I feel good. I'm a warrior, so I'm ready for whatever," said Alford.
The Bills were without Benford when they hosted the Patriots in Week 4 after the cornerback left the Week 3 game against the Los Angeles Chargers due to a non-contact toe injury .
Benford, who was temporarily wearing a walking boot in the immediate aftermath, returned to practice this week, logging back-to-back limited efforts.
"Day by day," said Benford after Thursday's practice.
Although it's not known if the injuries are similar, it's worth noting that Benford suffered a toe injury that forced him to miss one game last December.

title: Bills vs. Rams Expert Pick Roundup: Buffalo Faces Uphill Battle in Week 5
full_text:
Week 5 will feature the Buffalo Bills in primetime as they visit the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football .
Buffalo is coming off a frustrating loss to the New England Patriots , and things won't be any easier for them this week. Los Angeles comes into the game with a record of 2-2, but they're still one of the top contenders in the league and were just one game shy of making the Super Bowl in 2025.
A win would do wonders for the Bills' confidence, but can they pull that off? Here's a look at what some of the experts believe will happen as we check out several outlets to see who is favored to win this matchup.
Dan Parr gave his reasoning for picking the Rams, and he was focused on the Buffalo defense being unable to deal with the high-powered Los Angeles offense.
"We saw last week that the Bills have a get-right defense for quarterbacks, with Buffalo allowing Drake Maye to have his best game of the season -- by far -- after a horrendous start to 2026. I’m counting on Matthew Stafford to shake off his struggles (6:6 TD-INT ratio) against a defense that doesn’t appear up to the challenge of covering Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. The Bills rank among the bottom 10 in scoring and total defense, while Los Angeles ranks among the top 10 in both categories," Parr wrote.
Prisco's Pick: Rams 34, Bills 33
"This is one of the best games of the week. The Bills are coming off a tough loss to the Patriots, while the Rams rallied to beat the Eagles. Look for a lot of points in this one as Josh Allen and Matt Stafford have big games. In the end, the Rams will make the plays late to win it," Prisco wrote.
The experts are high on the Rams in this one, and it's easy to see why. Los Angeles hasn't looked like the team we thought they would be, but they played well down the stretch against the Philadelphia Eagles to pull off a big win on the road last week.
Now, they're at home, and they get to face a team that has to travel across the country. Throw in the fact that Buffalo hasn't played exceptionally well over the past two weeks, and it seems like a game they could wind up losing.
There's also the fact that Joe Brady is still a young head coach, and Sean McVay is a Super Bowl winner who knows how to exploit a team's weaknesses. That said, this Rams team doesn't look like the juggernaut we're used to, and the Bills will be focused following their loss to the Pats. That's why I see them pulling off an upset on the road.
Final score: Bills 28, Rams 23

title: Revisiting Huge Josh Allen Performance That Wasn't Enough Last Time Bills Faced Rams
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have certainly been involved in their share of high-scoring games in recent years, and this season has been no exception.
Joe Brady’s team leads the NFL with 127 points after four weeks of play. There was the Week 1 victory at Houston, 36-31. Four days later, the Bills reached the end zone early and often in a 41-31 prime time win over the visiting Detroit Lions.
On Monday night, the Los Angeles Rams will be hosting Josh Allen and company for the third time in five years .
Only the Chicago Bears have gained more total yards per game than Sean McVay’s team, while Buffalo’s offense ranked was ranked sixth in the league in this same category entering Week 5. Brady’s team also leads the NFL in points per game (31.7) this season.
Obviously, there have been a few notable changes for both clubs since these two perennial playoff teams met two years ago at SoFi Stadium. Sean McDermott was still head coach of the Bills. As for the Rams, wide receiver Davante Adams was a member of the New York Jets, and defensive tackle Aaron Donald had retired after the 2023 season.
The last time the (6-6) Rams STUNNED the 10-2 Bills in 2024 🫪 pic.twitter.com/C2EkhoFhT2
In Week 14 of 2024, McVay’s squad outlasted the Bills , 44-42. The clubs combined for 902 yards of total offense, with the Rams owning the slight edge, 457-445. Both clubs played turnover-free football. And while Rams’ quarterback Matthew Stafford was on point with 320 yards through the air (23-of-30) and touchdown tosses to Puka Nacua and Cooper Kupp (now with the Seattle Seahawks), Allen put on quite a show in a losing effort.
The teams were tied 7-7 after 15 minutes of play. Both clubs drove 70 yards for touchdowns in the first quarter. And as it turned out, the Bills would never have the lead in this 86-point shootout. They trailed by 17 points twice in the third quarter and would outscore the Rams, 21-6, in the fourth quarter.
Throwback to one of the most INSANE fantasy performances we’ve ever seen. 🤯🔥 Josh Allen vs. the Rams in 2024: 🎯 342 passing yards 🏈 3 passing TDs 💨 82 rushing yards 🏈 3 rushing TDs 💥 6 TOTAL TDs 📈 51.88 fantasy points The first player in NFL history with 3 passing TDs… https://t.co/eNbOZ8f3Ry pic.twitter.com/rJ7mQWKoUG
As for Allen, he accounted for all of Buffalo’s six touchdowns one way or another. He hit on 22-of-37 throws for 342 yards and three scores. He was the Bills’ leading rusher in attempts (10) and yards (82) and ran for three TDs—all one-year jaunts. Amari Cooper led the team with six receptions, while Khalil Shakir, Mack Hollins (now with the Patriots), and Ty Johnson were on the receiving end of Allen’s touchdown tosses.
One Sunday later, the Bills outlasted Dan Campbell’s club at Ford Field, 48-42. Allen had another huge performance and Buffalo needed all of that to avoid a second straight loss. This Monday evening in Inglewood, he may have to be at his turnover-free best if the club is to avoid back-to-back losses this season.

title: Bills' Week 5 Friday Practice Status for Christian Benford, DJ Moore And More
full_text:
Three Buffalo Bills' starters missed their second consecutive practice on Friday in Orchard Park.
As the Bills prepare for their Monday Night Football road game against the Los Angeles Rams, wide receiver DJ Moore, defensive lineman Ed Oliver and slot cornerback Dee Alford were not present during the media-viewing portion of practice for the second day in a row (h/t WGR's Sal Capaccio ).
While Moore has been fighting through a shoulder injury since midway through the Week 2 win over the Detroit Lions, Oliver and Alford were banged up during the Week 4 loss to the New England Patriots. All three players left the October 4 game early.
Although they're not visibly active during practice, the injured players could still wind up being available on Monday night.
"Our guys are going to prepare," said first-year head coach Joe Brady. "There's going to be guys that might not practice, but you guys know how I am with that, and we're going to do everything we can."
Moore, who has appeared in 91 consecutive games dating back to 2020, is likely doing what it takes to prepare his body for a Week 5 appearance.
"DJ's a competitor," said Brady who spent two years coaching Moore with the Carolina Panthers. "You see the difference with us with DJ out on the football field. I think that that's natural and that's real. He is always going to do, literally, everything he can to be out there, not just for himself, but for his teammates."
Whether it's Moore, Oliver, Alford or all three, the chances of playing increase as a result of the Monday game.
"We also have the luxury of having a full day, an extra day with that. We're gonna give some guys [the chance] all the way through to game day. Knowing that if they give us the best opportunity to win, we're gonna roll with it," said Brady.
Oliver took a hit to the knee area last Sunday, and he exited. He spent the rest of the game in uniform on the sideline sans helmet.
Alford tweaked his ankle, and sounded optimistic when addressing reporters after the game in the locker room.
Although their Week 5 availability is in question, Brady said they were not expected to be long-term issues.
The Bills will need all hands on deck to slow down the Rams' potent passing attack and elite receiving corps. In a positive development, it appears as if starting cornerback Christian Benford is nearing a return after missing the Week 4 loss.
Benford, who suffered a non-contact toe injury during the third quarter against the Los Angeles Chargers on September 27, practiced for the second straight day . He was a non-participant the entire week leading into the Patriots matchup.
With Alford also sidelined and backup nickel Jordan Hancock on Injured Reserve, the Bills are somewhat shorthanded at the position.

title: Three Bold Predictions for Buffalo Bills vs. Los Angeles Rams on Monday
full_text:
All eyes will be on the Buffalo Bills this week as they play in the final game of Week 5 . The Bills will travel to Southern California to take on the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football .
Los Angeles is coming off an impressive win, coming back in the fourth quarter to beat the Philadelphia Eagles. That win moved them to 2-2, which is surprising considering they entered the season as one of the huge favorites to win it all.
Buffalo was also seen as a favorite and while they're 3-1, they haven't looked sharp over the past two games. They still have the talent to defeat any team in the league, including the Rams, and have a far better chance of doing so if these three bold predictions come true.
Here's what the Bills' first injury report of the week looks like.
Through four games, Keon Coleman has been one of the biggest surprises for the Bills . He has 14 receptions for 217 yards and a touchdown, and is coming off his best game of the year. With DJ Moore dealing with a shoulder injury , Coleman stepped up and had 116 yards and a touchdown on six receptions.
He's been earning Josh Allen's trust and that should lead to even more opportunities going forward. In this first bold prediction, Coleman takes advantage of those opportunities and records 100 yards receiving with a touchdown for the second week in a row.
Matthew Stafford is going to be a problem for the Bills since he's one of the more accurate quarterbacks in the NFL. That doesn't mean they can't have some success against him, especially when it comes to the pass rush.
At 38 years old, Stafford isn't the most mobile quarterback, which is one of the reasons he's been sacked six times. That's good news for a Buffalo defense that has seen Greg Rousseau, Deone Walker , and Bradley Chubb all play well. In this bold prediction, all three continue to perform at a high level as each records a sack on Stafford.
During their wins over the Lions and Chargers, the Bills leaned heavily on James Cook as he had 135 yards on the ground in Week 2 and 154 yards in Week 3. Against the Patriots, he had 75 yards, but was still ripping off 6.2 yards per attempt. The problem was that he had just 12 attempts.
Against the Rams, that can't be the case. Cook needs to be a huge part of the game plan and in this final prediction, that's exactly what happens as he runs for more than 150 yards for the second time this season.

title: Nobody Drafted This Panthers Rookie & That Already Looks Like a Mistake
full_text:
Coming into the season, Lee Hunter was the rookie defensive tackle I expected to be talking about. The Carolina Panthers took him with the 49th pick, and so far, he's given them plenty to feel good about.
Aaron Hall was a different story. He went through all seven rounds without hearing his name called, signed with Carolina out of Duke, and came into camp just trying to find a way onto the roster. Honestly, I wasn't paying much attention to him at the time.
Four games later, I am now.
Hall has played in every game, already has 10 tackles, and has even made a start. Six of those tackles came in Carolina's 34-3 win over Atlanta, and he also has a fumble recovery. That's a pretty good start for a guy nobody drafted.
The funny thing is, maybe the Panthers aren't nearly as surprised by this as the rest of us. After Hall made the 53-man roster, general manager Dan Morgan said the rookie "kind of blew us away" with his ability to handle double teams, rush the passer, and play with a high motor.
Turns out Morgan might have been telling us something.
What really made me take notice was NFL.com's early All-Rookie team . Hunter made the first team at defensive tackle, which is already a pretty good development for Carolina, considering how much they invested in him.
Then I kept reading, and there was Hall on the second team alongside Kansas City first-round pick Peter Woods. Think about how different those paths were just a few months ago. Woods heard his name called in the first round, Hunter went in the second, and Hall sat through the entire draft without getting picked.
Now all three are on the same list.
That's what makes Hall's first four games such a good story. This isn't just an undrafted rookie hanging around at the bottom of the roster. He's getting snaps, he's already started a game and he's showing that he belongs out there.
Hall had a pretty good résumé at Duke, too. He finished his final season with 44 tackles and 2.5 sacks and was a two-time team captain. He also grew up in North Carolina and watched the Panthers during the Cam Newton years, which makes the way this has started even better.
And Carolina might have gotten a little lucky here. Every team had a chance to draft Hall. Nobody did, and the Panthers were able to bring him in without using a pick.
Nobody knows what Hall's career is going to look like after four games, but that's not really the point of this story. Going from undrafted in April to making an NFL roster was already an accomplishment. Now he's playing meaningful snaps and getting recognized alongside some of the best rookies in the league.
Hall didn't hear his name called during the draft.
He's giving people a reason to remember it now.

title: The Panthers Have Suddenly Become a Defensive Coordinator's Nightmare
full_text:
I remember when the biggest question around Bryce Young was whether the Panthers had given him enough help. Actually, I feel like we've been asking that almost since the day Carolina drafted him.
I'm not sure we need to ask it anymore. I've watched this offense for four games now, and I'm starting to wonder about something completely different. If you're playing the Panthers right now, who are you trying to take away?
I guess the obvious answer is Tetairoa McMillan. After what he did against Detroit, I'd probably start there, too. I'm just not sure that fixes the problem.
McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit. He became the first player in Panthers history with at least 10 catches, 175 receiving yards, and two touchdowns in a game, and he was named NFC Offensive Player of the Week.
Panthers.com broke down McMillan's huge night , including how Carolina kept moving him around instead of letting Detroit know exactly where he'd be. Dave Canales credited the staff for “putting him in different situations, getting matchups right.”
So yeah, I'm probably making sure I know where No. 4 is before every snap. But if I'm spending that much attention on McMillan, now I've got Chuba Hubbard to worry about.
Hubbard just ran for 122 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit. I've complained plenty about Carolina getting away from him too quickly, but if he's running the ball like that, you can't spend the entire game worrying about McMillan and let Hubbard keep getting five or six yards at a time.
And then there's Jalen Coker. He didn't even play against Detroit, but we're only a few weeks removed from him catching eight passes for 138 yards and two touchdowns against Chicago. Hubbard has also caught 10 passes with two touchdowns this season, and Darren Waller caught two touchdowns against Atlanta.
I don't remember the last time Carolina had this many answers on offense.
I know it's only four games. I've also watched this team go from getting embarrassed by Chicago to beating Detroit on Sunday night, so I'm trying not to decide too much about the Panthers from one week to the next.
Still, 121 points is 121 points.
According to Panthers.com , that's the most points through four games in franchise history. Carolina has also scored at least 30 points three times, something no Panthers team had ever done in three of its first four games.
I definitely didn't see that coming.
Young has thrown for 1,268 yards and nine touchdowns. McMillan already has 385 receiving yards, Hubbard is coming off his best rushing game of the season, and Coker hasn't even been available the last couple of weeks.
Maybe I'm making this too simple, but isn't this what Carolina has been trying to give Young all along?
For most of his career, we've talked about what he didn't have. The offensive line wasn't good enough. He needed another receiver. The running game disappeared. It always felt like we were talking about what Carolina needed to add next.
I'm having a harder time doing that now.
I'm not ready to put this offense up there with the best in the NFL after four games. That's too far for me, especially with how different this team has looked from one Sunday to the next.
But I also don't think what we're seeing is nothing. McMillan just took over a game, Hubbard ran for 122 yards, Young threw for 329, and Coker wasn't even on the field.
For once, I'm not asking whether Young has enough help.
I'm trying to figure out who defenses are supposed to stop first.

title: Bryce Young's Stunning Turnaround Just Reached a Level Nobody Expected
full_text:
Yeah, I wasn't ready for that one.
I've spent most of the last few weeks trying to figure out exactly how far I'm willing to go with Bryce Young. The MVP chants against Detroit were fun, and I've already said I'm done acting like every good game needs to come with a “let's see him do it again.”
Then I saw PFF's first-quarter All-Pro team . Young is the second-team quarterback, with only Lamar Jackson ahead of him.
I had to think about that for a minute because it really wasn't that long ago that Young was getting benched for Andy Dalton. He spent time running the scout team, and there were plenty of people wondering if Carolina had completely blown the No. 1 pick.
Now we're talking about him as one of the best quarterbacks in football.
My first thought when I saw the PFF list was whether we're getting a little carried away. Young just threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit, the Panthers got a huge win, and everybody is feeling pretty good about where this thing is going.
Apparently, PFF isn't looking at it as just one big night, either. In its latest quarterback rankings, PFF called Young's game against Detroit a “scintillating outing” that capped what it described as an outstanding four-game start.
So I went back and looked at what he's actually done, and I don't know. PFF might have a point.
Young has thrown for 1,268 yards and nine touchdowns. He's second among qualified quarterbacks in passing yards and third in touchdown passes, so it's not like one huge game is making his numbers look better than they really are.
Young also has an 88.6 overall PFF grade , which ranks second among 33 qualified quarterbacks. PFF has also credited him with eight big-time throws and only one turnover-worthy play.
That's probably the number I keep coming back to. We've seen Young make some throws this season that I don't think he was making consistently before, but he also hasn't been putting the ball in danger very often.
Now, I'm not forgetting Cleveland. That interception at the end was unfortunate, and it helped kill Carolina's chance to win. I'm not going to pretend it didn't happen just because everything around Young feels good right now.
But I'm also not going to let one throw while his arm is being hit erase everything else he's done.
Young threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns against Chicago. Then it was 287 yards and three touchdowns against Atlanta, 291 against Cleveland, and 329 against Detroit.
That's at least 287 passing yards in every game.
Four games aren't enough for me to say Young is going to be an All-Pro when the season ends. There's way too much football left, and we've already seen how quickly things can change with this team.
I just don't know how much more we can ask from him right now.
That's probably where I've changed the most on Young. Earlier this season, I kept wanting to see the next game before I bought into what was happening. He'd play well, and I'd immediately start wondering whether he could do it again.
Well, he's done it again. And then he did it again after that.
Maybe it doesn't last. Maybe we get to November, and this PFF All-Pro team looks completely different. That's the risk of doing something like this after only four games.
The question is whether Young has played like an All-Pro quarterback so far, and after looking at the numbers, I don't think PFF's choice is nearly as crazy as I thought it was when I first saw it.
Two years ago, we were wondering if Carolina had drafted the wrong quarterback. A few weeks ago, we were wondering whether Young was finally breaking out.
Now we're debating whether he's an All-Pro.
I definitely didn't have that one on my Panthers bingo card.

title: A Panthers Player Said He Had to Change His Life. Four Games Later, It's Working
full_text:
I don't think Princely Umanmielen had a bad rookie season. He played in 16 games, had 24 tackles and 1.5 sacks, and for a rookie, that's not exactly something I'd be worried about.
Umanmielen obviously felt differently.
He looked back at his first year and decided there were things he needed to change. And I'm not talking about adding another pass-rush move or spending a little more time in the weight room. He started looking at how he was eating, sleeping, recovering, and pretty much everything else he was doing.
“I had to change my life,” Umanmielen told Panthers.com.
That's a pretty big statement for a guy coming off his rookie season. When I first read it, I wasn't really sure what to make of it. Now that we're four games into this season, it makes a little more sense.
Panthers.com went into everything Umanmielen changed during the offseason . His diet changed. Sleep became more important. So did recovery and what he was putting into his body.
We've all heard the offseason stories before. Somebody lost weight, somebody added muscle and somebody is supposedly in the best shape of his life. I usually don't pay much attention to those stories until I actually see something different on Sundays.
Well, I'm seeing something different with Umanmielen.
He already has three sacks through four games. That's twice as many as he had all of last season, and he's gotten a sack in three of Carolina's first four games.
According to Panthers.com , the last Panthers players to do that were Brian Burns and Haason Reddick in 2021.
I'm not saying that puts Umanmielen in that category. Three sacks isn't enough for me to start doing that, but it's definitely enough for me to start wondering what this could turn into, especially when you go back to what he said about changing his life.
I know Umanmielen had already recorded sacks against Chicago and Cleveland, but the one against Detroit probably stood out to me the most.
Dave Canales actually thought Umanmielen was too fired up early in the game. He wasn't playing like himself, so Canales found him on the sideline and basically told him to calm down and trust that his opportunity would come.
“Just settle in, just do your job, your time is going to come,” Canales told him.
Later in the fourth quarter, there was Umanmielen getting to Jared Goff for a huge sack.
Maybe I'm reading too much into one play, but I liked that. A young player gets told he's trying to do too much, settles himself down, and then makes one of the biggest defensive plays of the game.
And really, that's kind of where I'm at with his season. I'm not ready to call Umanmielen a breakout player after four games. I've watched enough football to know three sacks can turn into three sacks through eight games pretty quickly.
But I've also watched him get to the quarterback in three of four games. I've seen him already double his sack total from last season, and now I know how much he changed, trying to make sure his second year didn't look like his first.
Maybe this keeps going. Maybe we look back in a couple of months and three sacks through four games was just a nice start.
Right now, though, I'm starting to believe Umanmielen when he says he needed to change his life.
Because something definitely changed.

title: Bryce Young Has a Secret Weapon Nobody Is Talking About
full_text:
If you asked me who Bryce Young's best target has been this season, I'd say Tetairoa McMillan. After watching him catch 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit, I don't think I'd have to think about it very long.
Then I saw something from PFF that caught me off guard. Young has a 138.1 passer rating when targeting Chuba Hubbard this season, which ranks 14th among 152 qualifying quarterback-pass catcher combinations with at least 10 targets.
I'll be honest, Hubbard wasn't even close to the first guy I would've guessed.
I've written about Hubbard plenty this season, and most of the time it's been about the same thing: Give him the ball. I've wondered why Carolina has gotten away from the running game at times, and after Hubbard ran for 122 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit, I probably won't stop talking about it anytime soon.
But I really haven't paid much attention to what he's doing when Young throws him the ball.
Hubbard has caught 10 of his 11 targets for 84 yards and two touchdowns through four games. It's only 11 targets, so we're not talking about a huge sample. Still, a 138.1 passer rating when Young goes his way is pretty hard for me to ignore. The EPA/play is highest when targeting Hubbard, too.
Maybe Carolina needs to find a few more ways to use him there. I'm not talking about turning Hubbard into a receiver or doing anything crazy. Get him the ball underneath, give him some room, and let him do what he does.
We just watched what can happen when Carolina gets Hubbard going against Detroit. The nice thing about using him in the passing game is Young doesn't have to make some difficult throw down the field for it to work. Sometimes it's just getting the ball out of his hands and letting Hubbard do the rest.
Young could probably use a little more of that.
That's where I started thinking about this a little differently, because Hubbard isn't really the story by himself.
Look at who Young has around him now. McMillan looks every bit like a No. 1 receiver through four games. Jalen Coker had eight catches for 138 yards and two touchdowns against Chicago, and Darren Waller has already shown he can give Young another option around the end zone.
Now Hubbard is sitting there as one of Young's most efficient targets.
I don't remember having this problem with Young before. For most of his career, we've spent our time asking whether Carolina had given him enough help. I know I've asked it plenty, and there were Sundays when it felt like Young had to make something happen even when there wasn't much happening around him.
I don't think we can say that anymore.
Young has thrown for 1,268 yards and nine touchdowns through four games. He's playing better football, and I'm not taking anything away from what he's doing. But it sure helps when McMillan can go for 192 yards, Hubbard can give you something out of the backfield, and there are other guys Young can turn to when one of them isn't open.
That's a pretty big change from what we've watched around here the last few years.
I'm still taking McMillan if you ask me who Young's best target is. I'm not changing my answer because of one PFF number, especially after what McMillan just did against Detroit.
But seeing Hubbard's name that high did make me realize something. We've spent most of Young's career wondering if he had enough guys to throw to.
I'm not wondering that anymore.

title: Dave Canales Gave Up Something He Loved — It Might Be Saving the Panthers
full_text:
When Dave Canales announced before the season that he was giving up play-calling to Brad Idzik, I thought I understood why. Let Idzik call the offense and give Canales more time to worry about everything else that comes with being a head coach.
It made sense, but I was still mostly interested in what it would mean for Bryce Young and the offense. Four games later, I think I was looking at the wrong part of it.
Back in February, Canales explained why he was making the change in an interview with Panthers.com . He had gone back through the previous season and noticed things he was missing during games because he was so focused on calling the next play.
“Let's not wait until Monday, when I watch the film, to be able to help somebody,” Canales said.
Four games into the season, we're starting to see what he meant.
Canales admitted this week that he still misses calling plays. That's not surprising. He said the speed of making those decisions during a game is “really stimulating,” and it's pretty obvious he still loves that part of coaching.
But Darin Gantt of Panthers.com pointed out a couple of moments from the Detroit game that caught my attention.
Akayleb Evans was having a rough night. He had given up some plays, and Canales knew the Lions weren't going to stop coming after him. So he found Evans on the sideline, talked to him, and tried to get him ready for the next time Detroit came his way.
Canales had a similar conversation with Princely Umanmielen, whom he thought was a little too fired up early in the game and had gotten away from what he normally does. Canales told him, “Just settle in, just do your job, your time is going to come.”
Later, Umanmielen came up with a huge sack in the fourth quarter. He deserves the credit for making the play, but I think it matters that Canales noticed what was happening earlier and had the time to go talk to him. That's exactly what Canales was talking about back in February.
I've spent a lot of time looking at this move from the offensive side. Is Idzik a better play-caller? Is Young more comfortable with him? Why does the offense look so much better?
Maybe I've been asking the wrong questions.
Linebacker Bobby Okereke called Canales an “emotional intelligence savant” and said that giving up play-calling allows Canales to use that part of his personality more during games. We've heard plenty about how Canales relates to players since he got to Carolina. Now he actually has time during games to do something with it.
Canales can still have his hands on the offense during the week. He's part of putting the game plan together, and Idzik isn't running some completely different system. But once Sunday gets here, Canales doesn't have to spend the entire game worrying about the next offensive series.
The Panthers are 2-2, so I'm not saying they've suddenly figured everything out because Canales gave up play-calling. We watched Chicago score 59 points in Week 1. There's still plenty for this team to work on, and four games isn't enough to know how much this change will matter over an entire season.
But I keep going back to the question Canales asked when he made the decision in February: “Can I affect our whole team in a more positive way?”
I think we're starting to get the answer.
I thought giving up play-calling was mostly about finding out what Idzik could do with the offense. Maybe it was also about finding out what Canales could do as the head coach.

title: The Panthers May Have Found Something They Haven't Had Since Luke Kuechly
full_text:
I had to read this quote twice.
After Devin Lloyd's game against Atlanta, Dave Canales said, “I don't know if I've seen a better performance out of a linebacker in 17 years of coaching in the NFL.” That's a lot to say about anybody, especially a guy playing his second game for your team.
Canales has been around some pretty good linebackers during those 17 years, too. He spent a long time in Seattle and saw plenty of Luke Kuechly from the other sideline. And no, I'm not calling Lloyd the next Kuechly because three games in a Panthers uniform isn't getting me anywhere close to that.
But I am starting to wonder if Carolina finally has somebody at linebacker who can become one of the guys this defense is built around.
I knew Lloyd was good against the Falcons. I don't think I realized just how ridiculous the whole stat line was until I went back and looked at it.
Nine tackles, two interceptions, three passes defended, and a sack. He took one of those interceptions back for a touchdown, and another pass he got his hands on ended up being intercepted by Bobby Okereke.
Lloyd became the first NFL linebacker since sacks became an official stat in 1982 to have nine tackles, two interceptions, an interception return for a touchdown, and a sack in the same game. He was also named NFC Defensive Player of the Week. Panthers.com detailed just how historic Lloyd's performance was .
Maybe Canales wasn't getting carried away when he said it. Jaelan Phillips definitely didn't think so, calling Lloyd an “incredible leader” and an “incredible talent” before going even further.
“I've been saying this since OTAs that he's the best football player I've played with,” Phillips said.
That's another pretty strong statement about somebody who hasn't even been in Carolina for a full season. Lloyd has only played three games for the Panthers, but he already has 30 tackles, two interceptions, three passes defended, and a sack.
I'm not going to take three games and start figuring out what those numbers might look like in January. I don't need to because he's already making a difference, and you don't really have to dig through the numbers to see it.
The Panthers didn't bring Lloyd here just to be another linebacker. He was coming off an All-Pro season with Jacksonville, where he had five interceptions, and Carolina pretty clearly had something bigger in mind for him.
Before Lloyd had even played a regular-season game for the Panthers, Panthers.com was already describing him as the “centerpiece of the defense” . He was going to wear the green dot, call the defense, and become one of the guys everyone else could lean on.
Then there's the history that comes with playing linebacker in Carolina. Lloyd has talked about seeing Luke Kuechly, Thomas Davis, and Sam Mills when he first arrived in Charlotte. He even spent time watching film with Kuechly before the season, so it's not like he doesn't understand what playing that position for the Panthers means.
“There's a lineage of great linebacker play, and that's special to be a part of,” Lloyd said during training camp . “And I want to just continue to do everything I can to be the best player I can be, best leader, best everything I can for this team to carry on that torch.”
That's a pretty big torch to carry, and I'm still not putting Lloyd next to Kuechly after three games. Kuechly is in the Hall of Fame. There may never be another one of him in Carolina, and I don't think it's fair to expect Lloyd to be that guy anyway.
But that's not really what I'm asking. I'm asking if the Panthers finally have another linebacker who can take over a game — somebody who can stop the run, make a play in coverage, get after the quarterback and occasionally give the offense the football back.
Maybe by the end of the season, that Canales quote won't sound crazy at all.
