title: NFL Tier Rankings Put Just 1 NFC South Team in Contention for Panthers' Title
full_text:
Coming off a much-needed Week 4 win over the Detroit Lions, the Carolina Panthers are riding high during the bye week and are atop the NFC South standings.
While 2-2 isn't objectively a great start , the Panthers more than made up for their lackluster showing in Cleveland with a Week 3 win over the Browns.
Beating a Lions team with real playoff aspirations and expectations, on Sunday Night Football, is a statement win and a huge momentum booster.
The 32-26 win featured plenty of highlights, especially between Bryce Young and Tetairoa McMillan . Both dominated the awful Detroit defense as a good QB-WR duo should.
McMillan posted his best game of the season, with 14 catches, 192 receiving yards, and 2 touchdowns, while Young threw for 300+ yards for the third time this season.
After such a huge win, Carolina's stock has risen, but the Panthers aren't the clear frontrunner for the division, not yet, at least.
CBS Sports' Jared Dublin released his latest NFL rankings, placing every team into tiers . The Panthers landed in the "probably about average" tier, but Carolina wasn't alone. The Atlanta Falcons closed out Week 4 with a dominant road win over division rival New Orleans Saints.
The Falcons secure a 45-24 road win, once again showcasing an elite offense now that QB Michael Penix Jr. is back in uniform. Atlanta now has two straight dominant road wins. Like Carolina, the team's ceiling doesn't seem like a true contender, but making the dance is the first step toward that status.
Right below the Panthers and Falcons, the "probably not that good" tier features both the Buccaneers and Saints. Both teams need to be in separate categories from Carolina and Atlanta, with a combined 2-7 record.
While Carolina isn't leading the division in wins, the Panthers are the only NFC South team with a home win in the 2026 season. Aside from Carolina's SNF win over Detroit, every other NFC South win has been on the road.
Yes, the Falcons were without Michael Penix Jr., and the QB play was laughably bad; that said, Carolina sliced through this Atlanta defense like it was nothing. Carolina is the only team, in four weeks, to hang 30+ points against the Falcons, and they did so on the road.
Seven of those points were on defense, but Bryce Young and co. still got everything they wanted against a solid Atlanta defense that has a lot of talent.
Carolina's next divisional game is back at Bank of America Stadium, as they host the now 1-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who are currently operating with an undrafted free agent as their starting QB. The Panthers have a tough four weeks ahead, but can keep this season moving in the right direction

title: The Panthers Have a Hidden Advantage That Could Decide the NFC South
full_text:
I really didn't think I'd be talking about the Panthers winning the NFC South four games into the season. After Chicago put 59 points on Carolina in Week 1, I was more worried about how bad things might get if that was what the Panthers were going to look like every week.
Three weeks later, Carolina is 2-2 and coming off a win over Detroit. The Panthers haven't looked anything like that Week 1 team since, and now I'm starting to look at the rest of this season a little differently.
CBS Sports ranked Carolina as the fourth-most vulnerable division leader this week, but something else in there caught my attention. The Panthers are tied for the third-easiest remaining schedule in the NFL.
I don't know if I'd call Carolina's remaining schedule easy. Philadelphia is right there after the bye, and the Panthers still have trips to Green Bay and Pittsburgh. Baltimore and Seattle are still on there, too, and I'm definitely not going to start counting any of those as wins.
But when you look at the rest of it, I can see why the numbers like Carolina's schedule.
The Panthers still play Tampa Bay twice and New Orleans twice. Atlanta comes to Charlotte in Week 18, and Carolina also has Denver, Minnesota, and Cincinnati left. I'm not saying the Panthers should win all of those games, but there aren't many where I'm looking at the schedule and thinking they have no chance.
That's a lot different than how I looked at this schedule before the season.
I think that's what makes this interesting. The Panthers don't have to suddenly become one of the best teams in the NFC to win this division. They just have to be better than Atlanta, New Orleans, and Tampa Bay, and through four games, I don't think that's asking too much.
Atlanta is probably the team I'd worry about the most. Carolina already beat the Falcons 34-3 on the road, but that came with Cooper Rush at quarterback instead of Michael Penix Jr. Atlanta has looked different with Penix back, so I'm not going to look at what happened in Week 2 and assume Carolina is just better than the Falcons.
But that win still counts, and it could become pretty important later. The Panthers have five division games remaining, including Atlanta coming to Charlotte in Week 18. If Carolina can take care of its division games, I'm not sure how many of those tougher games on the schedule it actually has to win.
New Orleans and Tampa Bay haven't exactly scared me through the first month, either. It's still early, and I'm not writing either team off, but I also don't see any reason Carolina should look at those four games and think it can't win them.
The first few games after the bye might tell us a lot. Carolina goes to Philadelphia, comes home for Tampa Bay, and then has to turn around four days later and play at Green Bay. That's probably the part of the remaining schedule I like the least.
Even the Philadelphia game has one thing working in Carolina's favor. The Panthers will have two weeks to prepare, while the Eagles will be coming back from playing Jacksonville in London. I'm not saying that suddenly makes me want to pick Carolina, but having the extra preparation certainly doesn't hurt.
If the Panthers can get through that stretch and stay around the top of the division, that's when I think this schedule gets really interesting. There are going to be games Carolina should have a chance to win, and a lot of what happens in the NFC South is probably going to come down to those five remaining division games anyway.
Maybe I'm getting a little ahead of myself. After Week 1, I was wondering how bad this season could get, and now I'm sitting here looking at the schedule, trying to figure out how Carolina could win the division.
But that's how much the last three weeks have changed things for me. I'm still not ready to tell you the Panthers are going to win the NFC South, and after picking Detroit to beat them Sunday night, maybe I should stay away from predictions for a little while.
I just don't look at this schedule and wonder where Carolina is going to find enough wins anymore.
Now I'm wondering how many they can get.

title: The Panthers Don't Have an Identity — And That Might Be Their Biggest Strength
full_text:
I feel like I've asked the same question about the Panthers every week this season: What exactly is this team?
After Chicago put 59 points on them in Week 1, I thought I knew, and it wasn't good. Then Carolina went to Atlanta and won 34-3, and I started wondering if maybe I overreacted. They lost a game in Cleveland they probably could've won, then came home and beat a Detroit team I didn't think they were going to beat.
So, yeah, I haven't exactly had this team figured out.
I kept waiting for Carolina to show me that one thing it was going to be every week. Maybe the running game would carry the offense. Maybe the defense would be good enough to keep them in games. Maybe Bryce Young would take another step, and Carolina would start throwing it all over the place.
I'm starting to think I've been looking for something that isn't there, and maybe that's not a bad thing.
Look at what the Panthers have already dealt with through four games. Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are on injured reserve. Xavier Legette is on IR, Jalen Coker missed the Detroit game, and the offensive line has been moved around because of injuries.
It feels like every week I'm writing about somebody else who isn't going to play, yet Carolina is still 2-2. That's nothing to celebrate by itself, but after watching what happened against Chicago and then seeing the injuries start piling up, I didn't think I'd feel this good about Carolina going into the bye.
The offense is probably the biggest reason I do. Young has thrown for 1,268 yards through four games, and Carolina is averaging more than 400 yards of offense. I thought Young would be better this season, but I definitely didn't expect the Panthers to be doing this offensively.
Sunday night might've been the first time I watched them and thought, maybe this is what this offense is supposed to look like.
Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns. Chuba Hubbard finally got going with 122 rushing yards and two touchdowns, while Tetairoa McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns. It wasn't Young having to do everything, and it wasn't Carolina trying to force the running game when it wasn't there.
They just went with what was working.
I've spent four weeks trying to decide if Carolina should be a running team or if it should put everything on Young. Maybe I've been making that more complicated than it needs to be. If Hubbard is running as he did against Detroit, give him the ball, and if Young and McMillan are killing somebody through the air, keep throwing it.
I don't really care how they get there as long as it works.
Dave Canales said this week that the bye gives Carolina a chance to look at some of the things it spent all offseason working on and be willing to move away from the stuff that hasn't worked. I like that because four actual games should matter more than whatever the Panthers thought this team was going to be back in August.
If something isn't working, stop doing it. If something is, do more of it. I know it's not always that simple, but at some point it kind of is.
The defense is where I'm still trying to figure things out. Carolina gave up 59 points and 552 yards to Chicago, turned around and held Atlanta to three points, and then gave up 452 yards to Detroit. Those are three completely different performances, and I still don't know what I'm supposed to do with that.
But I keep going back to the end of the Detroit game. The Lions had a chance to go down the field and win it, and Carolina needed one stop.
Giving up 452 yards is still a problem, and I'm sure that's going to be one of the things Carolina looks at during the bye. But when the game was sitting there at the end Sunday night, the defense made the play it had to make. I'm starting to care more about that than whether everything looks good for four quarters.
Carolina hasn't won the same way twice. The defense carried them against Atlanta, Young has carried the offense at times, and Hubbard finally got going against Detroit. Somehow, the Panthers have also kept finding guys to fill in while the injuries keep piling up.
Maybe I've been waiting for Carolina to show me what kind of team it is when it's already been doing it.
I still don't know how good the Panthers are. Four games aren't enough for me to go that far, especially when I thought they might be terrible after Week 1. But I think I understand them a little better now.
Maybe Carolina's identity isn't one thing. Maybe it's figuring out what works that week and finding a way to win with it.

title: Chicago Bears vs. Green Bay Packers Inactives: Who's In, Who's Out For Week 5
full_text:
The Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers have put out their list of inactives ahead of the Week 5 contest on Sunday at Lambeau Field.
Despite entering the game with a questionable tag, quarterback Caleb Williams will not suit up for Chicago, as expected. Williams only logged a limited practice this week and it was always assumed he would miss at least three games.
With this being his third game out, Williams has an opportunity to get back next week. We'll have more on that shortly.
Another high-profile inactive is running back Kyle Monangai, who was ruled out on Friday due to toe and thumb injuries. The toe issue is the bigger concern, though.
Now, a look at the inactives for both teams.
QB Caleb Williams RB Kyle Monangai OL Ozzy Trapilo LB Keyshaun Elliott DL Jamree Kromah DL Jayden Loving
While Trapilo is practicing in full, he still apparently needs more ramp up time before being ready to play. Theo Benedet gets another start at left tackle with Braxton Jones in IR.
Elliott was ruled out on Friday because of a quadriceps injury, but the good news is the Bears are getting Noah Sewell back from the PUP list this week after he was activated on Saturday.
Kromah and Loving have been regular inactives this season.
OL Jacob Monk G Aaron Banks OL Donoavan Jennings DT Anthony Campbell
Earlier in the day, NFL Network's Mike Garafolo noted that the Bears quarterback is "pushing to play" in Week 6,
"Really good news for the Bears the other day, with Caleb Williams returning to practice with that hamstring injury," Garafolo said.
"Not good news for this week, really for next week, because this is Williams starting to work his way back and pushing to play next week. That's what I am told by multiple sources here," he added. "The team is going to see how he does through the course of the week, so we really don't know how this is going to go, but this is Williams trying to get back right on the timeline."
So, it looks like we may see the return of Williams next week. We'll have a clearer picture on Wednesday, when the Bears put out their first injury report of the week.
ESPN's Courtney Cronin reported that Monangai is currently week-to-week with his turf toe injury .
The good news is, Cronin says he is not a candidate for injured reserve, which means the Bears don't expect him to miss more than three games.
As is the case with Williams, we'll know more about Monangai on Wednesday, when the Bears return to practice. Any semblance of participation from him would be a good sign he'll return in Week 6.

title: How Bears Are Honoring Mike Ditka in Week 5 After Legendary Coach's Death
full_text:
The Chicago Bears lost a franchise legend this week after former tight end and head coach Mike Ditka passed away at the age of 86.
Ditka's passing led to an outpouring of tributes immediately, as he was well-respected throughout the NFL world for all that he accomplished during his coaching and playing careers.
Ditka was truly one of a kind and there will never be another one like him. His death isn't just a loss for the Bears and the NFL, it's also a loss for the city of Chicago, where he meant so much.
In advance of the Bears' Week 5 game against the Green Bay Packers, the team revealed it is honoring Ditka with a helmet decal.
The decal is a simple "89," which was Ditka's jersey number for most of his Hall of Fame playing career.
Bears helmets today will have the “89” sticker in memory of Mike Ditka. pic.twitter.com/xaHYH4rfCe
Despite the rivalry between the Bears and Packers, we anticipate Green Bay will honor the former Bears coach on Sunday in some form or fashion.
There will likely be an in-game tribute once Chicago gets home in Week 7, also.
After Ditka's death was announced by his family in a statement, the Bears put out their own to honor the legendary coach and tight end.
"Mike's impact on the Chicago Bears organization, over decades as a player, coach, and proud icon and ambassador for our organization, is immeasurable. His integral role in bringing world championships to our city and our franchise, both as a player and as our coach, established prominence and excellence at a world-class level, but also created a lifetime of cherished memories in the hearts and minds of Bears fans that will last for generations," the Bears said in a statement.
"We extend our love, prayers, and heartfelt condolences to the Ditka family, and join all Bears fans in deep sadness and reverence as we remember and honor Mike Ditka," the team added.
Head coach Ben Johnson also spoke about Ditka.
"Truthfully, that was a little bit before my time, so it's not like I grew up watching that," Johnson said . "And yet, when you hear about it, as a player he was a dominant force, and then certainly his impact as a coach as well. I feel like he carried that demeanor and mindset over to coaching the entire team, and those teams emulated what he was all about. No surprise the success they had."
Before he was a head coach, Ditka was a fantastic tight end who revolutionized the position by showing tight ends could be more than just blockers.
In his first season, Ditka ripped off a career-high 1,076 receiving yards, which was a rookie record that stood for a whopping 63 years before Brock Bowers broke it in 2024.
Ditka went on to tally 794 yards or more four times and notched five Pro Bowls and five All-Pro nods, including two first-team selections.
He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988 and became the first tight end to ever be honored.
After his playing career was over, Ditka spent 11 years as the Bears' head coach and won a Super Bowl in 1985. He posted a record of 106-62 as Chicago's head coach.
There is no doubt that Ditka will live on forever as one of the true legends in both Chicago and sports history.

title: What Bears Must Prove Against Packers Besides Cheese Graters and Chants
full_text:
The Bears need to prove two things on Sunday against the Green Bay Packers .
As much as it would be nice for one of those to be that they can win one for the late Mike Ditka , it isn't one of them
Ben Johnson needs to prove these, as much as anyone because there will be limitations on what the team can accomplish without Caleb Williams. And make no mistake, Williams will be watching when this game unfolds. Despite the late-week limited practice he had, he isn't ready and the team won't risk injuring his hamstring until he's showing speed and range of motion in full practices.
More than anything else, the Bears and Johnson need to prove they can go toe to toe against the Packers for a full game and come out on top.  They never did this last year.
Caleb Williams, DJ Moore, and Colston Loveland all put on cheese-grater hats 😭 pic.twitter.com/k9r2sCbke1
Despite all of the celebration and cheese graters, and the chants by Bears fans of "Green Bay sucks" at all manner of events in the Chicago area, the Bears never did this last season. They won two out of three games and did win in the most ridiculous fashions possible.
When they lost the first game, they never led and trailed for 34:51 of the game. They did tie it in the fourth quarter but the Packers drove for the winning score and the last Bears drive ended on the interception Williams underthrew to Cole Kmet, who was open at the back of the end zone.
Bears’ QB Caleb Williams with the crucial interception to end the game. Packers win. pic.twitter.com/x4AVC1qR40
When they played the regular-season game in Chicago, they were tied for only 12:49 and led only on the game's final play, the 46-yard Williams bomb to DJ Moore in overtime. They were actually down for two scores in 7:45 of the game before their late miracle rally.
Then, in the playoff game, the Packers had complete control with a 21-3 lead just inside the two-minute warning of the first half. The Bears had led 3-0 but once they lost it they never regained it until 1:43 remained remained on Williams' 25-yard TD pass to Moore.
The Green Bay Packers haven’t scored 30+ points in a game since Thanksgiving of last season vs Detroit. That’s changes this week. The Packers will hang 30+ in an upset win against the Bears. pic.twitter.com/6b5tuyO5Kn
As much as the NFL is a league where games get decided late, it's not usually under any of those circumstances. The Bears never controlled anything in those games and didn't really battle blow for blow against the Packers. They needed miracle rallies to win two games and missed a chance to rally and win the first game after they were behind most of it.
As Johnson often says, you're not playing the 2025 season again. That's the past. However, the Bears' four decades of history with losing to the Packers says they must show they actually do have the upper hand in the series instead of assuming it.
Green Bay sucks. Green Bay sucks. 📢 pic.twitter.com/WQtkPEec3Z
The other thing they need to do in the game is show this same type of control for the NFC North. They won the division last year with a 2-4 record in it. That's not much of a division title, although they don't ask that question at season's end when you're wearing the belt.
They started this season with a loss in the division, even if it came after a fumble at the 1-yard line, a rare and ridiculous blocked field goal from in close after a whiffed block, and Williams' hamstring injury at the 6-yard line.
There’s nobody on this Bears team who scares me… Their defense is straight up trash, especially that secondary. They’re giving up plays all over the field, and I don’t see anyone on that side of the ball who should scare Jordan Love… So seriously… WHO on this Bears offense… pic.twitter.com/Fv5ghAJuil
At some point, Johnson needs to show he actually can beat teams in the division. He's 1-3 against the Vikings as a head coach and 0-2 against the Lions. The Packers ar e the only team he has a winning record against at 2-1, and both wins were on the miraculous side as stated.
When the Bears hired Matt Nagy to coach the team, the late Mike Ditka gave him some advice.
"Win your division and beat Green Bay," is what Nagy said Ditka told him.
It's what Da Coach always preached.
Johnson has beaten Green Bay but he needs to "really" beat Green Bay. And the Bears definitely need to start controlling their division.
Accomplishing both Sunday would mean they really did represent Da Coach well.
Bears helmets today will have the “89” sticker in memory of Mike Ditka. pic.twitter.com/xaHYH4rfCe

title: Stat Predictions for Bears vs Packers Includes a Colston Loveland Breakout Game
full_text:
Week 5 is too early to declare a game a 'must-win' situation for most teams, but the Chicago Bears may qualify. They're looking to pick up a third straight victory against the Green Bay Packers for the first time in 20 years, an achievement that would mark a true reversal of fortunes in the NFL's oldest and best rivalry.
The Bears actually ended another 20-year streak already by being favored to win at Lambeau Field for the first time since 2006. Most people expect them to pick up this win, thanks in no small part to some key injuries in Green Bay, but it won't be easy. Not only is the weight of history against the Bears, but they're once again playing without their starting quarterback, Caleb Williams.
That said, I do expect them to win, and win big. Head coach Ben Johnson should have his offense rolling against a vulnerable Packers defense, and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen will put on a masterclass and shut the Packers offense down. Bears fans should get ready for some impressive performances from key playmakers, starting with a fan-favorite tight end.
Today is the day that the confusing disappearance of Colston Loveland to start this season ends. The Packers lost star linebacker Edgerrin Cooper to a season-ending injury last week, and that should create a mismatch nightmare for Loveland to exploit. I expect him to be Tyson Bagent's top target this afternoon, and he'll produce his first 100-yard outing of the year.
Despite a handful of poor passes last week, Tyson Bagent actually played an efficient game against what had been a top NFL defense. Now that he's warmed up, I expect Bagent to go off against a weak Green Bay defense. I'm predicting he completes an absurd 80% of his passes for 300 yards and a trio of touchdowns. He'll throw another interception, but he's going to take much better care of the ball this week.
The 'Motivated Dayo' meme got a lot of laughs from Bears fans this offseason, but Odeyingbo has quietly been off to a great start this season and we're nearing the point where Bears fans will owe him an apology. In fact, we'll hit that point today if Odeyingbo has the game I'm predicting for him, which is two sacks and four tackles-for-loss.
Odeyingbo has a sack in each of his last three games, and Green Bay's horrendous offensive line should give him plenty of opportunities to feast, especially on snaps when he lines up in the interior.
I almost didn't include this prediction because it feels really obvious to me. The Bears still have an elite offensive line even after the shocking retirement of Drew Dalman and being without Ozzy Trapilo to start the year. The fact is that Darnell Wright is the best right tackle in the NFL , and his linemates are all playing at a Pro Bowl caliber. Against a feeble pass rush in Green Bay, I'm predicting that they won't surrender a single sack.
In my Week 5 keys to victory, I concluded that Chicago's superiority in the trenches would win this game, and the proof of this will be in the postgame laundry situation. Jordan Love should end the game with plenty of grass stains on the back of jersey while Tyson Bagent's glistening white jersey can be hung right back up in his locker at Halas Hall.

title: Chicago Bears Week 5 Keys to Victory: Can Tyson Bagent Outduel Jordan Love?
full_text:
It's finally rivalry week for the Chicago Bears. They're taking on the Green Bay Packers in Week 5 and are actually favored to win, ending a 20-year streak as road underdogs at Lambeau Field . This is a pivotal game for both teams, despite the season still being early. The Packers are hoping a win against the favored Bears will prove they're still the top dog in this rivalry and that their season is nowhere near over.
As for the Bears, a win today would mark their third straight victory over the Packers, a feat they've not accomplished since Week 1 of the 2006 season. That would signal a true sea-change in this rivalry and keep the Bears in the running to claim their second straight NFC North title .
The Bears may be expected to win, but rivalry games have a way of defying expectations, especially a Bears-Packers rivalry game. With that in mind, here are three keys the Bears must hit in order to secure a win today.
For the first time since injuring his hamstring, Caleb Williams practiced with the team on Friday and was marked as 'Questionable' on the Bears' final Week 5 injury report , but you shouldn't expect to see him play today. Ben Johnson named Tyson Bagent the starter early in the week and that's almost certainly who's going to be leading the Bears against the Packers.
The Packers are a dangerous team regardless of what the stats say, especially on defense. Lukas Van Ness looks like he's experiencing a Year 4 breakout, and safety Xavier McKinney is a true ball-hawk in the secondary. If Bagent puts the ball in harms way as many times as he did last week against the New York Jets, the Packers can make him and the Bears pay.
Taking care of the football and hitting more explosive passes will be the keys for Bagent. These are two strengths of Caleb Williams, and while Bagent can't be the same kind of playmaker that Williams is, he'll need to do his best impression.
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers made the bizarre choice last week against the Packers to keep the blitzing to a minimum, and Jordan Love had arguably his best game of the season. The Bears can't make that same mistake. They need to rattle Love early and often by sending extra pass rushers against what has been the worst offensive line in the league.
Additionally, the pass rushers need to get to Love fast. Last week against Tampa Bay, Love was getting the ball out in 2.2 seconds flat on average, which partly explained why his offensive line looked better. If defensive coordinator Dennis Allen sends extra defenders and they hit Love fast, Green Bay's offense will struggle to move the ball at all.
Since an explosive performance in the season-opener , D'Andre Swift has struggled. He's averaging less than four years per carry over the last three games, has lost two fumbles, and scored zero touchdowns. His fumble last week against the Jets even got him benched in the second half, with head coach Ben Johnson calling it an egregious fumble .
Swift has to snap out of this funk today against the Packers, especially with Kyle Monangai being ruled out with a turf toe injury. If the Bears struggle to run the ball, that will only make life harder for Bagent, who is making just his second start in three years.
This game is going to be won or lost in the trenches, and the Bears are going to absolutely dominate there on both sides of the ball. Green Bay's offensive line may be slightly improved with their newest additions, but all they've done is rearrange the deck chairs on the Titanic. Chicago's defensive line, on the other hand, has been surprisingly good to start the year.
On the flip side of that, without Micah Parsons, the Packers don't have any pass rushers who pose a true threat against Chicago's dominant offensive line. Bagent should have plenty of time to pick apart Green Bay's secondary while Swift runs for 120 yards. The boo-birds will be heard by halftime, and the Packers "faithful" will begin an early exodus midway through the fourth quarter as Chicago rolls to a dominant, tone-setting victory.

title: Caleb Williams Injury Update Opens Door For Bears QB to Return in Week 6
full_text:
There was a sign of life from Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams on Friday that lends to the hope he will return soon.
Before the Bears put out their final injury report of the week , the former No. 1 overall pick made his return to practice on Friday, which amounted to his first practice participation since he suffered a hamstring injury in Week 2.
The Bears even left the light on for him to play on Sunday by giving Williams the questionable tag , although we find it extremely difficult to believe he's actually going to play.
What the limited practice on Friday does do is set the stage for Williams to return in Week 6, when the Bears play the Atlanta Falcons.
In fact, NFL Network's Mike Garafolo is reporting that Williams is now pushing to play next Sunday.
"Really good news for the Bears the other day, with Caleb Williams returning to practice with that hamstring injury," Garafolo said.
"Not good news for this week, really for next week, because this is Williams starting to work his way back and pushing to play next week. That's what I am told by multiple sources here," he added. "The team is going to see how he does through the course of the week, so we really don't know how this is going to go, but this is Williams trying to get back right on the timeline."
As Garafolo goes on to note, the expectation is Williams would miss three to four weeks . The Week 5 contest against the Green Bay Packers marks three weeks since his injury, so he's at the early end of that timeline.
A few things could factor into the Bears' decision to push Williams out one or even two more weeks.
One thing is how the Bears do against the Packers on Sunday. If the Bears win yet another game with a backup quarterback, they might feel comfortable enough to sit Williams another week and allow for even more time for an injury that can be tricky.
Another thing to consider is the possibility that the Bears won't want Willams to return on a short week, which is what Chicago has in Week 7 thanks to a Thursday night contest.
So, if he doesn't play in Week 6, it's conceivable we won't see him in Week 7, either, but this is speculation on our part.
All that said, we tend to believe Week 6 is the current target. We agree with Garafolo that the limited practice on Friday was to get the door open, now Williams has to walk through it next week in order to officially make his return to the field.

title: Is Caleb Williams Playing Today? Latest Injury Update On Bears QB For Week 5
full_text:
Things got interesting late in the week on the Caleb Williams injury front for the Chicago Bears.
With just a few days to go before their Week 5 matchup against the Green Bay Packers, the Bears saw Williams turn in a practice for the first time since suffering his Grade 2 hamstring strain .
Williams managed to log a limited session on Friday and was even given the questionable tag , which suggests he has a chance to play against Chicago's NFC North rival. We were waiting for the Bears to downgrade him on Saturday, but that didn't happen .
So, is Williams really going to make an unexpected comeback in Week 5 against the Packers at Lambeau Field?
UPDATE: Wiliams is now officially inactive for the Bears , and he isn't even listed as the emergency third quarterback.
UPDATE: NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported that Williams is now pushing to play in Week 6, so it doesn't look like his return will come this week, as expected.
"Really good news for the Bears the other day, with Caleb Williams returning to practice with that hamstring injury," he said. "Not good news for this week, really for next week, because this is Williams starting to work his way back and pushing to play next week.
Again, no definitive answer yet, but it's hard to fathom the Bears putting Williams out there on Sunday.
After all, Williams has logged just a single limited practice since his injury and we just cannot envision that being enough for the Bears to run him out there, even with how important this game is.
The Bears are almost certainly going to take the long view of this situation and aren't going to risk putting Williams out there before he's 100% ready, and especially with the risk of re-injury the hamstring normally presents.
What makes this decision easier is the fact that Green Bay has a lot of trusts in its backup quarterbacks, and that trust has only grown since Chicago has won both games without Williams.
We tend to believe the questionable tag for Williams was just a little gamesmanship from Johnson and it will be Tyson Bagent under center in Week 5.
With Williams returning to a limited practice on Friday, that at least puts him on the runway to be back in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons.
Williams was given a timeline of three to four weeks to return from his hamstring strain and we are now three weeks into that timeline.
The tricky part of the equation here is, if Williams doesn't return in Week 6 versus the Falcons, we wonder if the short week with the Bears playing on a Thursday in Week 7 against the New England Patriots might push Williams' return back to Week 8.
It's certainly something to consider, but we'll cross that bridge when we get to it. For now, we can say that there's at least a decent chance Chicago's starter will be back in Week 6.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit Week 5: Roschon Johnson, Luther Burden, Kalif Raymond
full_text:
The Chicago Bears will have a new-look backfield when they take on the Green Bay Packers in Week 5.
That's because Kyle Monangai has been ruled out with toe and thumb injuries, leaving Roschon Johnson as the next man up behind D'Andre Swift.
Thankfully for Chicago, the team is fully healthy at wide receiver, where Luther Burden and Kalif Raymond are the team's two most productive at the position through four games.
With a matchup against the Packers at Lambeau Field on tap, here is how we're handling start or sit decisions for this Bears trio.
Johnson gets an opportunity to play with Kyle Monangai sidelined due to injury, and he should soak up most of Monangai's RB2 role, although we would not be shocked to see Zavier Scott get some run, also.
A former fourth-round pick, Johnson had some opportunities in 2023 and 2024 to show his stuff, but he didn't do much with those opportunities and has since seen his role diminish considerably to just a special teams contributor.
During the preseason, Johnson didn't show much as a runner and averaged just 3.7 yards per carry. Taking it a step further, Salvon Ahmed was clearly the superior runner over Johnson and he probably only made the cut on the 53 because of his special teams value.
Johnson averaged four yards per carry in garbage time last week, and he's averaging just 3.8 yards per tote for his career. During the preseason, Johnson averaged 3.7 and he was not impressive as a runner. In fact, Salvon Ahmed was clearly better carrying the ball, but Johnson's special teams value helped him make the cut over Ahmed.
While the increased role at least puts Johnson on the fantasy map, we're just not sure he's going to get all of the work vacated by the absence of Monangai.
There's just too much uncertainty here to trust Johnson in lineups, even in a matchup against one of the league's worst run defenses.
Burden has posted at least four receptions and over 60 yards in three of four games, and he has found the end zone once while addeing three carries for 20 yards.
All of that is good enough to rank as WR25 overall, according to Fantasy Pros , which puts him on the weekly flex radar.
This isn't a great matchup on paper, with the Packers ceding the 11th-fewest fantasy points per game to wideouts this season, but context matters here. Teams have been running all over Green Bay this season, and its defense has faced four bottom-10 passing attacks in four contests.
We don't fear the Packers' pass defense at all, and that's another reason why you're starting a top-25 fantasy receiver in Week 5.
Raymond came crashing back down to earth last week, but the fact of the matter is he's still a top-25 wide receiver, ranking as WR23 overall.
As is the case with Burden, that makes Raymond an every-week flex option until further notice. And, again, we're not fully buying into what the Packers have done against wideouts in fantasy because of the factors we mentioned in the Burden write-up.
Our biggest concern is Raymond has not yet showed us he has good chemistry with Tyson Bagent.
We can understand why you'd start Raymond given his ranking, but we want to see some proof he and Bagent are on the same page before trusting Raymond in lineups again.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit Week 5: D'Andre Swift, Rome Odunze, Colston Loveland
full_text:
When the Chicago Bears take the field against the Green Bay Packers in Week 5, they will have running back D'Andre Swift, wideout Rome Odunze and tight end Colston Loveland all in action.
Odunze finally got going last week with six catches for 94 yards, and the same can be said for Loveland, who reeled in six grabs totaling 57 yards in what was his most productive game of the season.
Swift was on the opposite end of the spectrum. Not only did he finish with just 58 yards on 15 carries, he also lost a fumble that led to him getting benched from the third quarter on.
Now that we have set everything up, here's what we're doing with Swift, Loveland and Odunze in fantasy football lineups in Week 5.
After a monster Week 1, Swift has been pretty quiet, with the Bears running back ranking as RB25 overall since Week 2, according to Fantasy Pros .
While disappointing, that still makes Swift a viable flex option, but he's better than that this week with Kyle Monangai ruled out . Now, Swift is slated to take on more work than normal, with guys like Roschon Johnson and Zavier Scott mixing in behind him.
Another reason to love Swift this week is the fact that the Packers have been a sieve against the run, with Green Bay giving up the second-most fantasy points per game to the position this campaign.
Lock Swift in for what could be RB1 production in Week 5.
Odunze had his best game of the season last week with Tyson Bagent under center, and things are looking up for this week because Bagent is expected to start again .
On paper, the Packers look like a tough matchup, with Green Bay giving up the 11th-fewest fantasy points per contest to wide receivers this season.
But that is misleading for a few reasons, one of which has to do with the fact that teams have opted to attack them on the ground because of their awful run defense. In addition to that, Green Bay has played four of the bottom-eight passing attacks over its four games and got lit up pretty good by the Atlanta Falcons and Michael Penix Jr. for 256 yards and a score in Week 3.
All that said, Odunze still only has one week of adequate fantasy production out of four and his best game resulted in a WR21 finish. That's just not enough for us to trust him in lineups yet.
Loveland finally showed some signs of life last week, but he still only ranked as TE12 and we're still waiting on an elite showing from him.
A matchup against the Packers is not a threatening one, as Green Bay is ceding the 13th-fewest fantasy points per game to tight ends in 2026.
For most positions, we wouldn't be starting a player with the kind of production Loveland has had, even with his season-best game last week. But with how shallow the tight end position is, we're running Loveland out there in Week 5.

title: Bold Predictions For the Bears Week 5 Matchup Against the Packers
full_text:
The NFL's most storied rivalry will be on display on Sunday as the Chicago Bears travel to Lambeau Field to take on the Green Bay Packers.
Unlike semi-recent history, the current chapter of that story looks more promising for Chicago. It's not too often that the NFL would flex the clash to a less desirable time slot, but that's what they did with this matchup, which was initially scheduled for the FOX Game of the Week 3:25 kickoff.
While Caleb Williams not being in the lineup for Chicago certainly played a role in that decision, Green Bay's rough start to the season is more to blame. They're 2-2, but their two wins were uninspiring (they beat the Jets and Buccaneers by a combined six points), and their two losses were even duller.
According to DraftKings Sportsbook , the Bears are 1.5-point road favorites over their rivals, and the experts are going all in on them .
We also wanted to go all in on a few bold predictions for the matchup.
Not to brag, but we're 2/2 when boldly projecting running back performances. D'Andre Swift finished a mere one yard short of our 125-yard projection in the season opener (we don't care what you say, that's a win), and Kyle Monangai scored two touchdowns against the Jets last week.
We're going back to the well this week with another Swift projection. He'll be highly motivated to bounce back strong after getting benched against New York. Luckily, he'll have a great opportunity to do that against the league's fifth-worst rushing defense.
The Packers have allowed just under 140 rushing yards per game. With Kyle Monangai on the mend , Swift will have a full plate on Sunday. They'll lean into him heavily to keep Green Bay's pass rush from pinning their ears back in the pass-rush department.
Swift has never had more than 71 yards on the ground against Green Bay. He'll have more than double that amount this time around, though. Also, he won't fumble the ball this week. How's that for bold?
Montez Sweat is due for a big game. While the pass-rush has vastly outperformed expectations, he's been somewhat quiet. He does have two sacks, but Dayo Odeyingbo has been far more disruptive .
We think that changes on Sunday (although we also like Odeyingbo's ability to take advantage of Green Bay's weak offensive line). Sweat always seems to bring out his A-game against Green Bay. He had a sack in both regular-season matchups last season and hit Packers quarterback Jordan Love three times in the playoffs.
The 30-year-old should pick up right where he left off on Sunday. Green Bay's offensive line has struggled mightily this season. Sweat will take advantage of that fact with a two-sack performance.
Vegas got this one right. If Caleb Williams had been healthy, I'm confident the Bears would handle Green Bay easily. With Tyson Bagent under center for Chicago, the 1.5-point line makes sense. It'll be a close game.
The Bears have won three of the past four games against the Packers. They would've won four of the past five if Green Bay hadn't blocked their game-winning field goal attempt (after Matt Eberflus frustratingly didn't try to make it an easier attempt) in their Week 11 matchup of the 2024 season.
Bears kicker Cairo Santos will get a chance to exorcise some demons this week. Tyson Bagent gets them in position to hit a game-winner, and the Packers won't block this one. Santos will be lauded as the hero, and the NFL is going to regret flexing the game into a less desirable time slot.

title: Cincinnati Bengals Inactives: 2 of 3 Injured WRs Set To Play, Defensive Starter Back as Well
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals wide receivers Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are active for today’s game against the Miami Dolphins.
Chase (concussion) and Higgins (groin/neck) were listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report after suffering injuries in last week’s 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Higgins didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday, while Chase missed Wednesday’s practice and was limited Thursday. Both receivers went full Friday, and the team’s decision not to elevate a receiver from the practice squad Saturday was an indication both players would be playing today.
Rookie wide receiver Colbie Young also is inactive.
Young suffered a knee injury on the first play of the Sept. 27 loss at Pittsburgh and missed last week’s game against Jacksonville.
Young was limited Wednesday, went full Thursday but was limited again Friday, and the team listed him as questionable.
Also positive on the injury front is the fact that starting safety Bryan Cook is active.
Cook suffered an ankle injury two weeks ago in the 30-27 loss at Pittsburgh. After initially coming out of that game, he returned when replacement Kyle Dugger suffered a quadricep injury.
He said Thursday he was “very hopeful” to play.
"Kind of frustrating, but I'm trying to figure it out," Cook said at his locker. "Very hopeful. I'm trying to do everything I can to be out there."
Last week, P.J. Jules and Russ Yeast split reps in Cook’s spot, with Jules playing on base downs and Yeast in passing situations.
Yeast was the lone elevation from the practice squad Saturday, a move that appears precautionary with Cook active and expected to start.
Injured linebacker Swayze Bozeman, who missed last week's game against the Jaguars, also is active after being listed as questionable with a groin injury.
The other inactives for the Bengals are Dugger, center Connor Lew, offensive tackle Myles Hinton, tight end Jack Endries and defensive tackle Landon Robinson.
Defensive tackle B.J. Hill is active and will make his season debut. Hill has been battling an Achilles injury. He went full in Wednesday’s practice but was limited Thursday and did not practice Friday.
The fact that so many players are fighting through injuries to play today against 0-4 Miami with the bye on the other side of the game indicates how important the team views this game.
"It's early in the season, so you can't pay attention to the record. These guys, they got a new head coach that's kind of playing really hard. They got a really good coaching staff," Taylor said this week. "They've got some really good cornerstones of the team that they're building around right now. You're absolutely right in that there are just some things in those games that have kind of shot themselves in the foot a little bit, similar to our losses, that you could be in a totally different record right now, and that conversation about you is different.

title: Bengals Stars Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins Dolphins Playing Status Revealed
full_text:
The Bengals may not miss a beat with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins this week. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported both players are suiting up for the Dolphins game after gutting through injury recoveries.
Cincinnati would've been very thin at wide receiver, but it's back to nearly full strength after the report.
The two were questionable entering the weekend, Chase with a concussion and Higgins with a groin/neck injury. Now, they can try to end the short Bengals losing streak and continue one for the 0-4 Dolphins.
Neither player suited up for practice until the light session on Friday, but they are expected to be full go barring any setbacks in pregame warm-ups.
The Bengals can now "throw it more" if they want to, although it's not a winning strategy to get unbalanced in the NFL. Joe Burrow discussed that this week during his press conference.
Cincinnati ran for one of the team's lowest rushing tallies against Jacksonville (23 yards).
“Obviously you want to have balance as an offense, and the run game wasn't good enough on Sunday, and I feel confident in myself that you put it in my hands and I'm going to make it work,” Burrow said . “As you said, it’s very situational. When you get into a game like Sunday, and they're a really good defense, really good front seven, I felt like we were moving the ball pretty well in the pass game.
“I could have been better in spots to help our guys and not put our defense in bad positions with the turnovers. But yeah, we’ve got to be more balanced going forward, and a big part of that is the run game.”
Cincinnati is a seven-point betting favorite on DraftKings Sportsbook against the Dolphins as they try to avoid a terrible loss early in the season. Chase and Higgins are back to prevent that and help the team get on a roll against the easiest schedule in the NFL by many metrics.

title: Jordan Battle Faces Heavy Pressure Against Dolphins in Week 5
full_text:
Jordan Battle has failed to show much improvement as a tackler this season compared to last year where he finished with the third-most missed tackles in the league with 21. He has five missed tackles so far this season through four Bengals games .
Battle himself has acknowledged his struggles to make tackles and provided a theory as to why he continues to not take defenders down on contact. He contributed his misses to continuously running at full speed and attempting to make hard hits rather than making adjustments to best get ball carriers down.
“I feel like sometimes I just tend to just go full speed, don't break down, just try to run through a guy,” Battle said this week. “Later on that drive, I did a better job of coming to, gathering and then getting them on the ground.
Controversy sparked early in the week after Battle explained a key detail to Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis' game as a passer. He said that Willis has a tell as to when he is about to get rid of the football in the form of tapping the ball before throwing. Battle emphasized that he and the Bengals defense could use this to make better breaks on the football.
“He has a little slight little tap before every throw, feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball," Battle said. "He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that that gives the read the break."
It is debatable as to whether or not Battle should make that kind of statement before playing an opponent. However, the level of confidence shown from Battle only adds to the pressure he now faces to show immediate improvement.
Zac Taylor defended Battle after many criticized him for his missed tackle against Jaguars tight end Brenton Strange last week where he converted on 3rd & 18 for a first down.
“I think there’s a lot of great examples of Jordan Battle tackling,” he said. “The (third-and-18) one coming out of the post is the one we got to get on the ground. There are a bunch of other examples where he does come out of the post and get people down with some tough tackles on the sidelines."
Defensive coordinator Al Golden also defended the play from Battle, saying that he does not agree with the criticism and that instead more players have to assist with tackling in that instance.
“If I'm being completely honest, I don't think the criticism on that one – we've always got to make a tackle; we understand that – but he needs friends on that one,” Golden said. “We've got to gang-tackle that."
His coaches have defended him, and his confidence is still high enough to where Battle should rebound from last week's struggles quickly.
The Bengals face a big game in Miami at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

title: Jaguars Defender Fined For Play That Concussed Ja'Marr Chase
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase got a little bit of justice after suffering a cheap-shot concussion last Sunday. The NFL fined Jaguars cornerback Jarrian Jones for the facemask that caused Chase to get hit in the head and suffer that concussion.
The Ringer's Tom Pelissero noted an $8,201 infraction for Jones.
"The NFL fined Jaguars CB Jarrian Jones $8,201 for a facemask on Bengals WR Ja’Marr Chase, who took another hit on the play and was ruled out with a concussion," Pelissero posted on X.
Cincinnati had to make big changes to the game plan without Chase and eventually Tee Higgins, contributing to a home loss.
The Bengals fell 22-17 and are in the AFC's 2-2 jumble.
"We just have to make it work. No one wants to hear any reason why that wouldn't work, you know? We got an unbelievable coaching staff that can problem-solve," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said about the situation after the loss. "The players understand it. I mean, you got a guy like Mitch (Tinsley), who just showed back up, and he's playing a lot of snaps for us. He and Dohnte (Meyers) are the last two receivers we have left, and they're out there making plays. And all four of our tight ends that are out there are doing exactly what we need them to do to put us in position. No one wants to hear it, but I am proud of the team for how they fought. There was a lot that went into that game.
"We're really disappointed that we lost. We're not that kind of team this year that's going to take consolation in the losses, but I am allowed to see the silver lining, and this team has a lot of fight. If I get this team for 14 more weeks or 13 more weeks, whatever it is — I'm signing up for that all day, because we're going to have a great year. It's just disappointing that we didn't get this one."
The team needs to take advantage of its relatively easy schedule the rest of the way, starting with Miami tomorrow. They hold the league's easiest strength of schedule on ESPN's FPI.
It's hard to win with cluster injuries like the Bengals are facing, but they have to overcome it in a league whose champion fights through more attrition than most along the way.
Cincinnati is hoping to have Chase (questionable) on the field tomorrow after the first concussion of his career.

title: Bengals Announce Roster Move Leading Into Road Miami Matchup
full_text:
Cincinnati made a few more of its typical practice squad call-ups for the Miami Dolphins game on Sunday.
The Bengals are bringing up safety Russ Yeast, and no wide receivers, a good sign about Ja'Marr Chase and/or Tee Higgins playing tomorrow. Yeast likely takes Kyle Dugger's spot on the roster.
Cincinnati is trying to stay in the thick of the AFC playoff race with a win on Sunday. It would also help them potentially climb from the basement of the AFC North, a division they led as the 2-0 team mere days ago.
The wide receiver room is looking much more stable than it did at the end of last Sunday's loss to Jacksonville, but the depth still needs to be ready to perform for Joe Burrow and the rest of the team.
"Fortunately, we're in a spot where the guys we're hoping will play Sunday have millions of reps, and they can make sure they're getting their bodies right," Burrow said on Wednesday. "The guys that haven't had a ton of reps will come in and take those practice reps. You get those reps and practice with those guys, still the hope the other guys will play. But if not, we have those reps banked throughout the week. We'll know more as we get closer and have some practices and have some more time for those guys to recover, but I feel confident whoever we put out there, we're going to make it work."
Burrow and the Bengals would love to get the under-center offense off the ground this week.
The depth will be key to that, as Cincinnati sports the worst yards per play in the NFL across those formations (3.3 YPP after being at 5.1 in 2025).
"I'm comfortable doing whatever is needed and will execute my best," Burrow said about that part of the game. "We obviously have to be better at it. We're still going to stick with it and keep getting reps invested in that. I think it's very valuable, so we have to be able to do it. But we need to be better.
"Under center play actions are built off the run game. Teams have to respect the run first and foremost so you don't just get jet rushers off the edge. That just puts your offensive linemen in a bad spot when they're trying to sell run, but the defense isn't respecting the run and just rushing the passer. That's not a recipe for success, so that starts with the run."
Cincinnati kicks off the Week 5 action at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

title: One Underrated Reason the Bengals Should Trade for Marvin Harrison Jr.
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals need to make a trade to add another wide receiver to their roster right now. They have one of the best wide receiver duos in the league with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, but both are battling injuries. To make matters worse, Andrei Iosivas and Colbie Young both suffered injuries in recent weeks.
The perfect idea is to trade for Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. Harrison has struggled with the Cardinals for the first few years of his career, but he has all the potential in the world. Coming into the NFL Draft, he was one of the highest-rated wide receiver prospects of this generation.
The Cardinals have reportedly agreed to a trade that will send Harrison to a new team, but the details haven't been shared yet. They will likely withhold these details until both teams involved in the trade finish their games this weekend.
The Bengals should be that team. They should go all-in on offense and bolster their passing game with Harrison Jr.
The Bengals need to be the team that takes a chance on Harrison. There are plenty of reasons that this deal makes sense. First of all, he has the potential to be a star. His talent jumps off the page, but it hasn't translated, and the Cardinals haven't put him in the best situations. The Bengals would put him in a much better situation.
The big underrated reason that this deal would make sense is Harrison's contract. Harrison is being paid $776,000 this season and will receive a base salary of $1.19 million next year with a roster bonus of $4.428 million. This is very team-friendly and would fit with the Bengals' payroll very well.
To put that in perspective, Iosivas is making $3.6 million this season.
The Bengals have spent a lot of money on their offense to this point. Joe Burrow's average salary of $55 million makes him tied for the third-highest-paid quarterback in the league. Chase has the second-highest average annual value among wide receivers at over $40 million, while Higgins is paid nearly $30 million per year, too. Adding a talented wide receiver No. 3 with the potential to be a star is the next move the Bengals need to make.
Harrison would be the perfect addition for the Bengals. Buying low on a top talent like him is the exact type if "risk" the Bengals should take.

title: Early Results Show Bengals Were Right About Trey Hendrickson
full_text:
Trey Hendrickson and the Bengals parted ways this offseason, in what many considered one of the worst-managed contract situations for too long. Now, a month into the regular season, it looks like the Bengals were right not to give Hendrickson a big payday and to build the rest of the defense.
Hendrickson has accounted for 14 pressures and one sack for the Ravens this season and is currently dealing with a finger injury that required surgery. Hendrickson signed a four-year, $112 million contract with Baltimore this offseason after the team backed out of a trade for Raiders All-Pro pass rusher Maxx Crosby.
Meanwhile, the Bengals traded for Dexter Lawrence, signed players like Boye Mafe and Jonathan Allen to build their defensive line, and drafted Cashius Howell to bolster their pass rush. Those four additions have accounted for 58 total pressures and seven sacks through four games.
Needless to say, the new additions to the Bengals' pass rush have drastically improved the defensive line's overall efficiency.
Investing heavily in the defensive line, rather than only in Hendrickson, has already paid dividends at the start of the season. Lawrence has proven his value as an elite interior presence, recording 15 pressures and three sacks this season while opening up opportunities for others on the d-line.
Hendrickson played at an elite level for the Bengals; however, his presence did not prompt many others to step up to even an average level of play on the defensive line. Some of the defensive linemen who played during Hendrickson's time in Cincinnati, though, have since made splash plays with Lawrence and the other additions.
Both Kris Jenkins Jr. and Myles Murphy have recorded 11 total pressures and 3.5 sacks combined so far this season. Those numbers are not eye-popping, but they are still an improvement over what we have seen from both players in years past.
Jenkins has shown more explosiveness and gotten to quarterbacks more this season with the depth improvement on the interior of the line.
Hendrickson should make explosive plays for the Ravens this season, but the Bengals' front office clearly made the right call four weeks into the season.
The Bengals and Ravens play in Week 7. Both teams should hopefully be healthy enough by then, in what should be an emotional game for Hendrickson and the Bengals.

title: Bengals Named Top Trade Fit For Pair of Veteran Defensive Backs Ahead of 2026 Deadline
full_text:
NFL contenders are always looking to improve , and Cincinnati could do that with a trade or two before the NFL's deadline on Nov. 10.
Pro Football Focus's Bradley Locker has two cornerbacks that are solid trade options for Cincinnati as the team works through injuries in that unit to start the season.
Buccaneers cornerback Zyon McCollum and Jet CB Brandon Stephens were his top picks for Cincinnati.
McCollum has played 240 snaps this season with a 56.6 Pro Football Focus grade.
It would be pretty shocking to see the Bengals add a player in the first year of a three-year, $48 million contract extension.
"McCollum enjoyed a tremendous start to the 2024 season, but since then, his production has certainly waned," Locker wrote . "Over the first four games of 2026, McCollum sports just a 58.3 PFF coverage grade, although his passer rating against (80.4) and forced incompletion rate (13.3%) are both in at least the 60th percentile.
"In the first year of a three-year, $48 million extension, McCollum is another defender the Buccaneers could look to shed. The Steelers could reunite McCollum with Jamel Dean after trading away Porter, while the Lions urgently need more talent in their secondary. The Bears and Bengals could also make particular sense given McCollum’s superior man coverage work (69.4 PFF coverage grade) and their higher rates of utilizing the look, although McCollum was actually better in zone in 2024 and 2025."
Stephens is in the second year of a three-year, $36 million extension and has been playing better than McCollum.
He is mostly an outside cornerback, though, whereas Cincinnati probably needs more help in the slot. Stephens has experience inside but not nearly as much as his outside time clocked.
"Stephens has become an effective cornerback since joining the Jets last offseason," Locker noted . "Since the start of 2025, his 70.2 overall PFF grade ranks 14th out of 40 qualified corners. Stephens has also tightened up his coverage this year, with his 74.4 PFF coverage mark the ninth-highest at the position.
"How much the 1-3 Jets will sell is unknown, but general manager Darren Mougey always seems open for business. Given that Stephens is a 2028 free agent and the team drafted D’Angelo Ponds in the second round, a trade may not be that implausible. Pittsburgh and Detroit could have interest given their needs, while Stephens’ 88.7 man coverage grade would be enticing to Chicago and Cincinnati."
Time will tell if either player wears stripes this year, but more and more contenders are pushing in some chips at the trade deadline in recent years.

title: How and Why the Bengals Can Crush the Dolphins in Miami
full_text:
After dropping two games that could've landed in their favor at the end, the Cincinnati Bengals catch a break in week five.
The winless Miami Dolphins are heading down the path that many projected for them coming into the season and the Bengals need a rebound.
Normally, I'd happily point out the flaws in the opponent’s game and maybe land a joke or two along the way, but this week feels like punching down and we've seen Bengals teams play down to their opponents before.
Yes, the 0-4 Miami Dolphins are currently a bad football team, but they have many rookies on their roster that I personally liked during draft season. Those guys can play, but they are rookies; you'll have your chances to welcome them to the NFL.
Instead, let's start at quarterback where Malik Willis needs to show enough to keep this franchise from drafting a QB with that likely top five selection in 2027.
Through four games, Willis hasn't exactly made a strong case for himself.
He owns the 30th ranked PFF grade for all quarterbacks and Willis is completing just 56% of his passes.
He's under a ton of pressure so far also. Willis is holding the ball and inviting some of it himself, but this offensive line ranks 27th in Pass Block Efficiency (PFF) and 24th in ESPN’s Pass Block Win Rate. Whoever is at fault, being under pressure on 46.9% of dropbacks is an unsustainable number.
Even when he's not under duress, Willis is completing the lowest rate of passes in the entire league. So he can't just blame the bodies around his feet.
To be fair, Willis is throwing the football down field at a very high rate. His 10.5 Average Depth of Target (ADoT) leads the league.
He's going to push that ball down field and if it isn't open, Willis can and will run. His 10.9% scramble rate is the highest of all QBs in the league. He's even had some nice runs called back due to penalties around him.
Largely, this passing offense just isn't working so far. Their 36% Success Rate is the worst in the league as the skill players are struggling to get open. Their average separation at the catch point is 27th in the league at 3.1 yards per attempt.
It's not just the passing game, the Dolphins run game lost budding star Devon Achane for the season and now they're 31st in Running Success Rate (32.3%).
Miami likes to run with a lead blocker in fullback DJ Herman, but the results have been poor so far as he owns the lowest run blocking grade from PFF of all backs in the NFL.
They're currently using 21-personnel at the third highest rate in the league, but getting a -0.12 EPA result with a 26% success rate when running the ball. Like the Bengals, Miami may have to re-think their fullback usage (Erick All) as they're averaging just 0.74 yards BEFORE contact when they run the football. That ranks 27th in the league.
Run or pass, this Dolphins offense owns the worst success rate in the entire NFL.
How about the defense? It's also trash.
Overall, Miami’s defense ranks 29th in EPA per play but almost all of that ranking is being sunk by their 31st ranked passing defense. Their 9th best run defense is formidable but has an area to attack.
Let's start with a familiar issue. The Dolphins are struggling to cover opposing tight ends. Good thing National Tight End day isn't for another couple of weeks. We don't need this getting any uglier.
So far this season, Miami has allowed 29 catches for 333 yards and two touchdowns to tight ends. Only the Bengals and Detroit Lions have allowed more yardage to the position.
And that's 29 catches on just 31 targets. So opposing QBs are completing 94% of their throws to tight ends. For the Dolphins, that's an average of 7 catches for 83 yards allowed per game to opposing tight ends.
Last week, Vikings’ TJ Hockenson went off. He saw 13 targets and caught 13 balls for 119 yards.
Hello, Mike Gesicki! Gesicki is currently on pace for 47 catches, 659 yards and 13 TDs this season.
And also maybe this is the week for Erick All Jr. to catch a pass?
Leaving themselves open and vulnerable in the middle of the field makes sense as Miami is second in the league for Cover-6 rate (22%). Using this coverage, Miami has already allowed 285 yards on 20 completions.
You can exploit Cover-6 over the intermediate part of the field and that's where the Bengals have had a ton of success this season with a second-best 122 passing yards per game and a fifth-best +0.73 EPA per pass.
Miami owns the 25th ranked EPA per play defense against Shotgun offenses. They are allowing a 50% success rate and completion percentage of 81.1 to opposing offenses. You may have guessed it, but that's the worst in the league.
On 3rd Downs, it doesn't get better for them as they're the 30th ranked defenses in EPA per play. Opposing offenses see their success rates rise to 54.5% and their completion percentage go up to 83.9% –  both bottom of the league numbers.
So what's the issue if the Miami run defense is good but their pass defense stinks?
Unlike the Bengals, who defend the run well with less defenders in the box, the Dolphins do it with extra defenders in the box at the sixth-highest rate in the NFL.
This leaves the Miami defense exposed on the back half and they cannot generate enough pressure to hide the coverage on the back end. Miami is 27th in pressure rate and 28th in sack rate on defense.
Defensive tackle Zach Sieler used to be a very good player in Miami but at 31-years old now, maybe he's starting to see a decline in play.
His 30.0 PFF run defense grades ranks him 74th amongst all interior defensive linemen through four weeks.
Teams are attacking him right now in the run game and without Kenneth Grant as their anchor inside, Miami has an exploitable weakness in run defense.
Amongst the rookies starting for the Dolphins is 5th rounder Michael Taaffe at safety. His PFF grade of 35.4 ranks him 69th of 70 starting safeties and his 25% missed tackle rate makes Jordan Battle look like prime John Lynch.
The Bengals are heavily favored in this game and it's easy to see why, but after two straight losses and nightmares of Mike White still lingering in my mind, I'm just going to sit and watch and try not to approach this game with too much excitement.
Go take care of business, Bengals.

title: Browns vs Jets Week 5 Injury Report: Cleveland Without 2 Key Pieces Defensively
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have started the 2026 NFL regular season 3-1.
And while it seems like nothing can slow this team down, the recent injury report casts such a sentiment in doubt.
On Sunday, Oct. 11, the Browns are slated to take on the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J., for what should be a fairly competitive contest. The Browns and Jets aren't the league's most prominent teams, especially with how young and raw they are, but they both have boom-or-bust potential.
Ahead of the showdown, the inactive list was announced , with Browns defensive linemen Mike Hall Jr. and Mason Graham stealing the spotlight.
#Browns inactives v #Jets : QB Taylen Green (3QB) WR Tylan Wallace TE Carsen Ryan DT Mike Hall Jr. C Parker Brailsford G Teven Jenkins DT Mason Graham
Both have been standouts on the line for the Browns this season, combining for 19 tackles, seven for a loss, six quarterback hits and five sacks. While many of those numbers skew in Graham's direction, his injury in last week's Thursday Night Football showdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers pushed Hall Jr. into a bigger role.
Fortunately, he did not disappoint.
But now, with both players banged up and out for Sunday's game, the Browns will have to dive into its depth with hopes of replacing such productivity.
On the line, the Browns are expected to deploy Maliek Collins, Adin Huntington, Chris Williams and Sam Kamara. Both Williams and Kamara were activated from the practice squad earlier in the week to fill Graham and Hall's voids.
"It's next man up. I think that's really what it is," head coach Todd Monken said earlier in the week when asked about the Browns' injuries. "That's why you have practice squad players and the ability to elevate them. It's going to take everybody on the roster, and that's why you're consistently trying to develop those players.
"So, when they get their number called, the expectation, the position, you're trying not to let that drop."
Outside of the defensive line, the Browns also are working through injuries on the offensive side of the ball.
Linemen Teven Jenkins and Parker Brailsford are both inactive, with Brailsford's reason being unknown. Jenkins, on the other hand, has missed much of the 2026 season due to a back injury. In his place, the Browns have turned to rookie Austin Barber, who has been one of the league's top first-year players.
Wideout Tylan Wallace is going to miss yet another game due to a knee injury, while tight end Carson Ryan stays off the gridiron due to a calf injury. Ryan was limited all week.
Both are not necessarily impacting the offense's capabilities much, but still, being without a few depth pieces will put more strain on the starters.
Quarterback Taylen Green rounds out the Browns' inactive report, as he will serve as the team's emergency QB.

title: Browns Trading for This Wideout Would Be an Unmitigated Disaster on Multiple Levels
full_text:
Over the course of the offseason, one common trade target mentioned in connection with the Cleveland Browns was current Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.
Fast forward to Week 5 of the NFL regular season, and that move makes zero sense for the Browns, for a number of reasons.
Here are the three main ones:
There’s no question Thomas is a talented wideout. His rookie season back in 2024 was actually pretty phenomenal, catching 87 balls for 1,282 yards and 10 scores, leading to a Pro Bowl nod and a fourth place in voting for the AP Offensive Rookie of the Year Award.
Then, something changed. Thomas just stopped being a critical part of the Jags offense, once Liam Coen was promoted from offensive coordinator to head coach last year. His numbers took a nosedive, with only 48 catches for 707 yards and two scores all last year, while former sixth rounder Parker Washington’s role grew exponentially.
This year, Thomas hasn’t found a way to reinsert himself back into prominence, and is currently not only standing behind Washington and Jakobi Meyers in receptions, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, but also has one less score than rookie sixth rounder Josh Cameron, who the team seems to really like. And that’s not even mentioning that tight end Brenton Strange has been more involved in the offense, as well.
Thomas’ snap count is also falling at an alarming rate. After starting out at an 80 percent of offensive plays as a rookie and 78 percent in his sophomore season, it currently stands at just 47 percent.
Drops have become a big issue for Thomas, and that’s something the Browns really don’t need, especially after Jerry Jeudy’s deeply disappointing 2025 season.
Second-rounder Denzel Boston is arguably the leading candidate for Offensive Rookie of the Year honors so far this season, and first-rounder KC Concepcion has been almost as good. Together, they’ve reenergized the Browns’ receiving to the point where Jeudy has become somewhat of an afterthought, sparking debate on whether he should actually be traded, too.
Cleveland looks set up nicely for the future with the trio of Boston, Concepcion and tight end Harold Fannin Jr., along with the expected development of Isaiah Bond. For a team that just a mere six months ago had no clue on who could be their WR1, they came away from the 2026 NFL Draft with two solid candidates.
Another prominent name from the 2024 NFL Draft, Marvin Harrison Jr., is currently being shopped around in Arizona according to multiple reports . Even if Harrison’s numbers as a pro are even more underwhelming than Thomas, there might be some logic in trading for him, as his ceiling is still considered much higher.
While Harrison has been generally viewed as a wideout capable of doing it all with a pretty complete array of tools, Thomas is now more or less considered just a deep threat receiver, who’s best trait is creating some space underneath for others to exploit.
However, don’t expect Cleveland to make some noise in the Harrison front, no matter how attractive it might be. For the right price, swapping Harrison for Jeudy on the Browns’ current roster looks enticing . In real life, Cleveland might be better served not getting into a bidding war with other clubs for Harrison’s services, no matter how much untapped potential there still might be lying around in there, somewhere.
The Browns have a good thing going on with their current core of young talent from the last two drafts, and giving up too much capital for Harrison or Thomas when you’re expected to need it down the road for a new quarterback doesn’t make sense.
If the Browns are going to be players before the trade deadline, they should be targeting the offensive backfield , defensive line or defensive backfield . Wide receiver is just not a position of need for this team anymore.
