title: Davis Webb Just Showed Broncos Fans What He's Really Made Of
full_text:
Just as Sean Payton foretold, Davis Webb is taking this week's professional setback quite well.
Payton said Webb would be "fantastic" at the podium on Friday, and he was. The Denver Broncos' 31-year-old offensive coordinator admitted his disappointment in Payton taking back the play-calling duties , while reaffirming his ongoing commitment to the team and his support for his head coach in no uncertain terms.
“I think anytime that happens in any aspect of your life, job-wise, it is a little bit [disappointing]," Webb said on Friday. "But in the same breath, that’s the NFL. You get going. I’ve been a backup QB, been up and down before, and that’s kind of how it goes.”
Webb is only four years into his NFL coaching career. In January of 2023, Payton literally pulled him from the quarterback ranks and onto his new Broncos coaching staff within weeks of Webb starting in the New York Giants' season finale.
Webb knew what he was getting into when he accepted the offensive coordinator job and play-calling duties. He sized up the opportunity from every angle and came to terms with the possible outcomes.
“I have taught myself early to think about the best- and worst-case scenarios," Webb said. "If you’re OK with both, then take that job on… Nothing I can really do about it now except be the best teammate and offensive coordinator I can be. That’s what I’m trying to do.”
Again, Webb is no stranger to professional setbacks. That was essentially the life he led as an NFL quarterback: more of a journeyman backup than an established starter.
Payton himself went through a similar situation in 2002 with the Giants when Jim Fassel took the play-calling duties from him. A few short years later, Payton was the head coach of the New Orleans Saints.
"I think for him, there was a lot of empathy with our conversation because that did happen to him," Webb said of Payton. "We talked about that for a long time, but in the same breath, it’s a different situation as well."
Payton relinquished the play-calling duties for a reason; he genuinely values Webb's unique talent, and when he made the decision early this past offseason, he believed it would be in the Broncos' best interest. Alas, as the offense has suffered from brutally slow starts and a lack of rhythm, Payton's fingers inched ever closer to taking the play sheet back before he finally took action.
"I don’t think anyone wanted to go through this right now, but he’s excited to get the chance to call plays," Webb said of Payton. "I know he’s itching, and we’ll see how it goes.”
As the coordinator, Webb is still in charge of running the offensive meetings and "helping out the quarterback room." Again, he's disappointed to be relieved of the play-calling duties, but his disappointment is more about the Broncos' failure to launch offensively early this season.
Amid the upheaval of Payton's big decision, the Broncos have been game-planning for the winless Los Angeles Chargers . The imperative of going into SoFi Stadium and winning this game takes precedence over all the drama, for lack of a better term.
“I think it’s more just how we started off offensively [with his disappointment], but I’m excited to see how our team responds this week," Webb said. "We’ll try to get a team win against a divisional opponent. It was a long week in some ways, but in other ways, it’s back to work.”
So much goes into the art of calling plays in the NFL. It's not just picking and choosing the right plays to put in the game plan or to roll out in the first 15 to 20 plays of a contest.
It's about sequencing, adjusting, and all the while, calling plays that maximize personnel strengths while attacking opponents' weaknesses. And so much more.
Gut feeling has much to do with it in-game, especially once a play-caller has burned through the scripted first 15. That's where talent and experience intersect.
Along the way, Webb feels confident that he was able to speed up the Broncos' play-calling process to cut out the delay-of-game penalties and give quarterback Bo Nix more time to survey the defense pre-snap. It may have been hard to deduce from watching on TV or from the stands, but Webb believes the Broncos' offensive operation was increasingly cleaner by the week.
Would that it was also increasingly productive. Webb learned a lot about himself — valuable information that will serve him down the road as his coaching career progresses.
"I think I’ve learned a ton when it comes to sequencing, to play selection, to how we game-plan, to really how the players respond to it," Webb said. "So I think everyone’s got a hand in that, and we’ll see what happens.”
The young OC ultimately takes responsibility for the unit's failure to launch on his watch, but even Payton and veterans like Bo Nix and Courtland Sutton said that everyone's fingerprints are on it. Nix has not looked like his usual self this season, which is obviously a big reason why Payton is taking back the reins.
"We were so close in a lot of areas. I think in the San Francisco game, you can see a few plays that were very, very close to being successful," Webb said. "Same with the week before against the Rams. We just didn’t put a full game together consistently enough. I take responsibility for that. I’m the play-caller, but we all have a hand in this, and hopefully we can get going this weekend a little bit faster.”
As we learned from Payton on Thursday, everyone at Broncos HQ who touches the offense feels like they let Webb down, including Nix . There's no question this was a collective failure.
Webb and Nix have a close relationship, and that won't change with Payton taking back the play-calling and being the voice in the quarterback's ear on game day. Webb confirmed that it was Payton who broke the news to Nix.
“I think Sean might have done that to be honest with you," Webb said of Nix. "But again, like I told him, I’m going to be like I always have been in my mind and his mind: I’m all in for him. I’m all in for everybody in this offensive unit, and I’m going to do everything I can to make sure everybody’s in a position to be successful.”
Webb is a selfless leader. His comportment and remarks at the podium on Friday were impressive. He's as mature and insightful as he is talented and knowledgeable, and Payton still sees a head-coaching job in his protégé's future, though this week's setback may have reset the timeline — but you never know.
The Broncos will rally behind Payton as the play-caller moving forward, which is how it's been for 54 of the 58 games (counting playoffs) he's served as the head coach. Webb will do everything in his power to help the offense get over the hump and break through the obstacle that has been holding it back.
But if Webb is right, it won't take much longer for Nix and the offense to finally break out.
“Extremely, extremely close," Webb said of the offense. "I think there are a few things in the pass game that were close last week, a few things in the run game that were close last week. You can see the second halves of the Jaguars game, the Rams game. I mean, I just mentioned three good teams right there. "
As I wrote in my Winners and Losers article analyzing Payton's play-calling decision, Nix stands to gain a lot from working under his head coach's experienced hand. Payton shepherded Drew Brees into the Pro Football Hall of Fame and helped Nix become the winningest and most statistically prolific quarterback in NFL history through his first two years.
It really is a bummer for Webb, and for Payton and Nix, to be honest. They all wanted this arrangement to work out.
But the NFL is a production-based business, and while the Broncos have managed to beat two of the league's four best teams thus far, the offense simply hasn't looked like a Super Bowl contender.
"Kansas City was tough on everybody… So I think getting off to this start, being at 2-2 is not what we wanted, but it’s where we’re at," Webb said. "I think that a lot of teams in the NFL will be OK with…

title: 5 Broncos Sleepers the Chargers May Not See Coming
full_text:
The Denver Broncos face a unique challenge this week, going into SoFi Stadium to face a Los Angeles Chargers team that is yet to win a game this weason.
The Broncos cannot overlook this AFC West rival.
The Chargers have struggled and are badly banged up , but the Broncos are dealing with some major injuries of their own. Fortunately, the Broncos have several sleepers who could be flying under the radar entering this Week 5 matchup.
We've examined the two crucial matchups of this game, revealed our keys to victory , and rendered our predictions and picks for Broncos-Chargers . Now, let's talk about the Broncos' sleepers the Chargers may not see coming.
With Pat Bryant on injured reserve, Denver will need to find a way to replace some of his explosiveness. Franklin is only a year removed from being this team's No. 2 receiver, having fallen to fifth on the depth chart.
But he is far more explosive than people realize.
The Broncos have used Franklin sparingly and in a specific role, and while Bo Nix hasn't always connected with him this season, the tandem will get the chance to make up for lost time this week. Given how beat-up the Chargers' secondary is, Franklin could have a big day if Sean Payton, as the new play-caller , can scheme the right matchups.
Adkins has been the Broncos' best tight end thus far and has looked like a quality starter, despite being third on the depth chart.
Given how he has played and the Chargers' injuries at the second and third levels of their defense, Adkins could be a key piece in the Broncos' offense when it comes to moving the ball down the field. and even getting lost by coverage in the redzone.
Opponents tend to lose Adkins in coverage in the red zone. Don't be surprised if Payton schemes something up, and Nix looks Adkins's way for six on Sunday.
Barron has been vaulted into the starting lineup with Patrick Surtain II out, which puts a lot of pressure on the second-year corner. The Chargers' wide receiver room isn't great, but it can give opposing corners fits.
Given Barron's limited size and experience, the Chargers could look to pick on him, but that's exactly why he's a sleeper impact player this week. If he struggles, the first-round bust label he's trying to shed may stick a while longer, but a good game could bury it as a trope.
The Broncos will also be without Riley Moss, which will force them to play their No. 4 and No. 5 corners in the starting lineup.
Abrams-Draine has played well when called upon, but his size and lack of physicality could be a detriment against the Chargers' receiving corps.
Both reserve corners will be under a lot of pressure to fill in for one of the best boundary duos in the NFL. But Abrams-Draine has had success against L.A. before, notching the first interception of his career against Justin Herbert as a rookie in 2024.
Mims's fumble on a punt return ended up being the turning point for the San Francisco 49ers last week, and it's surely been eating at him. He'll be looking to bounce back, and he could make a massive impact in the return game.
The Broncos could also look to Mims to generate explosive plays on offense and to help fill the Bryant void. Explosives have been sorely lacking thus far, but with Payton back at the controls, he knows exactly how to dial things up for Mims.
Mims's effort and route-running issues haven't completely gone away in Year 4, so he will need to improve there, but his returner ability against the Chargers' struggling coverage unit opens the door for game-changing plays.

title: Broncos Add Veteran DB—Here's What It Could Mean
full_text:
Entering Week 5's divisional road matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers , the Denver Broncos bit the bullet on Pat Bryant, placing him on injured reserve .
That'll put Bryant out of commission until Week 9, at the soonest. To fill his spot on the 53-man roster, the Broncos promoted veteran wideout Lil'Jordan Humphrey from the practice squad.
The Broncos will be without Bryant for the foreseeable future. As for Week 5, the Broncos will also be missing their two starting cornerbacks — Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss — both of whom were ruled out of action on Friday. Fortunately, the Chargers are also banged up, but the onus will fall on the young Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine to step in and keep the ship afloat alongside veteran nickel corner Ja'Quan McMillian.
With a practice squad spot open, the Broncos worked out eight players on Friday, all of whom were either defensive backs or linebackers. Ultimately, Denver liked what it saw from veteran cornerback Ugo Amadi, signing him to the practice squad.
Amadi joins rookie Brent Austin and the first-year Sean Fresch Jr. as cornerbacks on the practice squad. But Amadi is significantly more experienced than either.
A 2019 fourth-round pick by the Seattle Seahawks, Amadi is now on his seventh NFL team. The 5-foot-9, 201-pound Oregon product has appeared in 85 NFL games, with 17 career starts.
Amadi spent the previous three years with the New Orleans Saints. In 2024, he started five games for the Saints, totaling 65 tackles (52 solo), six tackles for a loss, two sacks, and seven pass break-ups. As you can see, physicality is not an issue for the 29-year-old defensive back.
As a nickel corner, Amadi is one inch shorter than McMillian, but he's nearly 20 pounds heavier. With how much big nickel the Broncos have had to play this season to counter the heavy tight end packages opponents have thrown at them, McMillian's snap share has gone down a little bit.
As the league moves toward this multiple-tight-end trend, it's forcing teams to prioritize bigger, more physical nickel players. Amadi doesn't have great height, but he's physical and can hang in the box.
McMillian is a feisty, physical nickel himself, but he's been neutralized somewhat by opponents' game plans this season. Amadi isn't coming in to replace anyone, but if the Broncos opt to elevate him in the near future — probably not this week — he could be rotated in to help against bigger tight end packages, if needed.
The Broncos have increasingly given No. 3 safety Devon Key more snaps to help counteract the way teams are attacking them with tight ends. It's mostly a run game thing. McMillian is physical enough to hang with most tight ends in coverage, even though he can be outsized height-wise, but when the Broncos are caught in their nickel package and opponents run the ball, that's where having a bit more size in the defensive backfield can be helpful.
Time will tell how Amadi ultimately fits in and whether the Broncos ever elevate him, but it's good to add some experience to cornerback room, especially with Surtain and Moss being injured currently.
In terms of the workouts the Broncos held on Friday, it's worth knowing the names because this team will often circle back to sign players it has worked out, sometimes several weeks in the past.
It's interesting that Denver is keeping an eye on the linebackers available out there currently. With Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad as the starters, the Broncos also have Karene Reid and Jordan Turner on the 53-man roster, with rookie Red Murdock on the practice squad.
The Amadi addition is about more than just depth. The Broncos are facing the reality that Surtain and Moss could miss more than just Week 5, and after Barron, Abrams-Draine, and McMillian, none of their cornerbacks had real NFL experience.
Amadi brings 208 tackles, 22 pass break-ups, a pair of sacks, an interception, two forced fumbles, and a fumble recovery to the table. He's played for vetearn defensive coordinators like Steve Spagnuolo and Ken Norton Jr., as well as younger coaches like Jonathon Gannon and Brandon Staley, among others.
It's good to have some experienced depth at cornerback as the Broncos roll with the injury punches.

title: Broncos Week 5 Injury Report: Final Decisions on Surtain, Moss
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's road tilt against the winless Los Angeles Chargers.
As expected, the Broncos will be without starting cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss, who went down with ankle and rib injuries, respectively, during last week's loss to San Francisco. They were ruled out after missing practice on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday.
Although it wasn't included on the report, Denver also placed wide receiver Pat Bryant — who suffered an ankle injury of his own in Week 4 — on short-term injured reserve. Bryant will be sidelined for at least the next four games before being eligible to return.
Listed as full practice participants on Friday and given no game designation were defensive end Zach Allen, running back Tyler Badie (foot), defensive lineman DJ Jones, outside linebacker Dondrea Tillman (hamstring), and tight end Adam Trautman (shoulder).
Friday's #DENvsLAC injury report: 📰 » https://t.co/pkZT6PjAXz pic.twitter.com/4DMyEOpFpt
On the Chargers' side , it's ... much messier. Los Angeles officially ruled out seven players; among them, starting tackle Joe Alt, safety Derwin James, wide receiver Quentin Johnston, and cornerback Donte Jackson. They also listed backup quarterback Trey Lance as doubtful, and five other players (including top WR Ladd McConkey) as questionable.
Beyond this week, the Broncos are expected to get Surtain and Moss back within a few games, as their issues are not considered long-term . RB Jonah Coleman is also eligible to come off IR in Week 7.
Such as they did against the Niners, with Surtain and Moss out of the lineup, the Broncos will turn to reserve cornerbacks Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine to contain a depleted Chargers receiving corps.
Both players held their own in Week 4 and the coaching staff is confident that will persist moving forward.
“They’re savvy players, they both have good football instincts and IQ," head coach Sean Payton said of Barron and Abrams-Draine on Wednesday. "One of the reasons you draft at that position is because it’s hard to find in free agency. So both were ready when they needed to be and that’s encouraging.”
With Bryant absent, Denver could lean more heavily on little-used WRs Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin while attempting to get veteran Courtland Sutton going following a slow start to the year. It, too, is possible — if not probable — that quarterback Bo Nix sprinkles a few additional targets to running back RJ Harvey, who's currently the club's leading pass-catcher.
“Some of it’s the soft zone coverage that went underneath," Payton explained Wednesday. "There are probably five different reasons to the team we played. Certainly, you come away from that game as a coach and you’re like, ‘All right, we have to find more touches for Courtland for “X” amount of receivers, even when they’re in these deeper zones.' We’ll be able to do that, but we start with a mirror right away with ourselves. So we know he can be a factor for… He doesn’t have to be just outside, he can be inside depending on the route.”

title: Broncos Can’t Afford to Lose These 2 Matchups vs. Chargers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos and Los Angeles Chargers have been a divisional matchup that Sean Payton and Bo Nix have yet to figure out.
Even with Denver at 2-2, the 0-4 Chargers still have plenty of ways to pull off an upset. The Broncos have plenty of flaws that could have seen them also limp out to an 0-4 start. Thankfully, that's not the case, but it's another example of why L.A. can't be overlooked.
Not only do the Broncos have their fair share of issues, but recent injuries could exacerbate things, and the Chargers have the talent to attack those issues. Denver has to be ready to handle this week's key matchups , especially with the injuries they're dealing with.
Let's break down those matchups to watch in Broncos-Chargers.
McGlinchey wasn't terrible against the San Francisco 49ers, but he wasn't good either. In the first three weeks of the season, he played a bench-worthy brand of football, and if Denver had a viable backup right tackle, maybe it would have happened.
Through four weeks, McGlinchey has been one of the worst tackles in the NFL.
On the flip side, the Chargers have received good showings from their two top edge rushers. Mack and Tuipulotu have combined for 28 pressures, 14 each, with three sacks for the former and one for the latter.
The Chargers also like to flip them around depending on the down and distance, which keeps tackles from getting into a rhythm against the same player.
Left tackle Garett Bolles has been good so far, and there is no reason to expect a drop-off, but Denver needs McGlinchey to step up opposite the All-Pro. If McGlinchey can't hold his own against these two pass rushers, it could make for a long day for Bo Nix and the Broncos' offense, given the quarterback's early struggles with pressure.
With Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss ruled out and likely Riley Moss, too, the Broncos are left with Ja'Quan McMillian, Jahdae Barron, and Kris Abrams-Draine at cornerback. McMillian and Barron lack the ideal size and length, while Abrams-Draine is lighter than you want and not overly physical.
This creates serious concerns against the Chargers' receiving corps, which will look to exploit those limitations.
Quentin Johnston has been ruled out for Week 5 (chest), but he, Tre Harris, and Ladd McConkey (questionable) have 53 combined targets through four games, with 32 catches, 500 yards, and a touchdown. McConkey is small but has taken McMillian to task before; Harris is long and fast, which could create issues for the Broncos' corners.
What could exacerbate the problem is tight end Oronde Gadsden II, given how the Chargers employ him. He can create issues for the Broncos' linebackers and force safety help, which would take away from their ability to shade help toward the boundary corners.
Vance Joseph has his work cut out for him in figuring out how to handle the Chargers' receivers with the cornerbacks at his disposal.

title: Cynthia Miller, Wife of Detroit Lions Play-by-Play Voice Dan Miller, Dies
full_text:
Detroit Lions play-by-play voice Dan Miller has lost his beloved wife, Cynthia Miller, who passed away on October 10, 2026.
According to Griffin Funeral Home , "Cynthia ‘Cindy‘ Louise Miller, born on October 3, 1963, in Falls Church, Virginia, to Roy and the late Valerie (Weber) Biondi, was a woman whose magnetic personality, infectious humor, and welcoming spirit made everyone feel like family. Cindy was the beloved wife of Dan Miller, with whom she shared 33 wonderful years of marriage. She was the devoted and fiercely loving mother of Sammi (Brendan) Burdette, Rikki Miller, Tony (Viona Veseli) Miller, and Robbie Miller, and the adoring grandmother of Daphne and Cecilia. She was the dear sister of Gino (Lisa) Biondi, Steve (Marissa) Biondi, and Julie (Chris) Griffin."
Cindy was passionate about the Detroit Lions. She attended each and every home game, sitting in the fifth row right behind the Lions bench.
"Some of her best memories were attending the two home playoff games with her daughters in 2024. Her family knows that she will be there in spirit when the Lions win it all."
A memorial gathering for Cindy will be held on Friday, October 16, from 3 p.m. until 6 p.m. at the L.J. Griffin Funeral Home, Northrop-Sassaman Chapel, on 19091 Northville Road (at 7 Mile Road). A funeral service celebrating Cindy's life will follow at 6 p.m.
Dan Miller has become one of the staples of broadcasting in the region, as he is one of the most popular play-by-play voices covering the National Football League.
He shared in a Social House News feature the passion his wife Cynthia and his children had for the Lions.
"My wife loves football (Cindy attends all Lions games), my kids love football," Dan expressed. "When I'd have a Saturday off in the fall, my daughters would come downstairs and ask, 'What college football games are on today? We'd sit around the TV, they'd have their computers on their lap and we'd watch games. When the noon games were about to end, they'd ask, 'What games are on at 3:30?' It was heaven for me."
Cynthia Miller battled Leptomeningeal disease.
The entire staff of Detroit Sports Podcast and Lions On SI sends its deepest condolences to the Miller family during this time of grief and sorrow.

title: Detroit Lions Week 5 Updated Depth Chart Against Cardinals
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are set to battle the Arizona Cardinals with a chance to get back over .500 ahead of their bye week.
Detroit is coming off a tough loss to the Carolina Panthers and has started the season 0-2 on the road. Against the 1-3 Cardinals, Dan Campbell's team has a chance to get some mojo with a road win. However, it won't be easy as the Cardinals have weapons that could be difficult for Detroit's defense to contain.
Here's an updated look at the Lions' depth chart for their matchup against the Cardinals.
Starter: Jared Goff. Backup: Joshua Dobbs.
Goff has been effective throughout the season and remains without a turnover. He ranks third in passing yards, behind Dak Prescott who played on Thursday and Bryce Young. He's also one of only three starters who have played in all four games to have not thrown an interception.
Starter: Jahmyr Gibbs. Backup: Sione Vaki. Reserve: Jacob Saylors. Inactive: Isiah Pacheco (Injured reserve).
Gibbs continues to be the dominant force in the backfield, with Vaki taking a majority of the reps when he's out of the game. Vaki has shown some improvements in pass-protection since the start of the year, and as a result has been continuing to earn more trust and opportunities.
Starters: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa. Backups: Tom Kennedy, Tay Martin. Inactive: Kendrick Law (Injured reserve).
Williams and TeSlaa are both coming up big for Detroit's passing game after slow starts, with TeSlaa coming off a career-best performance last week. The team continues to heavily lean on St. Brown, who ranks fourth in the league in receptions through four weeks.
Starter: Sam LaPorta. Backup: Brock Wright. Reserve: Jackson Meeks, Tyler Conklin
Even with the questions surrounding his future, LaPorta is off to a solid start early in the year. The Iowa product had a touchdown grab against the Panthers, and is up to 22 catches through four games. Wright is coming off a rough showing in which he received a fine and was penalized twice.
Starters: Penei Sewell (left), Blake Miller (right). Backup: Larry Borom Inactive: Gio Manu (Non-football injury)
The Lions have been able to maintain some stability up front with Sewell and Miller staying healthy to play their third consecutive game together. Miller continues to improve in his rookie season, while Sewell has maintained his reputation as one of the best tackles in the league.
Starters: Christian Mahogany (left), Tate Ratledge (right). Backup: Miles Frazier. Inactive: Ben Bartch (Out, Foot).
Bartch is sidelined for the third straight game with a foot injury, meaning Mahogany stays unchallenged at the left guard position as the competition simply hasn't materialized the way Campbell hoped it would. Ratledge has been solid up to this point on the right side.
Starter: Juice Scruggs. Backup: Seth McLaughlin. Reserve: Tate Ratledge. Inactive: Cade Mays (Out, Wrist).
A big development occurred earlier in the week with Cade Mays returning to practice. He won't play this week, but could return after the bye which would make things interesting for Scruggs. The veteran has been reliable at center, and could slide into a starting role at left guard or at the least provide valuable depth.
Starters: Tyleik Williams (Questionable, Foot), Alim McNeill. Backups: Skyler Gill-Howard, Levi Onwuzurike. Reserve: Mekhi Wingo.
Williams is listed as questionable but told reporters that he plans to play against the Cardinals. McNeill is coming off another big game in which he logged his third sack of the season, putting him well ahead of a career-high pace.
Starters: Aidan Hutchinson, D.J. Wonnum. Backups: Tyler Lacy, Derrick Moore. Reserves: Eric O'Neill, Ahmed Hassanein. Inactive: Payton Turner (Injured reserve).
Starters: Jack Campbell, Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez. Backups: Trevor Nowaske, Jimmy Rolder, Amen Ogbongbemiga Reserve: Devin White. Inactive: Damone Clark (Injured reserve).
The Lions have gone away from White after he played a starter role the first two weeks of the season, which also correlates with Rolder's increased role. Ultimately, the Lions appear to be comfortable utilizing the young option along with the athletic Nowaske in certain situations.
Starters: D.J. Reed, Roger McCreary. Backups: Ennis Rakestraw Jr., Keith Abney. Reserves: Khalil Dorsey. Inactive: Rock Ya-Sin (Out, Hamstring).
Ya-Sin has been ruled out, which seems to solidify either McCreary or Rakestraw getting another start. Of the two, Rakestraw has seemingly been better by a small margin and has positive moments including a pass breakup last week. Abney could see an increased role as well, be it at cornerback or safety.
The Lions won't have to worry about Marvin Harrison Jr ., who will be inactive with the anticipation of being traded early next week.
Starters: Chuck Clark, Christian Izien. Backups: Jalen Mills (Practice squad elevation), Bishop Fitzgerald. Inactive: Brian Branch (Out, Achilles), Kerby Joseph (PUP), Avonte Maddox (Injured reserve), Thomas Harper (Injured reserve).
Clark and Izien are both veteran presences who have had good moments, with Izien looking like one of Detroit's best offseason additions. Mills was called up from the practice squad for the third and final time, which means the team will have to decide whether or not to add him to the active roster moving forward.
Branch returned to practice and could be in line to return after the bye, which could make Mills and even potentially Fitzgerald expendable. Fitzgerald has yet to be active in a game since being poached off of the Steelers' practice squad.
Kicker: Jake Bates. Punter: Jack Fox. Long-snapper: Hogan Hatten. Kick returners: Tom Kennedy, Jacob Saylors. Punt returner: Tom Kennedy.
The Lions have yet to make any changes to their special teams units through four weeks. Bates remains perfect on field goal and extra point attempts.

title: Expert Predictions For Detroit Lions Matchup With Arizona Cardinals
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will try to get back on track when they square off with the Arizona Cardinals Sunday afternoon.
The Lions are coming off a disappointing 32-26 defeat at the hands of the Carolina Panthers. Meanwhile, the Cardinals will try to bounce back from a 36-24 loss to Jim Harbaugh and the N.Y. Giants.
Here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 5 matchup with Arizona.
The Lions are walking into a unique situation on Sunday. The Cardinals have made it public that they are holding Marvin Harrison Jr. out with the expectation that he will be traded early next week. As a result, it could be something of an ominous environment.
Arizona still has weapons surrounding Jacoby Brissett that could cause Detroit's league-worst defense some fits. Detroit's secondary personnel will be key to this game, as containing the Cardinals' passing attack is the biggest measure of success for them this week.
With a pair of divisional opponents waiting for them after the bye next week, Detroit needs this game to generate some momentum heading into a tough stretch. Getting to 3-2 won't be easy, but Jared Goff will be steady and turnover-free in leading his team to a gutsy win.
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions will battle with a Arizona Cardinals team which has fallen on tough times.
In fact, since beating Jim Harbaugh and the L.A. Chargers in Week 1, they have lost three straight games. And they have allowed at least 31 points in each of their three losses, including a season-high 36 points in Week 4 against John Harbaugh and the N.Y. Giants.
While the Cardinals do possess a pair of solid offensive weapons in tight end Trey McBride and wide receiver Michael Wilson, they will also enter their Week 5 tilt with Detroit with multiple injuries on the offensive line. Left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. is out for the season, and right guard Isaiah Adams was placed on injured reserve this week.
Subsequently, the Cardinals’ offensive line has been weakened, and Detroit's pass-rush should be able to take advantage.
I believe the Lions will generate just enough pressure against Arizona QB Jacoby Brissett to force a turnover or two and secure the Week 5 win.
The Lions caught a break with the news that wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. will be inactive this week.
Kelvin Sheppard’s defense has been under a heavy amount of scrutiny for their play in the first quarter of the season.
It feels like the Cardinals are the perfect elixir for a defense struggling with confidence and inconsistency executing Sheppard’s play calls.
Stopping Trey McBride and Michael Wilson will be vital, as Detroit has the worst passing defense in the NFL.
The offense and defense should respond well to being challenged by Dan Campbell. Jared Goff leads the offense on more touchdown drives and the defense forces a couple of turnovers to keep the game out of reach for Arizona.
The Lions look to bounce back following an unsettling loss to Carolina last week. The Cardinals get the advantage of being hosts and not traveling across the country, but will also be without starting receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. as he is expected to be traded during the weekend.
Arizona is down multiple linemen and corners, and have not had the best start to the season. The Lions offense has shown some struggles finishing in the red zone, but has still been able to put up high-scoring numbers.
This one likely ends up being a shootout of some fashion, although I see it more being a similar situation to Buffalo vs. Detroit, with the Cardinals playing catch-up with the Lions during the contest.
The Lions right the ship and get their first semi-comfortable victory of the year on a 200-yards from scrimmage day by Jahmyr Gibbs and a two-touchdown day for Amon-Ra St. Brown.

title: 3 Detroit Lions Players Who Need to Bounce Back Against Cardinals
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are looking for a strong bounceback performance following their disappointing Week 4 loss to the Carolina Panthers.
As they prepare for their Week 5 contest with the Arizona Cardinals, several players will need to deliver much better efforts in order for Dan Campbell's squad to get back on track.
Here are three Lions players who need to bounce back – and in a big way – against Arizona.
Rakestraw has logged snaps in just two games so far this season, and has produced a mixed bag of results.
He appeared in his first game of the 2026 campaign in Week 3, and had a decent day in coverage. He earned a 65.8 Pro Football Focus grade for his efforts against the pass (on 22 coverage snaps).
The Missouri product followed that up with a dismal performance in Week 4 against the Panthers. He, just like the rest of the Lions’ defensive backs, appeared a step slow all night long against Carolina's wideouts, especially Tetairoa McMillan. McMillan erupted for a 192-yard, two-touchdown outing against Rakestraw and Detroit defenders.
It was a forgettable performance from Rakestraw, who recorded a 51.0 PFF overall grade for his performance in the primetime affair.
The third-year corner will need to produce a much better effort in the Lions’ Week 5 matchup with Arizona.
Miller experienced his fair share of growing pains against the Panthers.
In what was the third game of his pro career, he was responsible for multiple false start penalties, and struggled mightily in his attempt to contain Carolina EDGE defender Jaelan Phillips. In fact, the Clemson product permitted five pressures in the Week 4 contest.
It was a disappointing showing from the rookie right tackle, and by far the worst outing of his young career. Additionally, for his efforts, he earned a 49.5 overall grade from Pro Football Focus , the lowest overall mark of any Lions offensive performer last week.
Detroit direly needs a stronger performance from the first-year pro in Week 5 and beyond.
The veteran EDGE recorded a subpar outing last week against Carolina.
He had a decent day rushing the passer, generating two pressures and securing a sack. Yet, he struggled to do much of anything else, and proved to be extremely ineffective against the run. And for his performance as a run defender, he earned a season-low mark of 28.0 from PFF. Plus, he earned a lowly overall mark of 48.8 for his efforts in the Week 4 tilt.
The Lions will be looking for a bounceback performance from Wonnum against Jacoby Brissett & Co.

title: Detroit Lions Safety Elevated From Practice Squad For Third Time
full_text:
The Detroit Lions announced one Week 5 NFL roster move before facing an Arizona Cardinals team that is reportedly set to trade wideout Marvin Harrison Jr.
According to the team, veteran safety Jalen Mills has been elevated from the practice squad to the active roster. It his third elevation of the season, meaning the Lions will have to sign him to the active roster if they wish to utilize him again.
Safety Brian Branch returned to practice this week and could be in line to return to the active roster after the team's Week 6 bye week. Mills has provided depth amidst injuries to Branch, Kerby Joseph and Avonte Maddox, but may not be as useful once Branch returns.
Earlier this week, head coach Dan Campbell explained he simply wanted defensive players in the right position and to focus this week on punching the football out and avoiding self-inflicted wounds.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard reiterated that the small details are important, and when the roster fails in practice, the coaching staff is going to remain diligent in coaching up the fine details.
“It sounds easy, like a lot of this stuff," said Sheppard. "That's what I'm saying. I'm being very cautious of, 'Oh, you do this, you do that,’ because it's lip service. It sounds easy. But those are the things that bite you, the things that you assume are easy, the things that you think that you may not necessarily take but take for granted. They're going to do that. Yeah, absolutely. The player even. I'm going to, 'Oh coach, I know I'm supposed to be there.' 'Then why on Sunday aren't we there? So no, we're going to do it one more time. We're going to do it one more time because it matters. It matters that your six-inch alignment is off.
"It matters because of the angle that you're creating, the disadvantage you're putting your brother next to you at because of that six-inch separation.' And then when you start to see that guys, it's a trickle effect. I told them guys, 'You are in the storm, storm coming, the dam breaks when it's a crack here and here's a second crack.' Well now, alright this guy's leaving his hold of this play to now go try to help over here because he doesn’t know if that guy's going to, and now that's when the whole damn thing collapsed down, man."
The coaching staff was encouraged last week, when the defense was able to earn stops in critical moments against the Panthers.
"That's what we can't have right now. Just do your job one more time," said Sheppard. "Even if that's boring, even if that's backside of a play. When you think, 'I'm not at the point of attacking, oh, let me go.' And there's the ball rolling back on you. Just do your job one more time at a championship level. Everybody wants these big, huge results. But really guys, the big, huge results come in the process and in the little things, man.
"We’ve gotten the stops in critical moments. In multiple games when we needed to get the offense the ball, we went out and did it. But what about the other 40 minutes guys? Why wait until the end of the game? 'Oh, we got to step.' We’ve got to bow up getting off the bus and make sure we're doing our end as a one-third of this football team to make sure we're coming away with the results that we want on game day.”

title: Two Detroit Lions Fined Against Panthers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions had two players receive a fine for actions in their Week 4 loss to the Carolina Panthers, according to the NFL's accountability log for Week 4 games released Saturday.
Detroit saw tight end Brock Wright fined for $17,911 for unnecessary roughness after a leg whip in Sunday's game. He was flagged for unnecessary roughness in the third quarter of Sunday's game after a low-block he attempted was called for tripping.
Additionally, linebacker Jack Campbell was fined $15,930 after a hip-drop tackle. Campbell was not penalized for the tackle during the game, which came in the first quarter.
Through four games, Wright has totaled four catches for 20 yards. He was hit with two penalties in Sunday's game, with the other being a false start in the first quarter.
Campbell, meanwhile, has had a difficult start to the season after signing a four-year contract extension this past offseason. Coming off an All-Pro season, Campbell has had difficulties performing at a high level.
Detroit lost, 32-26, to the Panthers to fall to 2-2 on the season. They struggled mightily against the Panthers' passing attack, with wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan logging 192 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 14 receptions.
The Lions have had at least one player fined in every week of the season up to this point. In Week 1, running back Jahmyr Gibbs received a fine but ultimately had it rescinded. Six different Lions players were fined in Week 2, with several being for celebrations.
In Week 3, wide receiver Jameson Williams received a fine for unnecessary roughness regarding the use of his helmet. In total, the team had been fined more than any other in the NFL with a total amount of $177,404.
It has been a busy season in the NFL through four weeks with regards to fines, as ESPN reported that the 963 accepted penalties in that span are the most since play-by-play data began being tracked in 1978.
Detroit returns to action Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals for their second-straight road game. Kick-off is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. at State Farm Stadium, and it will be Detroit's final game before their bye week.

title: How To Watch, Listen, Stream Detroit Lions Against Arizona Cardinals
full_text:
The last time the Detroit Lions faced the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium back in 2024, they departed with a 20-13 victory.
Detroit is seeking their third victory of the 2026 season, when Dan Campbell's squad again travels to Arizona to face a 1-3 Cardinals squad.
Drew Petzing served as the Cardinals offensive coordinator for three seasons prior to joining the Lions this offseason.
“I mean a huge part of my career. As you said, first time play-calling, worked with (Packers current defensive coordinator) Jonathan Gannon, (defensive coordinator) Nick Rallis, a number of guys on that staff for a number of years in my career," said Petzing. "So, had a chance to take the next step with them and grow as a coach and grow as a person and grow as a leader.
"So, invaluable what those guys taught me, what I learned from them, what hopefully I was able to impart on them. But it was, it was an amazing three years.”
After a disastrous start to the season for the defense, many now believe the offense must carry the team.
“I don't think you ever think about it that way as a coach," Petzing explained. "We’ve got three phases. We're going to go out and try to win a game by any means necessary. So, anytime we don't do that, I'm going to feel I want to challenge myself. I want to challenge the players. I think they want to be challenged. I think they challenge each other. I think that's just the nature of the beast in this League, no matter what the situation.”
Dan Campbell challenged the offense during his weeky radio interview, stating the unit should want to score 35 points a game, if they want to be considered great.
"I would hope that's our mindset on offense no matter. Yeah. And like I say it jokingly, but our goal is to score one more than them. And I don't care if that's 32-31. I don't care if it's 3-2," Petzing said. "As long as we have one more than them when that game ends, I'm good. We're always going to have stuff to clean up or be better at or be more efficient at, butat the end of the day, that's all we're focused on.”

title: Five Defensive Backs Who Make Sense For Detroit Lions to Add
full_text:
The Detroit Lions could be active buyers at the 2026 trade deadline.
This year, the deadline falls on Tuesday, Nov. 10, which is one month from Saturday. Detroit currently sits at 2-2, with a big game looming at the Arizona Cardinals before heading into their bye week.
Detroit has aspirations of competing for a division title, which would be their third in four years, but there have been clear defensive issues that appear to be a roadblock in a tough division.
With two consecutive division games looming after the bye week, there could be urgency for the team to make a move to add a defensive back to a secondary that has ranked last in the league sooner rather than later.
Here are five defensive backs who could be worthwhile trade targets ahead of the deadline for Detroit.
The Buccaneers notched their first win of the season on Thursday after starting 0-4. Though the NFC South's struggles could offer a pathway back into contention for them, their tough start to the year could force them into selling.
McCollum is an intriguing option who has had success throughout his career. Financially, it may be a challenging add for Detroit as he's in the first year of a three-year extension signed last year that came with $35 million in guaranteed money.
McCollum is a steady veteran who would help bring stability, and his ability to operate in man-coverage is something the Lions would value highly . However, one concerning element regarding McCollum is his missed tackle rate, which currently sits at a less-than-ideal 25 percent through five games.
The Giants took a big hit early in the season when quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury. To coach John Harbaugh's credit, though, the team has managed to stay afloat behind the efforts of veteran quarterback Jameis Winston and company.
However, if things go south, the Giants could look to deal Newsome who signed a one-year contract with them this offseason. He's been playing well, with an interception and five passes defensed up to this point. Newsome also has ideal size at 6-foot-2 for Detroit's coverage scheme.
Ringo is an intriguing young option who has struggled to find his footing in the NFL. Once thought to be one of the top cornerbacks in his draft class, Ringo fell into the third day of the 2023 NFL draft and his career has not materialized the way it was expected.
Through the first four weeks of the season, Ringo has played exclusively on special teams. If the Lions were interested, it likely wouldn't be a hefty cost as he's in the final year of his rookie deal and without a defined defensive role.
Another 2023 draft pick, Brents has a versatile background having played some safety in college. He's a long, athletic option at 6-foot-3, and has experienced some success despite not playing more than nine games in a season up to this point in his career.
A big part of Brents' appeal is that he's a reliable tackler. His missed tackle rate according to Pro Football Focus currently sits at 12.5 percent. He's also in the final year of his rookie contract, so he would be another rental option.
Winfield is an intriguing but expensive option from Tampa Bay. A two-time Pro Bowl honoree and a one-time First Team All-Pro, he would bring plenty of pedigree. However, he also has two years remaining on a contract extension that made him the highest-paid safety shortly after the Lions signed Kerby Joseph to a massive extension.
Detroit is set to get some help back at the safety position, as Brian Branch could return after the bye week. If the Lions were to make a deal for Winfield, it would likely be because they got not good news on the Joseph front with the injury that has kept him out for the start of the season.
Winfield would bring another talented option to their secondary and immediately solve some of their issues, but is the biggest long-shot of this group.

title: Lions' Defense Faces One Less Cardinals Weapon: Will It Help?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will take on an Arizona Cardinals team Sunday that is set to make a big shake-up to their roster.
On Saturday, NFL reports surfaced that the Cardinals will make wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. inactive for Sunday's game as they finalize a trade involving him. It is uncertain what team will be acquiring Harrison and the terms of the trade.
"The one certainty is that Marvin Harrison's time in Arizona is done. Arizona feels comfortable enough to know it can and will trade Harrison, which is why he will be inactive Sunday. But no Harrison trade will be completed until after Sunday's games are played.
One team that Schefter reported as being in on the trade talks to acquire Harrison is the Houston Texans.
This is big news for the Lions , as their opponent will be down one of their biggest offensive weapons. Harrison was the Cardinals' fourth-overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, but his career has not materialized the way it was expected to.
Detroit's defense has been one of the worst in the league up to this point, ranking near the bottom of the league in many categories. These include 31.8 points per game (31st), 423.8 yards allowed per game (32nd) and 304 passing yards per game (32nd).
The one certainty is that Marvin Harrison’s time in Arizona is done. Arizona feels comfortable enough to know it can and will trade Harrison, which is why he will be inactive Sunday. But no Harrison trade will be completed until after Sunday’s games are played. https://t.co/qEGc9qtht0
Without Harrison, the Cardinals will be down a weapon and it could be beneficial for the Lions. However, Harrison's usage hasn't lived up to his billing throughout the start of the season and as a result a trade could be beneficial for both parties.
Through four games this season, Harrison has recorded a total of five receptions for 85 yards and one touchdown. In his career, the Ohio State product has notched 108 catches for 1,578 yards and 13 touchdowns.
Trade talks had been surrounding Harrison in recent weeks, as he was asked by local reporters about the speculation involving whether or not he would be dealt before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
"Truthfully, I pay it no mind. I'm only focused on Detroit, helping the Cardinals win football games at the moment." Harrison said, via ESPN . "So, whatever rumors you're talking about, I don't pay it no mind."
Arizona still has several options who could do damage against Detroit's struggling defense, including wide receiver Michael Wilson and tight end Trey McBride. Wilson leads the team with 258 receiving yards, while McBride leads the Cardinals with 33 receptions.
Ultimately, Harrison's struggles over the past two years have led to his role diminishing within new head coach Mike LaFleur's offensive scheme. This, in turn, made the former top pick available and expendable via trade.
Harrison's absence from Sunday's game will certainly have an impact despite his smaller role. For starters, the Lions' defense has struggled against big, physical receivers as evidenced by their inability to contain Tetairoa McMillan last week in their loss to Carolina.
The Ohio State product has a similar profile and may have been a tough assignment for the likes of D.J. Reed, Roger McCreary and Ennis Rakestraw.
Along with Wilson and McBride, other receiving threats at Arizona's disposal include receivers Kendrick Bourne and Jalen Brooks along with tight ends Elijah Higgins and Hunter Long.
The Cardinals also have Simi Fehoko, Devin Duvernay and Reggie Virgil on the roster at receiver, and could elevate rookie Harrison Wallace III from the practice squad to give them depth on short notice.

title: Five Players Lions Must Scout: Versatile Safety Fits Kerby Joseph Mold
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions head out to play the Arizona Cardinals following a disappointing loss to Carolina. The Lions look for a revenge game for offensive coordinator Drew Petzing, who was let go when the entire regime changed for the Cardinals.
The scouting department remains hard at work, with week six being the midpoint for most teams in college football during the season. Here are five players the Lions must have eyes on this Saturday.
Lopa was a reserve safety for Oregon last year, and he sought the portal with the Ducks bringing in Minnesota’s Koi Perich. The safety landed at Cal and has promptly put the college football world on notice.
At 6-foot-5, the defensive back towers over his peers. He is a former receiver that still plays like he’s catching passes, high pointing the ball. The California native has five picks on the year, including three against Syracuse.
The top concern on him is that Lopa is a one-year wonder who struggles to fill run lanes at points. However, his athleticism and range make him a top tier asset for the Lions. The Lions have found similar success before, as Kerby Joseph was called a one-year wonder in his draft class.
Lopa will be tasked with defending Ethan Grunkmeyer and Virginia Tech. Last week, Grunkmeyer passed for over 400 yards as James Franklin’s squad lost their first game of the season. The matchup kicks at 3:30 p.m. EST.
Hubbard had an excellent 2025, ranking as the top safety in the SEC against the run in terms of stops, along with four interceptions and three forced fumbles. He has elite instincts, which make him one of the best players on the field.
Hubbard ranked as a top ten safety on PFF in different categories over the last two seasons, but is struggling in rankings this year. Hubbard is a playmaker, but his missed tackle percentage is currently at 19 percent, which has him with a second round grade so far.
Hubbard will need to be at his best on Saturday, as Alabama faces Georgia at 7:30 p.m. EST in the game of the week.
Smith has been a force for the Gophers for the last three seasons, sticking the course and is looking to finish out his senior campaign strong. He has over 1,500 career snaps in college and bypassed the NFL Draft last season after 12.5 sacks.
Smith has three tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks this season as he faces more double teams. At 6-foot-6, 280 pounds, Smith is a cliché “big end” that can bump on the inside for Motown next season. He is an instant impact player with a very high floor and ceiling for a day two pick.
Minnesota will take on a stout Purdue team at 8 p.m. EST on Saturday.
An offensive player will make an appearance on the board this week. Justin Evans holds down the center of Nebraska’s offensive line, and he is off to a strong start in 2026. After being a top 10 center on PFF last season, and the highest among all returning Power Four conference players. He ranks No. 16 among all centers heading into game six of this year.
Evans is a former left guard converted to center, and that position flexibility could be perfect for Motown as the guard play has been one of the small complaints on the offense. The center has yet to allow a sack, hit, or quarterback hurry this season. Since switching to center, he is not credited with a sack allowed to date.
Evans will be put to the test on Saturday, with his Cornhuskers hosting defending National Champion Indiana at noon EST.
Clarke is the Group of Six representative this week. Clarke, a native of the United Kingdom, posted one of the top PFF scores last season for all tight ends, no. 2 overall and no. 4 in the Wins Above Average Stat.
Clarke is a block-first tight end, and that grade elevates his eyes with NFL Scouts. At 6-foot-6, 265 pounds, he has the frame needed. His receiving game needs improvement, with only seven catches for Temple through five games. However, the run block ability in tight ends has become a premium, as saw in this year’s NFL Draft with multiple second round selections underwhelming in their receiving stats.
Clarke, as he evaluates currently, would be an unorthodox pick for the Lions. This is due to their belief in Isaac TeSlaa’s run block ability freeing them up from utilizing as many 12- and 13-personnel situations. That said, considering their real interest in Michigan product Marlin Klein last season, Clarke is a player that could be on their radars.
The Owls take on UConn at 3:45 p.m. EST on Saturday.

title: Packers-Bears Inactives: Will Kevin Zeitler Play? And Will He Start?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Kevin Zeitler is active for the Green Bay Packers for Sunday’s rivalry showdown against the Chicago Bears.
Presumably, that means he will be in the starting lineup, though that will have to wait until the players come out for pregame warmups.
The Packers had to list only four inactives. All of them are linemen:
RG Jacob Monk will miss his second consecutive game with an injured quad. He returned to practice on Friday and was doubtful.
LG Aaron Banks will miss his third consecutive game with knee and toe injuries. He’s played only one-half of a game this season, 22 snaps against the Jets in Week 2. He also returned to practice on Friday and was doubtful.
G/C Donovan Jennings started the season as the next man up at left guard in place of Banks. Now, he’s a healthy scratch after the veteran additions of Kevin Zeitler and Laken Tomlinson.
DT Anthony Campbell will miss a third consecutive game with an ankle injury sustained at the Jets.
The bigger news is that Javon Hargrave, the veteran defensive tackle who is coming off a strong game against Tampa Bay, is active. He was added to the injury report on Friday with a toe injury and listed as questionable.
Rookie guard/center Jager Burton, who missed time this week following back spasms and was questionable is active, as well. He got the call over Jennings.
With Chris Brooks out, running back Pierre Strong is active. Strong was elevated from the practice squad three times last year but never played in a game.
“Man, I could just thank the Lord,” he said after practice on Friday . “Like you said, it was a while but God’s timing is better than everybody’s timing. I’m here now so got to continue to get better.”
Packers. Bears. A glorious Sunday at Lambeau Field for the 214th matchup. pic.twitter.com/MCaCmlAwb3
Out for Chicago are quarterback Caleb Williams and running back Kyle Monangai. Those are two of the team’s best players on offense.
Williams will miss a third consecutive game following a hamstring injury. He practiced on Friday and was listed as questionable but that was just gamesmanship from coach Ben Johnson.
Tyson Bagent will start for a second consecutive game. He threw one interception in a blowout win over the Jets last week but penalties nullified three others.
“I think you go into each week the exact same as far as; Wednesday, Thursday, Friday getting the plan down, being locked in, taking it extremely seriously,” Bagent said of the rivalry this week.
“But to say that this is just like any game just wouldn't be true. It's one of the greatest rivalries in all of sports. Easy for the fans to get up for, easy for us to get up for. It'll certainly be a different feel out there and that's why it's so important that we put in the amount of work that we need to this week, get acclimated in a smart way but also in a hurry so we can have our best foot forward going into this weekend.”
Even with a backup quarterback, they are 1.5-point favorites at FanDuel Sportsbook on Sunday .
The other inactives for Chicago.
Inactives for #CHIvsGB : pic.twitter.com/naxqaxFcTP
With Zeitler active, he presumably will play.
“We’ll see,” coach Matt LaFleur said before Friday’s practice. “He’s been practicing the last two days. He’ll be out there today. A lot of it is just how comfortable he is, and we’ll go from there.”
How would that be determined?
“There’s a lot of communication with the player and certainly how they’re performing out there, as well.”
So, what would Zeitler say as part of that conversion?
The veteran wouldn’t bite.
“I’m just going to keep going,” he said after Friday’s practice. “I’m going to let that be on the coaches. If they know what they see and everything and I know what I feel, we’ll keep attacking and when game day gets here, we’ll make the call.”
Either the Packers will line up with their fifth combination of guards or they’ll have stability for the first time this season. Here’s how it’s looked to start the season.
Week 1 vs. the Vikings: LG Donovan Jennings, RG Jacob Monk.
Week 2 vs. the Jets: LG Aaron Banks, RG Jacob Monk.
Week 3 vs. the Falcons: LG Jager Burton, RG Jacob Monk.
Week 4 vs. the Buccaneers: LG Laken Tomlinson, RG Travis Glover.

title: Packers-Bears Rivalry Is Real, It’s Spectacular And It’s Hit Pivotal Moment
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – It’s been a long, long time since the ancient rivalry between the Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears, which will be played for the 214th time on Sunday at Lambeau Field, had real fangs.
The feud’s been bitter, to be sure – recall Mark Lee’s ejection in 1985 and Charles Martin’s infamous cheap shot against Jim McMahon in 1986 – but it’s usually been a battle of bullies. The Packers and Bears have had long runs of dominance, with one team being really good and one team really bad.
Until last year, the Packers and Bears hadn’t qualified for the playoffs with winning records in the same season since 2010.
The Bears had a huge lead in the series until Brett Favre arrived on the scene. Then Aaron Rodgers stomped on the accelerator. Beginning on Nov. 22, 1992, when Favre led the Packers to a 17-3 win, through last year’s victory at Lambeau Field, which was clinched by Keisean Nixon’s interception, the Packers went 52-15.
Favre went 22-10 against Chicago. Rodgers went a remarkable 25-5, including the 2010 NFC Championship Game.
However, the Bears enter this game with wins in three of the last four meetings. Before that, they had three wins in the previous 29 matchups. Packers coach Matt LaFleur won his first 11 games against Chicago; the Bears have a chance to win three in a row for the first time in 20 years.
For a long time, this wasn’t a rivalry. It was bullying. When Rodgers screamed in the end zone that he owned the Bears, who was going to argue with him?
Bears coach Ben Johnson has replaced Rodgers as the dynamo in the rivalry. When he screamed “F*** the Packers” in the locker room after last year’s playoff win, who was going to tell him he was out of line? After years of being given wedgies and swirlies, the Bears were back.
Sunday’s game at Lambeau Field is as big as it gets. No, it’s not a playoff game, like last year. No, it’s not for the NFC North championship, as was the case in 2013.
Especially for the Packers.
Yeah, revenge is a factor after Green Bay’s all-time implosion in last year’s wild-card game. Yeah, the standings are a factor, with one win (or loss) feeling like it could be worth four or five for the Packers, who have looked like pretenders throughout their 2-2 start to the season.
“Definitely a lot of history,” quarterback Jordan Love said. “We always talk about the oldest rivalry in all of the NFL, so it goes back a long way, a lot of history in this game. So, yeah, it’s a good rivalry. Obviously, NFC North matchup and all these teams we take just a little more pride in these games. We gotta win these ones. They mean so much throughout the course of the season, so definitely going to be a good game.”
Love, who was abused by the Bears last season with nobody really having his back, will never be as outspoken as Rodgers. It’s just not in his nature.
So, leave it to his teammates to provide the real talk.
“Yeah, anytime it’s a division game, you kind of got to get your piss hot for the most part, understanding that these are going to have long-term effects on the standings for where we want to be at the end of the year,” safety Evan Williams said.
“And also carrying over from last year, understanding we also have a bad taste in our mouth from what happened. You can understand a 12-round fight. It’s going to be a fistfight for sure. We wouldn’t want anything else.”
It can’t be anything else. Because while playing a winning standard of football is important after four mistake-plagued games, and the standings are important given the difference between 3-2 and 2-3, where this game is of critical importance is for the rivalry. If the Bears shove the Packers into a locker again while playing without starting quarterback Caleb Williams, it could mark another run of one-sided dominance in the border battle.
Johnson, who started jabbing at LaFleur from the moment he was hired, is the driving force behind the rivalry’s renewed relevance.
“Some sh** don’t slide, and you don’t let that sh** go,” center Sean Rhyan said of Johnson’s locker room comments after last year’s playoff meltdown.
Jordan Morgan has been a part of the rivalry since he was drafted in 2024. This will be his first start at left tackle in the series.
“He’s dissing us. He’s dissing the Packers,” he said of Johnson. “A lot of people in here, I’m pretty sure, take that to heart. And we got a chance to prove to everybody on Sunday that we the best team.”
Added Williams: “That’s part of the rivalry. We understand how they feel about us, and we feel the same way, is what I’ll say. It’s a rivalry for a reason. We’re both competing to be the best in not only our conference, but the league. You get two powerhouses going up against each other, and on any given Sunday, you’re going to have those feelings spill out, for sure. I’m not going to quite say exactly what you want me to say, but it’s mutual. It’s mutual.”
Tight end Tucker Kraft missed all three games last season following his torn ACL.
“I talk with my pads, so I’ll just wait ‘til Sunday,” he said.
This will be Zaire Franklin’s first taste of the rivalry. He already knows this one’s different.
“It’s a lot of bad blood. A lot of bad blood,” he said. “A lot of genuine dislike, which is a little different than nowadays. Nowadays, most rivalries are just on social media and in the offseason, you’re hanging out. I don’t think nobody want to hang out with the Bears in the offseason. I think it’s a real issue between both sides.
“The beautiful part of it is we got nothing but space and opportunity to figure it out. Looking forward to it.”
New Packers guard Kevin Zeitler, who might make his starting debut, grew up in Wisconsin so knows what the rivalry is all about.
“Growing up in Wisconsin, obviously all about the Packers vs. Bears and everything, and it's cool to be a part of that now officially,” he said. “It's a very heated rivalry for obvious reasons and got to bring your A game.”
Safety Javon Bullard said this will be a primetime game, no matter the time.
“We’re playing the Bears. They don’t like us, we don’t like them,” he said.
“Sh**, once you respect the game in a way, you appreciate the rivalries,” he added. “Everybody got their game. I grew up watching these types of games. You’ve got Baltimore-Pittsburgh, you’ve got Seattle-San Fran, us and the Bears. So, it’s not just us. Everybody got their game and we treat every game like it’s the same game but, at the end of the day, they them boys from across the street so we’ve got to knock them off.”
For more than three decades, the Packers turned the so-called Monsters of the Midway into cute little stuffed animals. Led by Johnson, is there a new era in this agent feud? Or will the Packers restore order and punch the want-to-be bullies in the face?
The time for talk is done. It’s time to battle. It’s time to do the punching or be the punching bag.
“It’s something that doesn’t really have to be said,” Evan Williams said. “It’s just a type of energy that we understand how they feel about us, and we know how we feel about them. All of that is talk for me.
“For the most part it’s about who’s going to show up and who’s going to do their job violently. That’s really what it’s all about. As far as the energy goes, I feel like both sides understand how pivotal not only the game is, but understanding the type of energy the other side is going to bring. You’ve just got to put your hard hat on and be ready for a fight.”

title: Packers-Bears Predictions: Rivalry-Changing Opportunity Is on Silver Platter
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – It’s gameday.
And it’s not just any other gameday. And it’s especially not just any other gameday in this historic rivalry.
For more than three decades, the Green Bay Packers owned the Chicago Bears. Brett Favre turned the series around and Aaron Rodgers stepped on the gas.
Now, the rivalry is headed in the other direction. The Bears have won three of the last four games, including last year’s wild-card game, when the Packers collapsed like a house of cards. The Packers need to win this game for themselves, for the standings and for the rivalry.
Will they be up to the task? Will they beat the Bears or will they beat themselves?
Here are our weekly predictions.
An opportunity to flip the rivalry back in Green Bay’s direction has been handed to Matt LaFleur’s team on a silver platter.
The Packers have the advantage of playing at home. Chicago gave up 37 points in its only road game this season and allowed a league-worst 30.4 points per game on the road last season.
The Packers have the advantage at quarterback. With Bears star Caleb Williams out with a hamstring injury, the quarterback matchup will be Jordan Love vs. Tyson Bagent. Bagent threw one interception last week but had three more overturned by penalties. Those came against the Jets, who hadn’t intercepted a pass since the 2024 season.
The Packers also won’t have to deal with Bears running back Kyle Monangai, who ranks among the league leaders in rushing yards and yards after contact. His backup, D’Andre Swift fumbled twice last week.
The Packers have the advantage in motivation. A lot of times in matchups between good teams, the team that needs the win more tends to get the win. The Packers are 2-2 and the Bears are 3-1. In the rugged NFC North, it could be getting late in a hurry for Green Bay with another loss.
And, finally, there’s the revenge factor. Green Bay imploded in horrific fashion at Chicago in Week 16 and again in the playoffs. The Bears have bragging rights – and they’ve certainly been bragging. The Packers have heard all the talk from their rivals and are sick of it.
That’s a lot of advantages pointing Green Bay’s way.
Then there are the more tangible advantages.
The Packers lead the NFL with 344 penalty yards. The Bears have only 189.
The Packers have a league-high 10 fumbles. The Bears have only five.
The Packers have a league-high 13 dropped passes. The Bears have only six.
On offense, the Bears are first in total yards and rushing yards. They are sixth on third down. The Packers are 20th in total yards and 32nd in rushing yards. They are 32nd on third down.
Even with backup quarterbacks playing for most of the season, the Bears are eighth in scoring. With Jordan Love playing every snap, the Packers are 28th.
On the other side of the ball, the Bears are fourth in points allowed and Green Bay is 23rd.
Remember Green Bay’s putrid third-down offense? Chicago is second in third-down defense.
Simply put, when looking at performance instead of intangibles, the Bears have the advantage. And, in some cases, they have overwhelming advantages.
The intangibles matter. Motivation, revenge – all that stuff counts for something. However, what really matters is what’s between the white lines. And that’s where the Bears have the advantages.
And here’s the thing. The intangible factors only matter for so long. Will the Packers be driven by their desire to avenge last year’s playoff debacle once the second quarter or second half begins? No. Will the Bears’ powerful offensive line be a factor in the second quarter and second half? Yes.
At the end of the day, what matters is talent and execution. Chicago is the better team. Yes, it’s an apples-to-oranges comparison, but the Packers barely beat the Jets while the Bears mauled them into submission.
The Bears won’t have Williams or Monangai but the Packers won’t have Micah Parsons or Edgerrin Cooper. If you’re Bears coach Ben Johnson, who is the front-seven defender who could wreck the game? The fact is, there isn’t one capable of blowing up his offensive game plan.
Ultimately, this will be a close, hotly contested game. In my mind, unless Bagent or Swift provide a couple game-changing giveaways, the Bears will tack on a touchdown late to make the disparity seem larger than reality.
Prediction: Bears 31, Packers 21.
Until the Green Bay Packers prove they are a good team, they are a bad one.
Yes, it’s a backup quarterback, but I’m not sure how much that really matters when Chicago’s run game is as dominant as it has been this season.
So, the mistake-ridden Packers will lose their third consecutive game against Chicago for the first time since the 2005-06 seasons.
Prediction: Bears 34, Packers 17.
