title: 3 Matchups That Could Make or Break the Colts in Pittsburgh
full_text:
For whatever reason, the Indianapolis Colts just do not play well when they travel to Pittsburgh.
The Colts haven't won in Pittsburgh since 2008, including a 27-20 loss at Acrisure Stadium last season. But this time around, Indianapolis has a pretty clean path to finally ending that drought.
Both teams enter Sunday at 2-2, with Indianapolis sitting as a 2.5-point underdog ahead of the 1 p.m. ET kickoff on CBS.
This game should come down to creating pressure and forcing the other quarterback to make mistakes.
Here are three matchups that could decide it.
This one is pretty simple: Make Aaron Rodgers move.
Indianapolis enters Sunday with a 35% pass-rush win rate, which ranks dead last in the entire NFL, via ESPN. They are lined up against Pittsburgh's 10th-ranked pass-blocking unit, and generating pressure has to be the priority.
Rodgers has completed 88 of 153 passes for 999 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions, but he has already been sacked 13 times.
And at 42 years old, he isn't exactly escaping the pocket and turning broken plays into 20-yard gains anymore. Rodgers has just seven rushing attempts for 12 yards this season.
If the Colts can consistently win up front and force Rodgers to extend plays with his legs, Pittsburgh's offense becomes significantly more uncomfortable.
The formula isn't complicated. Get Rodgers off his spot, make him move and force him into poor decisions.
Gardner has himself a prove-it game after what happened in London.
He allowed four catches on five targets for 117 yards and a touchdown against Washington, including completions of 47 and 48 yards. Gardner later called his performance "unacceptable," and Sunday gives him an immediate opportunity to respond.
His job is usually pretty simple: Take away the opponent's No. 1 receiver.
This week, that means DK Metcalf.
Metcalf has 16 catches for 213 yards and a touchdown through four games, and he is coming off a 115-yard performance against Cleveland.
Indianapolis absolutely cannot allow Rodgers and Metcalf to get comfortable, especially on the deep ball. Gardner gave up a couple big shots in London, and I would imagine he is itching to pitch a shutout this time around.
This might be the most important matchup of the afternoon.
Jones has been far too careless with the football through four weeks, throwing four interceptions while also putting the ball on the ground multiple times.
Watt already has 4.5 sacks, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery and even a pick-six this season. If Jones gets careless with the football again Sunday, Watt is exactly the kind of player who will make him pay for it.
Jones has to know where No. 90 is at all times.
Get the ball out quickly or roll out to Watt's opposite side. Just don't give him the opportunity to completely wreck the game.
Indianapolis does not need to complicate its game plan this Sunday. Pressure Rodgers, don't let Metcalf beat you deep and keep Watt away from the football.
The formula is right in front of Indianapolis. Now it's a matter of executing it in a stadium that has given this franchise problems for nearly two decades.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Colts-Steelers Final Injury Report: Who’s In and Who’s Out for Week 5?
full_text:
The final injury reports are in ahead of the Colts and Steelers’ Week 5 clash on Sunday. Both teams go into the weekend with different questions they each need answered before kickoff as they each look to improve to 3-2 on the year.
Let’s take a look at both teams’ reports, determine who’s likely to play, who’s likely to sit out and what each injury means going into an important early-season bout between two conference foes.
Indianapolis Colts Final Injury Report
Indianapolis rules out four players, with no true surprises. That said, the Colts will be down two starters on defense. Defensive end Arden Key is expected to miss multiple games with his hamstring injury, with this week being the first. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies, who had an interception for the Colts last week, also suffered a rib injury that will keep him out of this Sunday’s contest.
Expect plenty of rookie action on Sunday as a result of these knocks. CJ Allen and Bryce Boettcher to both take snaps at linebacker while the edge duo of Caden Curry and George Gumbs Jr. should see some playing time as well. Gumbs is yet to suit up for an NFL game, so his professional debut could be on the horizon.
Ashton Dulin will miss his third game of the season already, so the Colts will have to make things work on special teams without their top gunner. Tight end Will Mallory just had his 21-day practice window opened on Wednesday after starting the season on injured reserve, but him being ruled out against Pittsburgh proves the Colts are using an abundance of caution with him moving forward.
Center Tanor Bortolini went from limited on Wednesday to a full participant Thursday, and now logged another full practice Friday. He enters the weekend without an injury designation and will start. That’s an underrated development, as Indy’s offensive line has been stellar through the first month and losing continuity would be a big hit to the unit’s current positive momentum.
There’s three Colts listed as questionable this week, with two wide receivers. Keenan Allen is questionable for the second week in a row, but completed a full practice on Friday, which is a significant step towards suiting up this weekend. Darius Slayton is a new addition to the injury report late in the week having been limited on Friday with a knee injury. Given the issue appears to have just popped up, Slayton may have to wait yet another week to make his Colts debut.
Cornerback Charvarius Ward is trending towards playing. After two straight days being limited, Ward was a full participant in the week’s final session. The questionable tag does add a little uncertainty, but a week of progress indicates Ward should be good to go.
Finally, it’s worth noting that defensive tackle DeForest Buckner did not practice Friday due to rest. No reason to worry about the veteran, though, as he doesn’t have any injury designation.
Overall, the final report for Indianapolis could’ve been much longer. Twelve different names showed up on the practice report this week, but only seven enter Week 5 with a designation. The possibility of being down three wide receivers is far from ideal, making that group the main on to monitor ahead of Sunday. On the practice squad, the Colts could turn to Nick Westbrook-Ikhine like they did last week should they need extra bodies.
For defensive practice squad elevations, Carl Lawson is likely to get the nod. WIthout Key, the Colts defensive end room lacks significant experience, so getting the 31-year-old into the mix could prove beneficial.
Pittsburgh Steelers Final Injury Report
Not as long a final list for the Steelers, but a top-heavy report. Worst case scenario, Pittsburgh could be without four starters. Michael Pittman Jr.’s foot injury got worse throughout the week, so he won’t be playing his former team. No Jamel Dean hurts the secondary, especially with Jalen Ramsey also carrying a questionable tag. If both can’t go, the Steelers will have to turn to their backup cornerbacks Daylen Everette and Sean Murphy-Bunting, who was signed off the Buccaneers’ practice squad earlier in the week.
Safety DeShon Elliott’s 21-day practice window was opened this week but he’s yet to be activated off injured reserve, so he’s unavailable to dress until that transaction occurs.
Rico Dowdle was limited all week and is officially questionable with the toe injury that’s kept him out of Pittsburgh’s last two contests as well.
Comparing the two reports, I’d give the Steelers a slight advantage, although Pittsburgh’s secondary concerns and Indy’s injuries at wide receiver make for an interesting storyline entering the game. Those matchups on the outside could have a major influence on the eventual outcome, so how effectively each team takes advantage of the other’s personnel concerns could be a deciding factor.

title: Colts Are Keeping Themselves Alive By Dominating In These Key Areas
full_text:
Despite having as many wins as they have losses, the Indianapolis Colts have gotten off to a rocky start to the 2026 regular season.
The 2-2 Colts struggled immensely on defense to start the year, specifically during the team's first two matchups against the Baltimore Ravens and Kansas City Chiefs, but have since found their footing with back-to-back wins over the Houston Texans and Washington Commanders.
However, both the Texans and Commanders sported subpar offensive units, with injuries giving the Colts advantages defensively, so there's reason to believe they'll go back to struggling against more respectable offenses.
Furthermore, the Colts' offense has largely kept them in each of their four games so far in 2026, though inconsistency sprouting from turnovers and a revolving door of pass-catching options has kept them from putting together an efficient operation.
With that said, the Colts have managed to, for the most part, stay competitive through one month of regular-season play thanks to their top-tier execution in a few areas of the game that are typically overlooked.
Without further ado, let's break down the three areas in question where the Colts are raising their overall floor.
The Indianapolis Colts have struggled to replicate their efficient output from a season ago through four weeks of the 2026 regular season, but when they've gotten into the red zone, it's almost a guarantee that they're scoring.
According to Sumer Sports via Locked On Colts' Zach Hicks, the Colts' offense ranks in the following red zone categories entering Week 5:
3rd in total EPA (Expected Points Added) 4th in EPA/play 5th in overall success rate 5th in EPA/pass 4th in pass success rate 3rd in EPA/rush
According to Team Rankings, the Colts rank 6th in the NFL in red zone touchdown rate. Indianapolis is scoring a touchdown on 75% of its red zone trips.
Head coach Shane Steichen's Colts offense doesn't have an issue with scoring in the red zone; they have a problem getting into red zone territory altogether.
They are tied for the 17th-most red zone scoring attempts (3.0 per game) with several teams, which shows that they have untapped potential offensively.
If starting quarterback Daniel Jones can limit his turnovers, and if pass protection gets sorted out, the Colts' offense can begin to unlock its potential.
Fourth-year special teams coordinator Brian Mason has only improved his unit with each year in Indianapolis.
So far in 2026, the Colts' special teams unit looks like one of the best in the entire NFL - and that's without having longtime special teams ace Ashton Dulin available for half of their games.
Mason made the impossible decision of choosing between Spencer Shrader and Blake Grupe to become the team's starting kicker before the regular season arrived, and his choice has aged flawlessly.
Spencer Shrader was named the Colts' starting kicker ahead of the season after dominating the team's preseason slate, and he's gotten off to a tremendous start in 2026.
Shrader missed his first kick of the new year, an extra point attempt in the team's season opener, but has been perfect since going 11-for-11 on field goal attempts.
The Colts' kicker has nailed each of his four 50+ yard attempts so far this season, including a 53-yard game-winner against the Houston Texans in Week 3, and the special teams unit as a whole (kickoff, punt, etc.) has been just as effective.
Indianapolis's rookie class has been a strong injection of talent to the special teams unit, with running back Seth McGowan flashing as a kick returner, and defenders Caden Curry and Bryce Boettcher showing up on kickoffs.
The Indianapolis Colts still have some things to clean up if they want to be treated as legitimate playoff contenders, but their special teams operation is not one of them.
The Indianapolis Colts have been the most disciplined team in the NFL through one month of regular-season play.
According to Tru Media analytics via Rotowire's Ian Hartitz, the Colts have been flagged for the fewest penalties on both sides of the ball through four weeks.
Colts have been flagged for the fewest penalties on offense *and* defense this season pic.twitter.com/1FyN2lIPmo
There's been plenty to critique so far this season, but playing disciplined football has not been one of them.
If anything, the Colts' disciplined play has been one of the main reasons they're sitting with a 2-2 record entering Week 5.
Football is a game of inches and margins, and the Colts' success in these three areas has allowed them to stay afloat as they iron out their deficiencies on both sides of the ball.

title: 3 Burning Questions Facing the Colts Heading Into Pittsburgh
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are back to .500 after winning two straight, but there are still some major questions surrounding this team heading into Pittsburgh.
The defense has taken a noticeable step forward. The offense has not, and Daniel Jones suddenly looks nothing like the quarterback Indianapolis saw last season.
Here are three questions the Colts need to answer against the Steelers.
Just to put it blatantly, Jones has not been good enough through the first month of the season.
He has completed 63.6% of his passes for 754 yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions, while also losing three fumbles. He has now thrown an interception in all four games.
That is a massive change from the quarterback Indianapolis watched last season, when Jones threw 19 touchdowns to eight interceptions, added five scores on the ground and finished with a 100.2 passer rating before tearing his Achilles.
The Colts gave Jones a two-year, $88 million deal this offseason that can climb toward $100 million with incentives because they believed that version of him was real.
Maybe we are expecting too much from a quarterback who returned roughly nine months after tearing his Achilles. Or maybe Jones' 2025 performance was simply an outlier?
Kirk Cousins struggled with inconsistency after returning from the same injury, so there is at least some recent precedent for a quarterback needing time to completely look like himself again.
Either way, Indianapolis needs Jones to start taking care of the football. If this becomes Giants DJ again, the Colts are in trouble.
Indianapolis allowed 41 points against Baltimore and 33 against Kansas City.
Since then? Seventeen against Houston and 13 against Washington.
That is progress, but I am not completely sold yet.
Houston is still searching for its first win of the season, and Washington was eventually forced to turn to seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis after Marcus Mariota left the game with a knee injury.
The defense looks much better, but I still want to see what happens when Indianapolis desperately needs a stop against an offense capable of putting real pressure on them.
Another storyline to watch is CJ Allen.
The Colts' first selection in April's draft has played just 11 defensive snaps through four games and did not see the field defensively in London. At some point, Lou Anarumo has to start easing the No. 53 overall pick into the rotation.
The Colts desperately need somebody who can stretch the field.
Jones averaged 8.1 yards per attempt last season. That number has fallen to 5.7 this year, and Alec Pierce's absence has completely changed the complexion of this passing attack.
That is where Slayton could come in.
The veteran has averaged roughly 15 yards per reception throughout his career and already has extensive history with Jones, catching 200 passes for 2,912 yards and 12 touchdowns with him in New York.
Slayton has yet to play a regular-season snap for Indianapolis, but said this week that he feels ready to go against Pittsburgh.
There is no guarantee he becomes the missing piece immediately, but the Colts need somebody who can threaten defenses vertically and give Jones a reliable veteran target in big moments.
Two straight wins have put Indianapolis back on track, but until these questions are answered, it is hard to know just how good this Colts team really is.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: 4 Colts Rookies Who Could See More Playing Time Against Steelers
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts ' front office focused on injecting youth, speed, and experience via the draft into their roster for the 2026 season, and throughout four regular-season games so far, it looks like they've achieved that goal.
However, the Colts' eight rookies in question have hardly gotten an opportunity to show their worth . They've shown up when they've been called upon, but their number has only been called in spurts.
As a result of injuries to key starters, specifically on the defensive side of the ball, numerous Colts rookies have been granted a massive opportunity ahead of Indianapolis's Week 5 road matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
The Colts have historically struggled against the Steelers, and they haven't won in Pittsburgh since Peyton Manning was still leading the charge (2008), so this will be a tough environment for the rookies, but they'll take anything they can get as budding NFL contributors.
With that being said, let's break down the Colts' rookie defenders in question who are primed for an increased workload in Week 5.
The Indianapolis Colts infamously missed out on the Trey Hendrickson sweepstakes earlier this offseason, and this caused them to pivot their construction of their new-look pass rush by adding low-risk veterans and rookies as a result.
Veterans Arden Key and Micheal Clemons were brought in to replace the longtime rotational trio of Kwity Paye, Samson Ebukam, and Tyquan Lewis, but they're both out for the foreseeable future with injuries.
The Colts finished their defensive line room by drafting rookies George Gumbs Jr. and Caden Curry in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, but only the latter has seen any playing time through four weeks, and even then, Curry has mainly been a special teams contributor.
With Key and Clemons' injuries causing them to miss time, it'll be second-year defensive end Jaylahn Tuimoloau filling the void in the starting unit.
However, Curry and Gumbs Jr. both serve as the man up.
Veteran Carl Lawson was signed to the Colts' practice squad earlier this week, reuniting him with defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo from their days together in Cincinnati.
Lawson may very well see a gameday elevation to the active roster, given that Anarumo tends to favor familiarity and proven experience, but don't count out the rookie duo in question from getting some more run.
Defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo has been rolling with veterans Akeem Davis-Gaither and Jaylon Carlies as his starting linebacker tandem through four weeks, but injuries to both players have opened the door for rookies CJ Allen and Bryce Boettcher.
Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) did not practice on Tuesday but was a full participant on Wednesday; therefore, it's likely we still see him suit up on Sunday, but his place in the defense remains to be seen.
Davis-Gaither has served as the defense's green dot since Week 2, but now could be a worthwhile opportunity to have CJ Allen take over the MIKE linebacker role that Anarumo, Steichen, and Ballard all envisioned he'd become, and slide Davis-Gaither over to WILL linebacker.
Jaylon Carlies (ribs) has missed both practices ahead of the Colts' Week 5 matchup against the Steelers, putting him at risk of missing the game altogether.
If Davis-Gaither plays and Carlies is out, Anarumo may look to start Bryce Boettcher alongside Davis-Gaither, as the spot Carlies plays - WILL linebacker - is the role that Boettcher was envisioned to play.
However, there's still a chance that Anarumo and Co. look to ramp up Allen's workload by starting him at the WILL linebacker spot.
We'll have to see what Friday's practice brings in terms of gameday availability, but it's trending toward at least one rookie linebacker getting some serious first-team run for the first time this season.

title: Colts-Steelers Thursday Injury Report: Colts Get Promising News as Steelers Lose Major Piece
full_text:
The injury reports for the Indianapolis Colts and Pittsburgh Steelers are starting to take shape.
Both Indianapolis and Pittsburgh released their initial injury reports on Wednesday , giving us a look at which players are in jeopardy of missing out on the Week 5 clash. But Thursday provided some more clarity as to who’s going to be available and who will be watching from the sidelines.
Let’s take a look at both teams’ reports with one more practice to go before Sunday’s game.
Indianapolis Colts Injury Report (As of 10/8)
Positive news for center Tanor Bortolini and linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither. Bortolini practiced, albeit in a limited fashion, while wearing knee and elbow braces. Interestingly, the Colts only list the ankle as an issue, so definitely something worth monitoring. Getting Davis-Gaither back to full participation is huge, too, as Indy can’t afford another change at the green dot. Tight end Will Mallory had his second full practice in a row as well. Indy may elect to use caution with him coming off a thumb injury, but Mallory is certainly trending in the right direction and could play this weekend.
#Colts starting C Tanor Bortolini, who did not practice yesterday due to a right ankle injury, *is* practicing today. He has a brace on his right ankle as well as a brace on his left arm/elbow. pic.twitter.com/qg5TkM71nc
Only defensive tackle Grover Stewart is new to the injury report on his rest day, but Charvarius Ward is now listed with a groin issue after getting Wednesday off to rest. Another situation worth monitoring. No practice for Arden Key, as he’ll miss significant time with his hamstring injury . Jonathan Taylor was back to a regular workload after a rest day to start the week.
It could be another week with slim pickings at wide receiver for Indianapolis. Keenan Allen, a limited participant in back-to-back days, has not made any progress as he works back from a groin injury. Ashton Dulin remains week-to-week with his hamstring injury. Having not practiced at all Wednesday or Thursday, he’s trending towards another week on the sidelines. That could open the door for Darius Slayton to make his Colts debut. Slayton signed with the Colts on Sept. 22 but hasn’t dressed in the two games he’s been available for, so a chance to make a strong first impression for the 29-year-old.
Linebacker Jaylon Carlies is the third Colt with back-to-back days as a non-participant, putting his chances to play up in the air. Bryce Boettcher is the backup WILL linebacker if Carlies doesn’t suit up, but the Colts would be remiss if they didn’t give their top draft choice in CJ Allen a chance to make an impact. Allen, despite being drafted 53rd overall, has found snaps hard to come by thus far , logging just 11 across the first four games.
Overall, there’s definitely some positive news on the injury front for the Colts. Getting Mallory back to full health is a plus, and if Davis-Gaither and Bortolini are fit enough to play, both would go a long way towards maintaining continuity and chemistry on their respective sides of the ball. Ward and Carlies are the key ones to watch, as either one of them being unavailable changes the equation defensively. But there's plenty of reasons for optimism otherwise.
Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report (As of 10/8)
The major news for Pittsburgh is that wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. not only is trending in the wrong direction (was a limited participant on Wednesday), but he’s expected to miss several weeks after raggravating the foot injury that’s held him out of practice this week. So a hit to the top of their wide receiver depth chart. From a Colts perspective, they will have to wait to play against Pittman for the first time since trading him to the Steelers in March.
Steelers HC Mike McCarthy said WR Michael Pittman re-injured his foot and now is expected to miss multiple weeks. pic.twitter.com/4YEtQaKuCP
Cornerback Jalen Ramsey improved from not participating Wednesday to practicing in a limited capacity. Good news for the Steelers secondary, which also opened safety DeShon Elliott’s practice window as he’s been on injured reserve with a knee injury. However, Jamel Dean has missed two straight practices, suggesting he’s a longshot to play on Sunday.
No progress for Rico Dowdle, whose two straight days as a limited participant make him a coin toss for Sunday. Dowdle has missed the last two weeks and is yet to log a full practice, so he’s likely to miss his third consecutive game.
Cam Heyward was back to full participation after a rest day. The 37-year-old veteran remains one of Pittsburgh’s most valuable pieces.
Looking at how the week has gone thus far, Pittsburgh would’ve hoped to be in a better position by now. But instead, they’re down at least one offense skill player for several weeks, likely without their backup running back and are banged up in the secondary. Friday will be crucial for the team to figure out who they’ll be playing without as they look to maintain a home winning streak against Indianapolis that stretches back to 2008.

title: Colts Quarter-Season Report Card: Surprises, Disappointments Through Four Games
full_text:
Just like that, a quarter of the NFL season has come and gone.
It’s been an eventful first four weeks in Indianapolis. The Indianapolis Colts started out with back-to-back losses, but rebounded and now sit at 2-2, good for second place in the AFC South.
Some players have come out of nowhere to emerge as surprise contributors, while others haven’t lived up to their potential. Here’s a look at which Colts players have surprised, and who’s disappointed through four games.
DeForest Buckner’s play through this first quarter has been a pleasant surprise. Coming off a neck injury which caused him to miss seven games last season and undergo surgery, the expectations for what Buckner could provide coming off the operation were on the ground. Whatever he could produce would be a bonus.
But Buckner has roared out to a tremendous start. His three sacks and four tackles for loss in four games both lead the team. He’s been one of the few bright spots for a Colts pass rush which has been highly ineffective so far. With injuries continuing to pile up at defensive end, Buckner has remained a consistent source of disruption from the interior.
At 32 years old and coming off a major injury, Buckner wasn’t expected to be carrying the Colts’ pass rush, especially this early in the season. Instead, he has looked like the same disruptive force Indianapolis has relied on since his arrival in 2020.
Like Buckner, Spencer Shrader entered this season with questions to answer regarding an injury. His 2025 season was off to a great start, but ended abruptly due to a knee injury.
Shrader not only got back healthy, but barely beat Blake Grupe out for the kicking job in training camp and is now off to a tremendous start. Aside from missing his first PAT attempt of the season, Shrader’s been otherwise perfect. He’s made all 11 of his field goal tries, with 8 of the 11 coming from beyond 40 yards.
Shrader has quickly become a weapon for the Colts, and has been a lifesaver for an offense which has struggled to score touchdowns at the same high rate they did a season ago.
Akeem Davis-Gaither has been one of the biggest surprises for the Colts after signing as a free agent in March.
Davis-Gaither entered 2026 as a relatively unheralded addition to a linebacker room that had plenty of questions surrounding it. Instead, he has become an important piece of the Colts’ defense.
Davis-Gaither leads the team with 37 tackles through four games and has played nearly every defensive snap along the way. He has also taken on the green-dot responsibilities as the defense’s primary communicator.
His impact was particularly evident in Week 4, when Davis-Gaither recorded eight tackles and helped anchor a defense that allowed just 13 points to Washington. He was also named to PFF’s Week 4 Team of the Week .
Davis-Gaither was never expected to be a defensive focal point when he signed with Indianapolis, but four games in, anf it's difficult to imagine where the Colts’ defense may be without him.
Matt Goncalves has quietly become one of the Colts’ most valuable pieces through the first four games.
After playing tackle in college and as a rookie, Goncalves made the transition to right guard in 2025 and started all 16 games at the position. He was solid in his first season there, but the Colts needed him to take another step forward in 2026.
So far, he has done exactly that.
Goncalves has started all four games, earning a 81.6 PFF grade, which ranks ninth among 74 qualified guards. He's allowed just two pressures and one sack in pass protection and is yet to be penalized.
His play has helped make the interior of the Colts’ offensive line a strength, with PFF ranking Indy’s offensive line third in the NFL entering Week 5 and specifically highlighting Goncalves as one of the unit’s strongest performers.
Goncalves entered the season as a promising young player still establishing himself at guard. Four games in, he looks like another great find on the offensive line by the Colts scouting department.
The first four weeks of the season have been a sobering reminder of the quarterback that Daniel Jones has been most of his career.
While Jones played some of the best football of his career in his first 10 games with the Colts, leading the team to an NFL-best 8-2 record, he hasn’t been on the same level in 2026.
Jones finished his injury-shortened 2025 with 3,101 passing yards, 19 touchdowns, eight interceptions and a 100.2 passer rating. Through four games this season, he has 754 passing yards, three touchdowns, four interceptions and a 73.9 passer rating. His yards per attempt has also dropped from 8.1 to 5.7.
But the biggest concern has been his inability to protect the football. Jones has committed at least one turnover in every game this season and has already accounted for seven of the Colts’ eight total  turnovers.
That is a dramatic departure from the version of Jones the Colts saw last season, and it has made his uneven play one of the team's biggest issues through the first month of 2026.
One of the most confusing storylines of the season so far is the lack of involvement for CJ Allen. The Colts drafted Allen 53rd overall this past April as the first player in their draft class. With glaring holes at linebacker, the expectation was that Allen would have an impact right away.
Instead, Allen has hardly gotten an opportunity .
The rookie has only appeared in two of four games so far, managing one tackle in just 11 snaps. As a result, Allen is one of the most difficult Colts players to evaluate. But it’s clear that he hasn’t lived up to what was expected of him.
If there’s any chance for Allen to turn things around, it could be this week against Pittsburgh. Both Davis-Gaither and Jaylon Carlies appeared on Wednesday’s injury report , so there’s a window of opportunity for Allen. Should either one of them not be 100 percent on Sunday, then the rookie could see the most snaps of his young career to date.
But until that happens, the first quarter of Allen’s rookie season has been nothing short of a disaster.
Alec Pierce’s 2025 breakout season created plenty of excitement for what he could do in his second year with Daniel Jones. Instead, his 2026 season has been derailed by injury.
Pierce recorded 1,003 receiving yards and six touchdowns last season, establishing himself as one of the league’s biggest big-play threats and earning a massive four-year, $114 million contract extension. The expectation was that he would build on that success this season and remain one of the Colts’ most important weapons in the passing game.
That hasn’t happened. Pierce suffered a heel injury in Week 2 and was subsequently placed on injured reserve, with his availability for the remainder of the season unclear. His absence has left Indianapolis without its most dangerous downfield weapon at a time when the passing game has already struggled.
There’s still time for Pierce to return and make an impact, but his inability to stay on the field has prevented him from building on his breakout 2025 campaign. If he were at least able to stay on the field, then this could be a much different conversation.
Laiatu Latu entered his third NFL season with the expectation to take another step forward and emerging as a go-to pass rush maestro. Instead, the former first-round pick has gone backward.
Latu recorded 8.5 sacks and 45 tackles last season, establishing himself as one of the Colts’ most important pieces along the defensive line. This year, Latu has just one sack and 13 total pressures, with his 60.0 PFF pass-rush grade ranking 68th among 110 qualified edge defenders.
Latu's individual struggles are also a symptom of a horrific pass rush unit as a collective. Per Next Gen Stats, the Colts' 25.5% pressure rate through four games ranks dead last in the NFL.
There have been flashes, including a sack of Marcus Mariota last week, but Latu hasn’t consistently created the kind of pressure the Colts need from him. His lack of impact, plus injuries…

title: Sauce Gardner Takes Accountability After Ugly Week 4 Showing
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts walked away from London with their second straight victory on Sunday, but it was a completely different storyline for star cornerback Sauce Gardner.
Gardner put together arguably the worst performance of his NFL career against the Washington Commanders, and he isn't making any excuses for it.
According to NFL Pro and Next Gen Stats, Gardner allowed four receptions on five targets for 117 yards and a touchdown, the most receiving yards he has surrendered in a single game throughout his career.
To make matters worse, much of that damage came against seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, who was forced into action after Marcus Mariota suffered a knee injury in the first quarter.
Gardner also allowed a 156.3 passer rating when targeted, tied for the highest mark among cornerbacks in Week 4, via PFF.
But surprisingly, those coverage numbers weren't even Gardner's biggest concern when he went back and watched the film.
"I wasn't giving my best effort. I wasn't really giving my best effort in the run game," Gardner admitted Wednesday.
Gardner specifically pointed to multiple plays where he failed to pursue the ball with the effort he expects from himself, including an 87-yard catch-and-run that was eventually called back due to penalties.
"But it was definitely an embarrassing watch," Gardner said. "To just look back at that tape, it was like my effort when the ball is on the other side, it was like an embarrassing watch, an embarrassing feeling."
"That's not what I stand for. That's not the type of person I am. That's not the type of player I am, and that'll never happen again."
I think that response says quite a bit about the type of player Indianapolis has in its secondary.
There is a difference between having a bad game and allowing that performance to become your standard. Gardner clearly has no intention of letting that happen.
Naturally, Sunday's performance has brought back some criticism surrounding the massive price Indianapolis paid to acquire Gardner last November.
But I still believe you have to look at that trade through a much wider lens.
The Colts were 7-2 and sitting atop the AFC when Chris Ballard sent two first-round picks and Adonai Mitchell to New York. At that moment, Indianapolis looked like it could be one elite cornerback away from making a legitimate championship run.
It was exactly the type of aggressive move Colts fans had been begging Ballard to make for years.
And from my perspective, Gardner is still a future Hall of Fame-caliber cornerback. The chances of finding someone with his talent in either of those first rounds were never particularly high.
More importantly, Sunday's performance was a clear outlier compared to what we saw through the first three weeks.
Gardner had allowed just five completions on 10 targets entering the Washington matchup, making his struggles in London that much more surprising.
Even the best defensive backs in football have bad afternoons, and one performance isn't going to change my evaluation of Gardner.
What matters now is how he responds, and judging by his comments Wednesday, I would expect a completely different player the next time he takes the field.
"That performance –  I ain't got to worry about seeing that ever again," Gardner said.
For a player who has already established himself as one of the premier corners in football, I wouldn't bet against him.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Colts-Steelers First Injury Report: Multiple Starters Miss Practice
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts and Pittsburgh Steelers have released their first practice reports ahead of their clash in Week 5.
Both teams are seeing injuries start to pile up now that the season is in full swing. Each defense is dealing with thin position groups at different levels and have several starters listed after the first practice of the week.
Let’s break down each team’s report and what it means going into the weekend.
Indianapolis Colts Injury Report (As of 10/7)
Tanor Bortolini and Akeem Davis-Gaither are new names to the injury report, as Arden Key, Jaylon Carlies and Ashton Dulin’s issues were all disclosed in head coach Shane Steichen’s postgame press conference. Key is expected to miss “some time,” leading the Colts to sign defensive end Carl Lawson to their practice squad . While Jaylahn Tuimoloau is the most likely option to start in Key’s place, Lawson is likely to be elevated and rotate in at some point.
Bortolini has been a revelation for the Colts this year, anchoring the center of their stout offensive line. Dulin played on Sunday after missing two games with the same hamstring issue, so seeing him pop up is a concern. Steichen had initially considered Dulin to be “week-to-week.” Davis-Gaither, who was not included in the postgame injury updates by Steichen, now has a knee injury, raising the question if he suffered something during practice. Both he and Carlies are coming off stellar performances in which they both posted PFF grades in the 90s .
No real concern over running back Jonathan Taylor, who gets the day off after becoming the NFL’s all-time leading rusher in international games last week. Wednesday is typically a veteran rest day, which explains wide receiver Keenan Allen and cornerback Charvarius Ward’s absences. That said, Allen did not play in London with a groin injury and needs to show progress the remainder of the week to feel more comfortable about his status going into Sunday.
Wednesday’s practice report for #INDvsPIT pic.twitter.com/H7qNmJBqaQ
The best news of the day for Indianapolis is tight end Will Mallory’s return to practice after starting the season on injured reserve. The team opened his 21-day practice window today and not surprisingly, Mallory was a full participant. Should the Colts deem he’s ready to go for Sunday, the Colts may look to get the 27-year-old involved in the offense.
The initial forecast projects another week with a thin group at wide receiver . Injuries were part of the reason Indianapolis brought Darius Slayton in and signed him directly to the roster, but he’s yet to play despite having two weeks to acclimate. The Colts also signed former Philadelphia Eagles receiver Quez Watkins to the practice squad, so he’s in play for an elevation, but the 28-year-old hasn’t taken an NFL snap since 2023.
If there’s a silver lining to double injuries at linebacker, it would be that the door is now open for the Colts’ top draft choice in CJ Allen to get the most playing time of his young career thus far. The second-round pick has only played in two of four games thus far, registering only 11 snaps.
Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report (As of 10/7)
Pittsburgh has a slightly better looking report, though it’s quite top-heavy. Four of the five players listed are starters.
The immediate concern for Pittsburgh would be the secondary. Both starting nickel Jalen Ramsey and outside starter Jamel Dean did not practice. Should neither be able to go, the Steelers will turn to Brandin Echols in the slot and Daylen Everett on the perimeter, though the team did sign Sean Murphy-Bunting off the Buccaneers’ practice squad on Tuesday, so he could play a role if needed.
We have signed CB Sean Murphy-Bunting to the Active Roster off the Tampa Bay Practice Squad, signed LB Marte Mapu to the Practice Squad, waived DB Doneiko Slaughter and placed DT Derrick Harmon on the Reserve/Injured List. @BordasLaw 📝: https://t.co/VWvvwTwFi5 pic.twitter.com/WV7kVe6s3l
The 37-year-old Cameron Heyward gets a rest day, so his status for Sunday won’t become clearer until later this week.
If Indianapolis fans were looking forward to seeing former Colts receiver Michael Pittman Jr. for the first time since leaving the organization, they may have to wait a little longer. While Pittman is listed as a limited participant with a foot injury, local Pittsburgh media spotted Pittman wheeling around the facility on a scooter, so definitely one to watch. Running back Rico Dowdle has missed the last two games with his toe injury, so he seems to be trending in the right direction.
Michael Pittman Jr. was wheeling around the locker room after practice on a one-legged scooter. Something to monitor.
Broadly speaking for Pittsburgh, we’ll need to see how the week unfolds before coming to any sort of injury-related conclusions. But the pass game on both sides of the ball are the early areas to monitor.

title: Jaguars Announce Full Inactives Before Eagles Battle: Secondary Takes Big Hit
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars' secondary is officially a bit depleted entering Sunday's Week 5 matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles.
The Jaguars announced their entire list of inactives ahead of the London battle with the Eagles , and it features a key name in the defensive back room: Eric Murray.
The complete list of Jaguars inactives entering Week 5 is as follows: safety Eric Murray, wide receiver CJ Williams, cornerback Alijah Huzzie, cornerback Jaylon Jones, defensive lineman Daniel Faalele, defensive end Wesley Williams, and defensive tackle Albert Regis. Jones and Huzzie just joined the Jaguars this week after Jacksonville signed them as defensive back depth, while Faalele and Wesley Williams have been inactive each week this season. CJ Williams has been a healthy scratch since Week 1.
Regis is also a healthy scratch this week, with the Jaguars carrying extra defensive backs in practice squad cornerback Jabbar Muhammad and practice squad safety Kaevon Merriweather. Linebacker Jalen McLeod is also active and will play a role on special teams.
But it is the status of Murray that is most concerning for the Jaguars. Murray has played a significant role as a starting safety for the Jaguars since he signed with the team last March, and the Jaguars will now have a new safety starting across from fourth-year safety Antonio Johnson. Whether that player will be second-year defensive back Rayuan Lane or third-year rookie Jalen Huskey remains to be seen, but the fact is the Jaguars are now without two of their top-3 safeties in Murray and Caleb Ransaw.
“Eric means a lot to us. Eric is one of the guys you would kind of put him in a classification of he's a coach on the field," Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said this week. "You guys probably know that from being at practice. He's just really good communicator, knows the ins and outs of the defense and can kind of see problems before they start on the field. He's been great that way all the way through, the entire season last season, the beginning of this season. He's been a big part of our success."
Now with Huskey or Lane in the mix at the starting safety spot, the Jaguars will have to be at their best if they hope to improve to 4-1. This is the kind of game that will test the depth pieces the Jaguars have developed over the last two seasons, and it starts and ends with how the Jaguars see their safeties step up with Murray out of the lineup.
"Other guys, if they have to step up and do that, I have total confidence that they will, because we've really got a good bunch of communicators back there," Campanile said. "And that's one of the things we're always looking for at that position. A guy who has position flexibility, one. And then two, smart guys,  guys that love to play, that love to learn and obviously, know the ins and outs of all the calls, learn football.”

title: 3 Jaguars X-Factors vs. the Eagles in Week 5: Who Must Slow Down Jalen Hurts?
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- For the Jacksonville Jaguars, Week 5 is a big one.
The Jaguars have a chance to knock off the Philadelphia Eagles and improve to 4-1 with a win in London, and here are the X-Factors who will have to step up to ensure it happens.
Arik Armstead is coming off his best game of the season , and he is now set to face off against an Eagles team that has so many moving pieces along the offensive line. The Lane Johnson retirement is the biggest noteworthy change for the Eagles' front line, but they also have several things getting juggled along the interior offensive line due to injuries and the Cam Jurgens trade. Right now, they are hurting and the Jaguars need to take advantage of it.
That means this should be another week where Armstead takes over as a pass-rusher, just like he has over the last two weeks. Armstead has 10 pressures over the last two games, and this is a game that should be set up for him to another impact performer in Week 5. The Eagles have a history of developing offensive linemen, but Armstead can test that and help the Jaguars slow down Jalen Hurts.
The best parts about the Eagles' defense normally comes down to their pass defense: a very strong trio of defensive backs with Quinyon Mitchell, Tariq Woolen, and Cooper DeJean along with a host of pass-rushers like Jonathan Greenard, Jalen Carter, Moro Ojomo, Nolan Smith, and Jalyx Hunt. That means they might offer the Jaguars some actual resistance when it comes to their Trevor Lawrence-led passing attack, which could put this game in the hands of the rushing attack and Bhayshul Tuten.
Tuten has been one of the NFL's most effective running backs to start the 2026 season, and this could be a game that sees him have his true breakout performance. That game would have been last week if not for a few penalties and two called-back touchdowns, but I think the Jaguars are ready to lean on him and let him lead the way to a win.
Foyesade Oluokun has been a very strong veteran performe r for the Jaguars this season, getting high marks in metrics in both run- and pass-defense. This culminated with him making one of the most important plays of the season thus far with a red-zone interception of Joe Burrow last week, and the Jaguars will once again need him to set the tone against the Eagles. While Jalen Hurts is unlikely to test the Jaguars often in the middle of the field, Oluokun can still make an impact.
With the Eagles set to be without both Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby at running back this week, that means the Jaguars' run defense will face off against backup running backs Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce. The way for the Jaguars to beat the Eagles is to force Jalen Hurts into a dropback-heavy attack by suffocating their run defense, and Oluokun is set to be a pivotal part of the Jaguars' hopes to do that.

title: Why the Jaguars Must Keep Close Tabs on the Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade Compensation
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Marvin Harrison Jr. is on his way out of Arizona, and the outcome of his exit could be of some importance to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
That is not just because the most rumored landing spot for the former top-5 pick is to the AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans, who the Jaguars play in London in Week 6. Instead, the eventual conclusion of the Harrison trade saga and its final compensation for the Cardinals could be of great interest for the Jaguars moving forward.
Simply put, whatever the Cardinals end up getting for Harrison could indicate what the Jaguars could get if they end up wanting to trade away their own third-year wide receiver. The Jaguars continue to look no closer to considering trading wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr., which is not surprising. Thomas' snap counts and role in the offense have fluctuated through the first month of the season , though the Jaguars have always seemed content on sticking by Thomas even if is not a high-volume producer in their deep passing game.
This is not an argument for the Jaguars to deal Thomas, though I do think the Harrison trade could make it clear that it could still end up being the most advantageous move for the Jaguars ahead of next month's trade deadline. Whatever the Cardinals end up landing for Harrison over the next few days could make that even clearer.
There have been several reports that the Cardinals' asking price for Harrison is a second-round pick. If this is the case, then that would set a clear floor for what kind of value Thomas may offer on the trade market before the November deadline. That is simply the result of Thomas being a much more valuable player than Harrison; if Harrison can fetch a potential top-50 pick, then what the heck could Thomas land the Jaguars?
Simply put, Thomas has been a much better player than Harrison to start their careers. He outpaces Harrison in games played, AV (approximate value), receptions, receiving yards, catch rate, yards per target, yards after the catch per reception, and passer rating when targeted. Even with Thomas looking like the third or fourth pass-catcher in the pecking order this year, he still has more catches and yards than Harrison, who has run more than double of the amount of routes Thomas had.
In short, there is zero comparison for Thomas and Harrison. Both are young, former first-round picks from the same class, but Thomas has been the significantly better NFL receiver to start their careers. That means whatever the Cardinals get for Harrison should be nothing more than the start of the conversation if the Jaguars ever see teams make offers for Thomas.
It does not appear the Jaguars have any interest in moving Thomas, so it doesn't make much sense for the Jaguars to shop him. But that could not stop other teams from calling about him, and the Harrison trade compensation should help inform those teams what a meaningful call would really look like.

title: Jaguars Mailbag: Eagles Matchup, Depth Concerns, and Lessons Learned
full_text:
JACKSONVILE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are ready for Week 5.
The Jaguars face another tough test this week with the Philadelphia Eagles in a clash in London. In this week's Jaguars Mailbag, we take questions on that matchup, any potential injury or depth concerns, and more.
As the season has progressed, are we seeing safety/depth corner become a larger need than interior DL or Edge with regard to any potential move(s) made by the deadline?
A: I do not think safety is a concern unless Eric Murray's injury tends to linger. Rayuan Lane has done some good things when he has had to play in the defensive lineup over the last two seasons, and the Jaguars did take Jalen Huskey in the top-100 for a reason. Safety felt like a position the Jaguars ensured they would have depth it. Cornerback I think could be interesting because the Jaguars need at least four healthy cornerbacks to marginally function, but ideally would have five. The Bengals game was a good example of how far they can stretch their cornerback depth. I think the Jaguars like their EDGE group, but I would still think a defensive tackle would be attractive.
Just like at the draft in April, the interior of the defensive line needs help. Who are some realistic players the Jaguars could target before the trade deadline?
A: If the Jaguars could make the money work, Daron Payne is a great player. He is a bit expensive cap wise though and I would think the Jaguars would need to find a cheaper option. The player who I continue to believe makes the most sense is Eagles defensive tackle Moro Ojomo. If the Eagles go into sell mode sooner than later, they have no real reason to hold onto Ojomo on the last year of his deal considering the value he could bring them on the trade market.
Update on Lequint Allen Jr? How much is his injury holding him back? I feel like we went into the offseason with him being a tone setter on O and ST.
A: Considering he was still limited in practice up until this week, I think it makes sense to assume the injury was impacting him a bit. He was a full participant all week in practice this week, and he has seen his overall snaps (offense and special teams) increase with each week of the season. It is also worth noting that he is the team's passing down back, and the Jaguars rank No. 27 in the NFL in pass-rate after ranking No. 19 last season. The Jaguars have a very balanced offense that simply hasn't gone into dropback and chuck it mode this year, so his snaps will be a bit lower as a result.
Any talk of a revenge game after the near comeback loss vs the ‘24 Eagles SB champ squad two yrs ago? Lots of Jags players still around from that team. pic.twitter.com/WaekWsHDv8
A: I don't think so. I think the Jaguars want to beat the Eagles because the Eagles are simply the next opponent on the schedule. I also think so much has changed for the Jaguars since that game that we can throw anything pre-2025 out. Jaguars players still likely thought about the Bengals game, for example, because it happpened under Liam Coen last season.
Did the coaching staff learn anything from last year’s trip to avoid… whatever happened last time
A: I think the fact that they left a few days later means something. I also think, though, that most of last year's London loss can be chalked up to the Jaguars still being far away from competing with a team like the Rams. The Rams were one of the best teams in football last year, while the Jaguars were still giving Dyami Brown serious reps at receiver in Week 7 last year. It is a completely different offense, and team, right now than it was then. London will always be daunting due to the travel, but I do not think there are many comparisons worth making right now.
Saw someone throw out Jalen Ramsey as a potential target. Actually sounds kind of interesting with his ability to play safety. Pipe dream? Would it make any sense?
A: I could see it making sense considering Jalen Ramsey would be a good bit cheaper to acquire now than he ever has been before. The Jaguars could also use safety depth if they face any more injuries. But even at this stage of his career, I do not think Ramsey is signing up to be a part-time player. Unless the Jaguars were going to make him a full-time starter, which I do not see happening, then I do not think it is one scenario still worth talking about all that much. I do think Ramsey and Liam Coen's coaching style are a match made in heaven, however.
Cant remember if it was Gus or you that mentioned last week that the Jags play the 2nd highest rate of man on 3rd down. What did that look like vs Cincy?
A: The Jaguars go with man coverage the most when they get in the red-zone because they like to throw blitzes mixed in with zone coverage on the back end on a lot of third downs. I do not think man will ever become the staple of the defensive scheme, but it isn't surprising to me to see how much more the Jaguars are using it this year considering how good Travis Hunter and Jarrian Jones both are at it.
Would Moro Ojomo be a fit for Campanelli’s scheme?
A: 100%. His skill-set is actually a bit comparable to Ruke Ohorhoro's due to his usage and the fact that he is at his best as a penetrating three-technique who can use his burst and pas s-rush ability to get upfield. He is a really strong run defender, too, so I think he would fit right in with the amount of two-gapping the Jaguars ask their defensive linemen to do to free up the linebackers in the running game.
Are 44 and 41 earning their pay?
A: The Jaguars' defense would not be one of the best in the NFL without either of them. They are doing more than enough to earn their pay, unless sacks are the only way to determine their value which, of course, it is not. Walker has been their most disruptive lineman, while Hines-Allen has been elite against the run, created for other players due to the attention he draws, and has helped produce several takeaways such as Jourdan Lewis' interception against the Bengals a week ago.
If the Bengals had gotten that first down and went onto win the game, what do you think the biggest discussion this week would have been?
A: The Jaguars' offense not putting the game away with a four-minute drive at the end of the game. It would have been the second time in two losses that had happened, and it would likely become a real concern with their ability to close games. The offense is playing really well, but they do need to learn how to put teams away for good when they get the chance to do so.
Hainsey seems to be a weak point in the line. To the eye and with the questionable PFF scores. Any chance Monheim is given a shot?
A: I will be frank: I do not think PFF grades mean much. I think their stats on splits and usage are very helpful, but I would consider their grades to be by far the least important part of their data. With that said, I do think you could see Monheim push Hainsey next season.

title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Jaguars vs. Eagles: Travon Walker Can Decide the Game
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Every week in the NFL is about matchups, and that is what the Jacksonville Jaguars will have to focus on in Week 5.
The Philadelphia Eagles are entering the Week 5 matchup with bumps and bruises , which could grant the Jaguars a few key advantages in terms of mismatches entering the week. But which matchups must the Jaguars win to truly ensure they leave London with a victory? We break it down below.
The Eagles are set to start a new right tackle after the retirement of future Hall of Famer Lane Johnson earlier this week. While the Eagles have a few decent backup options such as Fred Johnson and rookie tackle Markel Bell, this should still be a matchup that now favors the Jaguars considering the start to the season that Travon Walker has had. While Walker has not racked up a ton of sacks, he has had his best start to the year as a pass-rusher in his career, and he has been the team's most consistently disruptive defensive lineman this year as a result.
Walker mostly lines up against the opposing right tackles, which means Josh Hines-Allen will draw talented left tackle Jordan Mailata for most of the game. This means Walker has the most advantageous matchup entering the week of all of the Jaguars' top pass-rushers. If he can prove to be as disruptive as he has been in past weeks, he could hold the key to the Jaguars forcing Jalen Hurts into mistakes.
If there is one clear edge the Jaguars have over the Eagles, it is the skill player matchups. The Eagles do have one of the best cornerback duos in the NFL that could make it difficult for the Jaguars to move the ball consistently on the outside, but they have struggled quite a bit at stopping passing games over the middle of the field. This was the same advantage the Jaguars had over the Cincinnati Bengals last week, and it is one they should hone in once again in Week 5.
The Eagles have seen former first-round linebacker Jihaad Campbell have his fair share of struggles in coverage this season, with Campbell ranking as the sixth-worst coverage linebacker in terms of EPA/Play this season. The second-worst linebacker has been Bengals' Demetrius Knight, and we saw what Strange and the Jaguars did to him last week. Getting Strange some one-on-one looks on money downs will be critical this week.
With the injuries the Jaguars have in the secondary, it should be expected for this to be another week where Travis Hunter spends most, if not all, of his snaps at the cornerback spot. The Jaguars are set to get Montaric Brown back this week, but the Jaguars can not afford to have Hunter off the field considering what kind of flow this game might get into. If the Jaguars can force the Eagles to become a pass-heavy offense early in the game, it could give Hunter a big chance to make another game-changing play.
The Eagles will be without DeVonta Smith, which means Dontayvion Wicks is clearly the Eagles' WR1 entering the game. If the Eagles go downfield, it is fair to assume that Wicks is who they will be targeting. That means Hunter will need to have some highlight wins, just like he has over the last two weeks. Hunter has been an impact player at cornerback for the Jaguars, and taking Wicks out of this game in coverage could be how he becomes an X-Factor this week.

title: 3 Biggest Jaguars Concerns Entering Eagles Tilt: Replacing Eric Murray
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- When it comes to the NFL, there is no such thing as a guarantee.
That is a critical lesson for the Jaguars to let sink in as they prepare for the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5. The Eagles are banged up and coming off back-to-back losses, but they are still the same Eagles team that has won big games night in and night out over the years.
So, what areas of the Eagles' team and their matchup with the Jaguars should be a concern for Jacksonville entering Week 5? We break it down below.
The Eagles' cornerback duo of Quinyon Mitchell and Tariq Woolen is one of the best cornerback pairs in the entire NFL. The Jaguars have faced some talented cornerbacks at the start of the season, and this week's battle against the Eagles is just another chapter in that story. As a result of those cornerback matchups, we have seen on and off weeks for the Jaguars' receivers in terms of production.
The Jaguars should have advantages over the Eagles when it comes to passing to tight ends and slot receivers, but getting the ball outside is a key part of the Jaguars' passing game. There is a good chance we see the Eagles limit the Jaguars' ability to do so, which could make things a bit slower for the Jaguars in terms of their offensive pacing.
Considering the injuries the Eagles have at wide receiver and running back right now, I would be surprised if Dallas Goedert is not the focal point of the Eagles' passing game this week. The Jaguars will need to be at their best to slow down Goedert as a pass-catcher, especially considering the Jaguars will be without Caleb Ransaw and will also likely be without Eric Murray.
The Jaguars' defense has played well all season long, thanks in large part to the Jaguars' linebackers Foyesade Oluokun and Ventrell Miller. But the Jaguars have also let tight ends get some production against them in recent weeks, whether it was Evan Engram or Nate Adkins in Week 2 or Mike Gesicki
 on his touchdown catch a week ago. The Eagles have seen Goedert deal with some injuries, though he is set to make his official return Sunday.
The Jaguars will need young safeties Rayuan Lane and Jalen Huskey to be ready to be challenged on Sunday in the likely event that Murray doesn't play. If not, this could end up being a big day for Goedert as a receiver, something the Jaguars can not afford to let happen.
While the Eagles' pass-rush has not been as productive at the start of this season as they have been in past years, they still pose a legit threat to the Jaguars. Nolan Smith, Jordan Davis, Jalen Carter, Jalyx Hunt, and Moro Ojomi have all been productive and disruptive defenders before and should bounce back sooner rather than later. Then there is Jonathan Greenard, who has been very productive in the two games he has played this season. Greenard is questionable, but he poses some real challenges if he plays.
We have seen the Jaguars' offense thrive more often than not since the start of the 2025 season. But the few times we have seen the Jaguars' offense struggle under Liam Coen has been when the Jaguars get overwhelmed by a talented defensive front. The Jaguars can not let that happen on Sunday like it did in Week 2.

title: Jaguars Gain Some Key Edges Over Eagles in Final Week 5 Injury Report
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The final injury report for Week 5 is out, and there is some good (and some bad) news for the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Both sides have had some extensive injury reports as the Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles prepare to face off in Week 5. The Jaguars got some better luck than the Eagles with Friday's injury report, however, leading to the Jaguars gaining some clear edges on the Eagles.
On the Jaguars' side of the things, there is some good and bad news ahead of Week 5. Eric Murray is listed as doubtful after returning to practice in a limited setting, which suggests the Jaguars are likely to be without their veteran leader of the secondary when they face off against the Eagles offense. This means the Jaguars will have to turn to either second-year safety Rayuan Lane or third-round rookie Jalen Huskey, who will be making his NFL debut.
The Jaguars also ruled out new cornerback Jaylon Jones, who joined the team earlier this week to play a special teams and backup role. Jones has been limited all week with a hamstring injury and is the only Jaguars player who has officially been ruled out.
But outside of Murray and Jones, there are not many injury questions. All of the other Jaguars who have been on the injury report this week, such as cornerbacks Jourdan Lewis, Jarrian Jones and Montaric Brown, offensive tackles Cole Van Lanen and Anton Harrison, and defensive linemen Davon Hamilton and Josh Hines-Allen carry no injury designation entering the game.
The same can not exactly be said for the Eagles. The Eagles have star defensive end Jonathan Greenard listed as questionable after he missed all week of practice with an ankle injury. The Eagles will also officially be without DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Marquise Brown, Marcus Epps, and Drew Kendall. Those are some key players, and the Jaguars are certainly the healthier team entering Sunday's game.
With that said, the Jaguars know they can not look past the Eagles in any area. The Eagles have won a lot of big games in recent years, and they have the type of staff and roster that can push through tough times like the ones they are going through now. That doesn't erase the Jaguars' advantage, but it does mean the Jaguars will have to be on alert.
“We've tried to look at it as we can't worry about that or if that even creeps into our minds, we're probably worrying about the wrong things because it is about us. It's about our execution, our game plan, our fundamentals, technique, communication," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Friday.
"Nick Sirianni does a great job. This team, this group won a Super Bowl a few years ago. They know how to handle adversity. They know how to handle some of these things. They've had a ton of guys play and help them win over the course of the last few years. I know they'll be ready to play, that's for sure. And it's really got to be about us. I mean, that's something that we continue to talk about as a team.”

title: 3 Overreactions to the Jaguars' First Month of the Season: 2025 Draft Wins and Losses
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are a month into the 2026 season, and there has certainly been a lot of good to this point.
But what has been real about the Jaguars to this point in the season? What overreactions are valid, and which are, well, just overreactions? We break it all down below ahead of Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Some of the biggest winners from the Jaguars' first month are members of the Jaguars' 2025 NFL Draft class. Travis Hunter has been a massive part of the Jaguars' defensive success, while Bhayshul Tuten has been amongst the best running backs in the NFL through the first month of the season. Add in Rayuan Lane and other quality depth pieces like LeQuint Allen and Jonah Monheim, and the Jaguars have some impact picks in their second seasons.
With that said, it has been a slow start for several other picks. Wyatt Milum is still just a backup and doesn't seem any closer to an expanded role, Caleb Ransaw is on injured reserve and will miss at least a month with a knee injury, and Jack Kiser has not yet been active. There are some sure wins form the 2025 draft class, but there are also a few other second-year players who have left something to be desired.
It isn't a stretch to say Travis Hunter is already the Jaguars' best cornerback just four games into the 2026 season. In fact, I think it has already gotten to the point where Hunter is one of the Jaguars' three best overall defenders behind just Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker. To be at that kind of spot after 11 career games and, really, just four games with an intense focus at cornerback says quite a bit about his talent.
“I think just any time you put a little bit more time into one job, it helps provide some clarity for the player and for him to be able to go play fast with a lot of confidence where he knows what he's doing a little bit more, where he's been more focused at that side of the football," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Friday. "Defense is so much—everybody thinks offense is more complicated, whereas defense is so much more communication in terms of the other guys and what their jobs are and how you're tied into that. I think he's done a nice job. I've been pleased with some of the confidence he continues to build.”
Hunter's focus on the defensive side of the ball has paid off. I expect him to be seen as a top-10 cornerback across the entire NFL by the end of the season, but he has already proven himself to be an X-Factor and a game-changer inside Duval.
The Jaguars' offensive line has had its ups and downs to start the 2026 season, and it is fair to say the Jaguars should keep their options open on the unit moving forward. While the Jaguars do not have many moving pieces along the line right now with the same five starters in every game to start the year, there could be a few open spots along the unit in the year's to come. As things stand today, rookie guard Emmanuel Pregnon should return to the lineup next year, but then there are some questions.
Left tackle Anton Harrison has had some really impressive performances, and then some not-so-impressive performances this season. He will be in Jacksonville on the fifth-year option next year, but I am not sure he has played up to a contract extension thus far at left tackle. Right tackle Cole Van Lanen should still be around due to his deal as well, but the Jaguars will clearly need more offensive tackle depth.
Center Robert Hainsey could be pushed by Jonah Monheim next season, while Ezra Cleveland is in a contract year and is unlikely to be extended. The line could still be spruced up moving into the future, and the 2026 performances so far haven't done much to change that.

title: 3 Questions the Jaguars Need to Answer vs. the Eagles: Will the DL Dominate?
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have answered some tough questions week in and week out, and their next matchup is no different.
The Jaguars are set to take on the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5 , a matchup that does seem to favor the Jaguars a bit but one that is far from a guaranteed win. So, which questions are facing the Jaguars entering Sunday, and how can they answer them?
With how many moving pieces the Eagles have around their offensive line , this needs to be a week where the Jaguars' front dominates. When the Jaguars get offensive line matchups that should point to big days for their defensive line, they need to take advantage of them. They have already done so at several points this season, and the Jaguars will have to do so again vs. the Eagles' shifting line in Week 5.
The departures of Lane Johnson and Cam Jurgens this week have the Eagles looking vulnerable along the offensive line. The right tackle spot is one spot the Jaguars should really focus their attack on, with the Eagles set to start either Fred Johnson or Markel Bell against the Jaguars and defensive end Travon Walker.
According to NextGenStats, Walker has generated 17 pressures this season, tied for the eighth-most among edge rushers, while being double-teamed on 19.6% of his pass rushes, the fifth-highest rate among edge rushers (min. 50 pass rushes). Walker has also aligned on the interior on 27.8% of his snaps, up from 19.0% in 2025. He has played very, very well to start the 2026 season, and this is one matchup he must win.
It seems like Jaguars rookie left guard Emmanuel Pregnon is drawing a blue-chip defensive tackle every week, but that is life for a rookie offensive lineman in today's NFL. Pregnon and the rest of the Jaguars' interior offensive line will have to face off against a talented Eagles defensive tackle room that consists of talents such as Jordan Davis, Jalen Carter, and Moro Ojomo, and the entire trio of Pregnon, Robert Hainsey, and Ezra Cleveland are bound to be tested once again.
The Jaguars' interior line had its moments last week against the Cincinnati Bengals, but the Bengalls' deensive tackles did combine for two sacks and five pressures. The Jaguars had a terrific outing in Week 3 against the Milton Williams/Christian Barmore duo, which should give them some encouragement, but the Eagles' trio of defensive tackles looks like the best unit the Jaguars have faced so far this year.
We have seen how interior pressure can impact the Jaguars' offense, with Zach Allen wrecking the Jaguars at times in Week 2. The Jaguars' interior offensive line must be at its very best this week to ensure the Jaguars' offense can continue to keep up its momentum from the first month of the season.
The Jaguars have done a good job of mixing up their passing game focus each week. Parker Washington led the Jaguars in receiving for the first two weeks, Jakobi Meyers led the unit in Week 3, and last week was the week where Brenton Strange had his breakout performance. It seems like one of the biggest strengths of the Jaguars' offense is the fact that they have such a deep depth chart of weapons that any single week could be someone's time to shine. The question now is which pass-catcher it will be against the Eagles.
The Eagles appear to have Quinyon Mitchell likely available this week, which means it might be another week where the Jaguars need to attack the middle of the field. According to NextGenStats, "the Eagles cornerbacks have primarily stuck to sides of the field rather than pure shadow coverage this season, with Quinyon Mitchell aligning at right outside cornerback on 95.0% of his snaps while Riq Woolen aligns at left outside corner on 99.2% of his.
 Mitchell has allowed 5.1 yards per target this season, 10th-lowest among 72 cornerbacks with at least 15 targets, while Woolen has allowed 6.8 (32nd)."
In short, the Eagles are playing good football at cornerback and both defenders will get reps against whoever the Jaguars put outside. The Eagles rank No. 6 in the NFL in EPA/Pass allowed to targets lined up on the outside, while they rank No. 22 against slot targets and No. 28 against tight ends. This could be another week for Strange, or even Washington.

title: While the Chiefs Enjoy a Bye Week, the Rest of the AFC West Has Plenty to Prove
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are 4-0 and the only undefeated team still standing in the AFC . That, of course, means the Chiefs are in command of the AFC West while the Las Vegas Raiders try to hold on to their second-place standing and the Denver Broncos look to improve on their .500 start.
Oh, and the Los Angeles Chargers would probably like to win a game sooner rather than later, too.
With the Chiefs enjoying their bye week, let's take a look at Sunday's pair of games containing AFC West squads, plus two primetime matchups with other AFC contenders.
The Raiders acquited themselves admirably against the Chiefs last week, taking their first loss of the season in decidedly un-Raider-y fashion. (Un-Raider-y isn't a word, but you know what it means!) In some ways, I'm more convinced that the Raiders are a legitimate playoff-adjacent team now than I was before their loss to the Chiefs. However, they're not getting a break from their upcoming schedule anytime soon.
Las Vegas gets the New England Patriots in Foxborough this week before hosting the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams in the next two weeks. The Raiders don't need to win all of those games to retain their new semi-contender status, but they can't lose four consecutive games and still be taken seriously in the second half of the year.
New England, on the other hand, is coming off an impressive win over the Bills in Buffalo last weekend, stabilizing the team after a blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 3.
The Raiders may still be a year of progress away from true contention, but Chiefs fans should obviously be pulling for the Patriots in this one.
these posts came a week apart life comes at you fast and all that pic.twitter.com/pVD2tc26og
Even with impressive home victories over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3, the vibes around quarterback Bo Nix and the Broncos' offense seem to have taken a considerable shift after last week's loss at the San Francisco 49ers. For what it's worth, I still think the Broncos are the second-best squad in the division and should be expected to return to the playoffs again this season, but that confidence would be severely shaken if the winless Chargers can pull off the upset in LA.
The Chargers have been one of the biggest disappointments in all of football this season, and they're running out of time to do something about it. After hosting the Broncos, the Chargers will head to Kansas City in Week 6 before "visiting" the Rams after their Week 7 bye. If there's any life left in the Chargers at all, they'll need to prove it against Denver.
Not that Chiefs fans need my guidance here, but a Chargers win would be good for both the Chiefs' lead over the Broncos and for a week of NFL comedy.
Beyond the AFC West, two of the Chiefs' top AFC rivals will go up against a pair of 2-2 NFC teams in primetime. The Baltimore Ravens (3-1) will face the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday Night Football, while the Bills (3-1) will travel to Los Angeles to take on the Rams for a Monday night showdown.
It's far too early in the year to be seriously considering playoff seeding, but any extra wiggle room for the Chiefs' hunt for the No. 1 seed would be beneficial, especially with Kansas City's Thanksgiving showdown with the Bills looming large.
Chiefs fans should enjoy the experience of rooting for Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson in their new homes on Monday Night Football while pulling for the Falcons to take a game from Baltimore on Sunday night.
Happy Championship Sunday! pic.twitter.com/Mw7LIStU11
