title: Chiefs’ Pass-Rush Unit Could Return a Sneaky Weapon From Injury Soon
full_text:
Much has been made of the Kansas City Chiefs' defensive line failing to record a sack in each of the past three games. However, Steve Spagnuolo's unit could be getting a huge boost in the upcoming weeks.
Following Kansas City's bye, the Chiefs will finally be eligible to get 2025 second-round pick Omarr Norman-Lott back on the field. He's been on the PUP (Physically Unable to Perform) list since training camp and was required to miss the opening four contests of the year, but Week 6 marks the first point at which he can return to game action. The University of Tennessee product tore his ACL in Week 7 of last season and has been rehabbing ever since. There was hope he'd progress to full health and participate in offseason sessions, but the front office elected to place him on the PUP list to allow him extra time to recover.
It's been almost a full year since Norman-Lott suffered the injury. Barring any setbacks, it shouldn't be too long before we see him active again. Of course, every ACL tear is different, and not everyone can make a nine-month return like Patrick Mahomes did.
Head coach Andy Reid alluded to Norman-Lott "potentially" returning after the bye in late September. It was the first positive injury update the Chiefs had received on him in quite some time.
Andy Reid also says Chiefs DT Omarr Norman-Lott is a possibility to return from IR after the bye week. Reid says he’s doing more and getting closer to a return.
The Chiefs certainly won't be in any rush to bring Norman-Lott back from a serious knee injury at 4-0. Once they open his 21-day practice window, KC must either activate him during that span or transfer him to the IR for the remainder of the season.
As a rookie, Norman-Lott played sparingly but was an effective interior lineman. Across five contests, he finished with one sack, four solo tackles, and one tackle for loss, earning a 54.2 Pro Football Focus (PFF) grade. While Norman-Lott plays on the inside, his profile is more as a pass rusher than a run defender. He's extremely explosive for his size and has a relentless motor when getting after the quarterback, boasting an impressive 18.9% pass-rush win rate as a senior in college.
As we've noted in recent days on Chiefs at SI, the pass rush hasn't really been as invisible as it seems. It especially started to come alive in the second half of the victory over the Las Vegas Raiders. However, Norman-Lott's return to the squad could open up a plethora of possibilities for the defensive line rotation.
The Chiefs drafted another defensive tackle early in this year's draft, selecting former Clemson standout Peter Woods with the No. 29 overall pick . He and Khyiris Tonga have split snaps throughout the season, with both playing a little under 50% of the defense's reps. Norman-Lott could slot in during passing downs to rush the quarterback alongside Chris Jones on the inside.
When Coach Reid speaks to the media on Monday, we could get more clarity on Norman-Lott's status. It's been quiet on the injury front for ONR lately, but the Chiefs could have a secret weapon in the pass rush ready to deploy when he's healthy.

title: Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams Star in a Bright Future for the Chiefs' Cornerback Room
full_text:
It was a bit of a surprise when the Kansas City Chiefs traded up to obtain the No. 6 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, then even more of a surprise when they used that selection on LSU cornerback Mansoor Delane . Immediately, Delane rightfully had sky-high expectations as the new face of the Chiefs' secondary.
Delane was limited throughout the majority of training camp due to a shoulder injury and then played just three snaps (including an interception of Bo Nix) in Weeks 1 and 2 due to an issue with the same shoulder. Even with just two full games under his belt, Delane looks to be worth that draft selection, and he's not alone as a rising star in Kansas City's overhauled cornerback room.
As any Chiefs or Los Angeles Rams fan knows by now, the Chiefs traded away cornerback Trent McDuffie to the Rams this offseason, and Jaylen Watson reunited with McDuffie after leaving for LA in free agency. That left a significant void for the Chiefs to fill at corner.
To begin 2026, veteran cornerback Kristian Fulton was entering the second year of his two-year deal with the Chiefs after a disappointing 2025, and '25 third-round draft pick Nohl Williams was looking to follow his promising rookie campaign with a more consistent workload in his sophomore season.
Delane, Williams and Fulton all hit the ground running .
Highest graded CBs in man coverage this season Mansoor Delane         93.8 Kristian Fulton             92.8 Nohl Williams               91.8 Trent McDuffie            90.9 Travis Hunter               90.3 pic.twitter.com/4Tv5R4kLLU
Delane has been excellent , even when asked to take on difficult coverage responsibilities, as he was asked to do at times against Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. He's also been a missile in run defense, playing with speed and physicality that fits Steve Spagnuolo's defense perfectly.
Mansoor Delane with one of the GREATEST two-play sequences you’ll see from a rook. Registers a TFL on Ashton Jeanty, and follows it up with CLAMPING Brock Bowers. The Chiefs rookie CB NEUTRALIZING some of the NFL’s top weapons 😳🔒 pic.twitter.com/oHzd3YU6qM
Delane has the fifth-highest overall cornerback grade from Pro Football Focus through the first four weeks of the 2026 season, while Fulton lands at No. 11. Williams appears at No. 41 in overall PFF grading but lands at No. 23 with his coverage grade alone.
good player this Mansoor Delane https://t.co/HNmzmM6Pbj pic.twitter.com/XPGheGgX3M
The one area of concern in the Chiefs' cornerback room comes in the slot, where veteran L'Jarius Sneed has provided some value and some tough snaps in his second act with the team. Sneed has the second-worst PFF grade among qualifying cornerbacks (No. 102 of 103), but he's been a positive force against the run and as a blitzer.
Sneed began the season in excellent fashion against the Denver Broncos in Week 1 before being routinely bested by Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs in Week 2. I'll argue that it's a bit too early (and a bit unnecessary) to rush to end the Sneed-reclaimation experiment, but he's certainly struggled more than the team's trio of outside corners to begin the year.
I'd be interested to see Delane get a bit of work in the slot if that would enable Williams and Fulton to hold the outside corner roles in nickel packages, but I'd also understand some hesitance, as Delane's potential value is probably highest as a shutdown outside corner, and he's still acclimating to the NFL game (though you wouldn't know that if you only watched him play).
What other options could the Chiefs have?
Rookie defensive back Jadon Canady was a healthy scratch in Week 4 as safety Chamarri Conner returned to the lineup, while slot corner Kader Kohou remains on the practice squad, so neither Canady nor Kohou seem particularly close to challenging Sneed for those slot corner reps. Versatile DB Chris Roland-Wallace took a season-high 29 defensive snaps against the Raiders, but Sneed has taken more than 72% of the defensive snaps in every game so far this season.
Ultimately, the Chiefs' slot corner position will require more monitoring (and, ideally, better play) in the weeks to come, but the Delane/Williams outside duo—with room for cameos from Fulton this season—appears to be one of the NFL's most promising young pairings.

title: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker Welcomes Potential Tyreek Hill Reunion in Kansas City
full_text:
While the Kansas City Chiefs are off to a 4-0 start heading into the bye, the front office is actively looking to bolster the roster. Kansas City will likely be without wide receiver Tyquan Thornton for the remainder of the regular season and could miss wide receiver Rashee Rice for some time as well.
KC has been linked to several wideouts, but the most obvious addition could come in the form of a reunion with Tyreek Hill . The speedster is coming off a dislocated knee last season and could make his return to the NFL with the team he started his career with. Rumors have been swirling between Hill and the Chiefs for quite some time. It's the worst-kept secret that Kansas City is showing interest in the 32-year-old. Recently, one of the AFC's biggest stars revealed his thoughts on Hill potentially returning to play for Andy Reid.
In an interview with Yahoo Sports on behalf of Orgain, running back Kenneth Walker III was asked what he thought about Hill potentially rejoining the Chiefs. The NFL's leading rusher is all for bringing "Cheetah" back.
"I've seen his speed. Everybody knows Tyreek Hill is just straight speed, and he's just an athlete in general," Walker said. "And just watching him over the years, I'm like, 'He's one of the best players that really played.' So, it's cool to see that. I think it's cool and it would be a great addition to our team."
Through the first four games of his Chiefs tenure, Walker has truly been an MVP candidate . He's currently sitting at 537 rushing yards with six total touchdowns. Chiefs fans knew he was talented when he signed with the franchise in March, but no one could have expected this level of production.
Part of the reason why Walker believes a reunion with Hill would work, as he later explained in the interview, is that it would make the Chiefs' offense more versatile. Between Patrick Mahomes' arm talent, Walker's dynamic running style , and Hill as a downfield threat, opposing defenses would have a difficult time containing those three players at once. While the backfield is set in Kansas City, the wide receiving corps is far less certain. The aforementioned injuries to Rice and Thornton will hinder KC, leaving the team with Xavier Worthy, Jalen Royals, Cyrus Allen, Nikko Remigio, and a potential practice squad elevation for next week's group of wideouts.
There's more at play than Brett Veach simply signing him to a cheap one-year contract, though. Hill is currently battling a civil assault and battery trial in court and has a pending Personal Conduct Policy investigation from the NFL. The Chiefs are already starting to look at other options, including former Chief champion Justin Watson .
Hill is coming off a devastating injury himself and hasn't played in an NFL game in over a year, but he's only two seasons removed from leading the league in receiving yards. If he's even 80% of his old self, he'd be a tremendous help to this offense, and Walker's comments reflect that.

title: Reported Chiefs Interest in WR Reunion Underscores a Harsh Reality
full_text:
Although the Kansas City Chiefs are on a bye week, many folks are still talking about the lone undefeated team left in the AFC. Some of that is for good reason, but there's also a glaring hole on the roster that needs to be addressed at some point.
With wide receiver Tyquan Thornton suffering a dislocated ankle in Week 4's win over the Las Vegas Raiders, it'd likely behoove general manager Brett Veach to add another pass catcher. The only issue is that the in-season talent pool doesn't contain many quality options, leaving the franchise in a tough spot.
The most recent bit of Chiefs-related wideout news sums that up pretty perfectly. According to Pete Sweeney of the Kansas City Star , Veach and Co. are "among several teams" interested in free agent Justin Watson.
The Chiefs are among several teams interested in WR Justin Watson, per source. Watson played for Kansas City from 2022-24 and is a three-time Super Bowl champion, having beaten the Chiefs with the Bucs before being part of their back-to-back title teams.
Watson being the latest name tied to KC emphasizes just how dried up the market is. Barring a trade that would almost surely cost NFL Draft capital, he's right in the thick of the tier of players the team could be vying for. Does a reunion with the three-time Super Bowl champ make any sense? Let's break it down.
They oftentimes come off as buzz phrases in Chiefs circles, but they do matter to the organization and come in handy given the timing of any potential signing once the season's rolling. Veteran experience, familiarity with the scheme, attention to detail, alignment versatility and more all carry significance. Watson checks each and every box there.
Now in his age-30 campaign, Watson has 1,716 regular-season offensive snaps under his belt as a member of the Chiefs and over 500 spanning five other years with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Houston Texans. Thinking from a Thornton-esque perspective regarding the operation of the offense, the former fifth-round pick also possesses proven chemistry with quarterback Patrick Mahomes on vertical passing concepts.
Watson carried a 17.2-yard average depth of target in Kansas City from 2022-2024. He averaged 13.9 yards before the catch per reception and owned an 89.8 passer rating when targeted. According to Pro Football Focus , Watson spent between 63.9% and 68.8% of his time lined up out wide over his three Chiefs seasons. Thornton was at 62.5% in 2025 and is at 70.9% in 2026.
It also doesn't hurt that Watson is a bigger-bodied player than most of the current Chiefs receiver room (6-foot-2, 215 pounds), is a willing and (mostly) capable blocker and can play special teams. Things like that stand out to the coaching staff and front office, for better or worse.
Simply put, Watson just wasn't a very good player during his time with the Chiefs. According to SumerSports , his 50.94% catch rate ranked sixth among all Kansas City wideouts in 2023. The following year, he owned an 0.72 yards per route run figure that was dead last in the group and trailed sixth-place Marquez Valdes-Scantling (0.89) by a decent margin.
The advanced data not being in Watson's favor doesn't stop there. NFL Pro pegs him as posting a -9.8% catch rate over expected in 2022, then a -1.3% mark in 2023 before it spiked to +6.0% in his final Kansas City season. He was worth 17.2 EPA in the latter campaign, but that can't be a reliable expectation baseline for the current year.
Other factors must also be considered, even with Thornton set to miss most or all of this season . What's the latest with Tyreek Hill? The Chiefs have been linked to him at every step over the last few weeks, although his ongoing legal situation muddies those waters quite a bit. Would a Watson addition put that potential acquisition on ice?
What about costing players like second-year man Jalen Royals and rookie Cyrus Allen developmental reps? Is Watson that much better than either option at this stage in his career? So many moving pieces make this far from a no-brainer of a decision.
Now on the wrong side of the aging curve, it's fair to question what Watson has left in the tank. His Texans tenure was virtually silent, but it's also not like he forgot how to function in a Kansas City-style offense after the end of the 2024-25 campaign. As long as there's still some speed, he can execute the same type of role he used to have.
If the Chiefs did sign Watson, this writer doesn't believe head coach Andy Reid and company would be quite as compelled to put him on the field as often as a JuJu Smith-Schuster. Additionally, Watson doesn't carry any off-the-field baggage and isn't recovering from a major injury, so he'd be a more immediate plug-and-play (and keep in the lineup) fit than someone like Hill.
At the end of the day, Watson might just be a more appropriate Thornton replacement than multiple internal options or free agent avenues. Even if he isn't a clear-cut needle-mover, it may not hurt to bring him in and see what he's got as a part-time player. An emphasis should be placed on the part, though, coming with the understanding that the double champion with the Chiefs wouldn't be saving the receiver room.
Again, that's an unfortunate reminder of where things are at. Help could be on the way while still not solving the current problem to the optimal degree.

title: The Chiefs' Pass Rush Has Room to Improve, But It's Probably Been Better Than You Think
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs haven't recorded a sack in three games. At face value, that's an alarming statistic that paints a grim picture of the team's pass rush. After a longer look, there are plenty of reasons to be optimistic that the team's defensive line will be able to put it all together after the bye week.
Using this week off to take a longer look at a few key position groups that will determine where the Chiefs go in the next act of the season, Kansas City's D-line has some work to do, but they have been better than their box score indicates.
First, find the Chiefs in this chart of key pass rush stats. (There's a lot of information for all 32 teams, so we'll break down the important parts next.) Surface-level, what do you see?
Key pass rush stats: pic.twitter.com/uq0LEa6pEK
There's a whole lot of green (which is good) throughout the Chiefs' row, with two dark purple (bad) cells. Why?
In that chart, the Chiefs are No. 6 in the NFL in pressure rate, No. 8 in quick pressure rate, No. 13 in non-blitz pressure rate and No. 8 in average time to pressure. Those are the numbers of a top-10 pass rush unit! Then, the purple boxes.
The Chiefs are No. 31 in sack rate (2.5%) and dead last, No. 32, in pressure-to-sack ratio (5.7%). The KC D-line is creating pressure at a top-10 rate, but they've been one of the worst-finishing teams on those opportunities. Ultimately, I think that paints a relatively positive picture of the pass rush, and it certainly beats the alternative.
Those numbers are supported by other individual stats, like the fact that George Karlaftis was credited with a whopping seven quarterback hits against Kirk Cousins by Pro Football Focus ( a performance supported by a longer look at the film ), giving him a total of 12 quarterback hits this season , despite getting zero sacks out of those hits.
Most QB hits this season, via @PFF George Karlaftis - 12 Greg Rousseau - 12 Dallas Turner - 9 Cameron Thomas - 9 Maxx Crosby - 9 Resulting Sacks Greg Rousseau - 6 Dallas Turner - 6 Maxx Crosby - 3 Cameron Thomas - 2 George Karlaftis - 0 pic.twitter.com/CdsAVfNdmt
Regarding the other defensive ends, rookie second-round pick R Mason Thomas has also flashed far beyond his one sack would suggest , while former first-round pick Felix Anudike-Uzomah (lined up over the center in the clip below) has had some of his best reps as a pro throughout the start of this season.
The way R Mason Thomas can accelerate towards the QB is just nuts. pic.twitter.com/ZsjpPTFvY6
Even second-year third-round pick Ashton Gillotte's season benefits from a deep dive into more advanced metrics, as Gillotte's "DIPRA" (defensive impact per rush attempt) is 10th-best in the league through four weeks.
The defensive tackles, particularly superstar veteran Chris Jones and first-round rookie Peter Woods, haven't had a series of game-wrecking moments so far this season, but Woods has shown tremendous physical tools , and Jones has been on the injury report with a calf issue to begin the year. I'm still very optimistic about Woods, and I'll wait a few more weeks before I'm willing to worry about Jones in his age-32 season.
Defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga has been a positive force against the run, and second-year lineman Omarr Norman-Lott is still on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list due to his ongoing recovery from last season's torn ACL.
Yes, the Chiefs' pass rush still needs to turn pressures and hits into sacks, but they appear to have the players to get to the quarterback; that's a much better problem than the issues they had last season.

title: How Does the Chiefs' Wide Receiver Room Stack Up at the Bye?
full_text:
On Sunday in Las Vegas, the Kansas City Chiefs' offense felt like it was hitting its stride, particularly in the deep passing game. Explosive plays had returned both on the ground and through the air, giving the Chiefs multiple ways to burn opposing defenses. Then, on one of those deep completions, wide receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a serious ankle injury, ending Thornton's two-touchdown, 111-yard day on a somber, season-threatening note.
For now, the Chiefs will at least be without Thornton for the foreseeable future , while Rashee Rice also exited the Raiders game with a tweaked hamstring. Even if the Chiefs do complete the much-speculated reunion with Tyreek Hill , he reportedly wouldn't be ready to return to the field until November . So, how will the offense adjust in the meantime?
Every *catchable* target for Worthy through 4 weeks. *Two route-pass location miscues not included, plus final pass vs LV + Best in open space & on the move (crossers and crossers) - 15/19 balls were caught against the body, double underhand - Rarely working back to the ball pic.twitter.com/d5x7D51rCf
Even as fan sentiment regarding third-year first-round wide receiver Xavier Worthy has shifted from excitement to frustration, the 23-year-old speedster is still the Chiefs' best chance to create explosive plays from the wide receiver position .
Yes, he's had his struggles with the deep ball. No, he hasn't yet found a way to turn his record-breaking speed into consistent NFL production. Yes, he still has a skillset that doesn't exist elsewhere on the roster (or many places throughout the NFL).
Worthy has already consistently been the Chiefs' most-used wide receiver by snap count (now at 80% of the offensive reps through four games), and the Chiefs' coaching staff has the benefit of an extra week to review Worthy's strengths and weaknesses while retooling the receiver room. For better or for worse, Worthy is even more important to the Chiefs now than he was before the season began.
Cyrus Allen target on third down.. like the idea of using him on possible M2M reps. Go get the DE’s hands down on a quick pass tho. pic.twitter.com/3Jbg3cqvkC
Elsewhere, Kansas City has no choice but to bring at least one of their most recent wide receiver draft picks into the fold. Second-year fourth-round pick Jalen Royals has played 60 offensive snaps through four games, with 38 of those reps coming in Vegas. Royals didn't take an offensive snap in Week 1 and has just three catches on the season, but he has been the team's No. 4 receiver so far.
Rookie fifth-round pick Cyrus Allen was the recipient of a massive amount of training camp hype , but he's taken only 10 snaps so far in the regular season —fewer offensive reps than defensive tackle/occasional fullback Khyiris Tonga.
Even with Allen's preseason hype, it always made more sense for him to be a late-season climber after he becomes more familiar with the offense and as the coaches and quarterback develop more trust in him. Now, however, the once-long runway could be shortening. If the Chiefs truly believe in Allen's skillset, the Chiefs' thinning receiver room needs playmakers wherever they can be found.

title: Will the Chiefs' Offensive Line Stabilize After the Bye Week?
full_text:
In some instances, an early Week 5 bye could be an unwelcome arrival for an NFL team, particularly for an undefeated squad with the type of momentum that only comes with four consecutive wins. For the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs, however, it might be exactly the right time for the sake of their uncertain offensive line.
While we use this bye week to evaluate a few key position groups for the current No. 1 seed in the AFC, you may not expect too much concern for the only unbeaten team in the conference.
Still, offensive line uncertainty has been one of the defining storylines of the Chiefs' strong start. How will the group come together after the bye week? That's the team's biggest issue to solve before they host the Los Angeles Chargers on October 18.
Starting left tackle Josh Simmons has missed the first four games of the season with a bulging disc, an injury the team only publicly defined on September 30 . Starting left guard Kingsley Suamataia was benched for the Chiefs' Week 4 showdown against the Las Vegas Raiders, reportedly due to a " coaching decision ."
Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has held up at left tackle in Simmons' absence, while veteran backup Mike Caliendo got the left guard reps in Las Vegas. Right tackle Jaylon Moore has had his ups and downs, leaving an interesting question for the Chiefs to answer— Benson or Moore at right tackle? —when Simmons returns.
Even All-Pro center Creed Humphrey has had some issues to begin the year, tossing some bad snaps and starting the year on pace to have career-low grades from Pro Football Focus .
To be fair, across an array of offensive line metrics , evaluation of the Chiefs' performance varies —a frequent phenomenon due to the variety of often-subjective ways O-lines are evaluated . Still, with such uncertainty at left tackle, it's seemed apparent that the unit has not yet fully gelled to be as solid as the sum of its parts.
Pass block grade of offensive linemen in true pass sets only Mahomes/Trevor good What happened to the Broncos' OL?? pic.twitter.com/DQCqy3lTpE
The Chiefs bolstered their depth on the O-line just before roster cutdowns, trading for veteran lineman Joshua Ezeudu from the New York Giants and undrafted rookie tackle Diego Pounds from the Baltimore Ravens.
Ezeudu has taken five offensive snaps for the Chiefs, while Pounds has been inactive through the Chiefs' first four games. Pounds remains an intriguing developmental tackle prospect, but his future on the field appears to be some time away. Ezeudu is on a one-year deal and provides short-term versatility at guard or tackle, though either Benson or Moore would clearly be the team's backup swing tackle when Simmons returns.

title: Chiefs Rookie and Sophomore Power Rankings: Assessing the Landscape at Bye Week
full_text:
Somehow, we're simultaneously about a month through the 2026 NFL season already but still have several months to go before we truly find out who some teams are. Don't get it twisted — multiple pretenders have already managed to stand out, but the cream of the crop won't be made obvious for quite some time.
Sitting at 4-0 on the year, the Kansas City Chiefs' hope is for them to be categorized as the latter once the postseason rolls around. That'll take continued impact from general manager Brett Veach's rookie and sophomore classes, which have presented both positive and negative value to this point.
At the bye week, let's break down the Chiefs' rookies and sophomores by ranking each 53-man roster member in tiers. Be sure to return to this series each week to see who's moving and shaking.
Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott isn't included due to him currently being on the physically unable to perform list .
There's no derailing the Nohl Williams hype train, even after an afternoon and evening in which the second-year cornerback got flagged for a pair of costly penalties . He remains a promising young building block in the secondary, forming a two-man show with rookie Mansoor Delane that could terrorize opposing offenses for years to come.
Second-round pick R Mason Thomas has bounced back from some rough moments in the last couple of weeks, flashing rare bend and quickness as a pass rusher on the outside. According to Pro Football Focus , he set a new career high with five Week 4 pressures. Late first-rounder Peter Woods may have just turned in his worst performance to date, although the interior lineman was also reportedly banged up at some point in the contest.
The real X-factor here might be Day 3 running back Emmett Johnson. While he earned a respectable 16 offensive snaps on Sunday, he only got one touch. Perhaps if Kenneth Walker III's workload dwindles a bit coming out of the bye, the Nebraska product will get his time to shine .
With left tackle Josh Simmons still working his way through a back injury , the Kahlil Benson roller coaster keeps on running in Kansas City. His level of play has undoubtedly slipped, but he was surprisingly fine in Week 4 considering he had a fill-in next to him at left guard and, per TruMedia , the Chiefs trailed only the Houston Texans in throws relative to the sticks on average.
An ankle dislocation for wideout Tyquan Thornton might just earn sophomore Jalen Royals some more snaps, but only if an external acquisition isn't made and the coaching staff deems the former Utah State standout worthy of the reps. Another member of the 2025 NFL Draft class, defensive end Ashton Gillotte has received more than a 40% workload share in three consecutive weeks and had a season-high three quarterback hurries in his last performance.
Bryson Eason , as promised, finds himself getting bumped up after being activated for the second week in a row. He could just as easily come back down given the restrictions capping him at three practice squad elevations per season. For now, he's worth keeping an eye on.
The only people who truly know when Simmons is coming back seem to be Simmons himself and those within the building at 1 Arrowhead Drive. Heck, there may not even be a solidified plan. Kansas City certainly hasn't done itself many favors with how it's handled the injury situation to one of its more polarizing youngsters, but all it'd take is a post-bye return for just about everyone to probably sweep that under the rug.
Late-round draft selection Cyrus Allen was the flavor of the summer in Chiefs circles; the Thornton injury will bring that buzz back around for the fall. Elsewhere on offense, tight end Jake Briningstool is still an occasional sighting on the field. Running back Brashard Smith is a special-teamer through and through . Barring injury, cornerback Jadon Canady is stuck in the same boat.
This is where things get a little interesting. Linebacker Jeffrey Bassa isn't in the huddle much on defense, but could forcing a fumble on special teams be the launching pad he needs for an increased overall role? Undrafted free agent Xavier Nwankpa helped seal the deal against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4 by picking off a pass on his only defensive snap. It doesn't get much more efficient than that.
Nothing much to see here, truthfully. Both tackle Diego Pounds and defensive end Jack Pyburn have made routine appearances on the game-day inactives list in recent weeks. Seventh-round quarterback Garrett Nussmeier always carries an outside shot to get on the field, although it'd take a catastrophic stretch of injuries to both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields for that to happen as the emergency third signal-caller.

title: Kenneth Walker Has Been Incredible, But Emmett Johnson's Time May Be Coming Soon
full_text:
Through the first four games of the 2026 NFL season, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker has been one of the best players in all of football and is firmly on track to be in the Offensive Player of the Year conversation in his first campaign with the Chiefs.
The only downside of Walker's 2026 so far? He's taken a whopping 99 touches through four games, putting him on pace for 420 touches this season. During his four years with the Seattle Seahawks, Walker recorded 255, 248, 199 and 252 regular season touches, respectively. It's still a compliment to note that Walker has been too dominant to take off the field, but with a long-term view of the Chiefs' season, another back will need to spell Walker at some point.
During the Chiefs' bye week, we'll be taking a closer look at a few key position groups to see how they've stacked up to preseason expectations and where they could improve after the bye. However, for the Chiefs' running backs, "improvement" seems almost impossible.
Walker has been darn near perfect through four games, and his impact on the Chiefs' offense has been remarkably evident. From his ability to be the "easy button" for Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes to his home run-hitting ability out of the backfield , Walker has exceeded even the most optimistic offseason expectations. Now, can the Chiefs keep Walker fresh enough to stay that consistent late into the year?
Outside of Kansas City, rookie fifth-round pick Emmett Johnson may be flying under the radar. He has 16 carries for 56 yards and five catches for 74—not quite enough to be added in most fantasy football leagues. However, Johnson's highlights have been about as impressive as anyone's.
Emmett Johnson has some MOVES 😮‍💨 (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/yEWu90SL7G
Even while currently standing in Walker's shadow, I'm confident that Johnson would have been the best running back in KC's 2025 backfield, and probably by a large margin.
Emmett Johnson is 1 of 5 RBs with 10+ missed tackles forced (MTFs) The 4 other RBs have 40+ touches each. Emmett Johnson has 10 MTFs on just 14 touches. Absurd.
Through four games, Walker has taken 75% of the Chiefs' offensive snaps (196) while Johnson has taken 26% (69). That's the 13th-most offensive snaps on the team for Johnson, and his role should only grow from there.
As long as Johnson is trusted by the coaching staff—and if he wasn't, I don't think the team would have parted ways with Emari Demercado during roster cuts—his workload should increase during the Chiefs' midseason grind as the team tries to spare Walker from a few hits while trying to keep him in top form for a postseason run similar to what he did for the Seahawks en route to his Super Bowl MVP award in February.
Even without significant statistical output so far, Johnson is dynamic enough that Walker can leave the field without allowing opposing defenses to let their guard down on the running game.
The only potential "negative" for the Chiefs' running back room so far would come in the evaluation of second-year seventh-round pick Brashard Smith. (Even then, "negative" is probably too strong.) Smith has taken only six offensive snaps this season, catching one pass but taking zero carries.
The optimistic case for Smith is that he's firmly behind one superstar back and one extremely promising rookie. On the other hand, Smith saw the field sparingly last season, recording just 44 carries (with 26 coming in the team's two games against the Las Vegas Raiders) in 2025. Smith's speed is still a unique enough trait that he should be worth keeping an eye on as the season unfolds, but he's more of a special teamer and injury insurance until further notice.

title: Is Quentin Johnston Playing Today? Broncos vs. Chargers Updates for Week 5
full_text:
As if the big Ladd McConkey injury situation wasn’t enough, there was also an injury saga around Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Quentin Johnston going into Week 5, too.
Johnston was another wide receiver expected to take a big leap in 2026 now that Mike McDaniel had arrived to help along Justin Herbert’s offense.
Instead, Johnston has regressed with some habitual problems popping up at times, all before a chest injury has put his status in jeopardy.
Here’s a live-updating look at the latest on Johnston before the Chargers play the Denver Broncos in Week 5.
From a fantasy football standpoint, even a low average draft position risk on Johnston was questionable. First-round status or not, Johnston has annually had drop issues and that’s continued, even with McDaniel in town.
Through four games, all losses, Johnston has caught just seven of his 18 targets for 108 yards. When he gets back to full strength, he still figures to fall behind McConkey and even the fast-rising Tre Harris on the depth chart.
Sunday against the Broncos, though, the Chargers are a mess at wideout. McConkey is unlikely to play and speedy rookie Brenen Thompson has already been ruled out. That leaves Tre Harris as the No. 1 with deep depth names like Marquez Valdes-Scantling possibly seeing some action in Herbert’s offense.
In fact, things are so bad at wideout that the Chargers had to sign wideout Theo Wease to the active roster before the game, making room for him by shifting star offensive tackle Rashawn Slater to injured reserve.

title: Is Ladd McConkey Playing Today? Broncos vs. Chargers Updates for Week 5
full_text:
Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey is once again one of the most interesting injury stories to watch.
This time, it’s McConkey injury watch as his team heads for a Week 5 showdown against the Denver Broncos. The Chargers star attempted to play through an injury last week, suffering another setback that had him, alongside major names like Joe Alt, all over the final injury report this week.
Here’s a live-updating look at the latest on McConkey before the Chargers play the Broncos
Another injury disaster for Ladd McConkey, both in the real football realm and in the fantasy football landscape.
McConkey, while fighting through what has been at least three different injuries now, still sits second on the Chargers in receiving through four games with 12 catches for 183 yards and one score.
McConkey continues to be a no-go in the fantasy football realm despite likely high average draft position because Mike McDaniel’s anticipated strong Chargers offense with Justin Herbert has instead been a massive flop.
With McConkey likely out, the Chargers will hope that Quentin Johnston is healthy enough to go and that Tre Harris can keep developing on the fly as a possible No. 1 target in McDaniel’s offense.
Against an AFC West foe and based on what the Chargers have put on tape so far, though, it’s probably best to not expect much from the offensive depth chart at all, especially if McConkey isn’t out there to keep defenses honest.

title: Predicting Chargers' Starters vs Broncos for NFL Week 5: Is There Anyone Left Alive?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-4, banged up and are already plugging roster holes with practice squad elevations and free agents off the street... it is only Week 5. They welcome in their division rivals the Denver Broncos to SoFi Stadium in week five with the hopes to snag their first win of the season.
The Chargers' 2026 season is barely breathing. The anemic offense showed signs of life in the second half against the Seahawks in week four. There is a path forward for them to save their season but any hope has to start with getting a win over the Broncos. It will be a tall task with their injuries.
Quarterback: Justin Herbert Running back: Omarion Hampton Fullback: Alec Ingold Tight end: Oronde Gadsden II Wide receiver: Tre' Harris Wide receiver: Marquez Valdez-Scantling Left tackle: Branson Taylor Left guard: Logan Taylor (R) Center: Jake Slaughter (R) Right guard: Cole Strange Right tackle: Travis Burke (R)
The Chargers will be sending out a makeshift offensive unit of backups and new roster additions to face off against the Denver Broncos. Los Angeles lost four of their starters on offense against the Seattle Seahawks including left tackle Rashawn Slater who just underwent tight-rope surgery to help a high ankle sprain heal.
Right tackle Joe Alt is also out of this game as is wide receiver Quentin Johnston who suffered a chest injury, likely on a 44 yard reception where he leaped into the air and took a free fall and landed flat on his back. Left guard Trevor Penning, who already was the Chargers' fifth option at left guard since training camp, was placed on injured reserve as well.
Second-year offensive lineman Branson Taylor will make his 2026 debut against Denver after being sidelined for the first four weeks after suffering an injury in the preseason and was placed on IR to start the season. In addition to the return of Taylor, veteran Daniel Brunskill was signed to the practice squad earlier this week and he was elevated for the game despite being with the team only a few days. He has experience at all five positions but has the majority of his career snaps at right guard and center.
The wide receiver room is absolutely barren with Johnston out and McConkey likely a game-time decision but limited if he plays. Tre' Harris recent roster addition Marquez Valdez-Scantling and Derius Davis will be joined by newly signed receiver from the practice squad Theo Wease Jr.

title: Jerry Jeudy Trade Rumors Heating Up: Chargers Should Target Browns Receiver
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers should be looking at every possible way to improve their offense, and Jerry Jeudy is a name worth considering. The Cleveland Browns receiver has become a subject of trade speculation, creating a potential opportunity to add another weapon for Justin Herbert.
NFL insider Adam Shefter revealed that Juedy could possibly be up for grabs at the trade deadline.
Sometimes, finding a player who needs a fresh start can be just as valuable as bringing in an established star. Jeudy has already shown that he can be productive in the NFL. The question is whether he can return to that level of play and become a more consistent part of an offense.
For a Chargers team looking for ways to get more out of its passing game, that is something worth investigating.
One of the biggest advantages of having a quarterback like Herbert is the ability to attack defenses in different ways. He can make difficult throws, push the ball downfield and give his receivers opportunities to make plays. But even a talented quarterback can benefit from having more options available when a defense takes away his first read.
That is where Jeudy could become an interesting addition.
The receiver recorded 1,229 receiving yards during the 2024 season with Cleveland, proving that he is capable of producing big numbers. His production fell to 602 yards in 2025, and he has gotten off to a quiet start this season. The coaching staff would have to determine how Jeudy fits into the existing offense. Also, how many opportunities he could realistically receive and whether he would improve the team’s current group of receivers.
That is why the asking price should be a major factor. If Cleveland demands a significant draft pick, Los Angeles should carefully consider whether the potential reward justifies the investment. If the Browns are willing to negotiate a more affordable deal, the conversation becomes much more interesting. We all should have some what of an idea what he is worth, which in my opinion it’s totally worth it.
His recent production shows that there are legitimate concerns, and the Chargers would need to be comfortable accepting that risk. Still, the potential upside deserves attention. Jeudy is not an unproven prospect who has never demonstrated what he can do at the professional level.
Ladd McConkey seems to be the only bright spot to this core, based on the last four games. Bringing in another playmaker could elevate the others purley based on competition. The bottom line is simply that the Chargers need help, and this could potentially be a perfect fit.

title: Chargers Confidence Meter: Does the Losing Cycle Finally End Against the Broncos?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers need a win that gives analysts and fans a reason to believe again.
Obviously potential has never been the only question surrounding this team. The bigger concern is whether the Bolts can put everything together when it matters most. Sunday’s divisional matchup against the Denver Broncos gives them another opportunity to prove they can compete.
Of course no divisional matchup is ever taken lightly, so there is always pressure when two AFC West rivals meet. Especially when a team is trying to change the direction of its season.
Denver will not make things easy. They have their own reasons to take advantage of this matchup. These type of games often come down to execution, discipline, and which team makes the fewest mistakes when the pressure starts building.
The image of Justin Herbert trying to escape Denver’s pass rush tells an important part of the story. The Chargers have a quarterback capable of making difficult throws and extending plays, but there is only so much one player can do when the opposition consistently disrupts the offense.
Herbert’s ability is not the issue. The challenge is giving him enough time and support to operate effectively. When defenders get into the backfield before routes develop, even a quarterback with his arm talent can find himself fighting an uphill battle.
The Bolts need to establish better offensive rhythm and avoid putting their quarterback in situations where every possession requires something extraordinary.
At the same time, Herbert has to remain patient. Not every play needs to become a highlight, and forcing a difficult throw can turn a promising drive into a wasted opportunity. The best version of this offense is one where he can make an impact without feeling like the entire game rests on his shoulders. That responsibility also falls on the coaching staff and the rest of the roster. They need their running game, protection, and playmakers to contribute. If the offense becomes too predictable, that elite defense will have more opportunities to dictate the pace.
Defensively, they must find a way to make life uncomfortable for Bo Nix without giving away easy opportunities. Winning third downs, limiting explosive plays, and creating pressure at the right moments could make a significant difference. The team cannot afford to spend the entire afternoon trying to recover from mistakes.
According to NFL senior insider Adam Schefter, Sean Payton will see an increase in play-calling moving forward. Which makes things for the defense way more complicated.
My biggest concern heading into this matchup is consistency. The Bolts need to demonstrate that they can respond when things do not go according to plan. Every team looks capable when the offense is moving and the defense is making stops. The real question is what happens after a turnover, a stalled drive, or an opponent’s scoring run.
That is when a team shows its character.
The Broncos are a serious divisional test, and the Bolts need to treat them accordingly. If they can put together a complete performance, it has a chance to change the conversation. Until then, questions about consistency will continue to follow this team.

title: NFL Trade Rumors Paint a Khalil Mack Bears Trade at Good Price for Chargers
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers sit 0-4 with an injury disaster on their hands ahead of what could be an 0-6 mark by the bye week.
Understandably, it’s time to talk about doing right by Khalil Mack and trading him .
Not a fun topic for Chargers fans. But given the state of things and the fact Mack might be on his final season in the NFL, most probably accept it by now.
Naturally, of the likely Mack trade landing spots , the Chicago Bears are by far the most sensible.
And if a rumor that suggests the asking price on a Mack trade is true, the Chargers might as well go ahead and do it.
The Chargers don’t have much leverage in a Mack trade. They’re bad and he’s older, so even desperate teams won’t cough up too much.
That tracks with new buzz from The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones , who spoke with a general manager and one assistant general manager in the NFL who pinned Mack’s trade value at about roughly a fifth-round pick.
Jones added this: “But Khalil Mack to Chicago is something multiple league sources told me makes the most sense if both teams continue on their respective trajectories.”
For the Chargers…might as well. They’re asking a team to take on about $5 million in remaining contract with Mack if he gets moved this week or next, too.
The Chargers probably aren’t going to find a sell-high moment better than this with Mack. He’s playing really good ball right now amid the chaos. And to their credit, the Chargers front office is pretty good at finding hits in the fifth round like Oronde Gadsden, Tarheeb Still and Cam Hart in recent years.
If the Chargers keep losing, the focus needs to shift to the future, anyway. Tuli Tuipulotu is the new heart of the pass-rush for the long-term and needs a new contract, while Akheem Mesidor is a first-round rookie who could use all the developmental snaps.
Again, not a super-fun topic for Chargers fans. But gently blowing up the roster (before potentially the coaching staff too) means selling off what they can and investing heavily in things beyond this season.
That includes Mack, who deserves a chance to go compete for a Super Bowl somewhere.

title: 3 Matchups Will Decide Chargers' Week 5 Game vs. Denver Broncos
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers  face a tough battle ahead against the Denver Broncos  in week five. The Chargers' season, currently standing at 0-4,  is on life support and any hope of a turnaround starts with taking down their AFC West rivals.
Los Angeles and Denver will face off in a battle of the backups with both teams facing significant injuries. The Chargers have more overall injuries by comparison but both will have to make adjustments to their gameplan.
As the Chargers fight to save their season and get back on track, several matchups will be critical for the outcome of this game. Let's dive into the most important on-field battles and how they will impact the game.
The Chargers are down at least wide receivers Quentin Johnston, Brenen Thompson and likely Ladd McConkey, who has not practiced all week. The Chargers simply do not have the bodies to attack heavily through the air. The run game will become a major factor for Los Angeles success.
The problem facing the Chargers is that the Broncos know that they have to run the ball. Denver's linebackers are downhill enforcers. Both Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad have a combined 23 defensive stops but also have a combined total of ten missed tackles on the season. The Chargers running backs have to forced missed tackles this week and find success to challenge the linebackers and get them triggering downhill to open up playaction.
The Chargers will be down tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt in this matchup. If they activate Branson Taylor from injured reserve, he will likely slide into one of the tackle spots while rookie Travis Burke will hold down the other. If Taylor is not activated, rookie Logan Taylor will likely slide out to tackle. The inexperience at tackle against edge rushers like Nik Bonitto is not ideal.
The Chargers tackles will need to own the run game against the edge rushers and reduce known passing situations. The Broncos top two edge rushers in terms of snap count, Bonitto and Jonah Elliss, both check in under 250lbs and can be attacked in the run game. If tight end Charlie Kolar makes his way back to the field this week, expect he and the tackles to be heavily involved in the the off tackle run game.
The Chargers defensive line has been one of few bright spots so far this season. The Broncos offensive line is talented but Denver's offense has been in a funk, leading to head coach Sean Payton taking offensive play calling duties back from offensive coordinator Davis Webb.
Quarterback Bo Nix has an average time to throw of 2.93 seconds ranking him near the bottom of the NFL. This indicates that Nix is holding onto the ball but has not been throwing it deep. He has the second-lowest average depth of target in the NFL ahead of only the trio of quarterbacks from the Atlanta Falcons. If this trend continues, the Chargers defensive line will get pass-rushing opportunities and they need to get home and disrupt Nix.
The defensive line will need to keep the Broncos rushing attack in check to ensure more pass rushing opportunities. Broncos top running back JK Dobbins is currently rushing for a career low average of 3.5 yards per carry and career low in yards after contact per attempt. The defensive line can't let the running backs get going and need to challenge Bo Nix, who will also be without emerging wide receiver Pat Bryant who was placed on injured reserve this week.

title: What is State of Chargers' Offensive Line Post Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater Injury News?
full_text:
It is Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Los Angeles Chargers are already back to the same spot they seemingly have been stuck in since the inception of the franchise. They are down a plethora of offensive linemen, with always the best players being held out due to injury.
With that, the Chargers' injury report was as long as a CVS receipt, with offensive linemen being the bulk of what was listed ahead of the Week 5 matchup against the Denver Broncos and their elite defense.
With all the injuries, what is the current state of the Chargers offensive line?
LT: Logan Taylor / Branson Taylor * LG: Alex Harkey C: Jake Slaughter RG: Cole Strange RT: Travis Burke
This is the expected starting group after Rashawn Slater was placed on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. Joe Alt is listed as OUT with a neck injury, coupled with Kayode Awosika and Trevor Penning also being out with a fibula injury and a concussion, respectively.
*It should be noted that Branson Taylor is officially listed as questionable, as he is coming off injured reserve. If he were to play, I would expect him to slot in as the left tackle, allowing Logan Taylor to play left guard in place of Alex Harkey.
This starting group should not instill any sort of confidence in fans or even the rest of the team. They will also be going up against a Denver Broncos defensive unit that has always given the Chargers fits, even when their OL was in better shape. Slaughter and Burke should be solid in their roles, given that they have shown enough this season to be NFL-caliber players. As for the rest of the group...we can only hope to see flashes of NFL-level play to allow for hope for the Chargers OL depth in the future.
Jacob Spomer will serve as the team's backup center option, if Slaughter were to go out or were to need to move to a guard spot. Spomer was arguably the team's best UDFA, being one of few making the team's final 53 man roster.
The Chargers will also have two more bodies that they are expected to elevate off the practice squad, those names being Laekin Vakalahi and the recently acquired Daniel Brunskill. Vakalahi is the Bolts' International Player Pathway individual who has raw athletic ability but needs much more time on task, likely making him the last-resort type of option for the team.
As for Brunskill, he is a long-time NFL veteran who has experience in the Mike McDaniel offensive scheme, starting five games for the Miami Dolphins and McDaniel in 2025. He is expected to be the first off the bench, knowing how to play all five spots across the OL, even if he was only signed three days ago .

title: 3 Storylines I'm Watching Most in Chargers' Week 5 Matchup vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are not dead yet, but their 2026 season is barely breathing. Justin Herbert and the Chargers showed that they still have fight left in them in the second half of their week four battle in Seattle against the Seahawks. There is a path forward for them to save their season but it all starts against the Denver Broncos at SoFi Stadium.
Los Angeles has been off to a rough start to 2026. Expectations entering the season were sky high and their struggles on the offensive side of the ball have been shocking to everyone around the NFL. If the Chargers have any hope of saving their season, it starts with the offense finding its identity.
Entering into the week five matchup against the Denver Broncos, the Chargers are dealing with a substantial amount of injuries and nearly their entire starting offensive line is out. As they try to fight to stay alive in 2026, let's dive into some of the key storylines of this game that I will be closely watching on game day.
The Los Angeles Chargers lost three out five starting offensive linemen in week four against the Seahawks and left guard Trevor Penning was already the fifth option at left guard looking back to training camp. The Chargers hope to activate Branson Taylor from injured reserve for this game but even if he returns to the lineup, they will still be sending out at least two rookies and potentially up to four to face the Denver Broncos.
The lack of experience and time on task will absolutely affect the play calling and available play calls for offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. A limited play sheet may be the best-case scenario for the offense to catch their breath and find a groove. The Chargers started moving the ball against the Seahawks in the second half of week four by keeping it relatively simple.
The Broncos run defense is giving up 4.1 yards per carry and are second to last in the NFL in defensive epa against the run. The Chargers enter Sunday down multiple receivers on top of the offensive line injuries, establishing the run is an absolute must for Mike McDaniel.
If the Chargers can establish the run, it will help the inexperienced offensive line face a very good front seven from the Broncos but it should also open up the play action passing attack and help Tre' Harris and whichever receiver is left available to play. Mike McDaniel has to nail the game plan to help out this offensive line.
The Chargers offensive weapons in the passing game outside of Ladd McConkey have been inconsistent. Harris and Johnston both came up clutch in the comeback attempt against Seattle and someone needs to carry that energy and momentum forward.
Johnston and Brenen Thompson are already ruled out for this week and McConkey may not play either which leaves Harris, Marquez Valdez-Scantling and Derius Davis as the only healthy receivers. Practice squad call ups for Greg Jennings and Theo Wease Jr are likely and tight end Oronde Gadsden should be involved as well.
The Chargers are leading the NFL in false start penalties and have consistently shot themselves in the foot with negative plays from either penalties or just from negative results. Mike McDaniel has not yet dramatically altered his play calling to adjust to the struggles. The offensive line that will be trotting out his Sunday should force his hand.
The Chargers will be facing the Broncos missing a significant chunk of their starting lineup and even if some of them play through injuries, they will have had limited to no practice all week. Complex plays and curveball snap counts should be dialed back.

title: Sunday Morning Rams Notebook: Sean McVay Linked to Amazon, Myles Garrett Update, and More
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 5 looking to build some momentum after their comeback victory over the Philadelphia Eagles. At 2-2, the Rams have an opportunity to get above .500 for the first time this season when they host the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football.
Several stories have emerged this week that are worth exploring further, including Myles Garrett’s return timeline and whether the Rams will be a team to watch ahead of the trade deadline. Let’s get into this week’s Sunday Morning Rams Notebook
It seems as if almost every year there is some speculation around Sean McVay leaving coaching and going into broadcasting. The door opened once again recently when details emerged from the new contract that Kirk Herbstreit signed with Amazon Prime.
According to Andrew Marchand from The Athletic , there is a clause in Herbstreit’s contract that would allow the network to move on from him if Sean McVay were to become available.
“The terms give Amazon flexibility to move on if one of its top targets, like Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay, becomes available, according to sources briefed on the decision who were not authorized to speak publicly,” wrote Marchand.
There is some history with McVay and Amazon Prime. Back in 2022, Prime tried to recruit McVay after the Rams went 5-12 and had a disastrous season. According to Marchand, Al Michaels preferred McVay over Herbstreit. However, McVay signed a new contract with the Rams and has remained with the team for the last four seasons.
With that said, McVay was close to leaving coaching for media after the 2022 season.McVay said this himself last year when he went on “Bussin’ With the Boys .”
"I almost quit coaching," McVay said. "And you can use the narrative that I was gonna go to media or whatever. But the truth would have been, I was quitting. I couldn't handle the losing. It was almost like a scarlet letter. I mean, there was moments…I was like counting down the days for that season to be over. Like, what a fraud."
There is some speculation that McVay won’t coach forever. He’s only 40 years old and has been coaching for 10 years. McVay has two kids with his wife Veronika Khomyn, and it’s possible that he leaves coaching at some point to get a better work-life balance.
Still, that doesn’t seem imminent, and the clause in Herbstreit’s contract appears to be more about the network protecting itself and maintaining flexibility. It’s possible that McVay leaves at some point. He could potentially tie himself to Matthew Stafford and leave once the Rams’ quarterback retires.
Mike Sando from The Athletic noted that some who know McVay suspect from afar that something has been bothering him this season. At the same time, with McVay’s input, the Rams just drafted a rookie quarterback in April to take over for Stafford. All of the McVay in the media rumors remain speculation at this point.
McVay was supposed to have an update for the media on Myles Garrett on Thursday, but didn’t. The result was some panic that the Rams were hiding more information than they were letting on when it came to Garrett. It was an understandable conclusion given how the Rams have handled the injury since July.
This trade has been a disaster for the Rams. https://t.co/VdXC1OzpJQ
However, McVay’s tone on Thursday when it was brought up was that he genuinely forgot. There were three days between McVay’s first media availability this week on Monday and when he spoke again on Thursday. The Rams’ head coach came ready with an update during Saturday’s media availability .
“He’s making good progress, but what I will say is he's not ready to say whether we'll open that window or not,” said McVay. “It's week to week in terms of how he feels, but I would say it's more likely that we do not start his clock next week.”
McVay stressed the importance of not just putting Garrett in a position to play, but in a position to return to performance. In Week 1, Garrett was in a position to play, but after the game he told the media that he didn’t feel like himself. The Rams will continue playing it safe with Garrett, which is how they’ve generally handled the situation since July.
While Garrett is eligible to return to practice next week ahead of the Rams’ game against the Arizona Cardinals, it doesn’t appear that he will. If you’ve followed our coverage here on Rams On SI, that shouldn’t come as a surprise.
A few weeks ago, it was reported by NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport that Garrett was given a six-week timeline following his arthroscopic knee surgery. However, last week, Jonathan Jones of The Athletic r eported that Garrett could return for Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Since the beginning, Garrett has been determined to beat the timeline, but that doesn’t mean the Rams aren’t going to continue erring on the side of caution. Four weeks always seemed optimistic, with five weeks being more realistic, and six weeks being a worst-case scenario.
We’ll have to wait and see what happens with Garrett, but waiting another week to open his practice window provides the Rams with more flexibility. It wouldn’t be surprising to see the Rams open his practice window ahead of the game against the Raiders, see how his knee responds, and then decide whether to activate him to the roster. Much like with Aaron Donald on the Commissioner’s Exempt List to begin the season, the Rams have some flexibility.
The NFL trade deadline is about a month away, but don’t expect the Rams to make any big splashes. Unless the situation drastically changes, it would be a surprise if they made a significant move. There are two main reasons for this, along with how the Rams’ front office and coaching staff may view their situation.
After signing Eric Kendricks to the practice squad this week, the Rams only have around $981k. That’s almost half as much as the next closest team. That little cap space makes it very difficult for the Rams to do anything via trade. It might not even be possible for the Rams to make it through the rest of the season on that number. At some point, they may have to rework a contract to open up some cap space, but their current financial situation makes a trade unlikely.
Additionally, the Rams don’t have the draft capital available to make a big trade. While the Rams have a second-round pick in 2027, if they were to move that, they wouldn’t pick until the fourth round. It’s possible they could look to move picks in 2028 like the Baltimore Ravens did when they acquired Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles last week. However, the Rams don’t have a second-round pick, and moving their first would put them in a difficult spot.
It’s possible the Rams don’t see their roster in a spot where they need to make a trade to get over the top. The front office and coaching staff will likely see Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson returning from injured reserve as in-season additions.
An argument can be made that the Rams need a third wide receiver, but they will see Ferguson as a player to fill that role in the offense. This isn’t to say that a trade won’t happen or that the Rams won’t explore anything. However, it does remain unlikely.
Earlier this week, Mike Ditka passed away at the age of 86. While I never got the pleasure of meeting Ditka, he was a big part of my NFL Sundays growing up. I remember watching Mike Ditka on ESPN’s Sunday NFL Countdown, which was a must-watch for me on Sunday mornings. I’ll always remember Ditka as a no-nonsense personality who wasn’t afraid to speak what was on his mind.

title: Rams Week 5 Injury Report: Aaron Donald Among Three Starters Set to Return vs. Bills
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to get multiple starters back as they head into Week 5 to take on the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football. After missing last week, tight end Colby Parkinson, cornerback Jaylen Watson, and defensive lineman Aaron Donald all look to be ready to go for Monday’s game. The only player with a game designation on Saturday’s injury report was safety Quentin Lake, who is listed as questionable.
Lake didn’t practice on Thursday or Friday with a hip injury, but was upgraded to limited on Saturday. There wasn’t too much concern with Lake this week with the Rams just being smart with him given his workload this season.
“He got it when he fell backwards on something so it's a weird deal, but he's doing good,” said McVay this week. “We're just being smart with him. He's played so many snaps. We just wanted to be smart.”
Edge rusher Josaiah Stewart also didn’t practice earlier in the week, but was limited on Saturday. Stewart wasn’t given a game designation and presumably will be good to play. The same can be said about linebacker Nate Landman, who has been banged up over the last couple of weeks. Landman was a full participant on Saturday.
While Donald didn’t practice on Saturday, that has been his routine this season. All indications are that Donald will play. Speaking to the media this week, Donald said, “I'm planning to play this week.”
The Rams missed Colby Parkinson last week, as they were unable to utilize their usual 13 personnel packages with three tight ends. Without Parkinson, the Rams utilized 11 personnel at an 88 percent rate , which was their highest since Week 5 of last season. Cornerback Jaylen Watson is also set to make his return. Josh Wallace played well in his absence, but getting Watson back will provide a big boost to the Rams’ secondary.
“They're good to go," McVay said.
On the Bills’ side, defensive lineman Ed Oliver and wide receiver Joshua Palmer have already been ruled out. The Rams will certainly be watching the status of wide receiver DJ Moore before Monday’s game. Moore is officially listed as questionable along with defensive lineman Landman Jackson and cornerback Dee Alford.
The Rams have struggled to find consistency through the first four weeks of the season, but getting healthier should help as they look to build on last week's win over the Eagles. With Donald, Parkinson, and Watson expected to return, the Rams will have several key pieces back in place for one of their toughest matchups of the season.

title: Rams Coaches Detail Biggest Challenges of Facing Josh Allen and Bills
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams a re set to take on the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5. Heading into the season, both teams were seen as Super Bowl contenders. It wouldn’t be surprising if this ended up being the Super Bowl matchup when all is said and done.
However, heading into Week 5, both teams are still trying to find their rhythm. The Bills are 3-1, but haven’t played well the last two weeks. They turned the ball over five times and somehow still managed to beat the Los Angeles Chargers. Meanwhile, the Rams have been up and down and have yet to get above .500. A win on Monday night could propel either team into a winning streak.
Throughout the week, the Rams’ coaching staff and players have spoken about some of the challenges that the Bills will present.
When the Rams and Bills played in 2024, Josh Allen threw for 342 yards and three touchdowns as he went on to win MVP. Allen not only has one of the best arms in the NFL, but he’s also a great athlete with the ability to make plays with his legs.
Allen has 1,039 yards passing this season to go with six touchdowns and three interceptions. His 0.18 EPA per play ranks fifth in the NFL. While the Rams have the No. 2 overall pass defense, Allen will provide a good test. Over the last three weeks, the Rams have faced Jameis Winston, Bo Nix, and Jalen Hurts. Allen will give the Rams their biggest test since playing Brock Purdy in Week 1.
“You can see he's obviously one of the ultimate competitors in this league,” said defensive coordinator Chris Shula. “He's a great quarterback standing there playing in the pocket. Then, you can see all the off-schedule plays that he makes. He's one of the best players, if not the best player, in the NFL right now.”
The Rams are set to get Aaron Donald back against the Bills as well, which should help against Allen.. Donald missed last week with a sore back, but is set to return for Monday night’s game against the Bills.
Donald has played against the Bills three times, but only twice has he faced Josh Allen. In 2022, the Rams lost to the Bills 31-10 in the season opener. Donald had one sack in that game. In 2020, Donald had a vintage performance, recording two sacks with a forced fumble and fumble recovery.
“He's a playmaker,” said Donald. “He's a different type of player. I call him a futuristic ‘Big Ben’, more athletic, harder to tackle, a lot faster, able to move a lot differently. He can hurt you in a lot of different ways. He's not easy to take down. He's a playmaker. That's all you can say. You have to find ways to keep him in the box, make sure when you get your hands on him, make sure you get him down to the ground. Don’t let him stiff arm you and be able to look downfield and throw a touchdown. He’s a guy that you have to worry about and have to try to find a way to affect [him].”
Back in 2020, the Rams previously had interest in Jim Leonhard, but ended up hiring Brandon Staley instead. Leonhard spent the last two years on the Denver Broncos’ coaching staff before he was brought in as the defensive coordinator for the Bills this offseason under Joe Brady.
The Bills currently rank 29th in defensive EPA and have especially struggled against the pass. They’ve allowed 0.11 EPA per pass, which ranks 26th in the NFL. Over the first four weeks of the season, the Rams have struggled to find some consistency in the passing game . Playing the Bills could provide them with an opportunity to get things back on track.
“I have a lot of respect for him, his career, his background, type of mentality that he has in general,” said Rams offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase. “You can see that all over their defense with their ability to challenge you with different looks, their ability to move guys into different spots and honestly have an attacking style. They do a great job up front. Their front makes their squad go. If you don't take care of those guys both in the run game and in the pass game, you can end up in some tough spots. As much as you can, you want to stay on track and not let those guys be able to set a rush and be able to pin their ears back.”
If the Rams are going to win this game, they’ll need their top two wide receivers in Davante Adams and Puka Nacua to step up and play well. With Nacua out of the lineup in Weeks 2 and 3, Adams played like he was in his prime, recording back-to-back 100 yard games. The Rams have yet to get both players going in the same game this season.
Last week, Romeo Doubs had success with the New England Patriots when facing off against Maxwell Hairston.Doubs scored two touchdowns on Hairston, and the Rams may try to get a similar matchup with Adams. However, this will be Adams’ first time facing a defense coordinated by Leonhard, and he spoke about that challenge on Friday.
“Watching as much tape as possible, whether that's stuff that they've done against us, this season, or things that they've done in the past,” said Adams. “Also, not getting too wrapped up in that because come gametime, you have to react to the coverages or whatever they decide to throw at you. You can get immersed in everything and think you have it figured out, but you still have to react once the call is made and once the play starts. I like to have a decent idea of what they like to do. Then go and roll with the punches from there during the game.”
