title: Rams Midweek Report: Searching for Consistency, Myles Garrett Update, Trade Deadline Outlook
full_text:
A big theme this week for the Los Angeles Rams has been whether they can find some consistency . The Rams have the No. 2 offense and No. 2 defense, but the 32nd-ranked special teams unit. They have a top-five offense but are just 19th in points per game. They have a top-5 offense, but are just 19th in points per game.
If the Rams are going to become the team that many expected coming into the season, they need to find consistency. This is a team that’s been penalized 21 times over the last two weeks, the most in a two-game stretch under head coach Sean McVay. They have a -5 turnover differential through four games, which is tied for 28th in the NFL. Untimely turnovers, penalties, and special teams gaffes have been a recurring problem for this team.
“I'm interested to see how we can play cleaner football,” said McVay on Monday. “We have to play better. We have to consistently do it in all three phases and we have to earn the right to play better quality football. We have to all coach better too.”
The Rams are doing things that we aren’t accustomed to seeing from a McVay-coached team. That’s what makes the penalties and untimely mistakes so baffling at times . McVay can become pass-happy at times, but over 100 pass attempts in a two-game stretch is unheard of even for him. Sunday marked the first time since 2012 that Stafford had 50 or more attempts in back-to-back games.
Through four weeks, Matthew Stafford has an EPA per pass of -0.01. At this time last year, it was 0.15. Stafford starting the season slowly is nothing unusual, but his mistakes have cost the Rams in big moments or put them in difficult positions.
“Definitely room for improvement. There have been some really bright moments and some stuff I'm really proud of and stuff that I definitely wish I could take back to help us be in a better position to win games,” said Stafford. “I want to do everything I can to put our team in the best position to succeed. I've done that sometimes this year and other times I have not. I want to make sure that I do that at a more consistent clip moving forward.”
Given that teams no longer play their starters in the preseason, there is some belief that it can take those first three or four weeks for starters to get up to speed. The Rams have now played four games. There are no more excuses.
Coming into the season, this was a team with high expectations, and they have yet to really play up to that level. A lot of that is because of the lack of consistency. After coming back from 10 points in the fourth quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles, the Rams seemed to find something. They’ll have a chance on Monday night to show whether they can carry that over or if it was just another flash in the pan.
"It's that time of the year where you're establishing your identity both schematically and the mentality that you play with," said offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase. "There are things that we can do to take care of stuff that we can control so that's been an area of emphasis for us, especially this week."
Prior to the season, the Rams placed a pair of offensive linemen in Keagen Trost and Justin Dedich on injured reserve. Trost injured his hamstring in the first preseason game and Dedich managed a hand injury all summer. With the Rams having played four games, both players are eligible to come off of injured reserve . However, it doesn’t appear as if the Rams are in any rush to do so.
“Those guys, they could,” said McVay. “We could open that up, but that's not a conversation that we've had at this point.”
It makes sense for the Rams to hold off for now, as both players are depth pieces and not immediate starters. The Rams only have eight injured reserve return designations to use and they are already set to use two on Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson. There’s a chance one or both are activated at some point, but given the current health of the offensive line, the Rams are waiting.
McVay was asked on Thursday whether Garrett will return to practice after his four-week injured reserve window. Monday night will mark Garrett’s fourth game that he’s missed and he’ll be eligible to return.
“I'm not sure yet,” said McVay. “I know that the rehab is progressing well. He's looked good in the meetings.”
The Rams’ head coach had previously mentioned that he would have more of an update, but that was not the case on Thursday. With that said, based on reports that exist , the Rams remain hopeful that Garrett will return next week, but Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders is more realistic. Garrett had a six-week timeline, which would have put him on track to return in Week 8 against the Los Angeles Chargers, but that was more of a worst-case scenario. Garrett has been progressing ahead of that.
Prior to Sunday’s game against the Eagles, the Rams placed Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve . Just when Ferguson was starting to have a positive impact on the offense and become a featured piece, a medial ankle sprain has forced him to miss time.
Ferguson will have to miss four games, which would put his return in Week 8 against the Chargers. Based on what McVay said on the Coach McVay Show this week with JB Long, it doesn’t seem like Ferguson will miss any more time beyond that.
“He’ll be back. He’ll be ready to go after those four weeks,” McVay said.
I wouldn’t expect the Rams to be active at the trade deadline. That doesn’t mean they won’t make a move, but it would be very difficult for them to do anything significant. It’s possible the Rams will see Myles Garrett’s return and getting Terrance Ferguson back as in-season additions.
There are a few things to note here. The Rams currently only have around $981,000 in cap space. That’s by far the lowest in the NFL. It would be nearly impossible for them to take on another contract at that number. TThe Rams also don’t have a lot of draft capital to send away. They don’t have a first- or third-round pick next year. If they moved that second-round pick, they wouldn’t select until the fourth round. Additionally, they don’t have a second-round pick in 2028. While the Rams could use a third wide receiver, it just isn’t something that will be in the cards.
It’s certainly possible that the Rams will beat the Bills on Monday night . The Bills are dealing with injuries in the secondary, which will provide the Rams an opportunity to get something going in the passing game. However, the Bills are coming off of a loss last week and will be ready to play a clean game.
A loss to the Bills isn’t the worst thing. That would put the Rams at 2-3 with two of their three losses against AFC opponents. The Rams can ‘get right’ against the Cardinals in Week 6 and then the schedule lightens up. It’s possible the Rams could rattle off six straight wins before playing the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 13. A Week 14 matchup against the 49ers will then provide an opportunity to avenge their loss in Week 1.
The Rams signed Eric Kendricks this week, which came as a bit of a surprise. While some have speculated that Kendricks is a special teams addition, it may have been more than that. Some of Kendricks’ early role may come on special teams. The Rams have already used two of Eli Neal’s three roster elevations. Grant Stuard is also dealing with an injury this week.
However, at 34, Kendricks likely wouldn’t have signed on simply to play special teams. He’s beyond that point of his career. His addition will give the Rams some flexibility to manage Nate Landman’s injury if needed, while also allowing Kendricks to rotate in alongside Omar Speights. He may have a bigger role once he settles in.
Eric Kendricks is joining the Los Angeles Rams! 🔥🍿 pic.twitter.com/CKNjIj1sO0
On Friday, several players had their designations upgraded. Defensive lineman Aaron Donald was limited on Thursday, but was a full participant on Friday. The same can be said about tight end Colby Parkinson. The Rams will be glad to have both players back against the Bills.

title: 5 Keys to Victory for the Rams Against the Bills in Week 5
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to host the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium on Monday Night Football in Week 5. With a win, the Rams could get above .500 for the first time this season . Over the first month, the Rams have been scrapping to get by, and Monday night will provide a good test against a team many consider to be a Super Bowl contender. Here are five keys to victory for the Rams to beat the Bills.
Under Joe Brady, the Buffalo Bills have had their most successful run game under Josh Allen. James Cook has a 52.9 percent rushing success rate. Cook’s 11.4 percent explosive run rate is also the highest in the NFL.
For the Rams defense to operate the way it wants to, stopping the run is key. It’s something that they didn’t do in Week 1. However, over the last three weeks, they’ve been much better. Their -0.2 EPA per rush allowed in that span ranks sixth in the NFL. The Rams need to be able to contain James Cook and limit the explosive runs. That will also limit what the Bills can do in the passing game with their tight ends in heavy personnel.
Last week, Kyren Williams became the first Rams running back since Todd Gurley to have at least 10 carries and 10 receptions in a game. The Rams have struggled to find a third wide receiver in the offense with Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve. It’s possible that Williams can be that third option in the passing game.
The Bills could provide another opportunity to get Williams involved. Defensively, the Bills have allowed the third-most targets to running backs with 21 receptions. Their 162 receiving yards allowed to running backs are the seventh-most and they’ve allowed three receiving touchdowns. This is an area where Williams showed last week that he can be a threat in this area, and the Rams may need him to contribute again.
For as solid as the Bills have been at tackle in the past, that hasn’t been the case this year. Dion Dawkins allowed a seven percent pressure rate last year and that’s up to 12 percent in 2026. For the most part, Dawkins has struggled this season.
#Patriots rookie Gabe Jacas's bull-rush puts five-time Pro Bowl LT Dion Dawkins on the ground. pic.twitter.com/8Wu10Z0Tle
This is a matchup that the Rams will have to win if they’re going to have a chance in this game. Byron Young has one of the highest pressure rates at 18.8 percent among edge rushers. That ranks 10th in the NFL. He also ranks eighth with 18 pressures. Without Myles Garrett, the Rams need Young to continue taking over games as he did last week.
The Bills have struggled at cornerback this season as they’ve dealt with some injuries. However, it’s also just not a position group that’s played well. The Rams should have the advantage here throughout the game. Puka Nacua returned from injury last week, but the Rams will also need Davante Adams to play like he did in Weeks 2 and 3.
If the Rams can get Adams isolated against Maxwell Hairston a few times, that’s a matchup they can take advantage of and find success with. Romeo Doubs scored two touchdowns against Hairston last week. The Rams haven’t gotten the connection between Stafford and Adams going in the red zone yet this season. Monday night could provide an opportunity.
When in doubt, attack Maxwell Hairston. He’s been horrible Bench him. Put in Kani Walker pic.twitter.com/MW1ELJHLKq
For as much as fans will want the Rams to play man coverage, that’s simply not something they can do against Josh Allen. Allen has the ability to scramble for large gains, which are effective against man. Against man coverage, Allen has a 0.36 EPA per play, which is the sixth-best in the NFL. Against zone coverage, that drops by more than half to 0.17.
This isn’t to say that the Rams should stay away from man coverage altogether. However, Chris Shula will need to mix up his coverages and do so selectively. He’ll need to pick his spots and do the same when he opts to blitz. This will be a good test for Shula and the defense, who haven’t faced a true challenge since playing the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1.

title: Matchups the Rams Must Win to Beat the Bills on Monday Night Football
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams play the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in what should be one of the best games of the week. When these two teams have gotten together in the past, it usually comes down to a dramatic finish. Two of the last three games have been decided by three points or less. Here are three matchups that could decide the game between the Rams and Bills.
This season, the Rams have averaged 1.5 yards before contact in the run game, which is the sixth-most in the NFL. However, when Deone Walker is on the field for the Bills, teams have averaged 0.1 yards before contact compared to 1.8 when he’s not on the field. Walker has been a key piece on the Bills’ defense, and they are much better when he’s on the field. On all plays, the Bills average 5.2 yards per play compared to 6.2 when he’s off it.
Deone Walker lol I'm not fully convinced he knows what he's doing on a down-to-down basis... but this dude is massive and athletic lol some straight freakazoid reps pic.twitter.com/WM4b45MrHY
If the Rams are going to get the most out of Matthew Stafford on Monday, they need to be able to remain balanced in the run game. They also need to protect the pocket. That starts with Coleman Shelton, Steve Avila, and Kevin Dotson against Walker. Walker’s 20 impact plays rank third in the NFL among interior defensive linemen.
It’s no secret that the weakness of the Rams’ defense is at linebacker. The Bills utilize heavy tight end sets more than any other team in the NFL. This season, the Bills have utilized 12 personnel on 20 percent of their offensive snaps and 13 personnel on 26 percent of their offensive snaps. Out of 12 personnel, the Bills rank third with 0.31 offensive EPA per play.
While Dalton Kincaid may not be a featured piece of the Bills’ offense, when he gets involved, he can be successful in the pass game. The Bills could have a huge matchup advantage here with Kincaid against Omar Speights, who can struggle in coverage. Speights has allowed 1.51 yards per coverage snap this season, which ranks as the eighth-most in the NFL. Both of the Rams’ linebackers are better in the run game.
The Rams will need to be ready on the offensive line as the Bills have the personnel up front to take over a game. Despite having to throw more than 100 times over the last two weeks, the Rams have done well from a protection standpoint. The Rams held one of the better pass rushes in the NFL in check two weeks ago against the Denver Broncos. The Bills will provide another challenge.
NFL sack leaders through Week 4 Greg Rousseau        6.0 Dallas Turner            5.5 T.J. Watt                      4.5 Will Anderson Jr.     4.5 Mason Graham       4.0 pic.twitter.com/IcCI3R05IF
This season, the Bills have a 45.8 percent pressure rate, which is the fourth-highest in the NFL. It’s a group led by Greg Rousseau. His 24 pressures rank fourth in the NFL, despite him facing the sixth-most double teams. He also leads the NFL with six sacks. Warren McClendon has been good, but he certainly has his deficiencies.

full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to take on the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5. Coming into this game, the Rams are 2-2 after beating the Philadelphia Eagles last week, 24-20, and coming back from 10 points down in the fourth quarter. Meanwhile, the Bills lost their first game of the season, falling to the New England Patriots, 29-26.
Through the first four games of the season, the Rams have yet to truly find their identity. Matthew Stafford has been inconsistent and special teams remain an issue.Already two games behind in the NFC West, the Rams can’t afford to fall much further behind.
For as inconsistent as the Rams have been, the Bills have had their moments as well. They turned the ball over five times against the Los Angeles Chargers and somehow managed to win. The Bills’ defense has struggled early on, and Drake Maye had his first strong game of the season after not playing well in the first three games.
If there was ever a chance for the Rams to get it right on offense, it’s this game against the Bills. The Bills rank 26th in pass defense EPA per play. Additionally, their 48.2 percent pass defense success rate ranks 30th. This is a team that has struggled to stop opposing passing attacks. While the Rams will be without Terrance Ferguson, this could be a game for Stafford, Davante Adams, and Puka Nacua to take over.
Hairston has allowed just eight receptions on 19 targets this season, which is an improvement over his rookie season. However, last week, he struggled against Romeo Doubs on the outside. Doubs had six receptions for 58 yards and two touchdowns. Both of Doubs’ touchdowns came against Hairston.
Maxwell Hairston is having TROUBLE today against Romeo Doubs. Hairston’s holding penalty on 3rd gives NE a fresh set of downs inside the five. Then gets beat by Doubs again for another TD… NE retakes the lead 21-17 #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/HsmMHCS8zI

There’s an opportunity for the offense to get going against the Bills’ secondary, but can Stafford and Co. be trusted not to make a costly mistake? With the Bills coming off of a loss, the Rams get a more focused Buffalo team and come up just short. Bills 30, Rams 27

title: Rams Injury Report: Aaron Donald Among Three Key Starters Who Could Return vs. Bills
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will hope to get multiple starters back in Week 5 as they get set to take on the Buffalo Bills. After missing Aaron Donald, Colby Parkinson, and Jaylen Watson against the Philadelphia Eagles last week, the Rams are hopeful that all three will be back for Monday night’s game.
"The expectation is that as long as they progress accordingly then they'll be ready to go," said head coach Sean McVay. "I want to see how Jaylen feels. We'll get a little shoulder harness out there, [see] how he's going to be able to block destruct. Colby is really progressing in a very positive direction. We'll be smart with the kind of reps that he takes. Then like I mentioned to you guys with Aaron, [we'll] see how his back responds. Everything is trended in the right direction.”
On the initial injury report, Donald, Parkinson, and Watson were all listed as limited participants on Monday. Donald was a surprise addition to the injury report last week after head coach Sean McVay said that he had a sore back after the game. The Rams erred on the side of caution by resting Donald last week, and the team was able to get a win without him. All indications are that Donald could play on Monday night .
Additionally, the Rams will hope to get Parkinson back after he was inactive last week with an AC sprain in his shoulder. The Rams will certainly welcome Parkinson back as they look to get back to 13 personnel this week. Without Parkinson, the Rams utilized 11 personnel at their highest rate since Week 5 of last season.
Jaylen Watson also missed last week after dislocating his shoulder in the loss to the Broncos. Getting Watson back before facing a good Bills offense would be a huge boost for the defense. The Rams will look to ramp up Donald, Parkinson, and Watson as the week progresses.
Also on the injury report were linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), edge rusher Josaiah Stewart (groin), safety Quentin Lake (hip), linebacker Nate Landman (shoulder), and wide receiver Davante Adams (rest). None of them participated in practice on Thursday.
According to The Athletic’s Nate Atkins, Lake’s injury is minor, and he was heavily iced after Sunday’s game. Landman has been on the injury report the last three weeks and has played. Stewart showed up on the injury report toward the end of last week and managed to play on Sunday. Still, he’ll be one to monitor.
"He's so tough. He pushed through it," said McVay. "He got it when he fell backwards on something so it's a weird deal, but he's doing good. We're just being smart with him."
Not practicing today will be DB Quentin Lake (hip), LB Grant Stuard (hamstring), OLB Josaiah Stewart (groin), ILB Nate Landman (shoulder) and WR Davante Adams (veteran rest day). Lake's injury is minor, Sean McVay said. Lake had it pretty iced up after the game on Sunday.
McVay mentioned that wide receiver Konata Mumpfield had a rotator cuff contusion during his Monday press conference. Mumpfield was a full participant on Thursday.
On the Bills’ side, the Rams will be monitoring the availability of wide receiver DJ Moore, defensive lineman Ed Oliver, and cornerback Dee Alford. All three did not practice on Thursday. Additionally, defensive lineman Landon Jackson and cornerback Christian Benford were limited.
The Rams will certainly hope to be as close to full strength as possible heading into Monday night’s matchup against the Bills. While they managed to overcome several key absences against the Eagles, doing so against the Bills will present a more difficult challenge. With Donald, Parkinson, and Watson trending in the right direction, the Rams could be getting some much-needed reinforcements at an important point in their season.

full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to take on the Buffalo Bills in Week 5 on Monday Night Football at SoFi Stadium. After beating the Philadelphia Eagles last week, the Rams are 2-2 and back at .500. Meanwhile, the Bills lost their first game in their new stadium, falling 29-26 to the New England Patriots.
Prior to losing to the Patriots , the Bills looked like an unstoppable force. They beat the Los Angeles Chargers the week before despite turning the ball over five times. Heading into Week 5, the Bills rank fourth overall in total DVOA.
The Rams were staring a 1-3 record in the face before overcoming a 10-point deficit in the fourth quarter. If they’re going to win at home against the Bills in primetime, they’ll need to find a way to be much more consistent.
For the second time this season, the Rams will play at home on Monday Night Football. They played the New York Giants in Week 2, snapping a five-game losing streak on Monday Night Football. The Rams last played the Bills in primetime to open the 2022 season and lost, 31-10.
Fans should expect plenty of penalties in this game. Scott Novak's crew is now responsible for the two games with the highest combined penalty totals this season. Last week, the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Chargers combined for 30 penalties for 280 yards. In Week 2, the Green Bay Packers and New York Jets combined for 27 penalties for 280 yards.
Bills-Rams MNF uniform matchup is set. Appreciate Buffalo going white pants against the royal-heavy Rams.  Best possible primary outcome for this one. pic.twitter.com/ZYOisQaFw5
The Rams and Bills have played some dramatic games in the past. When these two teams met in 2024, the Rams won 44-42 after the Bills nearly erased a 38-21 fourth-quarter deficit. The Rams almost came back from a 28-3 deficit in 2020, but lost 35-32. Back in 2012, Sam Bradford found Brandon Gibson with under a minute left to win 15-12. In the all-time series, the Bills lead 9-6 and have won three of the last four.
Over the past few seasons, Matthew Stafford and Josh Allen have been two of the most prolific quarterbacks in the NFL. They’ve met three times in the regular season, with Allen leading the head-to-head, 2-1. On Monday night, each player has an opportunity to reach a different milestone.
With a win on Monday Night Football, Josh Allen can become the fourth quarterback all-time with at least 100 wins, including the postseason, in his first nine seasons. He can also tie for the third-most regular season wins by a starting quarterback in his first nine seasons. Only Russell Wilson and Patrick Mahomes have more. Additionally, if Matthew Stafford throws a touchdown pass, he can surpass Ben Roethlisberger for the sixth-most touchdown passes, including the postseason, all-time. With three touchdown passes, he can become the first player in NFL history with at least 150 touchdown passes with two franchises.
This season, the Rams and Bills have used three-tight-end sets at the highest rates in the NFL. The Rams lead the NFL in 13 personnel usage at 31 percent. Meanwhile, the Bills are right behind them at 20 percent. Additionally, The Bills also frequently utilize 12 personnel, featuring two tight ends. Tight ends play a huge role in both offenses, making their usage something to watch on Monday night.

title: Rams' Penalty Problems Are Real, but the Numbers Tell a Bigger Story
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams lost to the Denver Broncos in Week 3, they were penalized 13 times for 91 yards. It was the most accepted penalties against the Rams in a game since Week 4 of 2020. Last week against the Eagles, the Rams were penalized eight times for 100 yards. The 21 accepted penalties for 191 yards against the Rams are their most over a two-game stretch during Sean McVay's tenure as head coach.
The recent uptick in penalties by the Rams is simply uncharacteristic of a Sean McVay-led team. Throughout the McVay era, the Rams have struggled to score in the red zone at times due to questionable play-calling. This season, the Rams have had to settle for field goals because of penalties.
“The things that really chapped me that I think are a reflection of an undisciplined team are the pre-snap, the procedural things,” said McVay this week. “Those are the things that we can control with focus and concentration. They'll happen from time to time, but we have to minimize those situationally whether that's jumping offsides offensively, things like that, even making decisions where there's no discrepancy on.”
The past 2 weeks, 21 accepted penalties against the Rams measured 191 yards. Both figures are the most in consecutive games in 10 season under Sean McVay, a span of time in which discipline has been a hallmark. I just looked through them all, a few things to note: *Penalties…
In Week 3 against the Broncos, the Rams had to settle for field goals after an offensive pass interference penalty on Davante Adams and a hold on Steve Avila.
Last week, the Rams settled for field goals after a holding penalty on Davis Allen. According to Warren Sharp of Sharp Football Analytics , red-zone holding is up 38 percent, second only to 2019. After taking over at the Eagles’ 38-yard line, a seven-yard run from Williams was called back because of a questionable illegal blindside block.
BLINDSIDE BLOCK…on Puka Nacua?! What happened to the beautiful game of football… pic.twitter.com/RjcsS1MepO
However, this isn’t only happening to the Rams. This season, there have been the most red zone penalties per game by offenses in NFL history according to Sharp. More than 56.55 percent of red zone flags are on offense, which is up from 48 percent. There have also been the most penalties on third and fourth downs in the second half of games in NFL history.
For as frustrating as some of the penalties have been at times, context is important. This season, the relationship between the NFL players, league, and its officials has hit a breaking point. This week, the NFL suspended two officials for their on-field behavior . The 2026 season has seen the most flags in over a decade.
Penalties are certainly up for the Rams, but that’s also the case around the league. Despite the Rams being penalized more, they are still only tied for the 10th-most penalties per game with five other teams, and there are eight teams between 7.5 and 8.0 penalties per game. They have lost 0.15 EPA per play due to penalties, which is the 11th-worst in the NFL. With that said, the Rams still have a net penalty count of -11, which is the fourth-worst.
Penalty Impact so far this year (Somehow another Vikings defense stat) pic.twitter.com/0DByDipxfG
This is a case where multiple things can be true at the same time. Penalties are up around the NFL as a whole. Comparatively speaking, the Rams are also committing more penalties and ranking higher than they have in the past. The Rams have also been on the wrong side of some of the 50-50 calls, most notably the defensive pass interference penalty on Josh Wallace at the end of the game against the Broncos.
Throughout McVay’s tenure, the Rams have generally been one of the more disciplined teams in the NFL. It’s part of what makes the more recent uptick so jarring. Some of the increase can be attributed to the league-wide trend, but the Rams are also to blame. McVay has made it clear that those are mistakes that they need to clean up.
The league-wide trend of more penalties being called certainly adds some context, but it doesn't completely excuse the Rams' lack of discipline over the last two weeks. There are still things that they can control. If the Rams are going to reach their ceiling as a Super Bowl contender, they can't continue allowing self-inflicted mistakes to take points off the board.

title: 3 Key Notes Before Raiders Take On Patriots

A win on the road against a tough Patriots team would set Klint Kubiak's squad up nicely, as the Raiders have a difficult stretch of games after this one. The Patriots haven't played as well as they were expected to this season, but they are not a team to take lightly.
Raiders-Patriots always seems to be a spectacle in one way or another, and there is a good chance we will see more fireworks between these two scrappy AFC teams.

The Raiders have beaten the Patriots in three straight games, dating back to 2022.
It's been six years since New England last beat the Silver and Black. The Patriots still lead the all-time series, but the Raiders can make it 18-18-1 with a win today.
The Raiders will come into this game confident with how the season has gone, while the Patriots haven't lived up to expectations thus far. This game is a chance for the Raiders to take care of business, although they should try to avoid a trap game.

title: Why Raiders Have Ample Opportunities To Upset Patriots
full_text:
It can be easy to get held up on a loss, especially after what could've been for the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4 against the Kansas City Chiefs.
The Raiders led at multiple points in the game, but mistakes for a team still considered to be in a rebuild proved costly in their 30-27 defeat to their AFC West rival. However, they are still 3-1 and remain the talk of the NFL. They went wire-to-wire with Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid, and that could be a morale booster as they travel on Sunday to face the reigning AFC champions, the New England Patriots.
It feels like the Patriots are learning the hard way what a first-place schedule can lead to early in the season. The team is 2-2 heading into Week 5, but there are issues to sort out, especially protecting the football, offensive line play, and consistency. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye has thrown more interceptions than touchdowns, but he had a much better display against the Buffalo Bills a week ago.
Yet this is a vulnerable team on both sides of the ball that didn't handle facing teams like the Seattle Seahawks and Jacksonville Jaguars well. I wouldn't call the Raiders similar to those two seeming juggernauts, but they are proving to be a difficult matchup for their opponents.
Much of the credit should go to two individuals from this franchise: head coach Klint Kubiak and defensive coordinator Rob Leonard. When you have coaches who can get the best out of their players by putting them in key roles and positions to succeed, everything else works itself out.
When you have a roster in its current state, as Las Vegas does, you need good coaching to get the best out of it. So far, they've done that, and it has led to some interesting situations, like Kirk Cousins leading the NFL in touchdown passes after four games; rookie Hezekiah Masses being the top Raiders cornerback; Cody White emerging as a go-to playmaker; or Nakobe Dean being the second-best player on the defense after the first quarter of the season.
Playing in New England is always tough, and the Raiders know it. They did win here last fall, and they can do it again with a better team this weekend.
The Raiders have a chance to bring down the reigning AFC champions and bolster confidence to take down other quality opponents remaining on the schedule in what will be a challenging seven-game stretch filled with postseason and championship contenders.
If the Raiders lose, they're likely exposing cracks in an already unstable foundation that likely never had a chance to compete for the postseason. Yet if they win, it's a sign Las Vegas will be incredibly competitive all season long and will have a chance in late November and December to do some magical things with the playoffs in sight.

title: How Raiders' Klint Kubiak Pushing All the Right Buttons
full_text:
For the first time in a long time, it feels like the Las Vegas Raiders have a bright future.
The Raiders are 3-1 and have looked like a force on both sides of the ball this season, coming up just short against a resurgent Kansas City Chiefs team. If things keep up, they could be in the mix for a Wild Card appearance.
What has worked for this Raiders team this season? All it took was getting adults in the room.
The Raiders hired Klint Kubiak after the Pete Carroll experiment failed for one season, hoping he would finally stop the coaching carousel they've been on for so many years. He's proven in the early going that he is the answer.
Kubiak is a play-calling head coach, and his offensive expertise has been evident to start the season. He has gotten excellent play out of Kirk Cousins at quarterback, and despite limited talent at receiver and a run game not moving well, the Raiders are putting up points.
Kubiak has called the right plays this season and has opened things up for the personnel he has. Granted, one of those players is Brock Bowers , but the rest of the talent doesn't stand out, yet this offense is producing.
This is the most evident sign of the culture Kubiak has instilled, as well as the effective scheme that has worked for his players. Who's to say these Raiders won't keep playing at a high level and beat teams they're not supposed to?
The schedule doesn't get any easier for the Raiders in the next few weeks. They'll battle the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams, two Super Bowl contenders.
Even if the Raiders don't win those games, they can show they belong by competing until the clock hits zero. That kind of competitiveness can be attributed to Kubiak.
It could be foolhardy to say Kubiak is 'the guy' after only four games, but after what some of the league's young offensive minds have done turning around bad programs in the last few years, it's hard not to believe Kubiak can do the same.
He has shown, through these first four games, that he knows what it takes to be competitive, especially given the lack of top-end talent on this roster. The bones of the organization are there, and that's why Raiders fans should be excited about what's to come.

title: How DeCamillis' Response to Critics Will Boost Raiders
full_text:
As the Las Vegas Raiders look to bounce back from their first loss of the season, they'll need an honest look at their first four games. The Raiders' front office and coaching staff have used that type of approach to jump out to a 3-1 start this season. It must continue.
After four games, Klint Kubiak's Raiders are undoubtedly much improved compared to last year's team. Yet as they continue through Kubiak's first season, they must keep improving. Las Vegas is 3-1, but a few plays away from being 2-2.
Conversely, the Raiders are also a few plays from being 4-0 heading into Week 5. The Kansas City Chiefs capitalized on mistakes the Raiders' other three opponents did not. The mistakes were still there during the Raiders' 3-0 start. Those mistakes just cost them a win against the Chiefs.
There are no moral victories, but one thing Las Vegas' coaching staff can take from last Sunday's loss is that they have things that, if corrected, should make winning more consistent. Las Vegas made several miscues against the Chiefs, especially on special teams.
Raiders' special teams coach Joe DeCamillis knows improvement is necessary, but also seemingly took exception with a former coach's assessment of one of his unit's miscues against the Chiefs last week.
"I've never seen this before" ~ @ChuckPaganoNFL I don't know what the Raiders are thinking here #PMSLive https://t.co/bWbeqwqZ1C pic.twitter.com/MivfYrdVhc
“That was a total misplay on my part. I got way too greedy. That was not for that part of the field. And really, I should have been much smarter than that because the last time we played [Dave] Toub, he talked about some of the battles," DeCamillis said after practice on Friday, while detailing a fake punt Kansas City converted early in Week 4.
"Well, the last time we played him in Kansas City, we ran a fade, got a first down on him, and we also got a turnover. So, I guarantee he was probably irritated just like I was after this game. So, that's just how it goes. But it's a great call on their part, and I'll learn from that situation and not get greedy.”
The fake punt that Kansas City converted last week was one of several mistakes Las Vegas' special teams have allowed. Luckily, that mistake was not as costly as some of the unit's other mistakes. However, the play was a microcosm of how crucial every little detail is in football.
The difference between 4-0 and 3-1 came down to a handful of crucial plays that didn't go Las Vegas' way. Yet some of those plays went against them because of their own doing. DeCamillis elaborated on the play, noting that Las Vegas used the technique earlier in the season.
"We did it in the first game too against Miami. So, we did it from a little better position, but you're trying to block people downfield. It's something that a lot of people do around the league. I saw on some podcast where the guy said, 'I've never seen anything like that.' Well, we scored a touchdown against you, dude. So obviously you have," DeCamillis said after practice on Friday.
"So, it's just one of those things that schematically that you try to work on, and it was obviously a bad play at that point in the game. Defense bailed us out, though. They did a heck of a job. I think we ended up getting a touchdown on that drive. So, kudos to them."
As Las Vegas prepares for a challenging stretch of games , it must clean up the small but important mistakes it has made in every facet.
Their close loss to the Chiefs confirmed that the Raiders have the roster to compete with any team in the league. Their Week 5 matchup against the Patriots will show whether they can quickly correct what needs fixing. So far, there is reason to believe they can, but time will tell.
The Raiders have a golden opportunity in Week 5, facing an injury-riddled Patriots team on the road. Any team can win on any given Sunday, but winning almost always comes down to executing at a high level in all three phases of the game.
If they hope to beat the Patriots and move to 4-1 on the season, Las Vegas must find a way to get back to playing clean football in all three phases for all four quarters.

title: How Raiders Secret Weapon No Longer a Secret
full_text:
The new-look Las Vegas Raiders sprinted out to a 3-1 start to the season, partially because opposing teams had no idea what Klin Kubiak and his coaching staff wanted to do on the field. Las Vegas' offseason of change gave them the advantage of being largely unknown heading into the season.
The four teams Las Vegas faced early in the season had little idea of what the Raiders would do in any given situation, as their tendencies in meaningful games were nonexistent. However, as the Kansas City Chiefs showed last week, the element of the unknown naturally wears off with time.
The Raiders decided to use a collection of under-the-radar but generally dependable wide receivers to fill out their roster this offseason. After the season's first four games, it's become clearer who the most dependable of those receivers are.
Las Vegas' plans of spreading the ball around have spread the yardage statistics out between the Raiders' receivers and tight ends, but have allowed receivers the chance to increase their value to the offense. Cody White is one of the players who have increased their value the most.
“If you watch the tape, there's a good two more opportunities that I felt I missed that would have given him a chance to really impact the game. So, I was kicking myself for those plays, but the ball just has found him. I don't have a great answer for you,” veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins said earlier this week.
“I think it's just kind of how the pocket allows me to get through the progression, and the ball finds him, and he's attacked the football. I think that's the trait that I would say has jumped off the tape, whether it was the Chargers touchdown or the goal ball last week, just attacking the football and saying, 'Ball's in the air, that's my ball.'"
Cousins noted how long he has known about the rising receiver. Both Cousins and White both played football at Michigan State University, albeit at different times. Arguably the best professional football player to ever play at MSU, Cousins has remained well connected to the school.
"I think probably going back to watching him at Michigan State a little bit as an alumnus. Seeing him make plays there in the number seven, and then that play against the Chargers where he attacked the football for a touchdown in tight coverage. I thought those traits surfaced, and he's been doing it since,” Cousins said.
The Raiders' approach to the wide receiver position has given any receiver on the roster who can catch the ball and play well within the scheme a chance to establish themselves further in the league. White, a sixth-year veteran, has made the most of his opportunity.
Through four games, White has accounted for five catches, three of which were crucial touchdowns in slim Raiders victories. Overall, none of the Raiders' receivers will fill up a stat sheet this season. That is by design. That lets them make more of an impact with less yardage.
Injuries to two of their top receivers have given White a chance to step up. Jack Bech and Jalen Nailor's absences put more responsibility on the other available receivers. As Las Vegas prepares to face the New England Patriots , it needs more from White and the rest of the group.
Las Vegas' receiver-by-committee plan is being put to the ultimate test right now, as the unit is extremely thin heading into Week 5. The Raiders will lean on arguably the best group of tight ends in the league to help shoulder the load, but still need their receivers to play well.
The Raiders are not only shorthanded at wide receiver, but White is no longer flying under the radar. This is especially true with Nailor and Bech out. White will likely draw more attention from New England's defense than he saw from other defenses during the first four weeks of the season.
Still, Week 5 presents White with another chance to add to an underdog story that has been commendable through the early part of the season. Hopefully, White's performances can keep forcing the Raiders' coaching staff to incorporate him more into the offense.

title: Key Area of the Field Raiders Must Improve Quickly
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are 3-1 on the season. Las Vegas' 3-0 start was followed by a Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Next, they face the New England Patriots. Overall, the Raiders have undeniably improved in every aspect.
Their early production on the field confirms as much. Las Vegas' early turnaround has happened from the top down. The Raiders' hot start is a testament to an offseason of quality wholesale changes from the coaching staff down to the last player on the practice squad.
During the offseason, Las Vegas' front office said its goal was to improve in every aspect. It is clear that improvement has happened. The Raiders' coaching staff would also admit that the improvement they seek is ongoing and will last throughout the season.
The importance of teams' offensive and defensive units goes without saying. Although most understand the importance of special teams, the unit is often overlooked. Las Vegas' coaching staff has done the opposite, giving their special teams unit ample time throughout the week to improve.
The Raiders' strengths and weaknesses have become more apparent as the season continues. It is hard not to notice that their special teams unit has impacted all four games Las Vegas has played this season. The unit has had a crucial play every week, whether it be positive or negative.
Raiders special teams coach Joe DeCamillis knows Sundays will only get increasingly harder for his unit as time goes on. The well-respected, experienced coach knows the Patriots will look to capitalize on any mistakes the Raiders' special teams may make.
“I mean, it's always a chess game every time. I mean, our stuff's on tape, so I mean, I have a lot of tape, so they've looked at a lot of tape. So, they did a great job last week, but this is another one that's going to be a challenge this week because Jeremy Springer, who's the coordinator there, was my assistant in LA for the first year when I was there, so they've got some MO on me too there,” DeCamillis said after practice on Friday.
For all the money the Raiders invested in their offense and defense to make much-needed changes, their special teams unit is becoming just as important. In Week 1, Dylan Laube averaged nearly 50 yards on kickoff returns. In the last two weeks, the unit has lost two fumbles.
The Raiders' Week 5 matchup against the Patriots is another chance for their special teams unit to make a positive impact after two weeks of costly mistakes. Yet, it will be the first time Las Vegas has played in an open-air stadium this season. Weather could affect the unit.
“Well, you look at the weather reports, all those type of things. Luckily, at this place, you get a lot of wind, which we've had that during training camp and all that stuff. It was 115 when it's like that, but I do think being in the wind is going to help both Matt [Gay] and AJ [Cole] and Alex [Ward] on that. That's really three that are the most important, and then the returners also," DeCamillis said.
Despite their Week 4 loss, the Raiders can move to 4-1 after winning seven games in the past two seasons combined. Even with a loss against the Patriots, Las Vegas is still technically ahead of schedule. However, as it stands, the Raiders still control their own destiny.
If the Raiders get back to their winning ways over the next few weeks, the future will not only be bright, but will also arrive sooner. More wins would make the playoffs all but a guarantee. However, that would be putting the cart before the horse if the special teams unit keeps making mistakes.
The beauty of the first few weeks of the season is that they make it clear where each team needs to improve. Needing improvement at this point in the season is not unique to the Raiders. All teams need improvement right now.
Heading into Week 5, Las Vegas needs improvement on both sides of the ball, but their special teams need the most attention.

title: How Raiders Can Adapt to Jeanty's Potential Availability Concerns
full_text:
Over the first four weeks of the 2026 NFL season, several surprising developments have emerged across the league.
That includes the Las Vegas Raiders, who have jumped out to a 3-1 start and are in second place in the AFC West . Their lone loss came against the Kansas City Chiefs, but it was an impressive performance. The Raiders are looking to bounce back when they take on the New England Patriots on Sunday.
It's been a nearly flawless start to the season for the Silver and Black. However, running back Ashton Jeanty could be dealing with potential injury concerns heading into Sunday. During the week of preparation leading up to Sunday's game against the Patriots, the 22-year-old running back's participation has been concerning. Here's a look at his practice status and what it means for Las Vegas in Week 5 and potentially beyond.
The second-year running back's participation in practice has been steadily declining. On Wednesday, Jeanty was a full participant, was limited on Thursday, and didn't practice on Friday. Jeanty is listed as questionable for Sunday, and his steady decline throughout the week could put his availability for Sunday in serious jeopardy.
During his press conference on Friday, head coach Klint Kubiak was asked about the extent of Jeanty's injury, but he didn't seem overly concerned that it had hindered the running game.
This may be an injury Jeanty deals with all season. As mentioned, he suffered a sprained ankle in training camp, and typically, sprained ankles can be tricky to navigate. The former 2025 first-round pick hasn't missed a game yet.
However, you can argue that the ailment has affected Jeanty, as he's averaged less than three yards per carry in two of the last three games. Additionally, Jeanty appeared to hurt his ankle against the Chiefs when it was rolled up on in the third quarter.
Overall, this isn't to say Raiders fans should panic, but it’s something worth monitoring as the season progresses, especially if Jeanty keeps playing through it. That could further aggravate the ailment or prevent Jeanty from playing at 100 percent this season. With Mike Washington Jr. in the backfield, Kubiak should use the rookie running back more often to ensure Jeanty stays as healthy as possible throughout the regular season. Sitting him out this week could be best for the long term.

title: Five Dolphins Players Who Have To Deliver in Week 5
full_text:
If the Miami Dolphins take down the Cincinnati Bengals, a lot would need to go their way, including a complete team effort from top to bottom.
The losses that the Dolphins have piled up are slowly improving in terms of the margin of victory for the opponent. They went from an undefeated Minnesota team to a 2-2 Bengals squad that was expected to compete for the AFC North but has had a rough start to the season.
Regardless of which side of the ball the Dolphins are on, there are a few players who need to step up for Miami. Some of them are still looking for a breakout performance, while others already have impressed this season, but Cincinnati will provide some of their most difficult matchups thus far.
After getting removed from the injury report Friday without a status designation, Wright needs to have a breakout game. Ollie Gordon II did well with 100 rushing yards and the team's lone touchdown against the Vikings, but Miami's offense regressed whenever Wright (Who started for this game) took the field, being shut down for 7 yards.
Wright has been thrust into a serious role in the run game and has underperformed. The Dolphins will have their hands full against a stout Cincinnati run defense. Gordon will give everything he has to move the ball, but he can't be the only running back contributing in this game.
So far, Brewer has played well enough to justify his three-year contract extension back in June. He hasn't given up a single sack and has only committed three penalties in 226 snaps. Against Minnesota, he was near-perfect with no QB hits, penalties, and only one pressure.
However, Brewer will be matched up against his toughest assignment so far — nose tackle Dexter Lawrence. Cincinnati acquired Lawrence from the New York Giants ahead of the 2026 NFL draft in exchange for their first-round pick, and he's helped turn their defense into a reliable unit, coordinated by former Miami Hurricanes head coach Al Golden.
Lawrence is having a great start to the season with 10 tackles, a team-leading three sacks, and five tackles for a loss. He and Cincinnati's front seven are doing a great job against the run, allowing just under 100 rushing yards per game (99.5), which doesn't bode well for a Miami offense that'll want to, once again, rely on the run game.
There's no secret when it comes to beating the Bengals since Joe Burrow was drafted in 2020: defenses need to apply pressure on the Pro Bowl quarterback. He's an excellent passer who will make opponents pay if they give him time in the pocket, having thrown for 1,171 yards and seven touchdowns through the air so far this season.
However, he's also been sacked nine times. Both Pittsburgh and Jacksonville applied heavy pressure on Burrow over the course of their contests in the past two weeks, sacking him twice in each game, and the Steelers and Jaguars came out on top.
It just so happens that Miami's pass rush is coming off its most successful game of the season against the Vikings, spearheaded by Sieler who registered two sacks on Kyler Murray. He'll need to bring the momentum of that game to Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday.
Usually, Burrow has a plethora of talented wide receivers to throw to, but that might not be the case on Sunday as Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (groin/neck), and Colbie Young (knee) are questionable for this game.
After not having to deal with Justin Jefferson last week, the Dolphins could find themselves facing yet another battered and bruised receiver corps. However, their Achilles' heel against the Vikings was their inability to limit the tight end, TJ Hockenson, who put the offense on his back for 119 yards.
Brooks, who claimed responsibility for Miami's struggles against Hockenson, will need to do a better job maintaining Cincinnati's tight end and former member of the Dolphins, Mike Gesicki. If Chase, Higgins, or Young are out, that could mean an expanded role for Gesicki, who caught Cincinnati's only receiving touchdown of the game against Jacksonville.
Except for their two-score win over Houston, the Bengals have been in close games all season, defeating Tampa Bay by six points but losing to Pittsburgh and Jacksonville by three and five points, respectively.
This is to say that Cincinnati is no stranger to one-score games. The Dolphins could be in a position where they'll need to turn to Patterson to keep this game within reach, or maybe even take the lead. If that were to happen, Patterson better not miss.
Patterson has been perfect when it comes to mid-range kicks between 20 and 40 yards, but missed a 41-yard field goal against Las Vegas, then a 51-yarder against San Francisco. These are distances that are slowly becoming more automatic for the next generation of NFL kickers.
Granted, Patterson has been perfect in his last two games, but hasn't been tested at the aforementioned long-range distances. While almost no major media outlet is expecting a Dolphins upset, there are a fair share of predictions for a one-score win for the Bengals. In a situation like this, the difference between a win or loss could simply come down to a kick.

title: Breaking Down the Grant Transaction and the other Week 5 Dolphins Saturday Moves
full_text:
Kenneth Grant indeed will make his 2026 debut for the Miami Dolphins in their Week 5 game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
The Dolphins activated Grant off IR on Saturday after he practiced all week with no setbacks after missing the first four games of the regular season because of a toe injury.
To make room on the 53-man roster for Grant, the Dolphins waived Brady Cook, who had served as the emergency third quarterback for each of the first four games.
His release means the Dolphins will have only two quarterback available for the game against the Bengals, starter Malik Willis and Kyle McCord, though it's likely that Cook will be re-signed to the practice squad at some point after he clears waivers, as one would suspect he will.
Additionally, the Dolphins elevated running back Carlos Washington Jr. and edge defender Rodney McGraw from the practice squad for the Cincinnati game.
Washington will serve as the third running back behind Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II because newcomer Kaytron Allen, claimed off waivers from the Washington Commanders on Friday, is too new to the team to be able to contribute right away.
Washington was on the 53-man roster for the game against the Minnesota Vikings last weekend and was active, but he did not play in the 15-10 loss.
McGraw is getting an elevation for a second consecutive game, a reward for making himself noticeable against the Vikings. This move indicates he's currently ahead of rookie seventh-round pick Max Llewellyn in the pecking order.
The one move the Dolphins didn't make was activating cornerback Storm Duck from Reserve/PUP after he was a full participant in practice all week.
Duck, who has been out recovering from his 2025 knee injury, was downgraded to OUT on a Saturday injury report.
He's got another full week of practice left before the Dolphins have to activate him or keep him on PUP for the rest of the 2026 season.
Grant clearly is a more significant player as the team's first-round pick in the 2025 NFL draft.
Grant will join the expected Dolphins rotation at defensive tackle alongside Zach Sieler, Jordan Philips and Zeek Biggers.
Without mentioning names, head coach Jeff Hafley indicated this week that Grant's presence provides more flexibility on the defensive line in terms of being able to use one of his interior defensive linemen outside, though Biggers logically is the player involved here.

Here's a roundup of national predictions on this game.
For the first time since the season, it's not a total sweep in terms of predicting a Dolphins loss because we have one brave soul going for an upset.

The Bengals are off to a 2-2 start, which is if anything a bit disappointing considering the lofty expectations some media members put on them after they beefed up their defense in the offseason with moves highlighted by the trade acquisition of former New York Giants DT Dexter Lawrence. Cincinnati has lost its last two games after Joe Burrow turned the ball over on a potential game-winning drive, a fumble against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3 and an interception against the Jacksonville Jaguars last Sunday. Burrow, though, remains the driving force for Cincinnati along with his star wide receiver tandem of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The Dolphins had chances to win in the fourth quarter of each of their last two games against Kansas City and Minnesota, and at some point they'll break through and make the plays down the stretch. The heat and humidity factor always should be considered for an early-season game at Hard Rock Stadium, but perhaps more significant is the fact that Chase and Higgins both missed practice time during the week.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Chase and Higgins both practiced Friday, and both of them playing changes the outlook of this game quite considerably. With both in the lineup, Burrow passed for 309 yards and four touchdowns at Hard Rock Stadium last December, and this Dolphins defense probably isn't as good as the one Burrow torched 10 months ago. Unless the Dolphins can control that Cincinnati offense, it's hard to envision them being able to keep up considering they haven't scored more than 13 points in any game this season.
The Dolphins defense is stepping up in weight class big time in this matchup if Chase and Higgins both play, even if it's only Chase, and stopping the tight end will become a minor problem for Miami as opposed to a major talking point. With Caleb Douglas likely out for a third consecutive game, it's just very difficult to envision the Dolphins scoring enough to get that elusive first victory. At this point, merely scoring two touchdowns would represent progress. Final Prediction: Bengals 27, Dolphins 17

title: What to Know About New Dolphins RB Kaytron Allen
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins filled their one vacancy on their 53-man roster Friday by claiming another rookie draft pick, this time running back Kaytron Allen from the Washington Commanders.
Allen was a sixth-round pick out of Penn State who was waived this week after the Commanders brought back veteran Austin Ekeler.
Allen played in each of Washington's first four games and had 12 rushing attempts for 41 yards (3.4 average). He played 25 snaps on offense in those four games and another 29 on special teams.
The Dolphins had a roster opening since they waived fellow running back Carlos Washington Jr., who since has been re-signed to the practice squad.
Allen joins Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II as running backs on the active roster, with De'Von Achane on IR and out for the season and Washington and Jarquez Hunter on the practice squad.
Heading into the draft, Allen was compared by NFL.com draft analyst Lance Zierlein to current Arizona Cardinals running back Tyler Allgeier and projected to go in the fifth round.
"Allen is productive with good size and vision but below-average explosiveness," Zierlein wrote before the draft. "He’s a fluid runner with ideal patience and a natural feel for when to cut off his blocks. He runs low to the ground with the strength to run through arm tackles and fall forward after contact. A feel for lane development allows him to fit any run scheme, but his lack of burst is likely to constrict the field and limit his ability to find explosive runs. Allen appears to lack third-down and special-teams value, but he could earn a spot as a solid backup."
In four seasons at Penn State, Allen averaged 1,045 yards a season, with a high of 1,303 yards in 2025 when he averaged 6.2 yards a carry and scored 15 touchdowns.
Allen was the ninth of 12 running backs selected in the 2026 draft.
Allen became the 13th player the Dolphins have claimed off waivers in 2026, a string that started in May when they landed defensive lineman James Ester from the Green Bay Packers and moved him to guard.
The Dolphins picked up seven players off waivers on August 31 after the roster cuts to the NFL limit of 53: QB Brady Cook (N.Y. Jets), CB Marcellas Dial Jr. (Dallas), T Chukwuebuka Godrick (Kansas City), TE Justin Joly (Denver), OL Jarrett Kingston (Houston), CB Reese Taylor (Denver) and S Julius Wood (Dallas).
Earlier in the summer (and at different times), the Dolphins got on waivers WR Ryan Miller from the New York Giants, CB Jai'Onte McMillan from the Indianapolis Colts, CB Ahmari Harvey from the Pittsburgh Steelers and TE Jeremiah Franklin from the New England Patriots.
Every player the Dolphins have claimed this year currently is on their 53-man roster except for Ester, who is on the practice squad; and McMillan, Harvey and Franklin, who were waived.

title: Why Passing on a QB Early in 2027 Draft Is Looking More and More Like the Right Call for Dolphins
full_text:
About this idea that the Miami Dolphins are or should be a slam dunk to select a quarterback at or near the top of the 2027 NFL draft, let us channel our inner Lee Corso.
On the contrary, as things stand right now, it very well could be that the Dolphins not only should force taking a quarterback, they downright should stay away from one.
Yes, finding a franchise quarterback should be the top priority for the organization because that kind of asset represents the fastest way back to perennial contender status (see Buffalo Bills, Josh Allen) and the verdict on Malik Willis has yet to come in definitively after a difficult first month operating under very difficult circumstances.
But there are two key factors at play here, and the first is that bringing in a stud quarterback is great but that player also needs to be given every opportunity to succeed and building a solid foundation around him is a great place to start.
So there's something to be said for beefing up the roster, not just on offense but defense as well before getting that quarterback in the draft and starting his clock toward that second contract — assuming that drafted QB is a hit — that will impact the team's entire salary structure.
The second factor, and the biggest one, is making sure you land the right quarterback and not drafting one for the sake of drafting a quarterback early.
As evidence, we can offer the last three quarterbacks the Dolphins selected in the first round.
In 1983, the Dolphins took Dan Marino with the 27th overall pick. Yes, they got lucky, but their Hall of Fame quarterback still wasn't a top 10 pick.
In 2012, the Dolphins selected Ryan Tannehill with the eighth overall pick after he had had limited experience at the position at Texas A&M — if you hadn't heard, he started out as a wide receiver — and that might have been the precise definition of forcing a QB pick.
And then in 2020, the Dolphins took Tua Tagovailoa fifth overall, and while there were positive results for the offense in 2022 and 2023, the team never got where it wanted to get.
So it's not like taking a quarterback with, say, a top 5 pick will guarantee a franchise-changing quarterback and taking the wrong quarterback could set back an organization just as much as not taking one and waiting a bit longer.
Now, if there's a slam-dunk QB prospect available when the Dolphins make their first selection in the 2027 draft, that's one thing.
But what if there weren't slam-dunk options for the Dolphins, whether at number 1, 2, 3 or whatever.
Based on a couple of national stories this week on ESPN.com and CBSSports.com, that's looking more and more likely.
Arch Manning is the big name out there, but is he really a slam dunk? And that's assuming he doesn't go back to Texas for another year, with the background that his uncles Peyton and Eli both entered the draft as seniors.
Depending on who you believe, the top quarterback prospects right now could be Drew Mestermaker or Darian Mensah or Dante Moore or Trinidad Chambliss or C.J. Carr.
None of them has slam dunk written all over them.
So why shouldn't the Dolphins just ride it out with Willis for another year and revisit the idea of a first-round quarterback in 2028 if they can get a foundational piece at another position with their top 5 pick in 2027?
Who that player could be is another discussion, but any of Jeremiah Smith, Leonard Moore or Colin Simmons might make more sense from this end.
The bottom line is that the Dolphins need to hit on that early draft pick in 2027 and that's more important than making sure it's a quarterback.

title: How Dolphins Coach Jeff Hafley Slapped Down the Willis "Ball Tap" Comment
full_text:
Those comments about how Miami Dolphins QB Malik Willis likes to pat the ball before throwing just became a big story very quickly, but head coach Jeff Hafley shot it down as a nothing burger just as quickly.
For those not aware, Cincinnati Bengals safety Jordan Battle — a native of Fort Lauderdale who played at national powerhouse St. Thomas Aquinas and had Jason Taylor as one of his assistants for two years, by the way — created the stir Thursday with those comments on camera.
There has been significant social media criticism of Battle from national media members for revealing that kind of info to an upcoming opponent, but Hafley said ball-patting isn't exactly uncommon in the NFL.
"I played high school quarterback," Hafley said before practice Friday. "I did the same thing. It never hurt me. I'm just joking. But I did play high school quarterback, and I probably patted the ball. Being very honest with you, I've studied quarterbacks for over 25 years, and that is not uncommon. A lot of quarterbacks pat the ball or take their hand off the ball. I mean, there's some I've studied that look up right before they throw the ball. I just I don't think there's anything revolutionary about that. It's a timing and rhythm thing with a lot of guys, and there's a lot of them that do that."
Another issue with that whole idea that the defense can get an advantage is that it doesn't necessarily work for defensive backs if they're in man coverage because they'll be looking at the receiver they're covering after the snap and not at the quarterback.
Maybe the whole thing was just more bizarre than anything because in today's NFL teams have become ultra-conservative with the info they share — to the point of paranoia — all in the name of "competitive advantage," so any player volunteering that kind of info was bound to raise eyebrows.
But, as Hafley pointed out, it was just a shame for the Dolphins that Battle didn't reveal something that could have a bigger impact into what happens at Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday.
"Any opponent that wants to share our tendencies with us, we'll take any time," Hafley said. "But there's nothing there on that. If there was something big, like he told us every time our left guard was in a three-point stance we were running the ball, I'd be like, all right, we've got to fix that. It's just there's nothing there."
It did make for a pretty story, though.

title: Counting Down the Five Best Dolphins Victories Against Cincinnati
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins will head into their Week 5 matchup at Hard Rock Stadium with a 17-9 all-time regular season record against the Cincinnati Bengals, but looking to snap a two-game losing streak in the series.
The series has featured its share of memorable games, including the one playoff matchup at the end of the 1973 season when the Dolphins defeated the Bengals on their way to a second consecutive Super Bowl title.
One crazy play turned the game around and may have saved the Dolphins from an embarrassing loss early in what became a playoff season. The 3-1 Dolphins were sleepwalking against the 0-3 Bengals and down 13-3 in the final seconds when the Bengals had the brilliant idea of having Akili Smith drop back to pass from their 37-yard line with 8 seconds left. Jason Taylor made them pay, sprinting around the left tackle, nailed Smith from behind, and producing a sack-strip-score that made it 13-10 at the half. The Dolphins never looked back, outscoring Cincinnati 21-3 in the second half.
This early-season game at the Orange Bowl also turned around on one play, and this was a very, very rare play. An onside punt. Not the kind we see nowadays when teams have to declare their intentions because of safety rules, but rather a surprise onside punt that came after the Dolphins gave up a safety and were forced to kick off (or punt) from their 20-yard line trailing 16-7 with 6:12 left in the fourth quarter. The Dolphins caught Cincinnati off guard, recovered the fumble and drove to a touchdown before a punt block set up the game-winning field goal.
There really was nothing particularly interesting about this game itself, which the Dolphins dominated on the strength of three interceptions by the defense and two touchdown passes by Dan Marino, but it was memorable nonetheless because of the head coach matchup between Don and David Shula. It was the first time a father had coached against his son in the history of the major North American sports league. The two would face each other again the next season, with the Dolphins again winning, that time by the score of 26-23.
The Dolphins' first playoff game as defending champions set the stage for a second Super Bowl run that actually was a lot more dominating than the perfect season of 1972. The Dolphins rushed for 241 yards, including 105 by Mercury Morris, and got two touchdown passes from Bob Griese. Cincinnati scored the last 13 points of the first half to make it a 21-16 game, but Miami ran away in the second half.
The Wake-Off game. Need we say more? Even before Cameron Wake sacked Andy Dalton in the end zone to win the Halloween night game for the Dolphins, this game had produced its share of big plays, including a 94-yard pick-six by Dolphins cornerback Brent Grimes and a dazzling 35-yard touchdown run by Cincinnati running back Gio Bernard. But Wake provided the fireworks with one of the greatest defensive plays in Dolphins history.

title: Projecting When the Dolphins Offense Will Break Out
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins' 0-4 record isn't necessarily shocking given all the roster sacrifices the team made to get its salary cap in order, but maybe the lack of offense wasn't totally expected.
A depressing stat surfaced after the Week 4 loss against the Minnesota Vikings, courtesy of Tim Reynolds from The Associated Press, indicating the Dolphins became the third team since 2004 to fail to score at least 14 points in any of their first four games.
The other two? The 2004 Dolphins and the 2019 Dolphins.
Like the 2026 edition, the 2019 Dolphins were in full rebuilding mode in Brian Flores' first year as head coach, though things were much different with the 2004 team.
The Dolphins were coming off a string of seven consecutive winning seasons, including a 10-6 finish in 2003, but things started going off the rails even before Ricky Williams blindsided the team by deciding to retire on the eve of training camp, with Joel Collier resigning as offensive coordinator in the spring citing exhaustion.
One big difference between the 2026 team and the previous two is that Malik Willis has been the only quarterback to play so far this season, while Jay Fiedler and A.J. Feeley split the first four starts in 2004 and Ryan Fitzpatrick and Josh Rosen did the same in 2019.
While the 2026 Dolphins at least have reached 10 points in each of their four games, the 2019 team reached 10 points twice in the first month that season and had a total of 26 during its 0-4 start, while the 2004 team was held under 10 points in three of its first four games.
Where the 2026 team is way ahead of those other two editions is in taking care of the ball because turnovers were a major problem in 2004 and 2019.
Through four games, the Dolphins have committed five turnovers this season, compared to nine in 2019 and a whopping 14 in 2004. The Dolphins also have been much better on third down, converting at a 38 percent clip this year, compard to 26.8 and 26 percent in those two other seasons.
And while Malik Willis' performance hasn't been good enough so far, the Dolphins still have gotten much better quarterbacking than they did in 2004 or 2019. Willis' passer rating currently stands at 73.0, while the two 2004 QBs were at 48.4 and Fitpatrick and Rosen combined for a 52.5 rating through four games in 2019.
The obvious question, of course, is when will the Dolphins offense reach at least 14 points and/or score more than one touchdown in a game.
The 2019 Dolphins' winless streak to start the season reached seven games before the 5-4 finish, but they did get to 16 points in their fifth game, a 17-16 loss against Washington.
The 2004 Dolphins failed to score at least 14 points through their first six games and were 0-6 before they finally broke out in a 31-14 victory against the St. Louis Rams.
The Dolphins' next game is against a Cincinnati Bengals defense that gave up 22 points against Jacksonville in Week 4 after allowing 30 against the Pittsburgh Steelers the previous Sunday.
So maybe this is the week for Miami. If not, the Dolphins will have to wait at least another two weeks because they have their bye in Week 6 before facing the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 25.
When the streak will end is anybody's guess and it should happen sooner rather than later, and it would have happened against the Minnesota Vikings last Sunday if not for Chris Bell barely stepping out of bounds before catching that long pass from Willis.
