title: How Dolphins Head Coach Jeff Hafley Addressed Three Key Problem Areas ... And Our Take On His Takes
full_text:
There are several issues the Miami Dolphins are facing right now, which is to be expected for a team that’s 0-4 and in the early stages of a pretty massive rebuilding project.
Three issues in particular stand out, and that Malik Willis’ performance at quarterback, Austin Jackson’s apparent pass-protection problems, and the defense giving up sizable numbers to opposing tight ends.
Head coach Jeff Hafley was asked all three topics during his pre-practice media session Wednesday, and we decide to examine his comments and offer our take on them.
We don’t need to remind everyone that Hafley and Jon-Eric Sullivan brought Willis from Green Bay because they believed in him, but the results obviously haven’t been good for the offense so far in 2026. Willis clearly is operating with a substandard supporting cast that got that much more mediocre when De’Von Achane tore his ACL, but Willis hasn’t yet done anywhere near enough to convince folks he should be the starting quarterback beyond this season.
Willis is near the bottom among NFL quarterbacks in both passer rating and completion percentage and he’s accounted for only two touchdowns with four turnovers (two fumbles, two picks),
He has twice as many turnovers as touchdowns produced. Is that a concern? We know that Malik is a work in progress. Is that a concern?
“I would say like everything else, like what can we do better, right? We’ve got to look ahead at this point and not behind and we’ve got to improve. And that's with everything that we're doing right now in all three phases with all the coaches and all the players and that's where we're at.”
Our take: Hafley is being very careful not to throw Willis or anybody else under the bus, so he is diverting specific questions about Willis to the entire offense, which is fair in a way because the whole offense is a big-time work in progress. That said, Willis isn’t without blame and there are improvements to be made in all areas, whether it be consistency, accuracy, decision-making, foot work, etc.
The Dolphins are coming off the loss at Minnesota where T.J Hockenson had 13 catches for 119 yards, including the game-clinching third-down before the two-minute warning. Before that, George Kittle had four catches for 80 yards, with a 40-yard reception and a wide open touchdown and Travis Kelce had a 48-yard catch and another wide open touchdown. And in the opener the Dolphins avoided Raiders star Brock Bowers because of an injury, but backup Michael Mayer wound up tying for the team lead with six receptions.
So I asked Hafley on Wednesday what’s been the biggest issue in defending tight ends, and he replied that he doesn’t look at the opponent by position but rather what needs to be done to keep them from scoring and then prioritizing the top threats, to which I followed up asking if he then ever would consider the tight end the player his defense needs to prioritize.
“Absolutely, yeah. If he's the most explosive player and we need to pay attention to that guy, for sure. But just in general, when you look at a team, it's who do we have to stop that can beat us the fastest? And you kind of go down in that order. Or who do we need to protect on our side of the ball that they're going to go after, right? So I think that all kind of balances out as you go. I mean, if you want to look at this week, there's a couple guys that we're going to have to pay very close attention to. You can't pay attention to all of them. So I respect the question, and there's some plays we need to play better on tight ends in situations where we're right there and there's some where they might get a five-yard pass because in zone defense there's a no cover zone that they're dumping the ball off to and you're rallying. There's give and take. Does that make sense?”
Our take: Yes, it makes sense, and there definitely was a pick-your-poison element when facing the 49ers or Chiefs offense because in addition to a star tight end, the 49ers have one of the top running backs in the NFL with Christian McCaffrey and an elite wide receiver with Mike Evans, while Kansas City has the league’s rushing leader with Kenneth Walker and speed galore at wide receiver. Maybe we have more of an issue here with Minnesota and being overly protective of the deep ball against a wide receiver corps that was missing Justin Jefferson. Yes, Jordan Addison is a former first-round pick and Aaron Jones is a solid running back, but wouldn’t it have made more sense to try to make Kyler Murray beat the Dolphins deep. What can’t be helped by scheme are the one-on-one battles the Dolphins lost, for which Jordyn Brooks took responsibility after the game.
The nature of playing tackle in the NFL is that getting beat is impossible to hide, and there was obvious pressure coming from the left side of the defensive formation in the Minnesota game, including the Dolphins’ final third down of the game, the throw down the middle to Chris Bell where Willis was hurried.
This has been a recurring them, but Hafley was quick to point out after earlier games that Jackson was going against stars like Maxx Crosby and Nick Bosa.
The question becomes, at what point does Jackson’s apparent protection issues become a real concern.
“I'm not concerned,” Hafley said. “I think if you really study that tape and watch the tape, you'll see improvement from Austin in that last game as well as the rest of our offensive line. So I am not concerned.”
Our take: Even if Jackson wasn’t constantly beaten in this game, there’s absolutely still room for improvement and having him beat so quickly on a key play late in the game like he was is just disappointing beyond words. That Hafley is backing his veteran is understandable, and the other fact that can’t be overlooked is that it’s not like the Dolphins have great options right now because moving Kadyn Proctor from left guard to right tackle after he’s gotten off a good start doesn’t seem wise at all and there’s a vast experience drop-off to Caedan Wallace or even Chukwueduka Godrick. We understand tackles will get beat from time to time, but at some point Jackson has to pitch a shutout.

title: Why Odell Beckham Jr. Might Have an Even Bigger Vikings Role Than Expected on Sunday
full_text:
UPDATE: The Vikings announced on Sunday morning that Beckham Jr. and Addison will both be inactive for today's game.
Vikings WR Justin Jefferson is ACTIVE for today's game against the Saints. WR Jordan Addison INACTIVE. WR Odell Beckham Jr. INACTIVE.
The Minnesota Vikings are in a sticky situation at wide receiver heading into Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season. Although the team signed Odell Beckham Jr. to the practice squad earlier this week, there is a good chance he could see the field on Sunday.
On Saturday afternoon, the Vikings elevated Beckham Jr. and Jeshaun Jones from the practice squad to the 53-man roster.
An ankle injury limited superstar pass catcher Justin Jefferson during practice this week, and he is listed as questionable for the game against the New Orleans Saints. Vikings WR2 Jordan Addison is on the injury report with a hamstring injury and is also questionable for the game.
If Jefferson and Addison are unable to play this week, Minnesota can't trust Jauan Jennings and Tai Felton to pick up the slack. Those two receivers have been non-factors this season despite getting offensive opportunities in previous games.
Beckham's recent history isn't very impressive. He hasn't caught a pass since Week 14 of the 2024 season and hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 14 of the 2023 season. However, he is a three-time Pro Bowl receiver who won Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2014, opening the door for him to contribute.
Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell needs to do whatever he can to spark this offense. The Vikings are ranked last in the league in passing yards per game (156) and have four passing touchdowns and two interceptions.
Giving quarterback Kyler Murray a veteran target with Beckham's accolades could create mismatches and assist other pass catchers in getting open. Even though he turns 34 years old later this year, this could be a great opportunity for the Super Bowl LVI champion to prove he still has gas left in his tank.
Even if Jefferson and Addison can suit up and play against the Saints, having them on the field for every offensive snap isn't wise. Therefore, having a capable player to take some of the weight off their shoulders will help.
If a player has to play while not being fully healthy, there's a calculated risk of aggravating the injury and forcing him to be out longer. Since Minnesota has a bye week in Week 6, it would make a lot of sense to play Jefferson and Addison as little as possible against New Orleans to give them the maximum amount of time to recover before returning from the bye.
That said, with Beckham being elevated to the 53-man roster, let's hope he can turn those opportunities into positive plays for Minnesota on Sunday afternoon.

title: Vikings at Saints: Who Wins and Why in Week 5
full_text:
It's Week 5, and the Minnesota Vikings have a few concerning injuries to monitor ahead of Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints. Christian Darrisaw has already been ruled out, and both Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison are questionable. Not ideal.
Still, the Saints' defense hasn't exactly been a model of consistency, and the Vikings will have opportunities to move the ball in New Orleans. So let's get into who wins and why in Minnesota's attempt to go 5-0 before the bye.
The Vikings offense is certainly getting plenty of chances to break out of their funk, getting the disastrous Miami Dolphins in Week 4 and now the 1-3 Saints in Week 5.
Outside of a Week 2 win against Baltimore, the Saints defense has been torched for 37 points per game in their other three contests, earning them the 32nd-ranked scoring defense in the NFL. That's welcome news for a Vikings team that is averaging just 21 points per game themselves.
Kyler Murray and the Minnesota offense looked respectable in the fourth quarter last week, going 13-for-14 for 120 yards against Miami. Bringing that momentum into New Orleans should be doable, but Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison's health could be a hindrance if one or both are limited. Newcomer Odell Beckham Jr. may see his first action of the season, which could be entertaining if nothing else.
The deciding factor in this game, though, could be how backup tackle Ryan Van Demark protects Murray's blindside. The Saints brought down Lamar Jackson three times, and without Christian Darrisaw, Murray may be sent on a running tour of the Superdome.
Tyler Shough is top-five in the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, and without starting running back Travis Etienne, he will be asked to carry the load again. He's thrown fewer than 40 times just once this year, so the Saints will almost surely be looking to air things out again. That's potentially a blessing for a blitz-happy Brian Flores, who could add to the 12 sacks Shough has already taken this year.
As for the run game, the six-touchdown Alvin Kamara of 2020 (not one of our better days) is far removed from the 2026 version, who has averaged just three yards per carry this season. Instead, the Vikings' secondary will get its first real test since Jordan Love in Week 1.
Even though Isaiah Rodgers and James Pierre have been extremely reliable this season, the same can't be said for the Vikings' safeties, who have allowed plenty of big plays on the back end.
Harrison Smith and Joshua Metellus are considered bottom-five safeties in the league by Pro Football Focus , but it doesn't take much more than a quick eye test to see they've been burned far too many times.
Saints receiver Chris Olave leads the NFL in receiving yards, and it's not unfathomable to think he has another big day against Minnesota's secondary.
Still, the Saints are probably too one-dimensional on offense to keep Dallas Turner and the rest of the pass rushers at bay. Without a running game threat, there's no reason Flores won't continue his 70% blitz rate in Week 5.

title: Vikings Have 3 Clear Advantages Over Saints in Week 5
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings hope to keep their winning ways alive on Sunday when they take on the New Orleans Saints. There is not much love between these two organizations, since they have caused each other heartbreak for many years.
One team will be leaving the Caesars Superdome with a loss on Sunday and it would be devastating if the team to hand Minnesota its first loss of the season was a team like the hated Saints.
Minnesota has some clear advantages over New Orleans that should make the difference in this weekend's game. If the Vikings can make the most of those opportunities , they should get a big road win to take them into the bye week with an undefeated record.
The Saints are tied for giving up the fourth-most sacks in the league through four games. They will need to do a great job protecting Tyler Shough against the aggressive pursuit of Brian Flores' defense.
New Orleans is going to struggle to keep pass rushers out of the backfield on Sunday. The Pro Football Focus grades for their offensive linemen tell a story of a team that is going to need to keep extra blockers to protect their quarterback.
The pass blocking of the tackles should play right into the hands of Minnesota edge rushers Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel. The tackles on the offensive line for the Saints are Taliese Fuaga and Asim Richards, both of whom have a PFF pass-blocking grade of under 50 for the season.
If the offensive line holds up for New Orleans on Sunday, it could be a long day for Minnesota's defensive secondary. The Saints are not only tied for the fourth-most passing touchdowns in the league (9), but they also have the fifth-most passing plays of 20 yards or more (15) and are tied for the seventh-most passing plays of 40 yards or more (3).
The bad thing for New Orleans is that Minnesota is allowing the lowest completion percentage to opposing quarterbacks (51.2) while being tied for the fewest passing touchdowns allowed (3) and racking up a league-high 16 sacks.
It is going to be interesting to watch the Saints try to pass against the Vikings in Week 5 and see which side wins this battle of strengths.
Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson had a huge game against the Dolphins last week. His 13 catches for 119 yards isn't likely to happen again, but he will create a tough matchup for New Orleans, particularly for the linebackers who try to take him down after catching the ball.
On the injury report , starting Saints linebacker Kaden Elliss is listed as out with a calf injury, while edge rusher Anfernee Jennings is also out with a knee injury. Not only that, but Jaylan Ford is questionable, and Carl Granderson was limited in practice earlier this week with an ankle injury.
New Orleans is all banged up in the middle of their defense, and Hockenson should be licking his chops at the opportunity to have another great day with Kyler Murray throwing him the football.

title: Vikings' WR Depth Will Be Tested If Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison Can't Play vs. Saints
full_text:
The Vikings released their final Week 5 injury report on Friday , and it could significantly impact Sunday’s game against the Saints in New Orleans (h/t: Vikings). Star left tackle Christian Darrisaw was confirmed to be out as he works through a concussion . Rookie corner and fan favorite Charles “Chuck” Demmings will also miss the game with a hamstring injury.
While confirmation of their status was disappointing, neither player being ruled out was a surprise.
Final #Vikings Week 5 injury report OUT: Christian Darrisaw and Chuck Demmings QUESTIONABLE: Jordan Addison, Justin Jefferson, Michael Jurgens*, Brian O’Neill and Ben Yurosek* *Currently in 21-day return to practice window pic.twitter.com/TLCCJUfUFF
The real intrigue came from the list of questionable players. Starting right tackle Brian O’Neill’s status is uncertain due to a knee injury, adding to concerns about an already depleted offensive line. Most significantly, the inclusion of wide receivers Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison suggests the team may be without both of its top receiving options.
Unfortunately for Vikings fans, the current depth at the position means Sunday’s game could get very interesting.
Let’s do what we can only assume head coach Kevin O’Connell is doing and mentally prepare for what Sunday could look like without Jefferson and Addison.
If neither can play, the WR room will likely include Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton, Myles Price, and practice-squad elevations for Jeshaun Jones and the newly signed Odell Beckham Jr. Based on the group’s production so far this season , they’ll need to hope someone in the room has a breakout performance.
Possible Vikings WR group for Sunday in New Orleans and their 2026 stats: *Jefferson and Addison listed as Questionable* - Jauan Jennings: 2 receptions for 9 yards. - OBJ: 0 receptions for 0 yards. -Tai Felton: 1 reception for 14 yards. - Myles Price: 2 receptions for 6…
Jennings would, in theory, be the team’s WR1 if Jefferson and Addison were to be ruled out. While his 2026 season has been a disappointment, the film tells a different story. Jennings is getting open , but he’s often too far down the list of progressions for Kyler Murray to find him while he works to figure out the timing of the offense (h/t: JClyyde)
WR Separation Score vs TPRR 📊 -- Carnell Tate building chemistry with Ward -- Downs, Doubs, Odunze, Pickens prime targets for positive regression -- MHJ in a league of his own pic.twitter.com/kDtxG8H22T
Felton, a 2025 third-rounder, looked to be coming into his own during this summer’s training camp, but has yet to make an impact so far this season. His inconsistent route-running makes him hard to count on in the passing game , but the team may not have a choice on Sunday.
Price is another interesting name to watch, as the special teams star flashed skills at the WR position during the preseason. But one name would naturally get all of the attention…
The Vikings signed the 33-year-old Beckham to the practice squad earlier this week. O’Connell’s comments to the press after his signing indicate he’s likely to be elevated regardless of Jefferson or Addison’s availability.
Beckham has largely been a non-factor in the league since totaling 565 receiving yards with the Ravens in 2023, before not even playing in the 2025 season. But his relationship with O’Connell from their Super Bowl run with the Rams, and the team's desperation in the passing game, could create opportunities on Sunday.
Luckily, I don't think anything short of an apocalyptic event will keep Justin Jefferson off the field on Sunday. His mid-week comments to the media made it clear he intends to play in what would be his first professional game in front of a crowd in his home state (h/t: ESPN' s Kevin Seifert).
Justin Jefferson on playing Sunday in New Orleans: "Hopefully so. That's definitely the plan. Being back at home, being in Louisiana, is definitely something that I want to do. So the plan is for me to play, but who knows? We going to take it day by day."
Addison’s status seems to be more of a mystery, but having one or both available on Sunday could help the offense find a desperately needed stride before the bye.

title: One Thought on All 11 Vikings Defensive Starters One Month Into the 2026 Season
full_text:
On Thursday, I broke down my thoughts on each of the Vikings' offensive starters now that the first month of the 2026 regular season is behind us. Today, let's dive into the defense and give one thought on each of the starters there.
The unit led by Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is playing among the best in the NFL, and it's no secret they've propelled the team to a 4-0 record.
Here are some quick hits about each Vikings defender's start to the season.
The Year 3 breakout is officially underway as Turner ranks second in the NFL in sacks with 5.5. He's also got a whopping 29 pressures through four games, but many have been quick to point out that 16 of those 29 were either unblocked or against a running back or tight end.
Still, Turner is a beast off the edge, and should never apologize for having a mad, scheming defensive coordinator getting him into favorable one-on-ones.
One of, if not the most underrated defenders in the league, Van Ginkel is once again playing at an All-Pro level this season.
With one of the most impressive stat lines in the NFL, with three sacks, three tackles for loss, an interception, and a forced fumble, 'Gink' truly does it all. In a contract year at 31 years old, his situation heading into next season will be something to monitor.
The sacks haven't been there in 2026 after a breakout season with six last year, but don't be fooled. Redmond is still playing really good football. His 90.1 Pro Football Focus run grade ranks first among all interior defensive linemen, and he has nine pressures to boot.
Redmond will be another big payday candidate in 2027.
A former seventh-round pick now starting is a success story in itself, but it isn't because the Vikings have no other options. Despite investing heavily up front in this year's draft, Rodriguez has been playing at a high level, notching six tackles and a sack at nose. The future is probably with Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange, but Rodriguez's relentless motor and ferocity will still be valued on this defense for a long time.
Yet another Kwesi Adofo-Mensah pick getting some run after the former general manager's departure, Ingram-Dawkins has been a nice stopgap in 2026. Like Rodriguez, he likely isn't the Vikings' long-term plans as a starter, but he's flashed at times, especially in the run game with two stuffs. Ingram-Dawkins came back in Year 2 leaner and potentially meaner, and is a key part of one of the best (and least expensive) defensive lines in the league.
If Van Ginkel is the most underrated defender in the league, Cashman may be a close second. The veteran has 15 straight games with at least seven tackles, the longest in franchise history, and has added 2.5 sacks so far this year for good measure.
Unfortunately, he's missed at least three games in each of his seasons with Minnesota, so here's to hoping he stays healthy in 2026.
Wilson had one elite game against Tampa Bay (10 tackles, 1.5 sacks) and three average ones beside it (14 tackles, no sacks). The 32-year-old was rewarded with a new deal after a breakout in 2025, and so far the results have clearly been mixed. He's definitely a player Flores loves, though, and as long as he can avoid accidental contact with officials this year, he'll remain a valuable piece.
The Vikings CB1 may actually be playing worse than CB2/3 this year. Murphy had a huge pick against Chicago, but otherwise has 15 catches allowed to just two breakups. The constant pressure Flores sends at opposing quarterbacks is also doing a pretty good job of keeping it off of Murphy.
Murphy is a solid corner, but he's yet to play up to his $54 million contract signed last March.
Rodgers has been playing some lights-out football in 2026 after a modest 2025 season outside of the wild Cincinnati game. He's allowing just 37% of passes thrown his way to be completed, combined with a 36.1 quarterback rating when targeted. Rodgers and James Pierre have been two bright spots in an otherwise troubling secondary.
If you look up from your bowl of guac and see an opposing receiver walking into the endzone, there's a decent chance Metellus was the closest defender. It's been a rough year on the back end for Metellus, who has been best deep on multiple occasions.
Metellus has allowed nearly 25 yards per reception when targeted, although part of that can be attributed to Flores constantly sending the other 10 guys at the quarterback. He's a team captain and leader, but there's no question he's been more of a liability than not.
It hurts to type, but Smith is playing like his age. His return was celebrated, as it should have been, but the play on the field has been rough. Still, his value at this stage is more about his brain than his brawn, and the Vikings are likely benefiting in ways not super apparent to the average viewer. He is graded as the third-worst safety in the NFL by PFF, for what it's worth.

title: Ryan Van Demark Under Vikings' Spotlight as Christian Darrisaw Misses Week 5 (and That's Not a Problem)
full_text:
The Vikings' offense hasn't lived up to expectations this season, and while some of the blame should fall on head coach Kevin O'Connell's shoulders, injuries have also played a part in the limited firepower . Unfortunately, Minnesota isn't even close to being out of the woods yet, as the left side of the offensive line could be without two of its anchors for the foreseeable future.
A torn meniscus has likely ended left guard Donovan Jackson's season , while left tackle Christian Darrisaw's outlook is murky as he keeps navigating the NFL's concussion protocol. His season might not be over like Jackson's, but Darrisaw will miss at least one more game after the Vikings officially ruled him out for Sunday's showdown against the Saints.
Final #Vikings Week 5 injury report OUT: Christian Darrisaw and Chuck Demmings QUESTIONABLE: Jordan Addison, Justin Jefferson, Michael Jurgens*, Brian O’Neill and Ben Yurosek* *Currently in 21-day return to practice window pic.twitter.com/TLCCJUfUFF
As great as it would've been to see Darrisaw back on the field this weekend, it's never a good idea to rush a player back from a concussion. On top of that, the Vikings have their bye coming up next week, giving the Virginia Tech product even more time to make a full recovery.
Until then, Minnesota needs the next man to step up. Although rookie OT Caleb Tiernan might benefit from Darrisaw's continued absence , likely Sunday starter Ryan Van Demark will be tasked with filling that role—and it might go better than some fans expect.
A former undrafted free agent signed by the Colts in 2022, Van Demark joined the Vikings on a one-year, $4.2 million contract in free agency after spending the last four seasons with the Bills. He played 558 offensive snaps across 43 games (six starts) during that stretch, giving him the type of experience Minnesota wanted in a backup tackle for a situation exactly like Darrisaw's injury.
Admittedly, Van Demark's pass protection isn't flawless, allowing 15 pressures despite only playing 250 pass-block downs for the Bills, according to Pro Football Focus . That said, his PFF pass-block grade improved with each passing season (27.2 to 51.8 to 65.6 in 2025), and he even looked extremely sound to close out last season.
He wasn't perfect by any means, but it's clear that Van Demark successfully handled a bigger role when the Bills needed him to play one. He even saved his best performance of the year for last, finishing Week 18 with season-high grades for run blocking (82.6), pass protection (82.3) and overall offense (84.5).
Van Demark's efficiency in keeping his quarterbacks on their feet continues into the 2026 preseason, as he didn't allow a single sack over 50 offensive snaps in three appearances. And even though he allowed three pressures when filling in for Darrisaw in last week's win over the Dolphins, it was the same old, same old for the 6-foot-7, 307-pounder: no sacks surrendered.
Van Demark's importance will only increase if starting right tackle Brian O'Neill (questionable) also can't suit up in Week 5. The good news is that Van Demark has experience at both tackle roles, so he could fill in for O'Neill if the Vikings prefer Tiernan on the left side.
Either way, fans can expect to see Van Demark early and often as he makes his first start in Purple and Gold, regardless of which side of the O-line he's on. All signs point to him being able to handle the task, which will be crucial if the Vikings want to remain perfect when their bye week begins on Monday.

title: 5 Vikings Who Will Likely Be Inactive vs. Saints in Week 5 After Friday's Injury Report
full_text:
On Sunday, the Vikings will face off against the Saints in a game that could create huge momentum for the Purple and Gold. A win would extend the winning streak to five games , while suffering their first loss would start their Week 6 bye on a low note.
The Vikings can have a maximum of 48 players active on game day, which means at least five individuals will need to be inactive against the Saints. Choosing which players to sit on Sunday could be the difference between a victory and a defeat.
Minnesota's inactive players won't be announced until a few hours before this weekend's game, but by looking at the injury report and the previous inactive players, five Vikings are more likely to sit out than others against the Saints in Week 5.
Minnesota's starting left tackle is on the injury report with a concussion and hasn't practiced all week. Christian Darrisaw was declared out on Friday afternoon (h/t Vikings), and Ryan Van Demark is expected to get the start at LT in New Orleans.
Final #Vikings Week 5 injury report OUT: Christian Darrisaw and Chuck Demmings QUESTIONABLE: Jordan Addison, Justin Jefferson, Michael Jurgens*, Brian O’Neill and Ben Yurosek* *Currently in 21-day return to practice window pic.twitter.com/TLCCJUfUFF
Although Van Demark doesn't offer the same kind of pass protection as Darrisaw, he is a quality run blocker. He earned a 75 run-blocking grade from Pro Football Focus this season and should be used to open holes for running backs while Darrisaw misses at least one game.
Like Darrisaw, Chuck Demmings is on the injury report this week. A hamstring injury prevented him from fully participating in practice this week, and he was declared out on Friday and will not play against New Orleans.
Demmings has played 26 total snaps for the Vikings this season, with only two of those coming on defense. Minnesota shouldn't have much trouble filling his role, especially on special teams. However, it will be great when the young defensive back returns to gain more experience on the field.
Defensive lineman Elijah Williams has been inactive for all four of the Vikings' games this season, and that trend likely won't stop in Week 5. Although he has experience from last season, playing 42 defensive snaps, Minnesota has enough depth and talent at the position to keep him inactive.
Besides, there are already players who are fighting for snaps on the defensive line. Rookies Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange need that experience to continue their development Jalen Redmond, Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, and Levi Drake Rodriguez hold down the trenches to allow the younger players time to adjust to the NFL.
This is another case where a player has been inactive all season. Jakobe Thomas ended the preseason with an ankle injury, and Minnesota hasn't rushed him back. But he hasn't appeared on the Vikings' injury report with that injury leading into any of the team's regular-season games, which means it shouldn't be an issue going forward.
Thomas was a third-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, so the Purple and Gold will want to get him on the field eventually. However, there is absolutely no reason to throw him into Brian Flores's complicated defense until he is ready to be a contributor.
Max Brosmer will technically be inactive, but he will dress for Week 5 against the Saints. He will act as the emergency third quarterback if something happens to Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz in that game and neither can continue.
By naming him the third quarterback, he receives an inactive designation and will not count against the roster limit for Week 5. If Brosmer has to enter the game, something very bad is happening in New Orleans.

title: Vikings Week 5: 3 Most Important Things to Watch for vs. Saints on Sunday  (Underrated Rivalry Continues)
full_text:
Your 4-0 Vikings head south this weekend to chase a perfect 5-0 record as they prepare to enter their bye week. In their way? A chippy Saints team led by head coach Kellen Moore and quarterback Tyler Shough.
Despite their record, facing the 1-3 Saints won’t exactly be a vacation to the French Quarter, as Shough has thrown for an impressive 1,203 yards and nine touchdowns to start the season.
The Vikings' defense will certainly need to keep up their patented aggression to limit Shough’s effectiveness, but the biggest story may be on the opposing side of the ball.
Here’s what to watch as the Vikings fight to remain perfect in 2026 against an opponent with whom they share quite a history.
If recent trends continue, the matchup between the Vikings and Saints may just be one of the more entertaining games of the weekend.
In fact, the two squads have built quite the rivalry over the years, despite being non-divisional foes on opposite sides of the country. Although Minnesota holds a dominant 25-13 all-time series lead, the two squads have had some incredible matchups over the last two decades.
Of course, there’s the 2009 NFC Championship/Bountygate scandal that we choose to ignore whenever possible, the Minneapolis Miracle in the 2017 divisional round, a Vikings OT walkoff Wild Card round win in 2019, Alvin Kamara’s six rushing touchdowns against the Vikings in 2020, and the peak of “Dobbs-sanity” as Josh Dobbs defeated the Saints in Minnesota in the last battle between the two teams.
Throwback to the last time the Vikings and Saints faced off in 2023 as Josh Dobbs plays lights out in his first start for the Vikings. - 268 passing yards - 1 passing TD - 1 sack taken - 101.1 passer rating - 44 rushing yards - 1 rushing TD Vikings win 27-19 pic.twitter.com/SYJUh1tED7
Needless to say, there’s not much love between these two franchises in recent years.
Drew Brees’s induction into the Saints’ Ring of Honor at halftime on Sunday adds extra fuel for Vikings fans in the stands who saw him win a Super Bowl with New Orleans after the controversial 2009 conference championship.
We started to see glimpses of what the Vikings’ pass game could look like at the end of Week 4’s matchup against Miami, and we’ll need to see the next steps in that marriage between coach and QB this weekend. Head coach Kevin O’Connell and quarterback Kyler Murray are clearly working through the difficult task of blending two completely different passing philosophies, and it has not always been perfect.
The Vikings are currently dead last in the NFL with 156 passing yards per game (h/t: ESPN ).  While it would be unfair to expect Murray to suddenly become Sam Darnold or Kirk Cousins and turn into a pure pocket passer, the team needs the passing offense to get on track if it wants to contend.
Luckily, we saw glimpses of what this could look like last week, as O’Connell began implementing more shotgun and quick-game concepts. Minnesota’s offense could start to take key strides this weekend if that trend continues.
Justin Jefferson was listed as a limited participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday and told the media he plans to play Sunday, barring any setbacks with his left ankle. Jefferson’s return in front of his hometown crowd could give the passing offense a much-needed boost, especially if he takes the field with fellow Louisiana legend and mentor Odell Beckham Jr.
Entering the bye week at 5-0 would be a major accomplishment for the Vikings, especially given how inconsistent their offense has been at the start of the season. With their schedule getting tougher, every win they can stack now gives them an additional buffer for a challenging November-through-December stretch.
The bye week also gives them chances to address concerns along the offensive line , the running back room, and in the passing game, regardless of Sunday’s outcome. If the Vikings use the bye week to retool and recover, they may be set up for a successful run through the gauntlet portion of their schedule that starts in November.
Being 5-0 on the break just happens to be the best possible circumstance.

title: Under-the-Radar CB Is Clearly Vikings' Best Offseason Addition One Month Into 2026 Season
full_text:
It's hard to believe that the first month of the 2026 NFL season is behind us , but here we are. The Vikings—against all odds—have an unblemished 4-0 record to show for their early efforts, and though there is room for improvement (looking at the offense), the Purple and Gold have given fans enough reason to believe that the best is yet to come.
Staying perfect won't be easy, but Minnesota can remain one of the NFL's top teams if its best contributors keep producing, which includes first-time Vikings. While some fresh faces (like Jauan Jennings) are struggling, others have thrived in the first month of action, setting the stage for what should be a promising rest-of-season performance.
That includes one under-the-radar defender who's quietly become a key cog in Brian Flores's defensive machine.
Isaiah Rodgers and Byron Murphy Jr. were always going to enter the 2026 season as the Vikings' top cornerback options, but they needed more depth than just Zemaiah Vaughn behind them. That's why, before using a fifth-round pick on rookie CB Chuck Demmings, Minnesota signed former undrafted free agent James Pierre to a two-year, $8.5 million contract in March .
The Florida Atlantic product was looking for a fresh start after playing 95 games (13 starts) across two stints with the Steelers, splitting his time almost evenly between defense (1,309 snaps) and special teams (1,359 snaps). Pierre amassed 102 solo tackles (1.1 per game), five forced fumbles and four interceptions during that stretch, which included a pick in each of the last three campaigns.
Pierre wasn't a household name, but his 87.4 Pro Football Focus coverage grade with the Steelers last season provided a glimpse of what he could do. Fortunately, the Vikings' free-agent signing picked up where he left off, as proven by his stats from the first four games:
James Pierre after 4 games
Defensive snaps (in coverage)
Sure, Pierre's sample size isn't the biggest at a glance, but his 75 coverage snaps rank third among Vikings CBs, trailing only Murphy (155) and Rodgers (154), and he's only been targeted 10 times.
It's clear that Flores & Co. have found a way to maximize Pierre's skills without needing to constantly have him on the field, which could be smart in the long run. Having the 30-year-old veteran more rested later in the year could let the Vikings use him more often while saving Murphy and Rodgers's energy for the postseason.
Pierre will have one more opportunity to build on his strong start to the 2026 season when the Vikings visit New Orleans to take on the 1-3 Saints this weekend .
The Saints average the fourth-most passing yards per game (278.5) on an NFL-leading 45.0 attempts, which means Pierre (and the rest of the Vikings' secondary) should have plenty of chances to make plays. New Orleans' offensive line is a work in progress and has already allowed QB Tyler Shough to be sacked 12 times (T-3rd-most), and the pressure has also led to three interceptions (T-9th-most).
In other words, Pierre has a busy Week 5 ahead. If he stays the course and keeps his foot on the gas, it could be another productive day in coverage, adding to the case that he's been the Vikings' best offseason addition and may deserve an expanded role as the season continues.

title: 3 Bold Predictions as Vikings Battle Saints for a 5-0 Start (Kyler Murray Remains Clean in the Big Easy)
full_text:
The Vikings head south to New Orleans this weekend to take on the 1-3 Saints, who are coming off a 45-24 home loss to their division rival Falcons.
The Saints are a feistier team than their record may suggest, and the Vikings have not always had the best of times in the Big Easy. Still, the opportunity to enter the bye week 5-0 means Sunday afternoon's contest is too important to downplay.
As the action nears, here are my three bold predictions as the Vikings fight to remain undefeated against the Saints in Week 5.
Admit it. Every Vikings fan has imagined themselves lining up at quarterback in the Superdome on Jan. 24, 2010, with a chance to get the team in range for a game-winning field goal to advance to the Super Bowl.
The reality of Brett Favre’s interception across his body (h/t: NFL) in that exact scenario has left a traumatic scar on generations of Vikings fans, including Kyler Murray, who wasted no time ingratiating himself with the fanbase when he signed in March, saying he cried “real tears” after Favre’s brutal NFC Championship interception .
Murray now has the chance to suit up for the team he grew up rooting for, in that same stadium. I predict he'll make sure history doesn't repeat itself. With the offense’s new focus on smart, safe football, I see Murray avoiding unnecessary risks.
Mark me down for a zero-turnover game from QB1 on Sunday.
After a relatively quiet two-sack performance (h/t: NFL) by the Vikings defense in Week 4, Sunday seems like a great chance to go all out before the bye week. The Vikings’ defense leads the NFL with 16 sacks so far this season, while the Saints offense is tied for third in total sacks allowed at 12.
Dallas Turner stays hot 🔥 MIAvsMIN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mL27DhWl9A
The Vikings have been attacking opposing QBs at an astounding rate, and Saints QB Tyler Shough may be the perfect target. Although he’s 27, he has yet to play a full season’s worth of games in the NFL.
Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores will be looking to play mind games with Shough and Saints head coach Kellen Moore.  Shough is currently third in the league in passing yards with 1,203 through four games, for an average of just over 300 yards per game. Taking him down will be essential to slowing down the Saints' passing attack.
This may be my boldest take of the week, as neither Justin Jefferson nor the newly signed Odell Beckham Jr. is guaranteed to play this weekend . Jefferson was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday and Thursday's practices after missing last week with an ankle injury. While his status is uncertain, he made it clear he intends to play on Sunday, barring any setbacks (h/t: ESPN’ s Kevin Seifert).
Beckham is currently on the team’s practice squad, but head coach Kevin O’Connell emphasized Wednesday that he has no concerns about his ability to be ready for an elevation on Sunday, referencing his signing and immediate use with the Rams in 2021 .
Kevin O’Connell says he’s confident Odell Beckham can be ready to impact the game Sunday if he is elevated. pic.twitter.com/gaGMvvc5UF
I'm confident one or both of the former LSU Tigers will take the field for their return home, and O’Connell will find a way to get at least one of them into the end zone. So far, Jefferson’s only pro game in New Orleans came on Christmas in 2020, when fans were not even allowed to attend.
Sunday marks his first chance to play in front of his home crowd in his career, and I feel like he’s about to put on a show.

title: Patriots Week 5 Inactives vs. Raiders: Secondary Taking Hit after Hit
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots are sitting at 2-2, but it's taken some crazy turns to get them to that point . Bad losses, thrilling wins and a myriad of injuries have them back at home for a date with the Las Vegas Raiders.
But they won't be taking the field at full strength.
Here are all the players on the Patriots and Raiders that won't be suiting up for the Week 5 game:
QB Behren Morton (emergency third QB)
QB Aidan O'Connell (emergency third QB)
CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder)
WR Jalen Nailor (concussion)
CB Karon Prunty (hamstring)
CB Channing Canada (hamstring)
The biggest story is Gonzalez and Davis sidelined once again . Gonzalez, who looked like he got banged up on a tackle in Week 3, told reporters after the game that he felt "good." But it's clear that he's dealing with something more serious than initially thought.
One big return will be Christian Barmore, who missed last week with a shoulder injury. He was questionable to play ( along with Rhamondre Stevenson ), but they will be out there.
Morton will only be allowed to play if both Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito get hurt. Practice squad elevation safety Elliott Davison will make his NFL debuts today. Linebacker K.J. Britt (practice squad) and safety Brenden Schooler (non-football injury list) will also make their season debuts.
Gonzalez missed last week, but it didn't seem like this injury — at least to me — would stretch into multiple weeks. Nope, the 24-year-old has missed six-straight practices and won't be dressing.
But it's not just Gonzalez who can't go. Davis, the Patriots' most physical cornerback at the line of scrimmage, is dealing with a neck injury that held him out of the team's Week 2 win against Pittsburgh. And then Karon Prunty and Channing Canada, both rookies, will miss the game with hamstring ailments.
To help fill the void at cornerback, the Patriots signed Kindle Vildor off of the practice squad to the 53-man roster . But that only brings the total active corners to three for the game.
The Patriots are rolling into the game with Vildor, Marcus Jones and Charles Woods (who entered the day questionable with a shoulder injury). I don't see the Raiders using their wide receivers a lot this game, so it might not be that big of a worry for New England. But this is easily the weakest part of the roster right now.
The Patriots are going to be without A.J. Brown for at least one more game, and then they had to put Mack Hollins on injured reserve with a calf injury . That leaves them with just four active wide receivers for the game (Kyle Dixon, Chandler Brayboy or Cameron Dorner weren't elevated off of the practice squad).
So it will be Romeo Doubs, Efton Chism III, DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams this week. Chism, who was the hero in Buffalo for his game-winning touchdown snag , could see an uptick in snaps compared to the start of the year. He was the one to helped step up for Hollins after the vet went down.
“It wouldn’t be right for me to sit up here and not talk about his work ethic and his character," offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels said this week. "Since the moment we got him, he has been at the highest level. It’s hard to say that an undrafted college free agent would be a pros pro, but I will tell you that’s what he is. He came in with that kind of demeanor, that kind of attitude. He understands that I’m going to be ready when my time is up, and he was and has been since he’s been here."
If Drake Maye and the Patriots want to stack wins for the first time this season, they'll need one of these wideouts to really break out. Doubs and Chism both found the end zone last week, but Douglas and Williams are due for a stellar outing.
The Patriots and Raiders will kick off from Gillette Stadium at 1 p.m. EST. It's going to be a fun one in Foxboro, as the Patriots plan to honor the 25th anniversary of their Super Bowl XXXVI-winning team before the game . At halftime, they'll also give recent Pro Football Hall of Fame inductee Adam Vinatieri his induction ring — the first Patriots player to receive it since Richard Seymour in 2022. This week will also be the first of two times this season that the Patriots break out their Pat Patriot red throwback jerseys.

title: Injuries Among Top Storylines for Patriots' Home Test with Raiders
full_text:
The New England Patriots said postgame in Buffalo that they felt like their comeback win got them back into the race. Now it's time to see if that's actually the case.
The Patriots are hosting the 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday for their Week 5 matchup. It's a chance for the Patriots to string some wins together, and try to settle in from an uneasy start to the season.
"We have to take the same approach as we did last week and understand how critical and important each week in the National Football League is," Mike Vrabel said. "It's a new opponent, but our preparation has to stay the same - our urgency, the energy level. I think that that can certainly carry over to an extent. But it has to translate to practice, and it has to build throughout the week."
Here are four things to watch out for today when the ball gets kicked off:
This season has been filled with injuries for New England. A.J. Brown, Mike Onwenu, Greg Van Roten, Marcus Bryant, Bryce Baringer, Dell Pettus and Quintayvious Hutchins were all on injured reserve heading into this week. Then they were joined by Reggie Gilliam and Mack Hollins yesterday .
The Patriots had to place 19 players on IR this year, three more than all of last season. It's forcing some of the other players on the roster — Efton Chism III, Elijah Ponder, Jaylen Reed — to step up at times.
This week will be no different.
Going on the injury theme, the Patriots are pretty banged up . Cornerback is the big one, where Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis, Channing Canada and Karon Prunty were all ruled out. That leaves just three cornerbacks on today's roster — Marcus Jones, Charles Woods and practice squad elevation Kindle Vildor.
Lucky for the Patriots, they're going up against a Raiders team that really doesn't have imposing threats at wideout. Tre Tucker, Cody White, Dareke Young and Malik Benson don't offer a whole lot of intimidating threats on the outside.
The Patriots should be getting Christian Barmore back, who missed last week with a shoulder injury. He and Milton Williams haven't had their true star performance yet this year, so a game where stopping the run and Las Vegas' bigger personnels could be a great opportunity to start.
Drake Maye shined last week against the Bills, throwing three touchdowns (one of them being the game winner). But we haven't seen him extend winning football into back-to-back weeks. Too often in 2026, Maye struggles with turnovers and the offense can't seem to get out of its own way.
That could change today, as Maye can start to truly right the ship that's been sailing the wrong direction . He'll have to do it with limited resources at the wide receiver position (only Romeo Doubs, Kyle Williams, DeMario Douglas and Chism are active).
"I'm trying to keep the same mindset when things don't go well, of next week and trying to bounce back from it," Maye said Wednesday. "Also, from this week, when you said, 'Riding the rollercoaster,' every week is a new week in this league, and every team is different and has different challenges. You know that it's any given week. Like I've said time and time again in this league, you have to play good football to end up on the right side of things."
The Raiders come into the game with two superstars on offense: running back Ashton Jeanty and tight end Brock Bowers. They've been big reasons for the surprising 3-1 start for Las Vegas. The Patriots will need to shut down both of these players if they want a chance to winning the game.
Jeanty, the sixth overall pick from a year ago, has 264 yards on the ground, but is still looking for his first touchdown of the season. Bowers — arguably the league's best tight end already — has caught 16 passes for 202 yards and two touchdowns in a pair of games.
"Really, Brock is a receiver," Vrabel said. "What he does at his size, the speed, the route craft, and being able to catch at the catch point. He's like a big slot receiver. He has downfield speed, he runs outward breaking routes, he runs routes like a receiver, but then also he's got the ability to double guys up inside."

title: 5 Patriots to Watch in Injury-Riddled Battle vs. Raiders
full_text:
The New England Patriots are back at home Sunday afternoon for a battle with the Las Vegas Raiders. Last time out against the Buffalo Bills, New England had by far its best offensive performance of the year.
The Patriots put up a season-high 29 points, while quarterback Drake Maye earned AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors.
So, can New England ride that momentum into this weekend against Las Vegas? Or will the injury-riddled squad falter? Here are the five players to keep an eye on may be the biggest contributors toward answering those questions.
Last week was easily Doubs' best as a Patriot. The 26-year-old tallied a season-high six receptions, notched 58 yards and scored his first two touchdowns as a member of New England's squad. Now, headed into this week, the Patriots offense may need to lean on the former Green Bay Packer.
New England heads into Sunday afternoon with just four wide receivers on its active roster, with A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins both on injured reserve.
"So, that was one of the cool things, to see him rewarded for the work he's put in and finally getting in the end zone," Maye said on Wednesday regarding Doubs' performance against the Bills. "He keeps on doing things the right way and he's going to keep on making plays for us."
While the Patriots wide receiver room is thin, the cornerback depth is substantially thinner. New England ruled out Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis III, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada for Sunday's battle. Vildor is one of just three Patriots corners expected to see action on Sunday.
The 28-year-old spent the preseason with New England, shining toward the end of training camp after a slow start to the summer. On Saturday, he was signed to the Patriots' active roster from the practice squad. No matter who he lines up across from, Vildor will play a substantial role against the Raiders.
Chism is in an extremely similar boat as Doubs: coming off a season-best game (two receptions, 42 yards, TD), working within a thin receiver room and expecting a larger-than-usual role this Sunday.
"I mean, guys continue to take advantage of their opportunities, they get more opportunities," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said on Monday. "I mean, we've been finding ways to work (Chism) in there previously. And it's a balance, but he certainly did a lot of things well. I know that he'll continue to do things well for us and continue to know a bunch of different spots."
It remains to be seen whether Chism can ride the momentum of his highlight-reel go-ahead touchdown against the Bills last week. However, it feels near-certain the former undrafted free agent will continue to see his role in the Patriots offense expand.
This choice is less-so about Moses and more-so about Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby. Although the 29-year-old has tallied just two sacks this year, he still sits top-five in the NFL in pressures.
Maxx Crosby is getting doubled at the highest rate among edge, but he's still making his way to the QB pic.twitter.com/EEAeiqZFWY
Quite simply, the Patriots will have to slow down Crosby to have any chance at victory.  While Moses has been far from perfect this season (his 59.4 PFF grade ranks 54th of eligble tackles), a stifling performance in the trenches may be the biggest key to victory for New England.
"Maxx will go wherever he wants to go, and he will do whatever he wants to do," Vrabel said on Wednesday. "And it's worked out really, really well. I have a lot of respect f or Maxx Crosby as a person and also as a player. So, we'll have to know where he is on every single play. It's been impressive."
The Patriots will need a full-effort performance from the entire defense, starting with its captain. Spillane may have to do a bit of everything on Sunday against his former squad. Due to the injuries in New England's cornerback room, he may be asked to assume further responsibilities in pass coverage.
Not to mention, Las Vegas sits top-five in the league in rush attempts per game despite averaging the fewest yards per attempt. If Spillane and New England can continue to slow down the ground game, it may take some pressure off the load for a depleted Patriots pass defense.

title: Looking Ahead to Patriots' Next 4 Games (Which Consists of Far Easier Opponents)
full_text:
This year's New England Patriots faced the hardest four game stretch of any NFL team since 1986. Combined, the Seattle Seahawks, Pittsburgh Steelers, Jacksonville Jaguars, and Buffalo Bills had a win percentage of .721 in 2025.
Looking back at the first four weeks of the NFL season, a 2-2 record is impressive for a Patriots team that met the challenge of a first-place schedule, an unprecedented amount of injuries, and plentiful roster turnover. Now, with 13 games to play in the 2026 NFL regular season, things are looking up for the Pats, who have made it through their most difficult stretch all year .
Before the full schedule is released, take a look at each team's strength of schedule for 2026. 👀 📺: NFL Schedule Release - Thursday at 8pm ET on ESPN/NFLN pic.twitter.com/eChBp3QMVa
According to ESPN’s football power index, the Patriots have the 27th-hardest schedule remaining in the 2026 season.
Of the 10 teams the Patriots have yet to face on their schedule, five of those made the playoffs last year (not counted is the Buffalo Bills who the Patriots already faced and beat 29-26 in Week 4).
Weeks 1 to 4 consisted of a four-game stretch against teams coming off playoff appearances. Though the Patriots will see six  2025 playoff teams this season, NFL records through four weeks of play indicate the next three quarters of the season could be much easier than the first.
The average win total of each New England opponent for the remainder of the season (including both games against the New York Jets and Miami Dolphins) is .481. This significant drop-off from the strength of schedule the Patriots faced in the first four weeks will play to New England’s benefit, as they gear up for a second straight playoff run.
In weeks 5 through 8, the Patriots will see the likes of the Las Vegas Raiders (3-1), Jets (3-1), Chicago Bears (3-1), and Miami Dolphins (0-4).
Another look at the 2026 schedule 🗓️ pic.twitter.com/ilq6rPxFeE
In this second quarter run, the Patriots will face two of the NFL’s worst teams from last season in the Raiders and the Jets, who each had three wins a season ago. Although, the Raiders have started hot under first year head coach Klint Kubiak, who faced Mike Vrabel’s Patriots in the Super Bowl as Seattle’s offensive coordinator.
The Jets, in the works of retooling their roster to be competitive in the AFC East, have showcased impressive young talent, especially from the likes of rookie first-rounders EDGE David Bailey and TE Kenyon Sadiq. However, with no real aspirations for much success this year, New York's dropped three consecutive games after beating the winless Tennessee Titans in their season opener.
Chicago, on the other hand, is proving to be a force in the NFC. Despite losing starting quarterback Caleb Williams with a hamstring injury, the Bears have managed an impressive 3-1 record under head coach Ben Johnson. Week 7’s Thursday Night Football action in Chicago will draw eyes from across the country as this matchup between third-year QBs and second-year head coaches hits the primetime window.
The Patriots will finish their first half of the season against the Dolphins, who are still looking for their first win under head coach Jeff Hafley. Star running back Devon Achane went down with a season-ending knee injury in week 3, leaving the offense dependent on free agent acquisition Malik Willis. Unless disaster strikes, New England should fly home from Miami with a comfortable win.
With schedule talks surrounding the team’s unforeseen success in 2025, the Patriots split their first four games of the season, proving to critics that they’re ready to meet the challenge of a stronger schedule. This early success has provided New England with room to make mistakes as they gear up for the next four weeks.

title: Mack Hollins to Injured Reserve: Here's Several WR Options the Patriots May Explore
full_text:
The start of the 2026 season for the New England Patriots has been unfavorable for the team’s roster availability. After placing WR Mack Hollins and FB Reggie Gilliam to the injured reserve, a total of 19 players have been listed on the reserve list this season.
Hollins, who suffered a calf injury in Week 4,  joins Brown on the list of receivers to miss extended time . Acquired by the Patriots for a 2028-first round pick and 2027-fifth round pick, Brown went down in the 3rd quarter of the season against Seattle in the league opener with a high ankle sprain. His expected return date ranges from Week 6 to Week 8.
Hollins has been a dependable replacement in the wake of Brown's injury. The 10-year veteran is the Patriots leading receiver on the season with 209 yards on 15 receptions. Last year, Hollins missed time at the end of the season with an abdomen injury before returning in the AFC Championship game against Denver.
On Monday, head coach Mike Vrabel said, “Anybody that can help us. We’ll go explore here shortly.” This came in response to a question regarding the Brown and Hollins injuries and their affect on the receiving corps.
The #Patriots will explore bringing in a wide receiver with A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins dealing with injuries, per HC Mike Vrabel. "Sure. Anybody that can help us, we'll go exploring here shortly." (🎥 @Patriots ) pic.twitter.com/Xa7E3D8Hl2
Currently, the receivers signed to the active roster include Romeo Doubs, Demario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III. The practice squad consists of three inexperienced wide receivers in Chandler Brayboy Kyle Dixon, and Cameron Dorner – none of them were elevated for Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders.
If the Patriots were to look into acquiring a receiver, they’d have to consider whether the goal is to fill the gap temporarily while Brown and Hollins rehab their injuries, or if they’re interested in a long-term addition to the receiving corps.
If Vice President of Player Personnel Eliot Wolf and Vrabel look for a temporary solution, they’ll most likely eye the practice squads of other teams or free agents.
Odell Beckham Jr. was just signed by the Minnesota Vikings on Wednesday to the practice squad, so acquiring him would mean signing him to the 53-man roster. Other signing options include veteran players like Gabe Davis and Zay Jones, who are towards the end of rehabbing injuries sustained last year.
There’s also proven NFL players like Noah Brown or Brandin Cooks – both awaiting another chance to step on the field. Of course, Tyreek Hill – showing enthusiasm for a comeback from his gruesome knee injury a year ago – has teased his interest in signing with an NFL team .
Whether or not the Patriots have shown interest in unsigned veteran receivers has remained to be reported on.
If the Patriots were to acquire a weapon by trade, this player would presumably stay on the active roster as long as they’re healthy. On Friday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Arizona Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison Jr. has been included in a finalized trade package with an unnamed team.
The fourth overall pick in the NFL Draft (one pick after Drake Maye) has had a lackluster start to his NFL career after hauling in 2,613 receiving yards and 31 touchdowns in three years at Ohio State. With this news coming the morning of Hollins’ injury designation, fans are left to wonder if the Patriots are the undisclosed team that acquired Harrison, or if the front office will make a better offer than the one already in place.
Breaking: the Arizona Cardinals are finalizing a deal to trade WR Marvin Harrison, sources tell me and @RapSheet . The team informed Harrison this morning that he will be inactive for Sunday’s game vs Detroit as details of the trade are finalized. pic.twitter.com/x6n0Hsfzzj
A less expensive purchase could come from the Cleveland Browns, who have minimized WR Jerry Jeudy’s offensive impact, or the Los Angeles Chargers – a ship that’s half-way sunken and ready to sell-out of players like WR Quentin Johnston.
The Patriot’s AFC East foe Miami Dolphins also look to be gearing up for the 2027 Draft and may exploit skill position players like Malik Washington or Jalen Torbert.
The Patriots currently have 52 players rostered , meaning that another addition or practice squad elevation could come before they face off against the Raiders on Sunday.
We’ll await to see if Vrabel’s comments on expanding the wide receiver room result in any transactions being made, and if these moves provide long or short-term impact.

title: Patriots Look to Preseason Star as Cornerback Room Suffers Significant Losses
full_text:
Friday’s injury report revealed a tightened cornerback room for the New England Patriots (2-2), as they prepare to host the Las Vegas Raiders (3-1) on Sunday.
The losses in the defensive secondary include Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), Carlton Davis III (neck), Karon Prunty (hamstring), and Channing Canada (hamstring).
In response to the injuries of all four cornerbacks listed above, the Patriots have signed CB Kindle Vildor and S Mike Brown to the 53-man roster and elevated S Elliott Davison.
Patriots make a myriad of roster moves today: Signed to 53-man roster — CB Kindle Vildor Placed on IR — FB Reggie Gilliam, WR Mack Hollins Activated off NFI — S Brenden Schooler Elevated from practice squad — LB K.J. Britt, S Elliott Davison
Prior to signing Vildor to the active roster, the Pats had just two corners eligible to play this week. Marcus Jones was listed as active, while Charles Woods has been designated as questionable with a shoulder injury.
With Vildor’s signing, the Patriots will likely carry three cornerbacks into their Week 5 matchup against the Raiders. While losing both Gonzalez and Davis is a massive detriment to the defense, here’s what you can expect from the backups:
On Thursday, the Patriots announced they were signing Mike Brown to the active roster. A 2026 free agent acquisition, Brown saw playing time in each of the previous two games against Jacksonville and Buffalo as an elevated practice squad player. Now in his fifth year in the NFL, Brown steps into a damaged secondary unit for the Patriots.
In addition to Brown’s signing, the Patriots elevated S Elliott Davison, who in his second year after going undrafted, will see his first regular season action in the NFL.
Friday’s injury report indicated one designation to the Patriots safeties. Craig Woodson is listed as questionable to play on Sunday with a shoulder injury. Despite a relatively healthy safety group in Kevin Byard, Woodson, and Jaylen Reed, the Patriots add two players to the positional lineup with Brown and Davison (note - New England brought S Brenden Schooler back from the non-football injury list, but he’ll primarily play special teams).
These roster changes suggest that we may see Brown, Davison or other safeties lineup at cornerback, or at the very least, in a hybrid corner-safety position.
One of the biggest preseason presences for the Patriots this summer was cornerback Kindle Vildor. An NFL journeyman in his eighth season and now, with his fifth different team, Vildor excelled in the preseason, recording 3 pass break-ups, 6 tackles, and an interception across three games.
Many were surprised to see Channing Canada get the fifth cornerback spot on the 53-man roster over Vildor. As a fifth-round pick out of Georgia Southern in the 2020 draft, Vildor’s career has been short of stellar, appearing in 81 games and registering two interceptions.
Now, Vildor will be asked to step into a huge role against the Raiders, who have presented one of the best scoring offenses in football. Averaging 28.8 points per game, the Raiders rank seventh in total scoring on the season in the NFL.
In addition, no quarterback has thrown for more touchdowns this season than Kirk Cousins, who is currently tied with the 49ers’ Brock Purdy for the league lead (11).
Cousins will look to receivers Tre Tucker and Cody White this weekend, with Jailen Nailor sidelined due to a concussion.
The real challenge for Vildor and the rest of the secondary is TE Brock Bowers, who’s historically dominated defensive secondaries of Raiders’ opponents . Considering the lack of size in the cornerback room (all three corners that haven’t been ruled out average a height of 5-foot-10), stopping the 6-foot-4, 235-pound Bowers will be the biggest challenge for this Patriots team.
Last week’s performance against the Buffalo Bills presents optimism for this week’s feat, as the Patriots injured secondary held skilled TE Dalton Kincaid to seven yards on one reception.
The Patriots defense, under the leadership of defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr, will take on the high-powered offense of the Las Vegas Raiders and their first-year head coach Klint Kubiak this Sunday at 1 p.m.

title: 6 Winners, 2 Losers From First Quarter of Patriots Season
full_text:
Ahead of the season, I had the New England Patriots sitting at 2-2 . But that was after they beat the Jacksonville Jaguars and lost to the Buffalo Bills. Both of those outcomes went the other way, and when you factor in two varying outcomes against Seattle and Pittsburgh, the Patriots are at .500 through four weeks.
I t hasn't been smooth sailing for New England to this point . Poor offensive play, along with plenty of injuries, have hindered this team's early-season growth. But the upset win over the Bills gives some hope ahead of what should be a relatively easier path for them.
Here are some of the biggest on-field winners and losers through the first quarter of the season.
When A.J. Brown went down in the season opener and was later placed on IR with a high-ankle sprain, it opened the door for more snaps for Hollins. He leads the team in targets (20), receptions (15) and receiving yards (209).
Even through Drake Maye's rough patch for the first three games, Hollins remained the top option and Maye's most trustworthy pass catcher.
Hollins will miss the team's Week 5 game against the Las Vegas Raiders with a calf injury , but has proven himself in what's become a contract season for the vet.
After a shaky postseason, the Patriots' first round selection from a year ago has flipped a switch .
His 78.2 pass block grade (Pro Football Focus) ranks 12th among all offensive tackles, and h's allowed just one sack in 265 snaps. Sure, he had a poor showing against the Bills — where he allowed six pressures. But he's been a complete 180 from the last time we saw Will Campbell take the field in Super Bowl LX.
An undrafted free agent from a year ago, injuries along the defensive line have allowed Ponder to step up. And step up he has .
Ponder has 15 total tackles, a team-high 2.5 sacks, 4.5 tackles for loss and two fumble recoveries. The first fumble recovery he had was good for a touchdown against the Steelers in Week 2, and he's been thrust into a starting role these last few weeks.
He's been a steal for this team, and has continued to get better each week.
One player that we just haven't seen enough of yet is Williams, who was drafted in the third round a season ago. He has just two catches for seven yards in the first four weeks of the season, and is getting outsnapped by Efton Chism III.
The one positive? His two catches went for a total of 44 yards, meaning his big-play ability is still in there somewhere. Williams has also been the team's top kick returner, tallying 273 yards in that area. He just hasn't been able to put together a string of productive showings on the field.
"I think he continues to improve, and sometimes it’s hard to hear that or believe that when you have to be able to see the football and to be able to get it," Mike Vrabel said this week. "He has helped us out on the kickoff returns. ... I would say that he’s committed to working and improving and understanding more than one spot, and we’re excited about where he’s going to go."
Jacas has completely erased what was a slow summer and has turned on the jets beyond belief. The second-round rookie has 1.5 sacks, an interception off of Aaron Rodgers and looks the part off the edge.
Against the Bills, Jacas had a 28.6% pass rush win rate, the fourth-highest among all NFL edge rushers. He also has a 69.3 PFF grade for the season, the most for any rookie edge rusher. This pick remains the crown jewel of New England's rookie class for this year.
Spillane hasn't missed a game this year, and he also hasn't missed a snap. The veteran linebacker, wbo was voted a captain for the second-straight season, has suited up and played on every single defensive snap the Patriots have taken this year.
His leadership permeates through the locker room and defensive huddle, and his 29 tackles lead the team. The Patriots defense will go as far as Spillane can possibly take them.
When Woodson is on the field, the Patriots defense looks a lot better. He was banged up with a shoulder injury and missed Week 3. That unit gave up five red zone touchdowns. When Woodson came back the next game, he nabbed the game-sealing interception.
He also has 15 tackles and two pass breakups in a unit that's going deep into three-safety sets this season.
"It was awesome," Kevin Byard said of Woodson . "Obviously Craig is another player that we trust on that can go out there and make plays. I think for what we both bring, just being versatile as far as our disguise and different things that we can do. ... It was good to have him back for sure."
Last season, the Patriots put 16 players on IR. As it stands right now, they've already surpassed that number.
The Patriots have placed 17 players on IR at this point, and some of them have been big names. Brown went down early , Mike Onwenu and Greg Van Roten suffered lower-body injuries, Dell Pettus and Quintayvious Hutchins both got hurt as well.
It's football, so injuries are going to happen. But the Patriots have gotten hurt at an alarming rate. They've also lost Christian Gonzalez for the last two games, so they'll need to get healthy ... and fast.

title: Predicting How Patriots Perform vs. Raiders in Week 5: Can They Overcome Injuries?
full_text:
The New England Patriots will be celebrating their 2001 Super Bowl team , as well as Hall of Fame kicker Adam Vinatieri, this week at Gillette Stadium. They'll also play host to the 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders as they look to win back-to-back games for the first time since last year's postseason.
These Raiders aren't the slouch that some might have expected before the season. They rattled off three wins to open up the year, and hung close with the Kansas City Chiefs a week ago. Kirk Cousins, Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers make up a pretty solid offensive trio that has given teams fits.
"They turn what would be a 5-yard gain into 15-yard gains because of his ability to see that quickly," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Wednesday. "So, it’s a great challenge, it’s a new opponent, and somebody that we have to really invest a lot of time in."
Ahead of Week 5, Patriots On SI beat reporters Ethan Hurwitz and Zac Ventola break down how the game will unfold, which players will be x-factors and predict a final score. Who do you think is right?
It was a fantastic bounce-back showing for the Patriots in Buffalo a week ago , but as it stands right now, that's a one-off. The Patriots — and Drake Maye — will need to start stacking those types of games together to really get back into the groove we saw a season ago.
Sure, his offense is banged up ( Mack Hollins won't play after suffering a calf injury ) and the running game hasn't been as consistent that you might have hoped. But Maye will need to look the part for the world to start taking him seriously again. If he can avoid the strong pass rush that's led by Maxx Crosby, Maye and this offense should start to look "normal" again.
A.J. Brown remains out for at least one more game, and Hollins won't be able to go after missing all three of the team's practices. So that leaves the Patriots' wide receivers down to Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams (with Kyle Dixon, Chandler Brayboy and Cameron Dorner on the practice squad). Doubs, who caught two touchdowns a week ago, has a big opportunity to become that "WR1" and rectify a slower-than-expected start to his first New England season.
Final Score Prediction: Patriots 26, Raiders 14
Coming into the game, the Raiders do have the better record. But let's now cloud our judgement and get ahead of ourselves. This is a game that the Patriots should come out on top. If Maye plays like he can, plus a banged up defense gets some timely plays, this should be just another one of those games that New England can celebrate.
If you are reading this, there is a non-zero chance the Patriots will need you to suit up at cornerback on Sunday. New England’s top players at the position, Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III, have both been ruled out for the game. Depth rookies Channing Canada and Karon Prunty have also been ruled out, while backup Charles Woods is marked as questionable to play.
That leaves Marcus Jones as the sole guarantee to play corner on Sunday from New England’s 53-man roster. The team also has a pair of practice squad options in Kindle Vildor and Al’Zillion Hamilton, who signed with the Patriots on Tuesday. With Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (who is utilized more similarly to an oversized receiver as a true tight end) coming to town, the New England secondary will have a tall task ahead.
X-Factor: CB Kindle Vildor
Yes, I predict a practice squad player to be the x-factor for the Patriots this weekend. With New England down Gonzalez , Davis, Canada, Prunty and possibly Woods, SOMEBODY is going to have to cover Bowers. So, with Jones standing eight inches shorter than the star tight end, and Hamilton having been signed just a handful of days ago, Vildor will play a substantial role in slowing down the Las Vegas pass offense.
Final Score Prediction: Patriots 30, Raiders 27
Although the Patriots defense may struggle due to its countless injuries, the offense finally found its groove last week. New England put up 29 points a week ago against the Buffalo Bills. Maye returned to his 2025 self, earning AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors . The Patriots offense must go shot-for-shot with the Raiders, which it should do with relative ease. New England comes out on top by three after a game-winner from kicker Andy Borregales.
