title: QB In His Corner: Sean Mannion Still Has Jalen Hurts' Endorsement
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — Jalen Hurts is not backing away from Sean Mannion.
With the Eagles’ offense stuck near the bottom of the league and questions mounting about the first-year coordinator’s scheme, the QB1 described Mannion as “a warrior, a soldier” at his weekly press availability and noted that the current rough stretch is building equity between the duo rather than tearing them apart.
“Obviously these times are where times you get to build with someone and go through things with someone, and I think that builds equity in everything that we do together,” Hurts said. “And so I’m excited to go to bat with him.”
The comments came as Philadelphia sits at 2-2 and searches for an identity four games into Mannion’s stint as offensive coordinator and play-caller.
The Eagles are averaging 18.8 points and about 270 yards a game, ranking near the bottom of the NFL in both categories, with the passing attack especially shaky. They have stalled in consecutive losses: a 27-7 defeat in Chicago followed by a 24-20 home loss to the Rams in which the offense totaled 172 yards and went 0-for-12 on third down.
Hurts has repeatedly framed those subpar performances as execution problems, not schematic ones.
After the Rams game, the QB1 used the phrase “poor execution” repeatedly and declined to pin the failure on Mannion’s plan.
Head coach Nick Sirianni has been more blunt about the public heat, saying of Mannion, “He’s gonna wear a lot of this. There’s no doubt.”
Mannion, hired from the Packers’ quarterbacks room with a background in the McVay-O’Connell-LaFleur tree, has shown no interest in abandoning the offense he was brought in to install.
He said this week the staff still believes in the under-center, outside-zone, play-action structure and intends to “keep leaning into” it.
“We're here and we're implementing something that we absolutely believe in,” said Mannion. “You're always looking, like we've said, throughout this process, to make it as good as it can be and add tweaks and add wrinkles here and there.
“We believe in the things that we've installed and that we've implemented from a fundamental perspective in terms of the structure of our offense. We're going to keep leaning into that and make it as good as it can be. … Really nothing's changed in terms of our outlook on our offense, and our identity and what we want to be offensively. But each week, you're always looking to attack in the best way possible, either by looking at yourself and the things that you can add and tweak or looking at your opponent and what needs to be tailored to that."
Through four games, the Eagles have run play-action at one of the league’s lowest rates and have been inefficient from under center, a gap critics have treated as evidence the new system and the personnel are not yet aligned.
Asked by Eagles On SI how Mannion is handling the adversity, and what he has seen in daily meetings, the quarterback stayed on the relationship, with the “warrior” sentiment.
That posture fits a pattern.
Early in the season, Hurts preached patience and building in-game chemistry with a play-caller working from the booth, something he had not done in the NFL, and about getting “hip-to-hip” with Mannion over time.
Wins over the Commanders and the Titans masked some of the growing pains. The last two games have not.
The Eagles are in London on Sunday to square off with a talented Jacksonville team while looking for the version of the offense they described in the spring.
And they will have to do it with a makeshift offensive line with no Lane Johnson (retired on Tuesday), Cam Jurgens (traded to Baltimore on Wednesday), and perhaps Drew Kendall, who missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday with a knee injury.
Mannion has insisted his core tenets are unwavering even though, all too often, they haven’t shown up on game days. For now, Hurts is still willing to absorb the shrapnel with the young offensive coordinator.
In Philadelphia, that kind of public cover from the quarterback buys time. It does not buy results. If the endorsement from Hurts is pulled and the messaging begins to change, Mannion will have one-and-done concerns to deal with.

title: Steelers Out of Marvin Harrison Jr. Race
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers will not be the landing spot for a former top pick.
According to insider Mark Kaboly, Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is not heading to the Steelers, though he is expected to be officially traded in the near future.
"Marvin Harrison Jr.'s trade will become official either later today or on Monday. Harrison is NOT coming to the Steelers, I've been told," Kaboly wrote on X.
Marvin Harrison Jr.'s trade will become official either later today or on Monday. Harrison is NOT coming to the Steelers, I've been told. #NoYeet
On October 10, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Cardinals were finalizing a deal involving Harrison Jr., and that the former No. 4 overall pick was told that he would be inactive for the team's Week 5 game against the Detroit Lions as all of the details were finalized.
No destination was announced at the time, which left the door open for plenty of speculation about Harrison Jr.'s landing spot.
As such, there was at least a possibility that Pittsburgh was among the suitors for Harrison Jr. The team already could've used another receiver before Michael Pittman Jr. was placed on the reserve/injured list after aggravating his foot injury, and the fact that he will now miss at least four games further exacerbated that need.
Now that Kaboly has noted that the Steelers won't be the team to strike a deal with Arizona for Harrison Jr., however, they'll have to look elsewhere if they plan on adding a receiver ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.
Harrison Jr. would've been an intriguing add for Pittsburgh considering he was largely considered a generational prospect out of Ohio State in the 2024 NFL Draft who hasn't lived up to expectations with the Cardinals.
Schefter also reported that Arizona had been searching for "first-round value" in exchange for Harrison Jr., though, which may have been far out of the range of the Steelers' comfort zone.
It remains to be seen what the Cardinals ultimately get for Harrison Jr. wherever they end up trading him. There are better uses of Day 1 and 2 picks in Pittsburgh's situation, and missing out isn't the worst outcome in the world.
The Steelers will count on DK Metcalf, Roman Wilson and Germie Bernard for as long as Pittman Jr. is out. That's a pretty solid group, but there is room for another mid-tier addition or so if the organization finds a move worth making.
There are other position groups around Pittsburgh's roster in more need of reinforcements, though, so it's no guarantee that the front office will supplement its receiving corps.

title: Three Reasons Steelers Beat Colts in Week 5
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers will be back home at Acrisure Stadium in Week 5 for a matchup with the Indianapolis Colts.
This game will mark the fifth-straight season in which the two teams have faced one another. The Steelers won the latest bout, defeating the Colts by a score of 27-20 in Week 9 last year.
Here are three reasons why Pittsburgh could defeat Indianapolis once again and move to 3-2 on the season.
Indianapolis' defense has been one of the worst in the league up to this point in the season. It is allowing the third-most yards per game (392.3), and the unit has struggled significantly to generate consistent pressure.
According to SumerSports , the Colts' pressure rate of 32.0 percent is the third-worst mark in the NFL.
Pittsburgh's offensive line hasn't done a good job of keeping Aaron Rodgers upright, evidenced by the fact that it allowed five sacks in a Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns to go with the unit's allowed pressure rate of 42.1 percent on the year (ninth-worst in league, per SumerSports ).
In the Steelers' best game of the season from a pass protection standpoint thus far in a Week 3 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals, however, Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns in what was one of his best performances for the black and gold.
The blueprint is there for a similar outing against Indianapolis, even with Michael Pittman Jr. out after aggravating his foot injury, given that Indianapolis' pass rush is well below-average.
T.J. Watt has completely bounced back from a disappointing 2025 campaign, as he's tied for the third-most sacks in the league with 4.5 while also having a forced fumble (and recovery) as well as a pick-six to his name.
Alex Highsmith isn't far behind Watt with 3.0 sacks, and while Nick Herbig doesn't have any sacks after signing a four-year, $100 million extension in the offseason, his 20.5 percent pressure rate (per SumerSports ) suggests he's due for some production on that front.
Colts starting left tackle Bernhard Raimann and right tackle Jalen Travis, meanwhile, are allowing pressure rates of 8.5 percent (12th-worst among offensive linemen with at least 100 snaps) and 10.3 percent (fourth-worst), respectively.
Watt, Highsmith and Herbig should all be able to feast as a result, and they could help shut down Indianapolis' passing attack while constantly getting to Daniel Jones in the pocket.
So far this season, Pittsburgh's defense has recorded four interceptions and recovered four fumbles while having a turnover margin of +2.
The Colts, meanwhile, currently own the worst turnover margin in the league at -6. They've thrown four interceptions and lost four fumbles while having forced just a single interception and recovered one fumble thus far on defense.
Though the Steelers will play without several key pieces on defense, including Derrick Harmon (placed on IR with foot injury) and Jamel Dean (ankle) while DeShon Elliott remains on IR after having his 21-day practice window opened this week , they still have an advantage when it comes to winning the turnover battle, and doing so is paramount to coming away with a victory.

title: Are Steelers in on Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade?
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers fanbase joined the rest of the NFL world this weekend is anxiously waiting to find out where Marvin Harrison Jr. was going to end up. And the big question for those rooting for the black and gold is: will it be with the Steelers?
The NFL world exploded when several insiders reported that Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. was going to be traded. The team ruled him inactive for their Week 5 matchup and all reports claimed that a deal was "being finalized," but that nothing was going to be announced until both teams played.
Why? That's a question for later. But who? That is what everyone is waiting to find out.
Breaking: the Arizona Cardinals are finalizing a deal to trade WR Marvin Harrison, sources tell me and @RapSheet . The team informed Harrison this morning that he will be inactive for Sunday’s game vs Detroit as details of the trade are finalized. pic.twitter.com/x6n0Hsfzzj
That we don't know yet. The Steelers weren't expected to be in on Harrison Jr. at this point in the season, but with Michael Pittman Jr. going on Injured Reserve and the team landing an extra 2028 second-round pick in exchange for Joey Porter Jr., they do have the option to make a move. And it wouldn't hurt them.
Don't expect Pittsburgh to be the front-runners, even if they're in on the deal, though. While this all feels like the Cardinals are trying to get a better offer last second, the Steelers won't be a team to try and overpay for Harrison Jr.
If they're negotiating, don't expect them to budge too much.
It does make sense for Pittsburgh, though. This team is without Pittman Jr. for the next four week, minimum. While they drafted Germie Bernard in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft , Aaron Rodgers hasn't shown too much faith in younger wide receivers, and Bernard may have to wait for his real opportunity to shine.
Roman Wilson and DK Metcalf are playing fine, but neither is looking like a bona fide star. Really, the Steelers could simply use options, and Harrison Jr. might be the best one out there.
While the former fourth-overall pick hasn't reached the peak many were hoping for this early in his career, he is just 24 years old and viewed as one of the highest-potential players in the NFL.
The Steelers would/do have an opportunity to bring in a young wide receiver who still has two years on his rookie contract and is eligible for a fifth-year option in 2028.
That wideout could grow with Drew Allar or Will Howard, or whoever they bring in next to be their young passer in 2027 . And with plenty of time together, Harrison Jr., Bernard, Wilson and a young QB could be the next evolution of the Steelers offense.
Are the Steelers determined enough to make something happen? Do they have interest in Harrison Jr. at all? These are all questions we'll find out at a later date.
Maybe with one simple answer, if they're on the opposite end of the deal. And until it's revealed where he's going, we'll all be on the edge of our seats, waiting to see - and waiting to see if the Steelers could shock us.

title: Steelers Add Training Camp Star to WR Room
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers need depth at wide receiver, and one player is getting a big opportunity.
The Steelers announced that they elevated wide receiver Brandon Smith from the Active/Inactive Roster ahead of their Week 5 game vs. the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium on Oct. 11.
Pittsburgh also announced that they signed defensive back Doneiko Slaughter to the 53-man roster and elevated Lew Nichols to the Active/Inactive Roster.
This comes after the Steelers placed wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. on the Reserve/Injured List, with Smith getting a spot for the game vs. the Colts.
Pittman re-aggravated his foot injury this week and will be out for weeks, per Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy.
The Steelers' wide receiver room consists of DK Metcalf and Ben Skowronek, Roman WIlson and rookies Germie Bernard and Kaden Wetjen, meaning Smith should be the sixth option vs. the Colts.
Smith likely won't get called upon vs. Indianapolis, but he'll need to be ready if so.
Smith signed a reserve/future contract with the Steelers back on Jan. 15. They waived him on Aug. 30 and then re-signed him to the practice squad.
He has been a part of five different NFL teams after going undrafted in 2020: the Dallas Cowboys, Arizona Cardinals, New York Jets and New England Patriots.
Smith hasn't made a catch, with just one offensive snap in his NFL career, so it would be a first if he does so against the Colts.
He played with the DC Defenders in the XFL, making 26 catches for 226 yards and three touchdowns in two seasons (2023 and 2024).
Smith also spent four seasons at Iowa (2017-20), making 91 catches for 1,046 yards and nine touchdowns in 39 games.
This marks the second time the Steelers have signed Slaughter from the practice squad to the 53-man roster, as they did it for the Week 4 matchup with the Cleveland Browns.
Pittsburgh released Slaughter on Oct. 5, he cleared waivers on Oct. 6, and then they re-signed him to the practices squad on Oct. 7.
Slaughter has only featured on the Steelers' punt returns, playing in all four games, so expect him to have a similar role on special teams vs. the Colts.
This marks the third time the Steelers elevated Nichols to the Active/Inactive roster from the practice squad, doing so for the past two games.
Nichols has only appeared in three snaps the past two games, acting as Jaylen Warren's backup, with  fellow running back Rico Dowdle injured.
Dowdle is questionable against the Colts, but this may signal that he won't play or will be limited.
The Steelers will also have to sign Nichols to the 53-man roster if they want to bring him back again, as he's reached his limit of three elevations from the practice squad.

title: Steelers Place Starting WR on IR
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers will lose one of their top wide receivers for the next few weeks at the very least.
According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) has landed on the reserve/injured list.
The Steelers are placing WR Michael Pittman (foot) on short-term IR, per sources. pic.twitter.com/ZLZM5V8hGd
Pittman Jr. aggravated his injury this week, per head coach Mike McCarthy, and he noted at the time that it was likely to keep him out for several weeks.
It's been a constant issue for Pittman Jr. throughout the season, which is often the case with plantar fasciitis. He missed the Steelers ' Week 2 game against the New England Patriots due to the injury, though he returned in Week 3 vs. the Cincinnati Bengals and was also active in Week 4 against the Cleveland Browns.
Pittman Jr. was not productive between those two contests, however, finishing with a combined 31 yards before now being placed on IR, which will keep him out for a minimum of four weeks.
For now, Pittsburgh will rely heavily on DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson at receiver while Pittman Jr. is on the mend, and second-round pick Germie Bernard will also see a rise in his playing time as well.
Metcalf had a string of drops over the first few games of the season and had just 98 yards heading into the Steelers' matchup with the Browns last week.
While Pittsburgh fell by a score of 27-24, Metcalf was among the bright spots for the team, as he broke out for 115 yards on five catches.
If he can keep putting up No. 1 receiver-type production on a weekly basis, that would go a long way towards the Steelers' passing game operating at a high level without Pittman Jr. on the field.
Wilson also had a nice outing vs. Cleveland, recording 74 yards and a touchdown. He's already exceeded his yard total from 2025 at 188, and as the No. 2 receiver for the time being, he's become all the more integral to Pittsburgh's offense.
Bernard has just 60 yards on seven receptions so far this year, though he did garner eight targets and hauled in four of them for 35 yards when Pittman Jr. was sidelined vs. New England.
He's likely not going to be targeted that much on a game-to-game basis while Pittman Jr. is out, though he should still factor in quite heavily.

title: Steelers Have Perfect Stretch to Make Daylen Everette Starter
full_text:
Rookie cornerback Daylen Everette has the perfect runway to begin his stint as a starter for the Pittsburgh Steelers on a high note.
As Jamel Dean deals with an ankle injury that will likely keep him out for several games, Everette is slated to start on the boundary opposite Asante Samuel Jr. for the time being.
The third-round pick has already played a healthy amount of snaps early in his career, including 79 over the past two weeks, which wasn't necessarily expected when he was selected in the 2026 NFL Draft.
Everette is still raw and needs ample time to develop. It's tough to make a real impact as a rookie corner, especially one taken towards the end of Day 2 of the draft, though the 22-year-old has a few favorable matchups ahead of him as he acclimates himself to being a starter for the Steelers .
In what will mark his first start, Everette and Pittsburgh get an Indianapolis Colts team in Week 5 that is without No. 1 wide receiver Alec Pierce.
Pierce, who posted 1,003 yards and six touchdowns last season before re-signing with the Colts on a four-year, $114 million deal in the offseason, went on the reserve/injured list with a heel injury ahead of Week 3.
A deep threat who was Daniel Jones' preferred target in 2025, not having to contend with Pierce should put less stress on Everette and make life easier for him as a whole in the contest.
Then, in Week 6, Everette has yet another opportunity for a strong showing against undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Baker Mayfield is dealing with a thumb injury that kept him out in Week 4 and will sideline him for the foreseeable future.
As a result, Daniels will be QB1 for the 0-4 Bucs vs. Pittsburgh. The Kansas product had a rough go of it during his first career start in Week 4 against the Green Bay Packers, going 19-of-27 for 148 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions.
Everette and the rest of the Steelers' secondary will be in an advantageous spot against Daniels, which should help the former build momentum and keep growing in-season.
Pittsburgh must embrace the ups and downs with Everette. Again, he wasn't ever supposed to be in a situation where was being called on to start as a rookie, especially this early.
With Dean's injury and the departure of Joey Porter Jr. via trade to the Dallas Cowboys amidst his contract dispute, however, it's now Everette's time to go out and prove himself.
According to SumerSports , Everette has allowed five receptions on nine targets for 116 yards thus far. Additionally, he has logged two pass breakups while also drawing a pass interference penalty.
There have been some promising flashes up to this point. On the flip side, Everette's certainly taken his fair share of losses, as anticipated.
He isn't going to be the savior for a secondary that's in rough shape right now. If Everette does come out of the gates hot as a starter vs. Indianapolis and Tampa Bay, though, which is a real possibility, perhaps he'll solidify his spot on the boundary and supersede Samuel Jr. on the depth chart once Dean returns from his injury.

title: Steelers vs. Colts Bold Predictions: DK Metcalf Goes Off
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are looking to move on from the Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns, and the best way to do so is to come away with a victory at home against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5.
Though they're dealing with injuries to several of their key starters, such as Derrick Harmon (who is on IR with a foot injury), Jamel Dean (ankle) and Michael Pittman Jr. (foot), the Steelers are still in a relatively good spot when it comes to matching up with Indianapolis.
As it attempts to move to 3-2 on the season, here are three bold predictions for Pittsburgh's upcoming bout with the Colts.
Jonathan Taylor is one of the NFL's elite running backs.
The 27-year-old is coming off a strong showing in a Week 4 win for the Colts over the Washington Commanders in London, where he rushed for 95 yards and a pair of touchdowns.
Taylor also posted a whopping 1,963 yards from scrimmage with a league-leading 19 touchdowns in 2025.
He had one of his worst outings last year against the Steelers, however, rushing for just 45 yards on 14 carries to go with two catches for 12 yards and no touchdowns in a 27-20 loss to Pittsburgh.
Taylor also hasn't been quite as efficient so far in 2026 as he has been in the past, averaging only 4.1 yards per carry.
He's still arguably the most important part of Indianapolis' offense, especially when considering Daniel Jones' struggles thus far, but the Steelers may have the formula to stop him.
Pittsburgh's run defense ranks near the middle of the pack in yards allowed per game at 112.8 (16th-most) and yards per carry at 4.34 (13th-most). Those numbers aren't overly impressive, though it has the pieces necessary to limit Taylor's production while being able to really hone in on him in their defensive game plan.
Metcalf finally broke out in Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns, particularly in the fourth quarter, en route to logging 115 yards on five receptions.
One of the major storylines over the first few weeks of the campaign for the Steelers was Metcalf's issues with drops as well as his low statistical output.
He's trending in the right direction after his outing against the Browns, considering he had just 98 yards going into that contest, and he has a perfect opportunity to keep things rolling against the Colts.
Pittman Jr. is set to miss multiple weeks after aggravating his foot injury, which should boost Metcalf's targets for as long as the former is out.
Indianapolis has given up the seventh-most passing yards on the season at 1,105, and star cornerback Sauce Gardner has really struggled in his first full season with the team after they traded two first-round picks to the New York Jets for him at last year's deadline.
Gardner is slated to line up plenty opposite Metcalf in Week 5, and with Rodgers likely to look his way quite a bit, the Steelers' No. 1 wide receiver should be in for another huge day and put up back-to-back 100-yard performances for the first time with the black and gold.
After signing a four-year, $100 million extension in June, Herbig's been quiet so far this season.
He has yet to record a sack, and he's also playing off-ball more than he has in the past, evidenced by the fact that he has 20 coverage reps already after having 50 throughout all of 2025 (per Pro Football Focus ).
Herbig has also only had 40 snaps as a pass rusher up to this point, according to PFF. That doesn't mean he isn't making an impact, though, as his 20.5 percent pressure rate is the sixth-highest among EDGE rushers with at least 100 total snaps on the season (per SumerSports ).
The Colts, on the other hand, are allowing a quarterback pressure rate of 41.4 percent, which is the sixth-worst mark in the NFL (per Next Gen Stats ).
As such, Week 5 offers a chance for Herbig to finally notch at least one sack and start putting some numbers up on the board.

title: Three College Guards Steelers Should Target
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- One emerging need moving forward for the Pittsburgh Steelers is shoring up their interior offensive line. With center Zach Frazier and left guard Mason McCormick on the roster, two out of three spots are secured for the 2026 season and beyond.
That still leaves an open and vulnerable spot for the Steelers' offensive line. 2023 seventh-round draft pick Spencer Anderson began the season but was replaced after two weeks by veteran Brock Hoffman. Hoffman has been serviceable in relief of Anderson, but the long-term promise is not quite there for Mike McCarthy's beloved lineman.
This points the Steelers towards prioritizing their interior line at next year's NFL Draft. Through the first five weeks of the NCAA season, several players have jumped to the top of my radar, and they should be at the top of the Steelers' list of 2027 NFL Draft targets.
This one might be a tad obvious, but the best guard prospect in the nation ahead of the 2027 NFL Draft is Minnesota's Greg Johnson. The 6'6" powerhouse has the entire NFL community talking, and rightly so.
He's big, mean and nasty, and when you look at the physical traits plus the dogged mentality he plays with, it's easy to see why many have him as their top-rated interior lineman of the 2027 class.
Already in his third year of starting for the Fighting Irish, Knapp has turned some heads due to a position change. Over his first two seasons, he was primarily a left tackle, where he showed promise. This year, however, he's played as the left guard, and he's had even more success.
It seems he might be a bit better suited for the interior of the offensive line, or at least that's what the early returns suggest. Through nearly the first half of Notre Dame's 2026 season, Knapp has been one of the most impressive players on the Fighting Irish's offense. Their running game is posting over 160 yards per game, and they are producing an average of 428.4 total yards on offense, according to Sports Reference data.
There's something very impressive about Cincinnati junior Evan Tengesdahl's game. An interior offensive lineman, he has the agility and the strength to be an impact player in both the run and pass game.
Of these three options, Tengesdahl is the smallest in height, coming in at 6'3". That shouldn't deter the Steelers from being interested, however. His physicality on the field speaks for itself, and it should endear the Steelers even more to the Bearcats' top lineman.

title: Steelers Top 4 College QB Options at Quarter-Season Mark
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers are going to be in on the quarterback class during the 2027 NFL Draft. Even with the addition of Drew Allar in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft and second-year QB Will Howard on the roster, the team is still searching for the team’s next starter after Aaron Rodgers.
Where things currently stand, the Steelers are still one of the teams to monitor in the quarterback hunt.
Luckily for the organization, the 2027 class has some promising options. Through Week 5 of the NCAA season, things are beginning to become clear as to what players will be at the top of the draft class. These three players in particular should be on the top of the Steelers’ wish list for the 2027 draft.
The Fighting Irish are off to a 5-0 start and CJ Carr has been a premier game-manager. Notre Dame is a run-first offense once again, but that doesn’t mean Carr hasn’t had his chance to shine. Through five games, he’s thrown 13 touchdowns and only one interception while completing over 70% of his passing attempts.
What’s even more impressive is that he’s thrown at least three touchdown passes in three of the first five games. The junior is poised and polished in the pocket, and while he’s not the flashiest prospect, he has a lot of tools that can translate to success in the NFL.
Darian Mensah is the latest quarterback to get the University of Miami bump, as he looks fantastic in a Hurricanes uniform. The 21-year-old Junior from San Luis Obispo, California has transitioned seamlessly from Duke to Miami, leading the Canes to a 5-0 record to start the campaign.
Through the first five games, he’s been the best performing quarterback in the country. He’s thrown 15 touchdowns and zero interceptions, completing 84.2% of his passing attempts. He’s showing the NFL that he’s the complete package and a top pick in the upcoming draft.
For the Steelers, he might be exactly what the organization needs to move forward. Big, athletic, a powerful arm, and an undisputed leader on the field. Mensah remains a critical name to watch.
Week 1 performance aside, Drew Mestemaker is the QB that has impressed me the most in the NCAA. He has the classic NFL QB arm and he looks like an absolute natural in the pocket. He’s eclipsed 300 passing yards in three consecutive contests and he’s tossed 11 touchdowns to five interceptions on the season.
Add in his NFL-ready frame (6’3”, 215 pounds) and he’s a top-10 pick right now.
Even with the loss to the University of Alabama and two interceptions thrown, Kamario Taylor remains the most fascinating college quarterback prospec t in the NCAA. He has the size, the speed, the arm, and he’s making some unreal plays for his team.
What I liked most about Taylor’s performance was how he responded to his failures against the Crimson Tide. He had a horrid start, but came back to lead several touchdown drives and finish with 258 passing yards and three touchdown passes. It wasn’t pretty, but he showed life in a disappointing contest. He’s not a likely entrant into the 2027 NFL Draft, but if he does enter, every NFL team will take a run at him.

title: Steelers Need Offensive Help, And Might Get It This Week
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers' offense could receive some major help against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5.
While wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) was ruled out against his former team after aggravating his injury this week, running back Rico Dowdle (toe) was listed as questionable after registering as a limited participant in each practice session this week.
Dowdle hasn't played since dislocating his toe twice in Week 2 against the New England Patriots, but there's now a shot he'll return vs. Indianapolis for a Steelers offense that could really use his skill set both on the ground and through the air.
Truth be told, the Steelers ' run game never quite got going when Dowdle was healthy over the first two weeks of the season.
A lot of the blame could be attributed to Pittsburgh's offensive line, which has now swapped in Brock Hoffman and Max Iheanachor at right guard and right tackle, respectively, in place of Spencer Anderson and Dylan Cook.
Those changes have paid off thus far, and Jaylen Warren has shined during Dowdle's absence while having more room to operate.
In the two games that Dowdle has been sidelined for while being on the mend, Warren has posted a combined 302 yards on 40 touches against the Cincinnati Bengals and Cleveland Browns.
It could be more of the same against a Colts defense that has allowed 131.0 rushing yards per game, which is the seventh-most in the NFL, while also being tied for the fifth-most EPA/rush according to SumerSports at 0.02.
Should Dowdle be back on the field vs. Indianapolis, he could have an easy runway towards a strong performance while likely being eased back in as Warren commands most of the workload out of the backfield.
When both Warren and Dowdle were fully healthy in the Steelers' Week 1 victory over the Atlanta Falcons, the former had 73 yards over 15 touches while the latter finished with 10 touches for 21 yards.
If Dowdle does play, which is still up in the air considering he's questionable, it's far to expect that Warren will continue to get a lion's share of the reps and touches.
Dowdle should still get the ball considerably more than Travis Homer did against the Browns (two carries for -1 yards) or Bengals (one carry for no yards) while serving as the No. 2 running back in the former's absence.
He won't be featured prominently in all likelihood, but Dowdle's number will still be called a handful of times at the very least if he does play against the Colts.

title: Seahawks Confidence Meter: Leonard Williams an X-Factor vs 49ers
full_text:
The injury bug hasn’t been kind to the Seattle Seahawks (3-1). The Seahawks are seeing the biggest injuries in their secondary, mostly in their safeties, and their rookie starting running back Jadarian Price is on IR. Late in the Week 4 home win over the Los Angeles Chargers, veteran Leonard Williams was down with an ankle injury.
​There were real concerns that Williams would miss the critical Week 5 home game versus the San Francisco 49ers (4-0). He missed Thursday’s practice after being limited on Wednesday’s practice. It was revealed on Friday that he would play on Sunday, which should be a huge sign of relief for the Seahawks. Williams might be Seattle’s most crucial player on Sunday.
​Williams is arguably one of the Seahawks’ most important defenders , along with linebacker Ernest Jones IV and cornerback Devon Witherspoon. Not only is he the leader on the defensive line, but he sets up the tempo and the intensity for the Dark Side Defense.
​In Week 1 of the game versus the 49ers last season, Williams accounted for a season-high seven total tackles, a tackle for loss and a quarterback hit. In the regular-season finale in Week 18 last season, the 49ers' offense focused their attention on Williams at the line of scrimmage. This allowed the rest of the Seahawks' defense to crash the line of scrimmage. Finally, in the 41-6 Divisional Round win, Williams accounted for two total tackles, one sack, one tackle for loss and two quarterback hits.
Williams is one of the key reasons why 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey is averaging only 3.2 yards or less versus the three games versus Seattle. The Seahawks haven't allowed McCaffrey to account for a rushing or receiving touchdown in the last five games. Williams has also been key in suppressing 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy by pressuring him, sacking him or keeping him from rushing for more yards in RPO.
The 49ers will be the Seahawks’ biggest test so far this season. San Francisco’s offensive line hasn’t allowed a sack in any of the four games this season and it faced the Los Angeles Rams and the Denver Broncos. One good reason is Purdy’s ability to escape the pocket and evade pressure. Purdy has played like one of the league’s best players, but he now faces Williams and the Dark Side Defense.
​The Seahawks will be the 49ers’ biggest test yet this season . Seattle ranks in the top five in most defensive categories through the first four games of the season. Seattle ranks first in the league in passing yards allowed per game, total yards allowed per game and tackles for loss. Williams is a big reason for that.
​He accounted for 13 total tackles, nine solo tackles, six quarterback hits, five tackles for loss and three sacks. If he isn't limited against the 49ers, there is a great chance it will be a battle every yard, every play. The Seahawks need Williams to be the X-Factor, even if he isn't 100%.

title: Trevon Diggs Gets More Opportunities With Seahawks in Week 5
full_text:
This 2026 NFL Season has been tough for the Seattle Seahawks (3-1) as they’ve been dealing with tough injuries and bad news. The Seahawks have seen injuries at the secondary, with a good portion of their young players on injured reserve. Not only is rookie cornerback Julian Neal on IR , but there is serious doubt that Terrion Arnold will play down for Seattle for a few more months, if able to.
​With Neal and Arnold out of the picture for the Seahawks, it gives veteran cornerback Trevon Diggs a chance to make his presence known with the team. Seattle signed Diggs off the practice squad ahead of the Week 5 home game versus the San Francisco 49ers (4-0). Diggs might get more chances with the Seahawks this season after making his first appearance last week in the 30-23 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
​The Seahawks believed their great talent and depth at the secondary would be an asset going into the season. Seattle, however, lost rookie safety Bud Clark for the season with a broken ankle during the preseason.
​Starting safety Ty Okada missed the first four games of the season with a hamstring injury. Their other starting safety Julian Love missed a key game in the road loss to the Washington Commanders. Finally, Neal is on IR with a hamstring injury.
​Arnold, meanwhile, is scheduled to have a court hearing for his eight felonies on Dec. 16. He isn’t likely to play a down for the Seahawks and remains on the commissioner’s exempt list while the legal process continues. The Seahawks haven’t devoted a lot of resources to having Arnold be on the field early, but they would’ve liked for him to be a top-tier coverage corner.
​The good news for Seattle is that it still has Diggs, who made his first appearance for the Seahawks in Week 4. Diggs participated in meaningful snaps for the Seahawks against the Chargers’ defense last week. He didn’t account for a tackle or a pass breakup, but he also didn’t allow a reception in the game.
​The Seahawks have been determined to keep developing their role players to help build depth. Diggs is now one of the only cornerbacks on the roster Seattle can turn to outside of Devon Witherspoon, Josh Jobe and Nehemiah Pritchett. The Seahawks could also turn to rookie Avery Smith, an undrafted free agent the Seahawks traded for right after training camp ended. Smith didn’t play in the last two games as a healthy scratch.
​Diggs is at his healthiest he has been in the last few seasons and he possesses great experience . The Seahawks might utilize him on the same level as Pritchett, who has been one of Seattle’s ascending coverage players.

title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Seahawks’ Week 5 Clash vs. 49ers
full_text:
Dating back to 2022, the Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers have met a total of 10 times in four seasons. There were playoff clashes in 2022, won by the Niners, and this past season— a 41-6 victory in the divisional round that propelled Mike Macdonald’s club to an eventual victory in Super Bowl LX.
Including that postseason clash, the Seahawks have won three of the last four meetings. Can Macdonald make it four out of five as he renews acquaintances with Kyle Shanahan? These three encounters could tell the story.
Seattle’s offensive front has been solid this season. Entering Week 5, they were the 10th-ranked unit by Pro Football Focus , up two spots from a week ago. The ‘Hawks have given up just six sacks in four games. Running back Jadarian Price is currently on injured reserve and it’s been backfield by committee, but the Seahawks are still averaging a respectable 110.3 yards per game on the ground.
Center Jalen Sundell has been solid at the pivot, but he faces an enormous challenge in four-time Pro Bowler and four-time First Team All-Pro Fred Warner. He was lost after six games this past season, but four weeks into 2026 and he leads the club with 40 tackles, two QB hits, three passes defensed, and a pair of forced fumbles.

title: Mike Macdonald Has Owned The Shanahan 49ers, Will He Continue To Do So?
full_text:
Christmas 2023. The Baltimore Ravens roll into San Francisco to take on a 49ers team sporting the MVP favorite in Brock Purdy. After Mike Macdonald got done with him, that particular aspiration was wrapped. The 49ers scored 17 offensive points, threw five interceptions, and had a -0.165 EPA per play. John Schneider definitely took note.
A couple months later, the Seattle Seahawks hired Macdonald , no doubt in part because they had taken five straight losses to the 49ers. And overall, they’ve been rewarded well. In 2024 week 11, the 49ers managed 17 points and 0.022 EPA. The 2025 opener, 17 points and 0.125 EPA (and a win). And then, of course, the two late-season games last year.
Week 18 for the division and NFC’s top seed, and San Fran manages 3 points and -0.359 EPA. Divisional round, how about 6 points and -0.456 EPA? Only once has Kyle come out on top in these matchups, week 6 in 2024, with 36 points and 0.32 EPA. It’s been one-sided , and it seems like Mike knows how to counter here. But now, we’re in a new season.
The reasons why the Seahawks have matched up so well against the 49ers in these areas are complex and multi-faceted. But two major reasons, in my mind, are taking advantage of Brock Purdy tendencies and deficiencies. Purdy spreads the ball around and gets the ball out of his hands quickly based on pre-snap reads. And Mike loves to mix things up pre-snap.
Brock also has a mediocre arm, which is the main reason why he fell so far in the draft. The current iteration of the 49ers also lack a true field-stretcher (as they did last season), unless you want to count Brandin Cooks. This makes it hard for their offense to force defenses back, condensing everything into a box around 20-25 yards from the line of scrimmage.
Put all that together, and you’ve got a recipe for an uphill battle. Against lesser defenses with weaker talent, it’s not a big problem. But trying to fit the ball into tight windows in the intermediate parts of the field against this Seattle defense that isn’t afraid of getting beat over the top, while you’re not getting as many easy pre-snap reads? Not fun.
All that being said, this is a new season, and Shanahan has had an entire offseason to try to figure out a counterpunch. Maybe that counter was De’Zhaun Stribling, who is hoping to return to the field in December, taking the top off the defense. But maybe he’s got something else more schematic in his back pocket. Can Mike handle it?
Whatever he may have planned, a few things remain constant. Brock Purdy doesn’t have a big arm, and his offense lacks a vertical threat. Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel may be better than what they had back in January, but they’re not burning up the field with speed. If Kyle figures out a way to crack Mike’s defense, maybe things aren’t as straightforward as they appear.

title: Seahawks, 49ers Release Final Injury Report With Key Game Statuses
full_text:
Yesterday provided some drama, in the form of two stars missing practice . So now, both the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks are providing their final word on who will be available and who won’t be on Sunday, at least until the hours before kickoff. Let’s run it down and get a sense of what this weekend might hold in store for us.
Opening up with the Seahawks, the big relief was the lack of any game status for Leonard Williams (ankle), which means he is good to go. I won’t pretend that he’s 100%, but this is about the best you could hope for after yesterday’s missed practice. Also in the clear is Ty Okada (hamstring), Nehemiah Pritchett (ankle) , and Tyrice Knight (ankle).
In fact, the only players who are unknown at the moment are George Holani (ribs) and Irv Charles (knee), both questionable. Based on what we’ve seen from George recently, he’s clearly not all there, but the team desperately needs running backs. Charles being questionable already is a great sign, and I look for him to inject life into this special teams unit.
The players declared out were Zach Charbonnet (knee) , Chazz Surratt (calf), and Julian Neal (hamstring). Charbonnet was declared unavailable this week days ago, Surratt got injured in practice last week, and Neal is a new addition to the injury ranks. Given where we were less than 24 hours ago, this is a great spot for the Seattle Seahawks.
San Francisco has a mixed report today. Starting with the good, Mike Evans (ribs) has no game designation and will be playing. Like Leonard, I won’t suggest he’s fully healthy. In fact, he’s probably in a lot of pain. But he’s toughing it out. Kaelon Black (illness), Jaden Dugger (shoulder), and Romello Height (hand) are good as well.
The things we don’t yet know concern two defenders that the 49ers are counting on this weekend. Upton Stout (shoulder) and Mykel Williams (knee) are questionable. My understanding is that Stout didn’t practice today, so I’m expecting Stout to sit and Williams to go. We’ll probably find out 90 minutes before kickoff, but that’s my current read.
The bad is mostly straightforward. Nick Bosa (knee, calf), Kyle Juszczyk (knee), Marques Sigle (ankle) and James Thompson (ankle) are out, as they were assumed to be earlier this week. Just because it was known doesn’t make it any less devastating, of course, as the 49ers are missing a lot of pieces they were counting on to win games like this.

title: 5 Key Things to Know About 49ers vs. Seahawks in Week 5
full_text:
The last time the San Francisco 49ers lost a football game, it was at Lumen Field in the 2025 NFC Divisional Playoffs. The Seattle Seahawks rolled to a 41-6 win, then knocked off the Los Angeles Rams and the New England Patriots on the way to winning Super Bowl LX .
Kyle Shanahan’s club is one of three teams that have not lost a game this season. The 49ers are ranked seventh in the league in both total offense and total defense, and only the Buffalo Bills had scored more points in the first four weeks of the season. The Seahawks have allowed the fewest total yard and passing yards per game in the NFL.
But how’s this for an oddity? While the Niners were handed their lunch at Seattle in the 2025 playoffs, Shanahan’s team has won its last four regular-season games at Lumen Field.
Rashid Shaheed with a 95 YARD KICKOFF TOUCHDOWN WITHIN 13 SECONDS 🏈🤯 49ers 0-7 Seahawks pic.twitter.com/Kv65759t5c
The franchises first met in 1976 during the Seahawks’ debut season in the NFL. Seattle was placed in the NFC West that year, then moved to the AFC West a year later where the team remained until realignment in 2002.
Including three postseason encounters, the ‘Hawks own a 33-24 overall lead in the series, including a 31-20 mark since ’02. A year ago, the clubs met three times for the second time in four seasons.
In Week 1 at Lumen Field, Seahawks’ quarterback lost a fumble in the closing minute deep in Niners’ territory and San Francisco held on for a 17-13 win. In the teams’ regular season finale at Levi’s Stadium, Seattle’s defense was the difference in a 13-3 victory. Two weeks later in the divisional round, Rashid Shaheed returned the opening kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown, Macdonald’s club opened up a 17-0 first-quarter lead and Seattle coasted to a stunning 41-6 victory.
Simply put, the Niners have not allowed a sack during their unbeaten start. Led by Leonard Williams (3.0) and Derick Hall (2.0), Seattle has totaled 11.0 sacks in four outings—the seventh-most in the league. The ‘Hawks have totaled two-plus QB traps in each game, and comes off a season-high four sacks in the 30-23 win over the Chargers.
Seahawks’ quarterback Sam Darnold has only played nine quarters of football this season, and has thrown a combined six touchdown passes the last two weeks. However, he has also served up three interceptions, including a pick-six vs. Washington. Last Sunday vs. the Chargers, his first pass attempt of the afternoon was intercepted.
Emanuel Wilson's first TD as a Seahawk! 🔥 @LACvsSEA on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RVKrkhoLku
In three games vs. the Seahawks a season ago, including the 41-6 playoff loss at Seattle, Shanahan’s team scored a total of 26 points. The 49ers averaged 264.3 total yards per game and their offense managed only two touchdowns, both in the Week 1 win at Seattle. The Niners gave up a half-dozen sacks and turned over the football six times.
While Super Bowl LX Kenneth Walker III is busy leading the league in rushing for the Chiefs, running back Emanuel Wilson leads the Seahawks with 53 carries and 190 yards, and has scored two total TDs. Jadarian Price (on IR) and George Holani have combined for 50 attempts and 189 yards on the ground, and neither has reached the end zone.

title: Why the Seahawks Could Give 49ers' Brock Purdy a Rough Performance
full_text:
Week 5 will be a huge opportunity for many teams this season. For the Seattle Seahawks (3-1), it’s an opportunity for them to make a statement win against an NFC West Divisional opponent as they host the San Francisco 49ers (4-0) on Sunday. The 49ers already got a statement win over a divisional opponent after defeating the heavily favored Los Angeles Rams 27-7 on Thursday Night Football in Week 1.
​Seattle takes on a dangerous San Francisco team that is not only a legitimate Super Bowl contender, despite the countless injuries, but also has league MVP-caliber performances from quarterback Brock Purdy. The 49ers have taken down some great teams with tough defenses, but Purdy’s bad luck against the Seahawks could continue in Week 5.
​ The 49ers go into Week 5 without their starting fullback Kyle Juszczyk . This likely forces San Francisco to go into the game utilizing a 12-personnel, which is one running back and two tight ends. One of the key aspects of the 49ers’ offense is motions and the usage of their fullback in the run game and passing game. San Francisco’s offense could be too predictable for the Seahawks, which might be a problem for Purdy.
​In the last four games versus the Seahawks , including the 41-6 Divisional Round win for Seattle this past January, Purdy completed 69.2% for only an average of 175.8 yards, three touchdowns, five interceptions and eight sacks. The Seahawks know how to get Purdy to throw interceptions and suppress him in a limited offense.
​Seattle is 3-1 in the last four games where its defense has held Purdy to under 160 passing yards. The Seahawks are coming into this deep with the league’s top-ranked passing offense (144.8) thanks to their ability to take away the deep passing game.
While cornerback Riq Woolen has been a great player for the Philadelphia Eagles’ defense, but Josh Jobe fits the Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense’s philosophies and schemes more. Seattle is also seeing Pro-Bowl caliber performances from cornerback Devon Witherspoon and safety Julian Love .
​Seattle has sacked Purdy eight times in the last four games. The Seahawks are coming off their best pass-rushing game of the season in the 30-23 Week 4 win over the Los Angeles Chargers , where they accounted for four sacks and nine tackles for loss. The Seahawks tormented Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert with 10 quarterback hits and still had some rough moments because of penalties.
​The 49ers haven’t allowed a sack through the first four games of the season. The Denver Broncos weren’t able to sack Purdy, but Denver Broncos defensive end Zach Allen accounted for three quarterback hits. San Francisco also faced an unmotivated and jet-lagged Rams defense. Even if the Seahawks can’t sack Purdy in the backfield because of his ability to escape the pressure, the Seahawks have the linebacker and defensive backs to defend the short-to-mid-range passing game.
​The Seahawks are coming off two games where they wanted to play better, encountered a defensive players-only meeting , and they heard all of the noise from the 49ers coming into this matchup. The Dark Side Defense will be motivated to bring down a 49ers team they are familiar with and know the weaknesses of.

title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Describes Brock Purdy's Mentality During Games
full_text:
Kyle Shanahan's coaching makes it notoriously difficult to impress him during San Francisco 49ers games.
He's relentless in his approach , but rightly so. Football is all about situational awareness and having the ability to anticipate every possible scenario before it unfolds.
Everybody within the 49ers organization always talks highly of what it's like to play under his leadership. He sets high standards for himself and his players, demanding them to be at the very best of their game.
In a recent interview, Shanahan spoke at length about why Brock Purdy is "awesome" to coach, explaining that the quarterback perfectly embodies what he wants from the position.
“On our first touchdown vs Denver, he had an awesome drive. He scored throwing that ball to Deebo and did his little Dougie, but there were a few plays on that drive where I thought he did lose his patience, where he just gave up on things a little quick, didn’t have confidence in them and broke the pocket and didn’t sit there and play quarterback," shared Shanahan with NBC Sports Bay Area .
"Sometimes it’s good, sometimes it’s bad. I remember him coming off the field and we didn’t have any play on the one Deebo scored on. It was an off-schedule and Brock found him and it was awesome. I was like 'Dude, we scored because of you on that drive, but settle down some. There was a couple plays in there that I thought you were losing your patience and getting out too quick' and that’s why Brock’s awesome.
"He doesn’t get offended, he’s like 'I know, it was unlucky wasn’t it', it was two plays he did it on. So you can keep coaching him no matter what the game’s like and you keep it moving after that.”
Shanahan has had multiple quarterbacks in his time at San Francisco, but none are on the same level as Purdy.
This applies to both his ability and his coachability. Purdy's ability to remain composed under pressure is a key quality. The best example is the NFC Championship Game against the Detroit Lions.
Purdy is the ideal quarterback for Shanahan's system. Now, the challenge is to translate that into another Super Bowl appearance and, ultimately, win it all.
They've come close twice, so anything's possible if Purdy remains the quarterback. It's still incredible to think about the circumstances that led the franchise to get him.

title: The One Attribute That 49ers QB Brock Purdy Has Over Elite Quarterbacks
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is again making headlines in the mainstream media.
This time it's mostly praise, which is well deserved. Through four games, Purdy has thrown for 1,007 yards, 11 touchdowns, and just one interception. He's also posted a 126.2 passer rating and a league-leading 89.2 quarterback rating.
He's taken his game to another level, producing at an even higher level than before. Based on those numbers, Purdy has firmly put himself in the MVP conversation and, by most statistical measures, deserves to be considered a serious contender for this year's award.
Yet members of the media are still faltering at giving him his flowers, with LeSean McCoy stating on Speakeasy : “This is the thing nowadays, it can’t just be like he’s really really good. He’s really really good.
"It’s either gotta be great and elite or you’re terrible. There’s nothing in the middle. I think Brock Purdy today, it’s not the first time Brock Purdy has played MVP caliber football, I think Brock is a phenomenal quarterback. He’s really really good. He’s damn good…
"I have a lot of respect for Brock Purdy and if he wins an MVP I’ll have even more respect for him, but for me, being around this game and watching it, and playing in it, there’s no way I’m ever gonna put Brock Purdy in the same boat as Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson. It’s just never gonna happen. But you can’t say he’s not playing as good as them guys.”
Patrick Mahomes aside, given that he's the best quarterback in the league, bringing up Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson completely misses the point being made.
Jackson is 3–5 in the postseason, with 10 touchdown passes, seven interceptions and a passer rating of 84.6. Allen, meanwhile, is 8–7, with 29 touchdown passes and just six interceptions.
Purdy, however, is 5–3 in the postseason, having led the 49ers to both the NFC Championship Game and the Super Bowl. Neither Jackson nor Allen has reached the Super Bowl, despite always being mentioned as the league's elite quarterbacks.
You can make the argument that Allen is the better quarterback overall, despite his relatively underwhelming postseason record. But Purdy has already demonstrated that he can deliver on the biggest stage. That's the distinction being overlooked when the media repeatedly champions the likes of Allen, Jackson and Justin Herbert, who, at this point, has yet to win a playoff game.
Ultimately, the argument isn't necessarily about who has the greatest individual talent. It's about who has actually delivered when the stakes are highest. And Purdy has already done that.

full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers Week 5 clash with the Seattle Seahawks could end up defining who wins the NFC West at the end of the season . If the 49ers want to win, they are going to need to dominate a few particular matchups.
Haynes has been struggling this year and has been splitting time with rookie Beau Stephens. They are unresolved at right guard. Mykel Williams will rush from the edge, but they love to slide him inside to get advantageous matchups.

However, the Seahawks interior defensive line is going to be one of the toughest competitions that this group will face all season. Is Puni really in for a career year, and did Connor Colby take a step forward? We will know for sure soon.

title: 49ers Could Target Strong Vita Vea Alternative at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are going to need defensive line help at the NFL trade deadline. While the Tampa Bay Buccaneers saved their season with a Week 5 win against the Dallas Cowboys, the team is sitting at 1-4 right now. They could end up being sellers.
If the Bucs are selling, a name to watch for the 49ers that is not Vita Vea is veteran A’Shawn Robinson. Bradley Locker from PFF sees Robinson as a great fit for the 49ers.
“Robinson may not be the flashiest name on this list, but he’s likely to be dealt given his work on the ground, not to mention being a 2027 free agent,” wrote Locker.
The fit makes more sense than Vea from a cost perspective.
Robinson is entering his 11th season in the NFL. He has played eight playoff games and was on a Carolina Panthers defense that turned things around and made a run into the playoffs. In 2021, he was on the Los Angeles Rams when they won a Super Bowl.
Robinson also has 110 career NFL starts. His combination of experience in the playoffs and in an NFL locker room would be an accepted presence.
He is only on a one-year deal. His deal is cheap enough that the 49ers could easily afford to bring on the entirety of his salary. The combination of him not having team control and bringing cap relief to the Bucs makes him an easy target that would cost a late third-round pick.
For the 49ers, they do not need flash on defense as much as they need stability. Osa Odighizuwa is making plays, but is on pace for more snaps this year than any other in his career.
Gracen Halton can get in the backfield, but the rookie has already left a game with cramps . There is a chance he will be hitting the rookie wall with all of the snaps he is getting. The rest of the depth chart is filled out by practice squad call-ups and players who were signed in the weeks after the season started.
Robinson would come in and start right away. He would take blocks away from Odighizuwa and would allow them to keep Halton fresh all year. For a low cost, the fit makes sense. If the 49ers do not want to spend big on Vea, Robinson is a perfect fit.

title: Why 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Tends Not to Draft Offensive Linemen Early
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' offensive line is one of the most surprising improvements on their roster this season.
It says a lot that, after the first four games - two of which were against teams that made the NFC and AFC Championship Games last season - not a single team has managed to sack quarterback Brock Purdy.
The position group has made a big improvement, whereas for the last few years, it was considered mediocre at best.
Head coach Kyle Shanahan has made only one Day 1 pick on the offensive line in the 10 years he's been in San Francisco. In the end, it was a wasted pick as Mike MCGlinchey wasn't elite and now he plays for the Denver Broncos.
Aside from Trent Williams , whom they traded from the Washington Redskins (now Commanders), the rest of the offensive line was selected in the third, fifth and seventh rounds, respectively. Jake Brendel came from free agency.
Now that the 49ers know that Williams' days are numbered due to him acknowledging he could retire after 2027, the front office opted not to use a Day 1 pick in this year's draft, which received some backlash.
It's all well and good that the unit is playing their best on the field, it doesn't change the fact that they should draft high on a Williams replacement.
Shanahan revealed more on his philosophy on drafting offensive linemen, stating to NBC Sports Bay Area : “By no means do we go into it and say it’s just our philosophy not to take those guys early, but we just don’t take them to take them.
"One thing I noticed a lot in this league, I think a lot of people take Olinemen just to take them. It’s one of safest things to do.
"If you take an Olineman, very rarely are you gonna get questioned. Very rarely does it turn into busts, even if they’re just an average guy.
"A guy who’s in the first round and plays like a fourth round guy, but still plays like a starter, there’s not that much difference.
"It’s hard to find starters, first round, fourth round, whatever, but there’s not that much of a difference until you find like a Pro Bowl type dude.”
It would be wise to find a left tackle to replace Williams before he retires. His eventual absence will be a huge loss to this roster.

title: Why the 49ers Will Beat the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5
full_text:
The Seahawks destroyed the 49ers the past two times these teams played each other, but both are decidedly different teams now.
Those 49ers had Jauan Jennings and Ricky Pearsall as their starting wide receivers. Pearsall had a PCL injury that rendered him practically useless -- not his fault, at least he played -- and Jennings got shut down both times. He caught six passes for 58 yards and no touchdowns total in both games.
This tandem's complete lack of speed allowed the Seahawks' defensive backs to attack the line of scrimmage and smother the short passes and the run game. This explains why the 49ers scored no touchdowns and reached the red zone only once in those two games against Seattle.
These 49ers have Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel as their starting wide receivers. Samuel seems completely rejuvenated, running harder than ever, he's still explosive and has scored three touchdowns in four games.
And Evans is a huge upgrade over Jennings. That's because Evans is a future Hall of Famer, and defenses must respect his size, catch radius, vertical ability and red-zone prowess. So, even when he's limited by a rib injury, as he is this week, he still alters coverages before the snap because defenses are scared of him. His mere presence on the field provides the 49ers with a schematic advantage.
Meanwhile, last season's Seahawks had Kenneth Walker, one of the best running backs in the NFL, and Klint Kubiak, one of the best offensive play callers in the league. This season's Seahawks don't have Walker anymore -- he's on the Chiefs. His replacements -- Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price -- both are injured, and neither will play on Sunday.
As a result, these Seahawks are one-dimensional on offense. And their new play caller, Brian Fleury, never has called plays before this season. And he's having trouble establishing anyone other than reigning Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba as a legitimate weapon. That's why the Seahawks offense stinks on third down this season.
Sam Darnold is a good quarterback when he can complement a strong running game, but he can't do that this season. Now, he's the focal point of Seattle's offense, and he's turnover-prone when he's under pressure.
That's why the 49ers will beat the Seahawks on Sunday. They have a better quarterback than Seattle, a better offensive play caller than Seattle, and a more balanced offense than Seattle. And while the Seahawks have a great defense, the 49ers' defense is really good in its own right.
This will be a grim, violent, low-scoring game that will come down to field goals.

title: How 49ers Can Take Advantage of Malik Mustapha Starting
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are going to be buyers at the NFL trade deadline. However, there is one player who might end up being worth selling if the price is right. Malik Mustapha has not played much in the new Raheem Morris defense after being a two-year starter for the 49ers.
The 49ers could trade the safety with starting experience if the price is right at the trade deadline.
Mustapha is a former fourth-rounder, drafted 125th overall. However, that did not stop him from seeing the field in a significant way as a rookie. Mustapha started in Week 4 and did not look back. He started 12 games in his rookie season and added 72 tackles.
Unfortunately, he tore his ACL in Week 18 of his rookie season. Mustapha missed the first six weeks of the 2025 season as he recovered from the injury. However, once he was healthy, the team started to bench rookie Marques Sigle to get Mustapha back into a full-time role.
Despite 22 starts in his first two seasons, new defensive coordinator Raheem Morris has not been as interested in getting him on the field. Mustapha missed some time in training camp, and it opened the door for Sigle to start in Week 1.
Sigle has an ankle injury , but will return in a few weeks. This could give Mustapha a chance to prove that he is valuable on the trade market in a short-term starting stint.
On one hand, the 49ers are a team with too many injuries and not enough depth. Trading a starter-caliber player, even if Sigle returns, could be unwise.
The other thought is that the team acquiring Mustapha will be adding him at a time when they have a year and a half of team control on his rookie contract. He is young and is a two-year starter.
The combination of experience, youth, team control, and a cost-effective deal would probably net more on the trade market than some would expect.
The 49ers could find a way to spin Mustapha into a player at a different position of need. They could also recoup draft capital. Given the top-heavy state of the roster and the age of some of their stars, it would not be a bad idea to try to add a few extra draft picks.
It will be interesting to see how the 49ers handle Mustapha.

title: Mike Evans Has Revealed His True Importance to the 49ers Since Rib Injury
full_text:
Even if he is 33 years old and no longer in his prime, the San Francisco 49ers having Mike Evans on their roster is a sight to behold.
It always felt like he was going to stay with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers his whole career. But he chose to join San Francisco for less money .
Already, upon hearing that, his motivation is clearly about winning and not about the digits increasing in his checking account. But financial deals aside, Evans has shown in a completely different way what a future first-ballot Hall of Famer wide receiver adds to the locker room.
The 49ers, at least in the Kyle Shanahan era, have had their fair share of injury problems. In some cases, players play through the pain, but it's extremely rare for someone to do so and still excel.
Evans embodies the latter. He said that his injury felt like he was stabbed, yet he suited up and delivered arguably his best game with San Francisco so far. Five receptions for 76 yards against a step-up Denver Broncos team was a very good effort.
But there was little chance Evans wasn't going to play in that game. General manager John Lynch shared this week just how determined the wide receiver was to take the field.
“I remember first time in the locker room going down there – you always want to hear it for yourself – and I said, ‘Mike, good news, we’ll have you for Seattle,’” Lynch recalled on KNBR . “And he said, ‘No, I’m playing this week.’ And he said it in a way like he’s playing this week.”
And that speaks volumes. He fits the Kyle Shanahan mould of a player who is not only tough but also intensely focused on winning football matches.
Evans signed a three-year deal in free agency, but even if he's around for just one, the 49ers are incredibly lucky to have a player with his tangible achievements, as well as the drive and willingness to produce at all costs.
Actions speak far louder than words, and Evans has shown exactly what he's willing to put on the line for this team.
I'm no doctor but I advocated for him to be rested , but upon seeing his actions from the last week, it would be far from surprising seeing him gear up for the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5 and deliver yet another good performance,

title: The One Brock Purdy Stat That Could Give the 49ers an Edge vs. Seattle
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers facing the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5 presents their biggest challenge of the season so far.
The 49ers are 4-0 so far, with two wins against the Los Angeles Rams and the Denver Broncos, teams who reached the AFC and NFC Championship last season.
That's a resounding positive. Now the next big test against the Seahawks is just around the corner - the very team that defeated San Francisco in both the regular season and in the playoffs last season.
Seattle went on to win the Super Bowl. In the game against the 49ers, you could feel the game slipping away from San Francisco after the Seahawks scored a touchdown following the opening punt.
So let's be honest, they represent a huge test. They have a great team in all three phases and heading to Lumen Field is always recognized as one of the most hostile environments in the league. A victory against Seattle shows they are truly a Super Bowl contender.
There is one Brock Purdy statistic that should favor the 49ers heading into this game though.
Since becoming the 49ers' starting quarterback, Purdy has never lost a regular-season road game against Seattle. The stat suggests complete dominance over a divisional rival, and when needed, he has found ways to get the job done in these crucial matchups.
Last season provided a perfect example. Granted, it came in Week 1, when neither team had fully found its footing, but Purdy still stepped up to lead the 49ers to victory. He was later diagnosed with turf toe, making his performance all the more respectable.
So far this season, Purdy is playing like an MVP-caliber quarterback . He's elevated his game to an even higher standard and is making it look effortless. His ridiculous 2026 stat line so far speaks for itself.
Compared to last season, when the offensive line was lacking, it now appears to be the best it has ever been. Purdy should have more time in the pocket and, overall, be in a much better position to perform than he was when the 49ers were knocked out.
A win against Seattle would justify the hype surrounding the 49ers' season prospects this year . A defeat wouldn't ruin those expectations completely, but it would indicate that they're still there or thereabouts, which was ultimately what was expected heading into the season. They just need results to go their way.

title: 5 Biggest Questions Facing 49ers Against Seahawks
full_text:
With the San Francisco 49ers sitting at 4-0, they now face their biggest test of the season with a road matchup against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. What are the biggest questions the 49ers have to answer in Week 5?
The 49ers essentially have two receivers on their current roster. Mike Evans has 213 receiving yards. Deebo Samuel has 185 receiving yards. Demarcus Robinson is next with 84 yards, and he is on the IR.
Jordan Watkins currently has 60 yards, while Khadarel Hodge has 18. They need somebody to step up.
The 49ers' interior offensive line has been one of the most impressive revelations of the season. However, they are going to see a much tougher test with the Seattle Seahawks. Byron Murphy and Leonard Williams have typically had their way with this group.
Still, Connor Colby and Dominick Puni look much improved from last season . Do they hold up?
Last season it was notable that the defensive coordinator Robert Saleh did not have Lenoir move from his outside spot to follow Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Raheem Morris said that Lenoir will not follow him everywhere, but noted that they have the ability to move Lenoir around more often than they did in recent years.
The Seahawks can move Smith-Njigba around and get him away from Lenoir, but we could see more of Lenoir in the slot this week than in past years?
Morris did not draft Mykel Williams, so it will be interesting to see how he aligns in the 49ers new defense. Williams is an edge rusher, but did most of his damage along the interior last year. Morris runs more five-man fronts than Saleh did last year. So, Williams can be a five-technique as an interior base end more than we saw as a rookie.
Do we see a more versatile Williams in this defense?
The 49ers' loss of Kyle Juszczyk is magnified by the reality that Jake Tonges is hurt and the team does not have a quality third wide receiver. They have their stars at receivers, tight end, and running back. The fifth skill player is almost always going to be a weak link at the moment. How do the 49ers fix that issue?

title: 3 Buccaneers Players Who Could Be Traded Before Deadline
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers may be coming off a win, but things still don't look great for them heading into the rest of the season. The team is 1-4, and if things go poorly, it could be staring at a rebuild next year with a new head coach.
If that's the case, general manager Jason Licht may want to get some new draft capital. Licht almost never trades midseason , but what if he did? And if he needed some draft picks, which Buccaneers players would he be willing to give up? Who would teams want?
We tried to answer all these questions with three potential Bucs players who could be moved before the deadline:
If the Bucs don't play well leading up to the deadline, they'd probably be down to get anything they could from Chris Godwin. Godwin is 30 years old and isn't getting a ton of use in Zac Robinson's scheme, and there are probably a few teams that wouldn't mind his veteran presence and experience at the position — and maybe a few that would utilize him just a bit more.
Godwin is currently playing on a $22 million deal this year after signing a three-year deal for that much on average. But his last deal is a team option, so any team that traded for Godwin could either extend him to the tune of $22 million more or simply let him walk. Godwin could be a rental for any team looking to take themselves over the line, and the Bucs could get a little capital on top.
Gainwell is another player the Bucs haven't been using much. He's only ran the ball 17 times for 44 yards, just 2.6 yards per carry — he's also only caught 11 passes for 54 yards and a touchdown.
RB-needy teams could easily call about Gainwell if needed. The Bucs have Sean Tucker available and Tucker has looked good in his limited snaps, so he could slide right into that RB2 postion (and he's be a lot cheaper). Any team that wants Gainwell would have to take on his two-year, $14 million contract, which he's currently in the first year of.
This one doesn't feel particularly likely, because the Bucs' pass rush hasn't been great. But if Tampa Bay really wants some capital back before what could be a rebuilding year next year, Diaby wouldn't be a bad player to move.
Diaby is on a contract year as it stands and will be a free agent in March. As a result, any team picking him up wouldn't have to worry about taking on a big contract and could instead watch him to see how he plays — if he pays well, they can extend him, and if not, he'd be a quick rental.
Diaby has five solo tackles and a pick without any sacks so far this season. The Bucs probably want to keep him around for now, but it might be wise to simply listen if a team comes calling.

title: Would Jason Licht Realistically Trade Any Buccaneers Players?
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is approaching. We're exactly one month away, and so any talks or significant developments on the trade market are beginning to fester as we approach Week 6 of the regular season and teams are more in-tune with what they need.
It's been a big week for trades, with center Cam Jurgens heading from Philidelphia to Baltimore and Arizona Cardinals wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. allegedly headed... somewhere after Sunday's slate. More trades will be soon to come, and all 32 teams likely have players that could be dealt this season.
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 1-4 heading into Week 6. Things looked particularly dire before the team's 24-16 win over the Cowboys on Thursday Night Football, but with a win, the Bucs can seek to become the second team in NFL history to make the playoffs off a 0-4 start.
Do they need firepower to do that? Should general manager Jason Licht go all in and make a trade? Should the Bucs begin their rebuild early and try to get rid of some veterans for extra capital?
Almost certainly not. There are a few reasons, but we'll start with the biggest one — Licht isn't really a big trader.
He's only made one in-season trade during his entire tenure as Bucs GM, and that was when he gave the New York Jets a sixth-round pick in exchange for defensive tackle Steve McLendon in 2020. He's also not a huge fan of giving high value — the most he's ever exchanged for a player is a third-round pick when he traded for edge rusher Jason Pierre-Paul in 2018.
On the flip side, Licht has a bit more recent history dealing aging players to get capital, but never during the season — he flipped cornerback Carlton Davis to the Detroit Lions in 2024 before the season started to get a third-round pick back from them.
The Bucs have a few aging veterans on the team, but they tend to like all of them. Some options, like wideout Chris Godwin Jr., have a contract far greater than their ability, so other teams probably wouldn't bite on a trade for any of Tampa Bay's mainstays.
The Bucs also went into this season believing they were competitive, and even at a 0-4 start, they likely still believe that. The Bucs will try and turn things around from a disastrous start, and with that in mind, they're very likely to stay put at the trade deadline and try to make things work with the talent they have — and they aren't in the mindset of rebuilding.
The Bucs will try plenty of things over the next few weeks to try and get things going in Tampa Bay. Just don't expect trades to be one of them.
