title: Why Todd Bowles Was Crouched In Pain After Buccaneers Sealed the Win
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers pulled off the improbable.
They went on the road as a 0-4 team in primetime with an undrafted rookie quarterback and won against one of the best offenses in the league, the Dallas Cowboys.
It was a thrilling game for the Bucs, who had to fight to the very end to make sure they were able to get their first win.
Once the Bucs sealed the victory with an interception by Alex Anzalone, head coach Todd Bowles could be seen kneeling down in some pain. That caused many to show concern, but we now know exactly what occurred and that Bowles will be okay.
According to ESPN's Jenna Laine, Bowles confirmed that it wasn't anything serious and that he just caught a helmet to the gut that caused him to go down to one knee.
I’m told that Todd Bowles is OK. Several of you asked. I was concerned as well. I’m not in Dallas but just heard back. He said he caught a celebration helmet to the gut but says he’ll be OK. That’s why he was crouched over like this. pic.twitter.com/cDwSSsAETj
For a moment, those who have been critical of Bowles forgot about the football side of things and hoped that he didn't suffer some type of medical emergency.
It's great to get some clarity on the situation, even though we knew Bowles was okay since he spoke with the media following the game.
Bowles coached his tail off in the matchup, showing signs of what this team could be if it all comes together.
The offense did what it was supposed to do by running the ball for a whopping 241 yards. And the defense, while still struggling to get pressure, was able to play CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens tight. The defense also showed up big time by winning the turnover battle with two interceptions and a fumble recovery on special teams.
While the win is big for how the team moves forward, it's impossible to ignore that they did this against one of the worst defenses in the league.
The road ahead doesn't get much easier for the Bucs, but if they are able to carry over this type of play and confidence as a team, they could find themselves right back in the mix of the NFC South.
The Bucs now have over a week until their next game, when they return home to Raymond James Stadium to face off against Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers.

title: Buccaneers Rookie Quarterback Makes NFL History With Cowboys Win
full_text:
It took awhile, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally have their first win of the season.
The Bucs defeated the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 on Thursday Night Football to move to 1-4 on the year. They did it with undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels under center, who is filling in for QB Baker Mayfield as Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb he suffered against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3.
Daniels played well against the Cowboys, completing 76% of his passes for 178 yards and a touchdown. But he also made history when he beat Dallas at AT&T Stadium, and it's a record that will never be broken.
Per FOX Sports' Greg Auman, Daniels is the only quarterback outside of the NFL's strike year in 1987 to ever defeat the Dallas Cowboys in a regular season football game.
Tampa Bay’s Jalon Daniels is the first undrafted rookie QB ever to beat the Cowboys, aside from a strike game with replacement players in 1987.
That stat makes sense — UDFA rookies rarely ever start football games anyway. Daniels is the first UDFA rookie to start for a team before Week 4 since the 1970 NFL-AFL merger. There have been just 10 UDFA rookie quarterbacks to start a game since 2013 — of those 10, one of them was Kendall Hinton, a wide receiver who had to play emergency QB.
Daniels has done a decent job filling in for Mayfield so far. Daniels has thrown two touchdowns and three interceptions on 55 attempts for 337 yards, and on top of that, he's rushed for  87 yards on 16 carries.
Daniels is set to start another game two Sundays from now against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 6. With Mayfield already looking to come back from his dislocated thumb, Daniels will likely have one more week to show his worth and cement himself as Tampa Bay's backup for the foreseeable future when the Steelers come to Tampa Bay.
The Bucs and Daniels will play the Steelers on Oct. 18. The Bucs have alternated wins and losses against the Steelers since 2002, so maybe Daniels will help continue that trend two Sundays from now.

title: Buccaneers Reveal Who They're Planning to Start at Quarterback vs. Steelers
full_text:
It took a while, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers officially got their first win on Thursday night.
Tampa Bay bested the Cowboys 24-16 to move to 1-4 on the year. There's still a lot of work to do and things to clean up, but Tampa Bay ran the ball exceptionally well and the defense showed up in a big way to help secure the victory.
The first win of the season didn't come with starting quarterback Baker Mayfield, though. It came with backup quarterback Jalon Daniels under center, who executed the offense well and took care of the football to help Tampa Bay win. Daniels is now 1-1 as a starter in Tampa Bay — but with a long week off and the Pittsburgh Steelers coming two Sundays from now, will he get to play a third game?
Head coach Todd Bowles spoke to media on Friday after the win, and he revealed who the Bucs are planning to go with against the Steelers — for now.
Bowles confirmed to the media that while he still needs to see what Mayfield looks like and how he can grip the football after the stitches in his thumb were removed, he's planning on going with Daniels against the Steelers at the moment.
"Right now, we plan on starting Jalon Daniels against the Steelers," Bowles said.
Todd Bowles says that he’ll see what Baker Mayfield looks like when he comes in and how he’s able to grip the ball, but the team is planning on starting Jalon Daniels again against the Steelers
Starting two games and appearing at the end of one, Daniels has thrown two touchdowns and three interceptions on 55 attempts for 337 yards. Daniels has also been a significant threat on the ground, already amassing 87 yards on 16 carries.
Despite Daniels being the plan for Week 6, it will be interesting to see if Mayfield begins to practice or has an outside shot at playing against Pittsburgh. Mayfield has been campaigning to play the game, per NFL insider James Palmer, and if the medical staff thinks he can grip the football well enough, Bowles may be faced with the decision to rest Mayfield or to let him get back in after the team has gotten its first win of the season.
Coach Baker Mayfield could return to player Baker Mayfield next week against the Steelers. I'm told Mayfield is pushing to play but it's 10 days out and it's too early for the Bucs to know medically if he can go. The stitches were taken out Monday and it's a matter of his thumb…
Mayfield has started three games for Tampa Bay and has thrown for 615 yards on 96 attempts with two touchdowns and two interceptions.
The Bucs have the rest of the week off before preparing for the Steelers, who they'll play on Oct. 18. That's plenty of time for Mayfield to recover, but it's also plenty of time for the Bucs to continue game planning with Daniels and the skill set he has as he goes into what is currently set to be his third NFL start.

title: Grading the Buccaneers' Week 5 Win Against the Dallas Cowboys
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally got their first win of the season, and it was in primetime against the Dallas Cowboys.
There was a great level of execution on the defensive and offensive sides of the ball. Let's go over our grades for the Bucs in their 24-16 win.
It was an overall very solid night for Jalon Daniels. He took what the Dallas defense gave him and didn't make any real mistakes, to the tune of 19/25 passing for 189 yards, one touchdown and no turnovers. He had seven carries on the ground for 23 yards.
The running game was the largest reason the Bucs won this matchup and it was by far the best thing the Bucs offense has produced this season.
Bucky Irving finished the day with 23 touches for 175 scrimmage yards and two total touchdowns. Irving also had the eighth-longest run in team history, with a 72-yard run in the contest as well.
Besides a great 64-yard reception where Tez Johnson broke the ankles of Daron Bland, the receiver room still didn't get much going. Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson tried to get Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin more involved, as they did combine for nine catches, but it still only went for 75 yards on the evening.
Egbuka did have a 14-yard end-around for a touchdown, which was a nice play, however.
Cade Otton finished the night with three catches for 25 yards and Payne Durham even got involved with a five-yard reception of his own. Still, this group is middling and hasn't done much of note this season.
This might have been the best performance of the Bucs offensive line this season. Now, they do get a good number of points off for penalties, as there were plenty from this group in this game.
However, they did do a fantastic job of opening up lanes in the rushing attack and Daniels' scrambling ability kept him to only getting sacked once.
The defensive line continued to be largely ineffective in this matchup, as Dak Prescott was not sacked once in this game and generally didn't face much pressure unless the team sent a blitz against them.
The Cowboys' run game did well in this matchup as well until they had to move away from it since they were down in the game. Also, Yaya Diaby had an interception in this game, which was fun to watch.
Who would've thought that Alex Anzalone would end up with the game-sealing interception for the Bucs, huh? I give a lot of points for that, and overall the unit did some pretty solid work, all things considered.
Jacob Parrish had an up-and-down night for the Buccaneers. He did finish with four passes defended — however, receiver George Pickens ate with nine catches for 130 yards and a touchdown.
Zyon McCollum was fantastic today in this one, holding CeeDee Lamb to two catches for nine yards in this contest. Also, I thought the safety duo of Tykee Smith and Ifeatu Melifonwu were solid in this game as well.
It was a great day for special teams as Miles Killebrew forced a fumble on Cowboys returner KaVontae Turpin to help the team pull further ahead. Chase McLaughlin made all of his kicks, and Riley Dixon was fine punting the ball as well.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Buccaneers' 24-16 Win Over the Cowboys
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers had their backs against the wall heading to Dallas on a short week to take on the Dallas Cowboys for Thursday Night Football.
Unlike every other game this season, there was finally some good things happening on the field for the Buccaneers, who managed to pull out an impressive 24-16 victory in Dallas.
Let's get right into the good, the bad and the ugly.
Daniels' career night started on the opening drive where, despite some mental lapses, Daniels led the longest drive for the Buccaneers' franchise since Jeff Garcia in 2007. He completed 8/8 passes for 49 yards and a TD on 15 plays in almost an entire quarter.
Daniels is 1-of-2 undrafted rookie quarterbacks since 1991 – and the first since 2013 – to earn a 100.0% completion percentage in a single quarter, while completing seven-or-more passes (also Matt McGloin, third quarter, 12/15/13 vs. Kansas City). https://t.co/vWKcc4ifXq
Daniels was excellent throughout this game. Was he perfect? No. But he did more than enough to put his team in a position to win a road game they absolutely had to have.
Although he looked a little too patient in the pocket early on, Daniels seemed to really settle into a nice rhythm in terms of his pocket poise, timing, and decisions about when to look downfield and when to tuck it and run.
Despite possessing a big arm and the speed to be a dual-threat quarterback, Daniels resisted the temptation to play hero ball and instead played like a seasoned game manager tonight, taking care of the football and controlling the clock, which is exactly what his team needed.
Through the first few weeks of the season, Bucky Irving looked like the team's only true weapon on offense. Tonight, Bucky looked like the team's best weapon, but it felt like he was finally getting some help from his offensive line and offensive coordinator.
The Cowboys' defense has struggled mightily this season, but this is still an NFL defense, and the Bucs made them look like they weren't when they handed it off. Irving looked electric in this game and showed just how dangerous he can be when given some half-decent lanes to run through.
The Bucs totaled a whopping 243 yards rushing in this game while averaging over six yards per carry as a team. Bucky Irving himself rushed for 165 yards on just 21 carries.
The Bucs' defense played a really solid game vs. the Cowboys. Most impressive was the performance of their cornerback room, with Jacob Parrish, Zyon McCollum and Tykee Smith all having a significant impact on the Cowboys' production through the air.
Jacob Parrish has recorded three-plus passes defensed in a game for the first time in his NFL career. Parrish's six passes defensed on the season are tied for the fourth-most across the NFL this season (teammate Zyon McCollum is also tied for 4th).
Had it not been for Todd Bowles' atrocious game management decisions, the Bucs would have likely hit the 30-point plateau for the first time this year. Zac Robinson has had a really rough start to his debut as the Bucs' OC, but he was in a tough spot trying to alter his offensive game plan to suit an undrafted rookie quarterback playing the Dallas Cowboys on the road.
Although Daniels executed, it needs to be acknowledged that Robinson put together a game plan that allowed the dynamic but inexperienced rookie quarterback to perform at his peak so early in his career. Robinson mixed the run with the pass really well on Thursday night, and the Bucs dominated the game on the ground throughout.
It's important to note that although Tristan Wirfs did leave the game with some sort of lower-body injury on two different occasions in the second half, he did return to finish the game.
Still, there's little doubt that Wirfs is the best player on the roster, regardless of position, and if the Buccaneers were to lose him for any period of time, it would be a catastrophic hit to a team that is trying to dig their way out of a very deep hole.
Unsure if it was non-contact or not here. Thought at first he got rolled up on but not really the case. pic.twitter.com/8rPNALXTf2
With 3:47 left in the first half and the game tied 7-7, Todd Bowles' indecision cost the Buccaneers three points. The Bucs were facing a third-and-six from around midfield after a Tristan Wirfs false start penalty set them back. Initially, it appeared as though Bowles might be planning to punt the ball away, but then he changed his mind and sent out the field goal unit so McLaughlin could attempt a 61-yarder.
Unfortunately, it took the Bucs too long to get set up for the kick, and Bowles did not use a timeout to buy his team enough time to recalibrate. Bowles' lack of decisiveness — something that has plagued Bowles throughout his tenure in Tampa Bay as a head coach — directly resulted in a delay-of-game penalty, which took the Buccaneers out of field goal range and ultimately cost them points they desperately needed.
Absolutely unbelievable levels of incompetence lol. A high school coach would be embarrassed to mess that up
With 8:36 left in the game and the Buccaneers leading 24-10, Bowles decided to go for it on fourth-and-goal as opposed to kicking the FG to make it a three-score game. The perplexing decision was one that not only reflects Bowles' lack of familiarity with holding a lead this year, but also contradicts his profile as an overly conservative decision-maker on fourth downs.
Throughout the first four weeks of the season, it could be argued that the Buccaneers lost in large part because of Bowles. On Thursday, they won a crucial road victory despite some terrible game management decisions he made,

title: Overreactions From Buccaneers' Thursday Night Football Win Over Cowboys
full_text:
It took five games, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a win.
The Bucs defeated the Dallas Cowboys on prime time in AT&T Stadium on Thursday Night Football to move to 1-4 on the year. It wasn't the prettiest win, with problems still present and the Cowboys almost coming back, but the Bucs got it done and outplayed the Cowboys to secure the victory 24-16.
It's a win, but there's still room for some overreactions after the game. Here are three of them as the Bucs get ready for a long week off after their Thursday Night Football matchup:
Walker is playing what is technically his rookie season after he tore his ACL in training camp last year, and boy, has he made the most of it. He pressured quarterback Dak Prescott multiple times on Thursday, disrupting the passing game and helping the defense in a big way. He also tipped a ball in coverage that resulted in a Yaya Diaby interception.
Walker is OLB5 on the depth chart behind Rueben Bain Jr., Yaya Diaby, Al-Quadin Muhammad and Anthony Nelson. So far this year, he's been better than all of them, and he needs the snaps to match.
Yes, this Cowboys defense is awful. But quarterback Jalon Daniels has executed fairly well these last two weeks, and he's played better than most expected him to for an undrafted free agent.
The Bucs took a chance on him after the draft and took an even bigger chance on him by making him QB2. Some were skeptical about what he could do as a UDFA, especially now that the Bucs need him to play, but he's done exactly what he needed to do and played about as well as he can over these past two games to prove the Bucs were right to gamble on him. He wasn't perfect — he almost threw a disastrous pick-six — but he has run the offense and got a win out of it.
Eventually, Mayfield will be back. But the Bucs will feel very comfortable with Daniels behind him.
The Bucs had an absolutely brutal night of penalties in the win, with 13 penalties for 87 yards. A good chunk of those were offensive penalties, with everything from holding to false starts plaguing Tampa Bay throughout the night.
The Bucs have no discipline on the offensive side of the ball. When the play is in motion, wideouts and the quarterback end up in various places the Bucs' line doesn't expect them to, and as a result, the team suffers from a good number of penalties every game.
There doesn't seem to be a fix to these issues in sight, even with this win. The Bucs have to be smoother in their entire operation from the ground up to find a way not to go backwards every week.

title: Buccaneers Matchup Against Cowboys Just Got Tougher
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers already have a tough task on Thursday night. They're set to play a red-hot Dallas Cowboys offense on Thursday Night Football on the road, and at 0-4, the Bucs really need a win to give themselves even a drop of hope for the remainder of the year.
Unfortunately for Tampa Bay, that task got a little bit harder for them once the Dallas Cowboys activated a key starter on the Thursday of the game.
Cowboys guard Tyler Smith was questionable on Dallas' injury report as he's been recovering from thumb surgery before the season. Per the NFL's Ian Rapoport, he's set to make his debut against the Bucs on Thursday night.
The #Cowboys are activating All-Pro G Tyler Smith from Injured Reserve to play tonight against the #Bucs . A big lift. One of the NFL's best, Smith had thumb surgery right before the season with hopes of returning as soon as possible. After a full practice Wednesday, he's back. pic.twitter.com/3XQLuAy8R2
Smith was a Second Team All-Pro in 2023 and is a stalwart on the Cowboys' offensive line. A three-time consecutive Pro Bowler dating back to 2023, Smith has been a crucial part of Dallas' offense and signed a four-year, $96 million contract in 2025.
Now that he's back to protect quarterback Dak Prescott, Tampa Bay's pass rush will have to step up on Thursday to get to him through Smith's efforts. That will include players like Calijah Kancey, Tampa Bay's pass-rushing DT, Vita Vea and A'Shawn Robinson to disrupt the middle and halt both the run and the pass against Dallas.
Tampa Bay is getting a player of its own back with Rueben Bain Jr., who missed the last two games due to a groin issue he suffered against the Cleveland Browns. The Bucs have lost safety Antoine Winfield Jr. for the next few weeks due to a rib injury, though, and they're also starting backup quarterback Jalon Daniels with Baker Mayfield recovering from a thumb injury.
The Bucs will play the Cowboys on Thursday night at 8:15. Head coach Todd Bowles will have to do everything he can to get pressure up the middle, and with Smith's return to the team, his job has gotten a bit harder in that regard.

title: 3 Storylines I'm Watching Most in Buccaneers Week 5 Matchup Against Cowboys
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are limping into a primetime matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football.
A 0-4 start hasn't instilled much confidence in this team, and they face yet another tall task in front of them as they search for their first win.
It doesn't seem like the Bucs will have much of a chance in this one, but these are the three storylines we will be watching when they take on the Cowboys in Jerry's World.
This will be Jalon Daniels' second-ever start, and it will come in primetime. The pressure will amp up, and Daniels will not only need to have an excellent game through the air but also on the ground.
Daniels, along with Bucky Irving, Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker, must all be at their best. They will have ample opportunities to make plays as Dallas is surrendering 150.3 rushing yards per game (31st in the NFL).
Zac Robinson must lean on his running backs and mobile quarterback in this one if they hope to match Dallas score-for-score, and it would also help with controlling the game clock, keeping the Cowboys' offense off the field and keeping themselves out of third-and-long situations.
It's the first 0-4 start in Tampa Bay since 2013, and head coach Todd Bowles' seat couldn't get much warmer.
It's desperation time for Bowles and the Bucs, so not showing up at all would quite literally be the straw that breaks the camel's back.
Getting blown out on national television would put the Bucs' record at 0-5, which would make it one of the worst starts in franchise history — the first since Tony Dungy's inaugural season back in 1996.
If that does indeed happen, the writing will most definitely be on the wall for Bowles and company.
Dallas boasts one of the best offenses in the league, which is headed by an elite passing game with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens leading the charge.
It was already going to be a massive challenge for a young Bucs' secondary, but that hill got even steeper with Antoine Winfield Jr. being ruled out as he deals with a rib fracture.
While Winfield hasn't been his best, the Bucs will now have to rely on backups to try and help slow down the Cowboys' passing attack. How Tampa Bay and Bowles adapt to the absence of Winfield against Dallas' passing game will be a major defining factor in whether they can keep this game close.

title: Where to Watch and 2 Things to Expect: Titans Host 0-4 Texans in Battle for First Victory
full_text:
Neither the Tennessee Titans nor the Houston Texans have pulled out a win this season. Both teams sit in that bottom-of-the-barrel level of NFL teams who simply haven't figured it out yet.
Today, the division rivals will butt heads at Nissan Stadium. It's Cam Ward vs. C.J. Stroud. JC Latham vs. Will Anderson Jr. Robert Saleh vs. DeMeco Ryans - we'll touch on that matchup specifically.
Here's our weekly guide on where to watch the Titans, as well as what to expect from Tennessee's team in Week 5 at home.
The Titans take on the Texans at 12:00 PM CT on Sunday, October 11, in Nashville. You can catch the contest live on CBS and streaming on NFL+ and Paramount+. Locally, Nashville affiliate WTVF NewsChannel 5 will have the game.
There are a handful of ways to watch this one, Titans fans, but we're bringing you just two major wrinkles to expect.
Cam Ward set his season high in passing yards in Week 4, throwing for 222 through the air againt the Baltimore Ravens. We should be in for a similar performance, if not one more focused on the deep ball.
Ward has been criticized time and time again this season for failing to connect on explosive plays, along with OC Brian Daboll. Even in losing to the Ravens, however, Tennessee's offense finally opened up the passing game. Carnell Tate had 145 yards all by himself.
Against a so-far lackluster Texans secondary, the Titans are facing a must-win scenario coming off their best passing performance of the year. It'd be shocking for Ward and Daboll not to lean into that apparent advantage today.
With head coach DeMeco Ryans taking over play-calling duties for Houston's defense, two of the league's most storied DCs will coach against one another today. Saleh and Ryans have met one time prior as HCs, back in 2023.
The Jets beat the Texans all that time ago, and now, Saleh will look to repeat. Both coaches looking for their first win in a divisional matchup certainly raises the stakes of this bittersweet reunion.
Expect varied looks on either side of the ball, and even potentially turnovers both ways. The Texans certainly have the better offense on paper, but at least prior to Ryans taking over, the Titans' defense could easily be granted an edge here.
It'll be a real clash of the defensive titans on the sidelines, no pun intended. The victor in this duel could end up being the overall victor as a direct result.

title: Titans' Anthony Hill Jr. Slots Lower Than Expected in NFL.com's Rookie Defensive Rankings
full_text:
It's been a rough start to the year for the Tennessee Titans, as the team is 0-4 on the season and their playoff hopes are already basically dead. However, there have still been some bright spots in what has been a dreadful season so far, including linebacker Anthony Hill Jr.
Hill, Tennessee's second-round pick in April, has been a standout on head coach Robert Saleh's defense . The Texas product has tallied 42 tackles, 13 defensive stops, two pass deflections, and a 73.5 Pro Football Focus tackling grade.
Though Hill has experienced the usual rookie growing pains, especially in pass coverage, the 21-year-old has brought refreshing youth to the Titans' linebacker room. But it looks like some of the national media has yet to take full notice of Hill's solid performance.
NFL.com's Gennaro Filice released his rankings of the top rookie defenders in the NFL through four games, and Hill came in at No. 7. Sonny Styles of the Washington Commanders earned the top spot.
"As the Mike linebacker and green-dot wearer in Robert Saleh’s defense, Hill is automatically subject to reckless Fred Warner comparisons. I won’t be making any of those here, but the rookie does deserve shine for his sideline-to-sideline range. Over the first three weeks of the season, Hill piled up an NFL-high 34 tackles, earning him Defensive Rookie of the Month honors for September. Against the pass, he’s flashed ability as a blitzer but lacks consistency in coverage," Filice wrote of Hill.
Hill has played every single defensive snap for the Titans in 2026, and has held his own as a plus starter on the unit. Though the rookies above, including Styles, Arvell Reese of the New York Giants, Dillon Thieneman of the Chicago Bears, Mansoor Delane of the Kansas City Chiefs, Jacob Rodriguez of the Miami Dolphins, and Caleb Downs of the Dallas Cowboys, have shown their flashes, Hill has already established himself as one of the most pivotal pieces of Saleh's roster.
If Hill were on a winning team and playing like he has so far, the 6-foot-2 linebacker would be garnering more respect. However, with the Titans winless, it's hard to blame Filice for underrating Hill's production and output.
Tennessee will be eyeing their first win of the season against the Houston Texans at Nissan Stadium. Hill will need to patrol the middle of the field at a high level, make progress in pass coverage, and continue being tenacious in the run game for the Titans to finally exit a Sunday with a victory.

title: 2 Bold Predictions That Could Decide Titans' Divisional Matchup With Texans
full_text:
One day out of Week 5, the Tennessee Titans still appear to be facing an uphill battle against the division rival Houston Texans. Things haven't gotten any easier for the reigning worst team in the AFC South.
However, with the Texans also coming into this game at 0-4, the Titans have reason to be slightly more hopeful here. Robert Saleh did say that Houston may be "the greatest 0-4 team in the history of football," but the record doesn't lie. These two teams are entering Sunday's matchup on even ground.
I've got a handful of bold predictions for the Titans' duel. Either coming true could undoubtedly change the contest's outcome, and there's one to represent both sides of the ball.
If the Titans are to find a way to beat the Texans, their offense will have to find a way to keep up with C.J. Stroud. Coming off his best game of the 2026 season, I predict that Cam Ward will throw multiple touchdowns for the first time therein.
Ward wasn't perfect last week, but his 222 yards and chunk of deep-ball connections inspired a new home amongst Tennessee fans. The second-year QB looked more comfortable in Brian Daboll's system. He looked ready to take chances again.
The Texans are allowing an average of 260 passing yards per game this season. Head coach DeMeco Ryans taking over defensive play-calling duties could have an impact in either direction, but the unit as it has stood this year presents an open window for Ward.
If he's really going to take steps forward this year, there's no better time to prove it than Week 5. I believe Ward will give the home crowd in Nashville something to cheer about through the air.
Defensively, I'll also predict that both teams force a turnover. Both Saleh and Ryans are former defensive coordinators (and for the San Francisco 49ers, at that), and each calling plays against one another should up the ante on that side of the ball.
Tennessee and Houston have combined for just three interceptions on the season, but with disruptors like Will Anderson Jr. on one side and Jeffery Simmons on the other, we could see some loose balls on the ground.
Either way, I expect this one to get scrappy. Both teams are desperate for a victory. Saleh and Ryans are each backed against the wall, even if in different circumstances. It's a divisional game in which both franchises are trying to save themselves some embarrassment.
If I had to get specific, I'd say Tennessee turns it over through the air, and Houston on the ground. Stroud hasn't thrown an interception yet this year, though the Texans have four fumbles (two of them lost) on the season. Both were lost by Stroud.
It's a shot in the dark, but arguably no battle is harder to predict than one between two teams with nothing to lose. Expect the unexpected in Week 5, Titans fans.

title: Staff Predictions for Titans vs. Ravens: Tennessee Comes Out on Top for 1 Main Reason
full_text:
Last week, the Titans On SI staff predicted a Tennessee loss across the board against the Baltimore Ravens. Unfortunately, we turned out to be correct. The Titans fell in Week 4 to a score of 24-18, in a game that saw Brian Daboll's offense progress just below a breakthrough.
This week, our two picks tell a different story. In a pivotal AFC South matchup that will see one of the Titans and Texans secure your first win, we're predicting Tennessee's offense to tick in the right direction at the exact right time.
Robert Saleh just expressed his confidence that this Titans season is not over yet. "I feel if we can win one, we can build momentum," Saleh said. We expect Tennessee to finally make good on that opportunity this week.
I don't know why, but I've got a good feeling about this one. On paper, Tennessee winning their first game in Week 5 last year - after an 0-4 start - feels like a good omen. The Titans and Texans are also 24-24 all-time. For semantic reasons, Tennessee holding on to the series at home would be huge.
But Week 5 also looks to offer a few advantages for Tennessee. The Texans' passing defense has been among the least efficient in the league this season, and head coach DeMeco Ryans taking over play-calling duties could lead to a rough transitional period for Houston.
On the other hand, Cam Ward is coming off his best game of the season. With Carnell Tate good to go and the Titans playing their first game in Nashville in three weeks, the cards are quietly stacked up for a revenge game here.
The divisional stakes make it all the more important. Call me crazy, but I have the Titans in a narrow, offense-leading victory.
Although the Titans' offense is yet to crack 20 points, they have been forced to play in either extraordinary heat or rain in each of their four games this season. The weather in Nashville is expected to be 60s with a chance of sprinkles on Sunday, a welcomed change for the home team.
Houston's defense has been disappointing, giving up the sixth most points despite an elite pass rush. I anticipate big outings from WR Wan'Dale Robinson and WR Carnell Tate, as the Titans seek, and secure, their first victory of the season.

title: Titans Red Zone Report: Tennessee's Major Key to Scoring When it Matters vs. Texans
full_text:
So long as the Tennessee Titans continue to be one of the NFL's least efficient offenses, these red zone reports will continue to feel more like futuristic wishful thinking than anything else. Brian Daboll and Cam Ward have to find a way to get on the same page, and fast.
However, Week 4's loss at the hands of the Baltimore Ravens provided us with a one-drive sample size to properly diagnose the team's problems. The Titans found momentum in the second half, but Robert Saleh could have had his first win had one series of plays gone Tennessee's way.
Down 14-7 in the second quarter, the Titans were facing a first and goal in the red zone. We've already hit this issue numerous times, so I'll keep it short: Daboll ran Tony Pollard four straight times, Tennessee got stuffed on the goal line, and Baltimore scored in the other direction prior to halftime.
The Titans ultimately closed the gap to six points by the game's end - the difference between the team finding a way in on that pivotal drive in the second. In Week 5, it's all about trusting Ward's progression and betting on the guy under center.
Pollard is effective as a consistent, early-down veteran in an offense otherwise filled with rising young assets. Daboll using him as a four-down workhorse, however, is both predictable and terrible ineffective.
Daboll confirmed this week that he "felt good" about the looks for Pollard, refusing to express any outward regret on the plane ride home looking back on the incident. Again, though, the offense gave Ward the keys to open things up downfield after that.
Tennessee's comeback effort may have fallen short, but Ward would find Wan'Dale Robinson for a passing score in the first quarter. He'd then hit Carnell Tate in the end zone for a successful two-point conversion, too.
Of the Titans' four red-zone touchdowns this year, three have come through the air. If the Titans are set on allowing Ward to have this season to hash out his issues - as expected - he'll need to be given a chance to do so in important situations.
In a contest with the Texans likely to yield opportunities for both offenses, the 0-4 Titans could ask for no better reason to open things up. In red-zone looks, the Titans can't hope for the best on the ground. In Week 5, Daboll and Tennessee have no choice but to scheme for Ward and his weapons if they want to keep up with high-scoring Houston.

title: The Titans Score Less Than Any Team in NFL — But Week 5 Looks Like a Breakthrough
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans are facing a high-powered, veteran-led Housto Texans offense in Week 5. Despite being in front of their home crowd, the lowly Titans aren't being given the benefit of the doubt by pretty much anyone in the space. It's another underdog opportunity for Robert Saleh's team.
This matchup, while not a nightmare for Tennessee, does present a great challenge for Brian Daboll's offense. To keep pace with C.J. Stroud, that unit will likely have to have their best game of the season.
Per PFF, the Titans have the lowest percentage of drives ending in a score this season, at 26.3%. Tennessee has only reached 20 points one time, and has scored 10 or less on two occasions. Last week's 18-point outing against the Ravens bore improvement across the board, but it still wasn't enough to dig the Titans out of the hole they're in.
Lowest % of drives ending in a score this season Titans           26.3% Patriots        26.8% Dolphins      27.0% Chargers      27.7% Steelers       29.8% pic.twitter.com/ZQ9g58vLmQ
Yet, the Texans' defense may promise a real chance for Tennessee to break through on that front. DeMeco Ryans is taking over play-calling starting in Week 5 due to the defense's struggles. The pieces are there for Houston, but the execution has been well beyond.
Cam Ward and Daboll have to jump on that. This could be the leap Titans fans have been waiting for.
The Texans' secondary has only picked the ball off one time this year. They've allowed 20+ points in every game but one, and that game saw the Indianapolis Colts put up 19. In two of those contests, Houston allowed 30 or more.
Of course, the Texans are also 0-4. Experts may be favoring Houston, but the gap between Tennessee and the visiting team isn't as big as some people may be anticipating.
That is especially apparent on defense. With Ward coming off a season-high 222 yards vs. Baltimore, and rookie WR Carnell Tate accounting for 145 of those yards in his own season-best showing, Daboll finally seems to be working out the kinks.
We've got every reason to think the Titans continue to find ways to score here. That doesn't mean Tennessee wins. Stopping the aforementioned Stroud will be a challenge that Saleh's defense must embrace, and at least partially succeed in.
Week 5 simply feels like a cross between positive momentum for the Titans' offense and a matchup vs. a defense that's already in a corner. If there's anything about Sunday to get your hopes up for, Titans fans, it's for Daboll's scoring unit to finally find their footing before it's too late.

title: Titans Need Alontae Taylor to Turn a Corner With Tennessee Staring at a Possible 0-5 Start
full_text:
One of the Tennessee Titans' prized free-agent additions was cornerback Alontae Taylor, who signed a three-year, $60 million deal with the team after spending his first four seasons with the New Orleans Saints.
Taylor, a second-round pick in the 2022 NFL Draft, established himself as a durable starting corner during his time in New Orleans. The 27-year-old's ability to play on the outside and in the slot is also a valuable asset he brings to the table.
Entering his debut campaign with Tennessee, Taylor was expected to be a solid No. 1 boundary corner for Robert Saleh's defense. Through four games, that expectation hasn't come to fruition.
It's been a rough start to 2026 for Taylor. The Tennessee product has allowed an 83.3% completion rate (15/18) when targeted, 149 passing yards, and a 101.2 passer rating. Taylor has also posted an abysmal 39.5 Pro Football Focus defensive grade, including a 31.5 coverage grade.
From Weeks 2 to 4 alone, Taylor surrendered 14 of 16 passes in coverage and over a 100 passer rating when targeted in Weeks 3 and 4.
The Titans' defense hasn't gotten much help from their offense this year, as the unit is constantly on the field because of offensive failures. However, the defense has also been incredibly inconsistent, and the secondary has struggled at times. Taylor can be blamed for some of those troubles, though nobody in the back end is playing at a high level right now.
Taylor has never been an elite cover corner or ball hawk, but Tennessee paid him way too much money for him to be a complete liability in the secondary. Taylor's entire 2027 salary of $20.5 million is guaranteed, and that is a scary sight for the Titans if the veteran defensive back is playing more like a backup than a quality starter.
Regardless, Tennessee needs Taylor to find his footing and play like a CB1. The Titans are staring at their first 0-5 start since 2009 if they fall to the fellow winless Houston Texans at home this week. For multiple individuals and the team as a whole, it's a make or break week in front of a desperate home crowd in Nashville.
If Taylor continues to struggle as he is matched up against Texans star wide receiver Nico Collins , it's going to be a long day for the Titans.

title: Week 5 Injury: Examining Titans’ Chances if Carnell Tate Can’t Play vs. Texans
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans were hit with some concerning news ahead of their Week 5 AFC South matchup against the Houston Texans.
According to ESPN’s Turron Davenport, rookie WR Carnell Tate appears to have tweaked his back during the individual portion of Thursday’s practice.
It’s unclear whether he returned, since media members are only allowed to watch certain parts of practice, but the Titans listed him as ‘limited’ on its official injury report.
The talented rookie is coming off a monster breakout performance against the Baltimore Ravens that saw him reel in nine catches for 145 yards. And those numbers would be inflated even further had some missed opportunities not gotten away from him.
Nonetheless, the former Buckeye has really started to come alive over the last two weeks, essentially becoming the focal point of Tennessee’s offense, totaling 21 targets and 15 grabs for 203 yards over that span.
If Tate can’t go, the Titans’ already lackluster offense could be without their most explosive and consistent weapon in a divisional game they desperately need to win as they try to avoid an 0-5 hole.
Tennessee may need to lean on the ground game spearheaded by RBs Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears. But without Tate, it will be up to Tennessee’s other group of pass catchers to keep the passing game afloat. This would be a great moment for the Titans to get their money’s worth out of one of their prized free agent acquisitions, WR Wan’Dale Robinson.
The Kentucky product has only caught 16 passes this season, one more than Tennessee’s rookie has over the last two weeks alone. Outside of him second year pass catchers Elic Ayomanor has only contributed in spurts, while WR Chim Dike and TE Gunnar Helm have been non-existent through four games.
Because of this, Titans QB Cam Ward would undoubtedly take the biggest hit should Tate’s injury keep him out of Sunday’s action. The two former top five picks have a budding connection that needs all the reps they can get together.
It would be a real shame if Tate’s sudden back injury prevents them from building off last week’s success. Only time will tell how all this plays out, but for the Titans’ sake, let’s hope they’re just being overly cautious with one of their most important players.
However, this situation definitely bears watching as kickoff draws nearer.

title: The 3 Matchups Titans Have to Win to Beat Texans in Week 5: Can Tennessee Stop C.J. Stroud?
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans are widely doubted against the Houston Texans this Sunday, despite returning from a two-game road stint. Titans fans are used to that song and dance by now.
Tennessee remains in pursuit of their first win, and Week 5 is specifically important due to it being their AFC South debut. For reference, the Titans went 0-6 in the divison last season. It was the first time they hit that low bar since the division's inception in 2002.
To say that the pressure is high for the Titans to find a way this week would be putting it lightly. Here are three matchups Tennessee has to find a way to win in order to come out on top on the scoreboard.
JC Latham has sneakily developed into one of the best RTs in the NFL in his third year with the Titans. He's yet to allow a sack this season, and is finally looking every part of the elite player Tennessee needs him to be.
Facing off against DE Will Anderson Jr., Latham will face his most important matchup of the season - perhaps even of his young career. With RG Fernando Carmona's absence already impacting the o-line, Latham being pitted against a defender like Anderson could make or break Ward's ability to make plays in the pocket.
Latham called the face-off a "battle of respect" as he looks to limit the 4.5-sack defender this coming Sunday. This is Latham's chance to plant his flag in what appears to be real long-term growth.
This is the big one. The Texans may be 0-4, but C.J. Stroud's revenge tour after his four-interception performance in the playoffs last season is very much alive.
Stroud has five touchdowns to zero interceptions this season. He's led the Texans to 30+ points in two of their four games, and has thrown more than 340 yards twice this year. PFF statistics have him in the league's top 10 in overall grade, passing yards (1141), and passing scores.
An expectedly healthy Titans' secondary, which Saleh acknowledged today "hasn't been great" adjusting to his system this season, will have to counter one of the most explosive passing offenses in the NFL.
For an 0-4 team, it simply is no longer a matter of paced development and inch-by-inch progress. If the Titans want to salvage this season as Saleh believes they can, what is arguably their weakest defensive unit will have to play above the line.
With defensive-minded coach DeMeco Ryans taking over play-calling duties on that side of the ball in Week 5, it will be a battle between Saleh and Ryans on the sideline.
Saleh already lost a similar duel to Aaron Glenn and the New York Jets at the beginning of this season. The secondary stopping Stroud is one thing, but with a new play-caller in place for Houston, we'll get to see two specialized defenses in direct comparison.
The head coach dove into what he dubbed a "unique" zone system for Tennessee today, as compared to match or man coverage. It's a compelling conversation that hasn't yet translated to consistent success on the field, even with pivotal veterans like DE Jacob Martin and EDGE Jermaine Johnson finally beginning to show progress under Saleh.
It must translate in Week 5 if the Titans are to pull off what is being perceived as an upset.

title: Titans' Front Office Firings Can't Distract From Franchise's Broken State
full_text:
How long can a rebuild be deemed a rebuild? When does a team trying to reshape things from the ground up transition from a multi-year project to something deeper than that? The Tennessee Titans haven't had a winning season since 2021. Robert Saleh is 0-4 in his first go-around.
Yesterday, it was announced that the Titans were firing three executives in an effort to overhaul the front office. These include: senior VP and chief revenue officer Adam Nuse, VP of creative Charles Jensen, and senior VP of brand marketing Erin Swartz.
The latter spearheaded Tennessee's recent aesthetic rebrand, seemingly leading the team into a new era that fans have long awaited. Now, as a result of that new era being fully implemented, Swartz has been let go alongside two of her colleagues.
We have an address from the organization regarding this sudden move that was issued to the Tennesseean :
“As the Titans prepare for the opening of our new stadium and the future of Titans football, we are making changes to how we lead the business side of the organization. We will hire an Executive Vice President and Chief Business Officer to lead our revenue, marketing, and communications teams. As part of these changes, Adam Nuse, Erin Swartz, and Charles Jensen are leaving the organization. We are grateful for everything they have contributed to the Titans and wish them the best in future endeavors.”
Burke Nihill has been the Titans' president and CEO since 2020. Under Nihill, the franchise has cycled through three head coaches and four general managers. Just about every level of the Titans' organization has undergone a change throughout their half-decade downward spiral.
The lone exception is, of course, Nihill himself. Is this all just a legendary streak of bad luck, or is there something to be said about the person pulling the strings for Tennessee's unending rebuild?
There may not be a direct answer, but something more has to be going south when a team is constantly recycling front office and sideline names to no avail. There's a deeply broken decision-making process in there somewhere, the blame for which can't be deferred forever.
In a leaked internal memo, Nihill tied off this news by saying: "We adapt when it's for the good of the team. I'm confident this structure sets us up to do special things together as a business and as a culture in 2027 and beyond."
Coach Saleh is still extremely early in his tenure, and GM Mike Borgonzi has helped usher in more than a few draft hits since his hiring at the beginning of last year. "The future is bright" is a common sentiment being floated around this 0-4 Titans team.
But how many times have we heard that in the past five years? More importantly, how much longer will fans accept that sentiment before it loses meaning? That is, if fans haven't reached that point already.

title: 10 Commanders Quotes That Define Washington Entering Week 5 vs. Giants
full_text:
The Washington Commanders are back home for Week 5 , and there's plenty riding on Sunday's matchup with the New York Giants. Jayden Daniels is returning, the injuries continue to pile up, and Washington has some things to clean up after last week's loss in London. Here are 10 quotes from this week's press conferences that help explain where the Commanders stand heading into this NFC East matchup.
Question: “Morning, David. It looks like the Giants have been able to limit tight ends in their previous four games, outside of maybe Trey McBride. What have you seen from what they’re doing to specifically take tight ends out?” “It’s man coverage. It’s safeties coming down out of the sky wanting to create matchups, and guys have to go out and win one-on-ones. That’s what they’ve wanted to create. It’s a good scheme. They’ve done a good job over there implementing it through the first four weeks, and we’ve got a good challenge on our hands with them coming to town this week.”
Question: “You’ve managed to get the ball to Terry and to Diggs and to Williams, and so has Marcus. Do you think it’s an issue that the tight ends haven’t been as involved yet? Do you think there’s a way to incorporate them into the game plan more, or is it just the guy who’s open gets the ball?” “The guy that’s open gets the ball. We’ve dealt with a lot of different injuries and stuff like that up to this point, where people are in and out of the lineup. And obviously, I think teams do a good job of covering our tight ends, too. So these other guys one-on-one outside, they win too. But we’re just out here playing point guard, trying to get the ball to the open guy.”
Question: “And with Mikey, what do you need to see from him to get back on the field, to kind of earn his way back on there? And how has he handled this rough stretch?” “Mike’s a pro. Mike has been a pro with that. Going into the game plan last week was a little different. It was more so, it wasn’t like keeping him off. We went from a regular personnel, so our true three linebackers against their 11 personnel on the early downs, and then when they got to got-to situations, we went to Big Nickel, which is where Mikey came onto the field. They just were in that 11 personnel early down more than that, and that’s where Kain Medrano was there on those situations. But Mikey as a whole, he understands his consistency and just doing the routine things routinely. He’s working on that day in, day out, and he has a great attitude towards that approach.”
Question: “For you guys, the second-half defense has not been there. The numbers are what they are. Why have there been struggles there in the second half?” “We’ve addressed that with our guys this week and just talking about our ability to sustain, which comes with, we say physical conditioning precedes all else. With that being said, you may be asked going into a game and say, ‘I’m only scheduled to play 25 snaps,’ and end up playing 40. We can’t let that be a determining factor. We can’t let things out of our control be a determining factor. So our ability to respond, our ability to sustain not only success but adversity as well, is building the mental toughness for that. That’s been the focus this week, just tapping into the mental toughness however it may shape and not letting anything outside of what we can control affect our play. And then also focus. I think a focus, play in, play out. We talk about, you don’t have to be great and locked in for 70 plays. Just have to be locked in and great, or damn good, for one play 70 times, and that way you can take one play at a time.”
Question: On the Giants' defense and what kind of game Washington expects Sunday. “Yeah, it is definitely a trenches game on both sides. I thought Dennard’s done a nice job with their unit. They’ve got speed out on the edges. They’ve got big guys inside, linebacker play. I’ve been impressed by what I’ve seen from them. As you’re going back and forth, different packages, run game premium for sure on both sides. Classic line-of-scrimmage football day. Might be some good football weather as well. Even if it’s not, we’re still going to have a line-of-scrimmage game.”
Question: “Speaking of a guy who likes to give advice, Jameis Winston is someone who has historically turned the ball over a lot. How does your approach change, if at all, when you know there’s a guy who is prone to giving up interceptions?” “Well, that same guy is also prone to making big plays. He’s done that in his career, which is why, obviously, it’s not a one-way street with Jameis. Jameis is a guy who is high risk, high reward, and because of his reward and the plays that he’s made in his profession is why he’s still doing the things he’s doing now, especially for the New York Giants and why they’re where they are right now is because of a lot of him and providing those opportunities. We can’t be mindful of, yeah, he’s going to turn the ball over. He can also put four or five touchdowns on you in a heartbeat, which I’ve experienced that back at the Bengals, back at the Dolphins, and even with the Vikings when he came in with the Saints when Derek Carr got injured. So his strength is his ability to one snap and clear. That’s dangerous for an opponent because whether it’s a great play, he can move on. Whether it’s a bad play, he can move on. Each play has a life and history of its own, and he’s the true definition of that. So you’ve got to be mindful of that.”
Question: “With regard to the offensive penalties that you’re having, I know you want to have some continuity, but you do have the power to remove people from the field if they continue to make those mistakes. Is that something that you consider doing?” “I would definitely consider that. And I’m certain that we are going to get this fixed. Certain. We have to. There’s no ifs, ands or buts about it. Losing big plays due to a pre-snap foul, and in the defensive case a post-snap foul, cost us. We’re going to work really hard to attack that.”
Question: “Along those lines, is that what you mean when you say this one’s different? Just the fact that you’ve gone through what this process is like, or is it something else that feels different?” “I mean, yeah, I went through the process and it wasn’t the end of everything. Like I said, I was blessed enough to still be allowed to play this game, and I’m just going to go out there. I’m going to embrace it. I’m going to embrace the brace. Not really worry too much about it and go out there and just be the best version of myself.”
Question: “You have a quarterback like Jayden coming back after the dislocation and he’s coming back wearing the brace. How does that affect your game plan in any way, knowing maybe what he may or may not still be able to fully do, or is he full-go and you can game plan without limitations?” “He’s full-go, man. We’re looking forward to having him back.”
Opening statement, injury update: “It’s not lost on me, a lot of names on our injury report. I’ll give you a full list at 4:00, but I do have a few updates. Jayden, Sam Cosmi and Rachaad White are all good to go, and that’s a big deal. Unfortunately, Stefon Diggs will be out. Terry, I thought, looked really good today. So we’ll decide as we get closer to the game. Today, that was excellent to have him back on the field. Outside of those, I won’t have any other injury updates, but I wanted to give you the information that I had. I could share that with you. So let’s get rolling.” Get your Commanders updates delivered instantly to your phone by subscribing to our Facebook Messenger News Channel .

title: Commanders-Giants Weather Forecast Brings Another Challenge for Jayden Daniels
full_text:
The Washington Commanders are getting Jayden Daniels back under center Sunday against the New York Giants, but the weather won't make his return any easier. Rain has already moved across the region ahead of the 1 p.m. kickoff at Northwest Stadium, and Daniels will be playing with a brace on his left elbow after missing the last two games. That's already going to take some getting used to without adding a wet football to the mix.
According to the National Weather Service’s updated hourly forecast, the rain chance is 90% at 11 a.m. and 78% at the 1 p.m. kickoff. Fans planning to get to Northwest Stadium early for tailgating should still expect wet conditions, with rain also likely during pregame warmups. The chance of rain is still 74% at 4 p.m., so there’s little reason to expect everything to clear up by halftime. That doesn’t necessarily mean it’s going to pour for four straight quarters, since the hourly forecast doesn’t tell us how heavy the rain will be or whether there will be breaks along the way, but both teams should still prepare for a wet afternoon.
We've updated our forecast for Hurricane Isaias's remnants, arriving in the DC area tonight. Rainfall totals have ticked upward, and there's a risk of strong tstorms and perhaps an isolated tornado Sunday afternoon or evening. The latest on timing, rainfall amounts and storm… pic.twitter.com/GN6EDWaDyF
Daniels has been working his way back from a dislocated elbow , and one thing that stood out during practice this week was how uncomfortable he appeared at times while handing the football off with the brace on his left arm. It's one thing to work through that during practice when the weather isn't a factor, but Sunday could present a much different situation if the football is wet. Washington needs to make sure the exchanges between Daniels and the running backs are clean, because the last thing this offense needs is to give New York extra opportunities because of something as simple as a botched handoff. The rain isn't the only concern, either. East winds are expected to be around 13 mph at kickoff, with gusts up to 26 mph, which could affect how Daniels and Giants quarterback Jameis Winston approach throwing the ball downfield. Neither quarterback can completely ignore the wind, especially when trying to connect on deeper throws, and there's a good chance both offenses will have to account for it at some point. Kicking could become an issue as well, and not just because of the wind. Getting the snap down and making a clean hold are going to be important if the rain is still coming down, while the kickers will also have to worry about their footing on longer field-goal attempts. A good kick doesn't mean much if the plant foot slips before contact. Then there's Washington's defense, which hasn't exactly done a great job finishing tackles through the first four games. Wet conditions aren't going to help a unit that has already struggled in that area, particularly if defenders aren't staying under control when closing on ball carriers. We've already seen too many short gains turn into bigger plays because Washington couldn't finish a tackle, and a slippery field could make that problem even worse against New York.
Anyone planning to attend Sunday's game should probably have rain gear ready before leaving home, especially if tailgating is part of the plan. Temperatures are expected to stay in the 60s throughout the afternoon, which isn't particularly cold for October, but spending several hours sitting in the rain with winds gusting close to 30 mph isn't going to be particularly comfortable, either. A poncho or rain jacket makes the most sense since umbrellas are prohibited inside Northwest Stadium. The NWS hourly forecast now shows a chance of thunderstorms around 5 p.m. and into the evening, so fans should keep an eye on the latest conditions throughout the afternoon and before heading home. The forecast could change before kickoff, but right now it looks like the Commanders and Giants could be dealing with the weather for much of the afternoon. For Daniels, that means his first game back could come with another challenge beyond simply getting comfortable playing with the brace. title: The Giants Let Lucas Patrick Go. Now Washington Is Counting on Him — Commanders Daily
full_text:
To understand how important Lucas Patrick is now, you have to understand that the Washington Commanders spent the entire offseason trying to convince anyone who asked that Nick Allegretti was the team's center after abruptly releasing Tyler Biadasz. Regardless of the reasoning or whether it was the right move, letting go of their veteran center left the team thinner at a massive position of need. Commanders GM Adam Peters insisted Allegretti was their guy until training camp, when Allegretti went down with a calf strain and stayed out. Allegretti started the first two games at center after returning to the lineup. Patrick was signed by Washington on September 16 , and 11 days later, he made his first start at center against Seattle when Allegretti shifted over to take the injured Sam Cosmi's spot at right guard. Last week in London, Patrick stayed at center while rookie Matt Gulbin replaced Allegretti at right guard.
Sick Bill's TD got called back. Great execution. Mariota and Lucas Patrick make some pre-snap checks at the line, formation shift gets Yankoff as a playside blocker. MM catches Seattle in a post-snap rotation and with fewer numbers playside. 3 v. 1 block + Patrick seal. TD smh pic.twitter.com/YsIVmjrGwO
Patrick's situation is interesting because he was with the New York Giants during their offseason program and training camp, having been released during roster cuts. Now, on Sunday, Patrick will snap the football to Jayden Daniels against the organization that released him just a few weeks ago. Patrick had previous stints in Green Bay, Chicago, New Orleans, and Cincinnati, but was signed by New York on April 6 and then released on August 30 during roster reductions. He entered the 2026 season having appeared in 113 games, including 65 starts, 28 at center, 19 at left guard, and 18 at right guard.
Pro Football Plus: Coach Quinn said that G/C Lucas Patrick will be the starter at Center a veteran that has seen it all, this week key is cleaning up all of these mistakes that have mainly come on the offensive side. pic.twitter.com/jKXpryq2RO
Patrick has done more than just fill a hole since arriving in Washington, too. According to Pro Football Focus , he's played 129 snaps at center, allowing just two pressures, no sacks, and hasn't committed a penalty. His overall grade of 65.9 ranks 11th among 33 qualifying centers, which isn't bad for a guy the Commanders picked up off the street less than a month ago. Especially considering Washington's issues keeping a consistent offensive line together. Quinn confirmed Friday that Patrick is now Washington's starting center, which tells us this isn't just a temporary move until Allegretti is healthy enough to return. Cosmi is also back this week, giving the Commanders their starting right guard again, but Patrick isn't going anywhere for now. That's a pretty significant change from what Peters and Quinn had planned entering training camp , especially when you consider how much confidence they expressed in Allegretti taking over for Biadasz. There's another part of this that interests me. Patrick's two starts came with Marcus Mariota and Athan Kaliakmanis at quarterback, meaning Sunday will be his first regular-season game snapping the football to Daniels . With Daniels coming off an elbow injury and Washington trying to get its offense moving in the right direction in what should be rainy conditions , having someone who can keep the middle of the line under control is going to be important. The Giants decided Patrick wasn't worth keeping at the end of August, and just over a month later, Washington is trusting him with one of the most important jobs on its offense against the very team that let him go. title: Commanders News: Giants Get Boost Before Sunday, Dolphins Claim Kaytron Allen | Burgundy Roundup
full_text:
The Washington Commanders got the news they've been waiting for Friday, as head coach Dan Quinn confirmed Jayden Daniels will start Sunday against the New York Giants after missing two games with an elbow injury. The good news didn't extend to the rest of the roster, however, as Stefon Diggs, Marcus Mariota, Percy Butler, Nick Cross, Charles Omenihu, and Tyler Owens have all been ruled out. Terry McLaurin returned to limited practice Friday but is questionable, leaving Washington with another big decision to make before Sunday. Just one day after Washington waived rookie running back Kaytron Allen, the Miami Dolphins claimed the sixth-round pick off waivers , ending any hopes the Commanders had of bringing him back to the practice squad. Allen had 41 rushing yards on 12 carries through four games, but Austin Ekeler's return pushed him further down the depth chart. With Robert Henry Jr. already heading to Seattle earlier in the week, Washington has now lost two of its young running backs in a matter of days. The Giants have some injury concerns of their own , although Friday brought them more good news than bad. Safety Jason Pinnock (concussion) and defensive lineman Chauncey Golston (neck) have both been ruled out, but Malik Nabers and Andrew Thomas returned to full participation after missing practice earlier in the week. Isaiah Likely, Chris Manhertz, and Cam Skattebo also practiced fully Friday, leaving New York in considerably better shape than it appeared to be Wednesday. While unlikely, the Commanders could also have some more help coming before Sunday's game, with Trey Amos, Jeremy McNichols, and Deatrich Wise Jr. all listed as questionable. The three began their return-to-practice windows Wednesday, but that doesn't necessarily mean they'll be ready to play against the Giants. All three are still on their respective reserve lists and would need to be activated before taking the field. Given the number of injuries Washington has dealt with through four games, getting even a couple of them back would certainly be welcome news.

But that's different from what Kliff Kingsbury was doing with Daniels in the shotgun and no-huddle. David Blough has him running a more traditional offense that allows for him to move once the play breaks down.

Waiting for them there, the Giants will find a defense that is much improved over last year's version. What has gone right: The Commanders have looked like a legitimate threat with Daniels under center, nearly stealing their season-opener at Philadelphia, then driving up and down the field at Dallas until Daniels dislocated his elbow on the final play of the first half. While veteran Marcus Mariota was a more-than-serviceable fill-in, leading the team to a (temporarily) season-saving upset of the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3, he, too, was lost to an injury (strained MCL), forcing third-stringer Athan Kaliakmanis into action during  in London last week. title: Commanders Rule Out Six Players, Leave Major Terry McLaurin Question Unanswered
full_text:
The Washington Commanders will enter Sunday's game without six players: WR Stefon Diggs (hamstring), Marcus Mariota (knee), Percy Butler (hamstring), Nick Cross (illness), Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle), and Tyler Owens (hamstring) will all be out after missing Friday's practice. Diggs is obviously the biggest name on the list, but four defensive players, including three safeties, will be out against the Giants . Since the first injury report came out on Wednesday , everyone has been worried that both Diggs and Terry McLaurin would miss this week's game. McLaurin is now officially listed as questionable after returning to limited participation in practice Friday. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn stopped short of confirming McLaurin would play Sunday when he spoke Friday afternoon: "Terry, I thought, looked really good today." Quinn added that the team would decide on McLaurin closer to game time. UPDATE: Terry McLaurin will play. The Commanders will get Jayden Daniels , Sam Cosmi, and Rachaad White back this week. Daniels was a full participant in practice every day, clearing the checkpoint Quinn established last week . Cosmi started the week limited on Wednesday , but was a full go both Thursday and Friday; White was limited all three days but had no game designation on the final report. The final report listed four Commanders as questionable: McLaurin, Trey Amos (ankle), Jeremy McNichols (quad), and Deatrich Wise Jr. (quad). Of the four, McLaurin is the only player currently on the active roster: the other three had their 21-day practice windows open early this week and would need to be activated first. Friday brought the most encouraging injury news, with Nick Allegretti moving from not practicing to being a full go on Friday. Frankie Luvu, Jacory Croskey-Merritt, and Chig Okonkwo improved from limited to full. Sonny Styles , Ben Sinnott, Treylon Burks, Javon Kinlaw, Fabian Moreau, and Jeremy Reaves all finished the week as full participants.

title: Commanders Mailbag: The Bigger Concern With Jayden Daniels’ Return
full_text:
We want to hear from you! Each week, we invite you, the Burgundy and Gold faithful, to send in your Commanders' questions about everything going on in Ashburn/Landover. We want to make sure everyone gets a chance to have their take heard in the HTTR4LIFE Mailbag, so we'll answer questions on either Monday or Friday, depending on the volume of responses each week. You can send your Washington Commanders questions for the HTTR4LIFE Mailbag to hailbng+si@gmail.com . The Commanders will play host to the New York Giants this week at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland. This week’s mailbag questions focus on protecting Jayden Daniels as he returns from his elbow injury and what Daronte Jones can change to fix Washington’s second-half defensive struggles.
Question via Stanley M on Facebook It's important to understand the difference between designed runs and scrambling when needed. Washington was already using less of the read option with Daniels than you saw with Marcus Mariota . What makes that hard to see is that when plays broke down, Daniels was moving around to extend the pocket, and yes, taking off when needed. But that's different from what Kliff Kingsbury was doing with Daniels in the shotgun and no-huddle. David Blough has him running a more traditional offense that allows for him to move once the play breaks down. With that in mind, he was running with the ball more than I would have liked before the injury, but he was also doing things to protect himself: mainly sliding, going out of bounds when necessary, and avoiding hits at all costs. He was injured on a freak no-contact play when he came from under center after guard Chris Paul stepped on his foot. He wasn't playing with no regard to getting injured; it just happened. What worries me more with Daniels is other teams targeting the arm as the pocket collapses. We already know he will leave the pocket, injury or not; the question is how well he can hold onto the ball and still protect himself outside the pocket. He looked a bit uncomfortable handing the ball off in practice with that brace on, but I don't think it will change much about how they use him otherwise. Blough said Thursday, " He’s full go ."
Jayden Daniels in action. Note: he did catch the ball with two hands later. Also took snaps again. As he has been doing since last week. pic.twitter.com/pQsD8Gm5L8
Question via Cindy C. on X Seems like a question we've been asking for years about several different defensive coordinators. Joe Gibbs mastered the second-half adjustment; Ron Rivera stunk at it. Let's hope Daronte Jones finds the end of the stick that doesn't get him fired , since there are multiple paths to fix issues depending on what team you're playing. First things first, that unit is giving up 17.8 second-half points per game, which is currently tied for worst in the league. Jones pointed to conditioning and focus when asked about the second-half struggles Thursday. He used the example of a player expecting to play 25 snaps and ending up playing 40. “We can't let things out of our control be a determining factor,” Jones said. He has his work cut out for him, with missed tackles and assignment mistakes plaguing the defense through the first four weeks. If an opponent keeps winning the same matchup after halftime, Jones needs to change the coverage or give that defender safety help. The players still have to execute those changes on the field . Even the right defensive call won't get Washington off the field if someone misses a tackle or blows an assignment. I expect Jones to send the house at Jameis Winston this weekend. The test comes when New York adjusts to that pressure. Jones has to give Winston a different look, and the players have to handle their assignments even if they're playing more snaps than expected. Making Winston uncomfortable early won't mean much if Washington falls apart after halftime. title: Commanders Scouting Report: How Washington Exploits Jameis Winston's Penchant for Mistakes
full_text:
The Washington Commanders have an old friend coming to town this week as the New York Football Giants will travel to Northwest Stadium on Sunday. Waiting for them there, the Giants will find a defense that is much improved over last year's version. Jameis Winston will find it harder to beat than the one he faced in Arizona in Week 4, which intercepted him twice and sacked him four times. Winston still produced 250 yards and three touchdown passes in New York's 36-24 win over the Cardinals. Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones was asked about Winston's tendency to turn the ball over: "Well, that same guy is also prone to making big plays," Jones said, adding, "He can also put four or five touchdowns on you in a heartbeat." Winston is an old bird among a league of younglings, but he showed last weekend he still has some of that gunslinger mentality, going 18-of-29 for 250 yards and tossing three touchdowns and two interceptions; it brought back memories of his 30/30 season of 2019 in Tampa Bay. I couldn't get much out of his film in the Tennessee game; the matchup was played during a nor'easter, and the weather was a major factor. One constant: teams were able to get at him, as he was sacked seven times across his two starts.
Washington blitzes 44% of the time 2nd-most in NFL Jameis Winston when blitzed this season: 36.8 passer rating (28th) 9 of 18 (50% comp) 3.9 yards per attempt When pressured? 8 of 24 with 2 INTs https://t.co/SnRJmlGXDa
In his two starts, Winston has targeted TE Isaiah Likely the most (17); Likely caught seven of those for 66 yards last weekend, leading the Giants in receptions against Arizona. With opposing tight ends acting like a thorn in the franchise's side for what seems like forever, Likely is the name to watch on Sunday, especially if Malik Nabers doesn't play (he was limited Thursday). Nabers has done well with Winston, catching 11 passes (13 targets) for 138 yards and a touchdown. Winston isn't afraid to throw downfield, and he's had some success lately. Against Arizona, he cashed in on several chunk plays, including a 40-yarder to Malachi Fields and two plays of 25+ to Nabers, who caught six for 112 yards and a touchdown. Winston is constantly working to get better: "I've got to do a better job of making sure our best players are touching the ball consistently," Winston said. Daronte Jones is focused on Likely and stopping TEs in the red zone: "Continue to point it out to the players, make the corrections, show the awareness of where certain players are, certain looks, and got to be dialed in," Jones said. "You got to understand the situation of the game and how they’re going to attack and what we’ve put on tape. And so, you know, it’s a copycat league, and so once you put something on tape, you got to take it off. And so, that’s been the focus."
Every play of Jameis Winston v. Cardinals 18/29 250 yards 3 TD 2 INT 4 Sacks pic.twitter.com/VJT9k9Q4hp
Washington has to find a way to get after Winston, who is susceptible to the pass rush and makes mistakes often. If they don't, Winston could have a field day with the weapons New York brings to the table. Isaiah Likely is a nightmare in the red zone, and Washington is a train wreck trying to stop tight ends in that section of the field. The Commanders must find a way to eliminate the chance of it happening altogether, since stopping it seems futile. I'd show Winston pressure, then bring four and drop an apparent blitzer into a passing lane. Give him a different picture after the snap, when he has less time to sort it out. With Likely getting that much attention, Washington should crowd his throwing windows and make Winston find another answer. If the front can generate pressure without extra help, Jones can keep a safety over Nabers instead of leaving his corner on an island. The idea is to tempt Winston into a throw that looks better before the snap than it does after it. That's an opportunity to turn his aggressive approach into a possession for Washington. The Commanders can't assume an interception means they've figured out Winston. He'll throw the next one like the last one never happened, and Jones knows it. The Commanders have to keep getting after him without losing their assignments behind the rush. Otherwise, the same quarterback they just picked off could come right back and put six on the board.
